# Architecture

Rates Workbench is a modular monolith with a React workbench, a FastAPI service,
a dedicated worker, native financial runtimes, and durable storage. The current
production policy is [rust-production-contract.md](rust-production-contract.md).
Python financial implementations are independent reference oracles for tests.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Agent[MCP client] --> MCP[Stdio HTTP adapter]
    MCP --> API
    UI[React workbench] --> Client[Typed API client]
    Client --> API[FastAPI]
    API --> SQL[SQLite / PostgreSQL revisions and jobs]
    API --> Objects[Immutable Parquet / JSON / Arrow artifacts]
    SQL --> Worker[One durable worker per workspace]
    Worker --> Rust[Rust financial runtime]
    Rust --> HiGHS[C++ HiGHS]
    Rust --> Ledger[Native daily ledger]
    Worker --> Verify[Independent Python journal verifier]
    Verify --> Publish[Atomic fenced publication]
    Publish --> SQL
    Publish --> Objects
```

## Ownership

| Layer | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| `apps/mcp` | Permission-scoped MCP tools/resources over HTTP, with separate operations and strategy profiles. Reviewed generated route coverage, enforced role actions, bounded result transport and exact-retry recovery; no financial runtime or database ownership. See [agent interface](../apps/mcp/README.md). |
| `apps/web` | Workbench interaction, tables/charts, polling and rendering. All transport goes through `src/lib/api.ts`. |
| `apps/api/app/main.py` and feature routers | Request/response validation, admission and durable enqueueing. No product mathematics. |
| `app/store.py` | Compatibility facade and the sole local materialization of durable revision state. |
| `app/state_views.py`, `app/contracts.py` | Snapshot restoration, explicit state port and typed metadata. |
| `app/operations.py` | Allowlisted application composition, preserving existing queued operation names. |
| `app/*_jobs.py` | Domain engine adapters. The caller supplies the state owner; no duplicated state dictionaries. |
| `app/telemetry.py`, `app/job_queue.py`, `app/result_transport.py` | Progress/workload metadata, queue orchestration and ARW1 transport. |
| `app/persistence.py`, `app/repository.py`, `app/artifacts.py` | Durable revisions/jobs, portable transactional SQL and immutable checksummed objects. Storage does not import feature handlers. |
| `app/worker.py` | Lease ownership, one heavy job at a time, recovery, native invocation and publication fencing. |
| `portfolio-risk` Python package | Public input/output adapters, explicit test reference calculations and independent verification. |
| `portfolio-risk-native` | Built-in pricing, calibration, shared draws, dependency graph, risk/income/forecast controllers and treasury. |
| `portfolio-decision-native` | Transactional edit/strategy coordinator, LP construction, HiGHS invocation, allocation validation and combined workflow. |
| `portfolio-ledger-native` | Raw daily-spec normalization, bounded daily event/GL execution and closing reduction. |
| `portfolio-model-core` | Shared bounded credit, exact-observation fitting, dated contracts and supplied-fixing arithmetic. Its analysis entrypoints do not imply full scenario/ledger integration. |
| `portfolio-compute-control` | Shared native deadline/cancellation checkpoints. |

## Revision and execution flow

Inputs are typed snapshots of books, markets, assumptions, settings and provenance.
An edit commits a new SQL revision and invalidates incompatible published
coefficients. Module dictionaries are a local materialization of this revision,
not another durable source of truth. Each deployment process serves one configured
tenant/workspace; request parameters cannot select a tenant or artifact prefix.

The API snapshots submitted inputs and enqueues an immutable request with its
revision and model/binary identity. A separate worker acquires a workspace lease,
claims an attempt token, resolves the named operation, and executes it against the
captured inputs. Cancellation, deadline, lost lease, stale revision or failed writes
must not publish interactive state or a completed manifest.

Large result tables live in immutable local/S3 Parquet objects. References commit
after writes succeed. Daily workflow postings are independently replayed before
the verified manifest is atomically published. Optional Iceberg delivery uses the
existing receipt/idempotency contract. SQLite and PostgreSQL share the SQL layer.

The memory queue and its thread executor are for isolated tests only. They are
not a selectable production Python calculation runtime. Production execution
requires Rust and matching native artifacts; historical Python settings/results
remain readable and require an explicit settings edit/rebuild before execution.

## Native boundaries

Explicit product-analysis jobs invoke bounded native contracts in a cancellable
standalone process; adapters store raw inputs, format native output and retain
source/executable identities. Dated library preparation publishes through the
same durable library transaction and recovery path as legacy prepared libraries.
Its synchronous evaluator consumes native coefficients without repricing. See
[product analysis and dated adoption](models/product-analysis-workbench.md).

Product batches use borrowed contiguous buffers over C ABI 10 or bounded tagged
JSON requests with opaque graph/session handles. Standalone lifecycle, strategy,
balance and workflow executables also accept bounded protocols. Large workflows
stream table partitions rather than constructing a full cashflow/journal JSON
document across Python/Rust. Native deadlines and the process watchdog protect
transport and execution; component budgets are not a claim of an aggregate RSS cap.

HiGHS remains C++. Rust constructs its financial problem, invokes the bounded
solver and validates allocation amounts. Python never provides a built-in financial
callback inside Rust. Custom Python research extensions remain explicitly separate.

## Financial contracts and interactivity

Each run shares common random numbers. Base OAS is calibrated once and held fixed
under scenario revaluation. Cashflow-factor generation is separate from spread
discounting, so spread solves reuse monthly factors or exact-time CSR schedules.
Scenario/path reuse and bounded dependency caches follow complete content identity;
eviction may cause recomputation, never changed economics. Numerical reduction
order, accounting anchors and final-output tolerances are correctness contracts.

Unit-library builds perform expensive pricing and prepare coefficients. Synchronous
strategy evaluation reads the atomically published revision/backend bundle and
combines coefficients; it never reprices or recovers a session in a request handler.
Slow rebuilds belong to durable jobs. Decision constraint-only updates invoke no
pricers. Source changes require explicit rebuilds rather than silently changing
saved economics. Unsupported prepayment edits retain RESTART_REQUIRED behavior.

## Model scope and verification

Research regulatory weights, approximate forward units, monthly captured flows,
supplied FTP/regulatory assumptions and unsupported hedge/netting mappings retain
their disclosed limits. Conditional forecasts remain income-only. New model-core
analysis contracts do not prove empirical predictive accuracy or replace all daily
product schedules. See [models/implementation-plan.md](models/implementation-plan.md).

Independent Python/native final-output parity, native ownership tests, fresh-process
production defaults, durable worker restart/failure tests and browser flows gate
changes. Static boundaries and generated contracts complement these behavioral
checks. [contracts/README.md](contracts/README.md) documents generators, transport
exceptions and reviewed dependency cycles. CI configuration records intended
coverage; a validation report records checks actually run on a stated platform.

## Build and extension workflow

### Destination layout

Keep the existing deployable crates and package names while organizing their
internals by domain. The following is the destination, not a claim that every
directory has already moved. Create directories when their first coherent set of
modules moves; do not fill the tree with empty placeholders.

```text
packages/
  portfolio-model-core/src/       # Reusable financial building blocks
    conventions/                 # Dates, calendars, day counts, supplied fixings
    cashflows/                   # Dated events, rights, accrual and settlement
    models/
      credit/                    # Transitions, hazards, recoveries, calibration
      behavior/                  # Retention, prepayment and exercise state
    products/                    # Contract terms and product state transitions
      mortgages/
      deposits/
      installment/
      revolving/
      commercial/
      term_deposits/
      derivatives/
      funding/
    math/                        # Domain-independent numerical primitives
    accounting/                  # Reviewed credit, fee and dated-income policies
    treasury/                    # Explicit shared FTP policy contracts
    validation/                  # Shared admission limits
    transport/                   # Strict original-byte JSON admission
  portfolio-risk-native/src/     # Valuation and portfolio calculations
    products/                    # Product pricing and risk composition
      mortgages/
      deposits/
      installment/
      revolving/
      commercial/
      term/                      # Shared corporate/CD schedules and pricing
      term_deposits/
      derivatives/
      funding/
    market/                      # Curves, quotes, paths, smiles and driver inputs
    models/                      # Pricing models and model calibration
    math/                        # Engine-local solvers and seeded random draws
    pricing/                     # Prepared-cashflow discount and fixed-OAS solving
    risk/                        # Shocks, sensitivities and portfolio aggregation
    income/                      # Frozen-yield income and conditional forecasts
    graph/                       # Dependency graph, identities and bounded caches
    portfolio/                   # Books, cohorts and unit coefficient preparation
    treasury/                    # Capital and FTP, with explicit policy inputs
    runtime/                     # Execution controls, profiling and lifecycle wiring
    transport/                   # ABI and bounded protocol dispatch
    bin/                         # Thin executable entrypoints
  portfolio-ledger-native/src/
    journal/                     # Posting and reconciliation
    owners/                      # Product-specific recognition and source ownership
    replay/                      # Monthly, dated and credit replay contracts
    reports/                     # Closing, consolidation and attribution
    transport/
  portfolio-decision-native/src/
    coefficients/                # Prepared unit/grid contracts
    optimization/                # HiGHS problem construction and solution replay
    coordinator/                 # Transactional edits and selective rebuilding
    workflows/                   # Combined pricing, allocation and journal execution
    transport/
  portfolio-compute-control/     # Shared cancellation/deadline primitive
  portfolio-risk/src/portfolio_risk/analytics/
    adapters/                    # Public Python input/output transport
    verification/                # Independent production publication gates
    reference/                   # Explicit test/research financial oracles
    contracts/                   # Generated and handwritten transport schemas
```

A product describes a contract and owns its product-specific state/cashflow logic.
A model describes an assumption or stochastic mechanism that products can select.
Market inputs describe supplied quotes, curves, histories and scenario drivers.
Math has no product, market or policy dependency. Product pricing composes these
pieces; graph and workflow layers coordinate them. Shared product state belongs in
model-core; portfolio pricing composition belongs in risk-native. Do not copy an
implementation into both locations.

Keep provider access in application adapters. Keep assumptions and calibration
code next to the model they configure, while immutable observed data, fixtures and
generated results remain outside source modules. Tests and benchmarks mirror the
owning domain. Small helpers stay private beside their caller; reusable helpers
get descriptive homes such as `conventions`, `math`, `runtime` or `transport`.
Avoid catch-all `utils`, `common` and `helpers` folders.

Move one product family at a time after the market/math foundation. Extract
transport dispatch only after its domain implementations have stable homes.
Retain compatibility exports until downstream callers and generated contracts
migrate together. Independent runtime verification must remain installed with the
application; it must not be moved into test-only dependencies.

### Domain migration, stage 1

Native market source now lives under `portfolio-risk-native/src/market/`:
`paths.rs` retains production market-path construction, `curves/quote_bootstrap.rs`
owns supplied quote bootstrapping, and `analysis/` retains the explicit supplied
curve/smile/joint analytical contract. These routes keep their existing financial
and adoption boundaries. No provider IO enters the engine.

`src/math/` owns bounded least squares, seeded random draws and their Ziggurat
constants. It cannot import products, market policy, graph execution or application
code. Existing public `market`, `model_market`, `market_bootstrap` and `random`
imports retain the same underlying implementations through reexports; no duplicate
implementation or runtime wrapper is introduced. ABI 10, protocol names, reduction
order, original OAS, CRN and numerical tolerances are unchanged by these moves.

The first product modules now live under `src/products/mortgages/` and
`src/products/deposits/`. Mortgage inputs, risk and graph modules share one home;
deposit lifecycle, graph and accounting-capture modules share another. Graph
admission, pricing, metrics and type submodules move with their owning family.
All six former root module names remain compatibility exports. Shared kernel/ABI
dispatch and cross-product coordination remain separate follow-up work.

`docs/contracts/native-domains.json` records the exact moves and remaining flat
modules. The architecture check rejects new flat modules, duplicate old locations,
lost public aliases and reversed math dependencies. The manifest is a migration
inventory, not a second runtime registry.

Next stages organize the remaining product families, then shared model-core states,
ledger ownership, decision workflows, and Python transport/reference/verification.
Independent publication verification stays installed at runtime. Package-directory
relocation comes last, together with build/source-identity/discovery updates;
existing package names and deployment paths remain stable in this stage.

### Domain migration, stage 2

Another 68 source files now live with their owning products. `installment/` and
`revolving/` own their supplied-history graphs; `commercial/` owns cash extraction,
credit compilation, fee and factor sources, exercise policies, graphs, income and
unit preparation. `derivatives/` owns contracts, CSA, reviewed accounting, saved
sources and hedge lifecycle; `funding/` owns funding contracts and their graph.

`term/` is the shared corporate/CD schedule, dated projection and risk foundation.
CD elections and chronological continuation live in `term_deposits/`; the previous
`term_enhancements::cd` and `cd_sequence` paths remain compatibility exports. Shared
term structures are not duplicated into commercial and CD modules. The private
commercial serialization boundary stays private to the crate.

The inventory now covers 92 relocated source files and checks both root and nested
compatibility exports. Fixture references move with their owners. Numerical bodies,
wire schemas, ABI versions, public function signatures and publication rules are
unchanged. Cross-product protocol dispatch, portfolio aggregation, graph/runtime
coordination, treasury and shared model-core organization remain subsequent stages.

Validate native unit/integration tests, legacy public imports, native ownership,
generated contracts and architecture boundaries before promoting each stage.
Any source-identity change requires fresh matching artifacts and explicit selected
library/session rebuilds. A source-only move does not authorize rewriting historical
manifests, deploying, or claiming empirical model acceptance.

Build all three native runtime artifacts with `make build-native`, restart
API/workers, and rebuild libraries/sessions whose identity changed. `make build`
also builds the web app. `make check-architecture` checks static rules and generated
contracts; `make test-py` and browser/native suites retain their existing gates.
New products follow the engine recipe first, then adapters, book UI/KRD keys and
unit templates. Financial logic belongs in Rust; adapters transport and format.

### Domain migration, stage 3

The cross-product layer now has explicit homes. Another 47 files moved, bringing
the relocation inventory to 139 files:

- `market/` owns shared market preparation, immutable market caches, supplied
  product sources and indexed input adaptation.
- `models/` owns calibration, observed market-driver fitting, joint market/credit
  generation and explicit shared-model analysis.
- `risk/` owns mixed-book risk and KPI aggregation; `income/` owns monthly
  accounting and the separate income-only conditional forecast lane.
- `graph/` owns incremental and indexed valuation graphs and their bounded cache.
- `portfolio/` owns cohorts and audits, indexed books, decision inputs, what-if
  preparation, monthly/aged/product units, coefficient replay, candidate sources,
  forward programs and explicit ledger mapping.
- `treasury/` owns capital/FTP evaluation, source bridges and modeled FTP policy.
- `runtime/` owns financial controllers, cancellation/deadline control and optional
  profiling; `transport/` owns generated ABI operation names and bounded dispatch.
- `conventions/` retains the existing calendar and coupon conventions. Funding
  coefficient reduction joins its owner under `products/funding/`.

Previous public module paths remain aliases, including the treasury facade and
feature-gated profiler. The generated ABI manifest writes directly to its new
transport location. The inventory rejects new flat modules and missing aliases.
No numerical bodies, schemas, tolerances or publication contracts change.

Only `lib.rs` and the mixed low-level `quant.rs` kernel remain as root source
files. Separating that kernel by calculation responsibility, organizing shared
model-core and the ledger/decision crates, and the application adapter/reference
layout remain subsequent work. This stage does not imply those moves are complete.

### Domain migration, stage 4

The mixed `quant.rs` implementation has been retired. Its 25 source sections,
plus runtime and prepared-cashflow code extracted from `lib.rs`, now occupy
20 focused files. The 139 earlier whole-file relocations remain recorded
separately from these extractions in the domain inventory.

`math/arrays.rs` owns borrowed numeric views and row assembly; `math/functions.rs`
owns scalar logistic, lookup-table and spline arithmetic. These primitives have
no financial-domain dependencies. Rate simulation, behavioral paths and volatility
live under `models/`. Mortgage, deposit, term/CD, swaption and money-market kernels
live with their products. Forward cashflows and coefficient-only evaluation live
under `portfolio/`; yield income and accrual live under `income/`; prepared-cashflow
discounting and OAS solving live under `pricing/`.

`transport/` owns C buffer descriptors, operation validation, array adaptation and
atomic dispatch. `runtime/compute.rs` owns the shared bounded thread pool and
lifecycle execution scope. `lib.rs` now contains module wiring, compatibility
exports, allocator selection and the profiling macro. Existing C symbols, buffer
layout, status codes and public Rust entrypoints remain unchanged. No arithmetic,
loop order, numerical bound, assertion or tolerance changes in this extraction.

The architecture check guards every extraction destination and rejects a restored
mixed root module. The experimental ablation builder uses fresh isolated snapshots
of the new source tree and its local dependency crates, preserving experimental
outputs under `.data`; `--check` validates variants without release builds. These
variants remain separate from production artifacts and numerical acceptance.

The native risk crate now has only its composition file at the source root.
Shared model-core, ledger/decision internals and the application adapter/reference
layout remain subsequent migration stages. Matching native artifacts and explicit
saved-library/session rebuilds remain required when source identity changes.

### Domain migration, stage 5

The shared `portfolio-model-core` crate now places 51 source files in domain
folders; only `lib.rs` remains at its source root. `products/` owns installment,
revolving, mortgage, deposit, commercial and funding state/accounting sources plus
shared consumer contracts. `models/credit/` owns transitions, operators, event-time
paths, covariates and exact/panel calibration; `models/behavior/` owns observed
deposit calibration. Joint drivers and observation contracts also live in `models/`.
`cashflows/`, `conventions/`, `accounting/`, `treasury/`, `validation/` and `transport/`
own their respective reusable contracts. Existing root module names remain
compatibility aliases; private mortgage implementation modules remain crate-private.

`docs/contracts/model-core-domains.json` records every move and guards compatibility
exports alongside the risk-crate inventory. Calculation bodies, assumptions,
numerical bounds, schemas and publication gates are unchanged. The independent
financial reference changes only its reviewed source digest and exact byte count.

The mortgage receipt still hashes the same nine logical source labels and their
actual compiled bytes. Eight source files are byte-for-byte unchanged. Updating
the receipt's include paths changes its source bytes and adds 156 charged bytes
to the binding (141,787 total). The digest is now
`c07d2a5bf213c5d3860a722ce27079bd4a10120b1fc7e3b62118437a51571e03`.
The independent verifier reads canonical locations, and `.gitattributes` preserves
LF for all nine files on every platform. Same-size edits and line-ending drift
still reject. Old immutable manifests retain their original receipts; fresh
execution requires matching rebuilt artifacts and explicitly rebuilt saved state.

The architecture check also verifies that compiled receipt includes resolve to
the canonical sources. It never substitutes a historical source copy. Ledger and
decision internals and the application adapter/reference layout remain subsequent
migration stages; current source organization does not imply additional product
adoption or empirical model acceptance.

### Domain migration, stage 6

The native ledger now has only `lib.rs` at its source root. Forty-one source files
move into `journal/`, `owners/`, `replay/`, `reports/`, `transport/` and `validation/`.
Product owners are grouped by consumer, commercial, deposit, mortgage, derivative
and shared product-event responsibilities. Replay separates daily, dated,
expected-credit, realized-credit and driver preparation, with bounded schedule
stores under `replay/stores/`. Closing and historical reports live in `reports/`;
`bin/` contains only the executable entrypoint.

The ordered atomic journal reducer and its original tests move out of `lib.rs`
into `journal/reduction.rs`. C buffer and JSON validation entrypoints move to
`transport/ffi.rs`; normalized specification types live in `transport/types.rs`,
and raw admission/normalization lives in `validation/specification.rs`.
The existing Rust module paths and C symbols remain available. Historical output
controls retain their test/feature gate, and private helpers stay crate-private.

`docs/contracts/ledger-domains.json` records relocations, extracted source sections
and compatibility exports under the architecture check. Calculation bodies,
reduction order, numerical bounds, protocols and publication gates are unchanged.
The shared model sources and mortgage receipt binding are unchanged. Matching
ledger and dependent workflow artifacts must be rebuilt before execution; deployed
API/workers and saved libraries/sessions retain the existing explicit rebuild rules.
Decision internals and application adapter/reference organization remain later stages.

Optional historical source-control tests also retain the existing explicit
liquidity applicability contract. Their duplicate suites previously compared a
pre-policy runner directly with current output. Parent-revision execution confirms
the same mismatches and identical complete output streams across this migration.
A shared test helper changes only the documented unconfigured liquidity fields
and absent HTM reclassification date; all remaining serialized bytes stay exact.
No historical fixture, financial calculation or numerical tolerance changes.

### Domain migration, stage 7

The native decision/workflow crate now has only the composition and compatibility
facade at its source root. Fifty-two source files move into financial domains:
`coefficients/` owns monthly, aged, product and commercial library preparation and
retained allocation sessions; `optimization/` owns HiGHS problem construction and
independent allocation replay. `workflows/` groups consumer, commercial, deposit,
candidate, mixed-book, mortgage and treasury orchestration. Raw-book pricing and
its bounded accounting/ledger execution remain together under `workflows/owned/`.

The former root implementation is separated into `coordinator/session.rs` for
transactional records, staged edits and coefficient-only evaluation,
`coordinator/actors.rs` for bounded owner-thread dispatch, `transport/ffi.rs` for
the C boundary, and the thin workflow entrypoint in `workflows/mod.rs`. The original
root tests move to `coordinator/tests.rs` with their assertions unchanged.
Commercial original-byte admission lives in `transport/commercial.rs`. The three
executables retain their public dispatch routes.

Existing public Rust paths and C symbols remain available through reexports;
private implementation modules stay crate-private. New internal visibility is
limited to the existing session/workflow and transport/registry dependencies.
`docs/contracts/decision-domains.json` records all moves, extractions and public
compatibility paths under the architecture check. Calculation bodies, financial
bounds, loop order, protocols and publication gates are unchanged. Model-core,
risk and ledger sources and independent financial references are untouched.

Matching decision/workflow artifacts must be rebuilt before use; deployment still
requires API/worker restart and explicit saved-library/session rebuilding. This
source organization adds no product adoption or empirical acceptance claim.
Application adapter/reference organization remains a subsequent migration stage.

The original pre-migration architectural discussion is preserved in
[reviews/2026-10-01-architecture-historical.md](reviews/2026-10-01-architecture-historical.md).
It describes earlier Numba/thread/in-memory stages, not current production policy.
docs/models/advanced-product-graph.md:
# Explicit actual-date consumer graph

`advanced-product-graph-1` is an additive native component. Its first product
variant is `consumer_installment`, dispatching the existing distinct auto/personal
models in `portfolio-model-core`. Original contracts and explicit scenario action
histories generate cash and states in Rust. There are no caller cashflow/metric
tensors, Python financial callbacks, custom discount backends or automatic changes
to saved monthly books. Source histories remain supplied assumptions rather than
fitted borrower behavior. The initial synthetic request is
`examples/models/advanced-product-graph-1.json`.

## Raw inputs, measures and native ownership

The request contains graph/model/input revision and supplied paired-history
source identity, actual as-of and reporting ordinals, currency, ordered scenarios
with explicit run ID/severity and raw collateral curves, a base scenario, bump
basis points and typed positions. Curves retain full source revision, discount
factor nodes, collateral role and explicit tail convention; native logDF lookup
uses the shared market implementation. This fixed-note slice consumes no index
curve. Indexed products must add a native typed index/reset model before adoption;
an index path or financial metric override cannot silently substitute here.

Each position has a native `consumer_installment` contract and complete history
coverage. The contract uses the existing `InstallmentRequest` field layout as a
**known template**, with `identity.measure="contractual"` and empty steps. This
template is never directly projected: the standalone core path correctly requires
physical or pricing measure. The graph explicitly builds four role-specific
requests by attaching the declared history, measure, run and assumption identity
to that same original/known opening state. No physical path is implicitly converted
to a pricing path. Loan/cohort/source identity, actual contractual dates, original
principal/payment, note rate/APR, initial state and recovery policy remain common.
Future action histories differ by role/scenario. Recovery policy currently stays
at its common supplied contract value; macro-linked/scenario recovery overrides
require further typed policy support, not an invented automatic stress.

Every position/scenario supplies `physical`, `pricing`, `pricing_down` and
`pricing_up` arrays. Paths include ordered ID, finite probability weight,
assumption ID and typed native actions. All pricing roles and scenarios require
the same ordered path IDs and exactly equal weights. Physical path probabilities
are separately declared. Each array sums to one within `1e-12`, without automatic
normalization. All paths project and retain complete native cash/state/recognition
and default records, including zero-weight paths; missing scenario coverage fails.
Outstanding terminal principal/interest/unrecognized income/fees or truncated
recovery tails fail rather than disappearing at the reporting horizon.

The supported randomness domain is `supplied_paired_histories-1`. It records a
stable supplied-history pairing, and **does not consume random numbers**. It is
not evidence of a calibrated native stochastic policy or an actual shared-normal
CRN generator. Such policies must later consume and validate native random inputs
and their complete rate/index/HPI/state dependency. The current module rejects
other randomness domains. Paired action histories are raw model inputs, not
caller-prepared financial coefficients.

## Frozen base calibration, signed valuation and scenario risk

`OasTarget` is either an explicit sourced locked spread or a positive-cash target.
The latter projects only the base pricing paths for calibration, requires
nonnegative **total** cash at every future settlement and positive probability-
weighted rights, then solves once within `[-5,5]` with 100 bounded bisections.
Log-sum-exp prices prevent endpoint overflow. A signed or empty/nonpositive
future-right set requires an explicit locked spread; the target is never silently
ignored or resolved under physical cash. Individual fee/cost components can be
negative when their complete event cash remains nonnegative and monotone in spread.

For a pricing path, closing-after-as-of-settlement value is:

`sum_{date > asof} (principal + interest + fees) * D((date-asof)/365) * exp(-base_oas*(date-asof)/365)`.

Signed event valuation uses a compensated native sum and monetary admission.
Path expectations use explicitly supplied weights. Day-zero cash is preserved
in the native source and excluded from this closing value. No survival haircut,
second credit loss or physical-schedule discount fallback is applied.

`BaseAnchor` retains complete canonical raw calibration content and per-position
spread. Collision-safe identity includes original/known contract, source/paired-
history/model identities, base pricing histories/probabilities, target and raw
base scenario/curve. `reprice` compares full canonical bytes and rejects changed
base dependencies with `BASE_ANCHOR_CHANGED`. It never recalibrates. `repriced`
returns a new immutable graph/current request/result retaining the original
anchor, so revised physical capture also uses that anchor. Caller publication
must retain the complete immutable raw request in addition to result identities;
nonbase and physical histories are not all duplicated into the calibration anchor.

Scenario `supplied_history_dv01` is `(PV_down - PV_up)/(2*bump_bp)`: native
projection of the supplied down/up **pricing** action histories, with native
negative/positive collateral zero-rate bumps, always at the same base OAS.
Identical down/up action histories isolate discount sensitivity. Different
supplied decisions add their explicitly declared cash sensitivity. This is not
a claim that the model estimated rate-dependent borrower decisions or full
effective DV01. Raw curves/histories and bumped measures stay independently
admitted; arbitrary saved monthly economics are not switched to this convention.

## Physical interest and credit-state outputs

Physical reporting uses exact `(left,right]` boundaries. Core recognition amounts
are allocated by overlap with their native actual-day simple-interest interval;
instant cash-basis recognition belongs to its explicit recognition date.
`gross_physical_contract_interest` is **gross supplied-policy note-interest**,
not frozen original effective-yield income, provision-adjusted NII, net income
or pricing-measure expected coupons. Fees, principal cash, economic default
principal and principal-only loss remain separate. Principal cash includes
recoveries and must not be mistaken for performing-principal retirement.

Native source defaults retain recognized/unrecognized accrued interest, fees,
principal retirement, gross recovery, cost, net recovery, principal loss and
recovery date. Default removal is not cash. Gross interest already recognized
can require reversal/retention/charge-off under a separately reviewed accounting
policy. Neither the graph nor its gross-interest metric invents that policy.
The original installment formulas and primary product references are documented
in [consumer-installment.md](consumer-installment.md).

## Strict scheduled capture boundary

`AdvancedGraph::capture_scheduled(owners, policy)` prepares typed sources only;
it does not execute a ledger or publish journals. Every position must have an
explicit unique account/source owner, source revision equal to the immutable
graph input revision, receipt direction and `fully_scenario_generated` ownership.
The explicit policy is `consumer_simple_interest_par-1`, book basis
`par_note_simple_interest`, fees `reject`. Opening par carrying value is native
known principal. This is a narrow accounting basis, not discount/premium EIR.

Every physical run must contain exactly one path with weight one. Default,
nonaccrual, delinquency, fees, day-zero settlement, unsupported opening accrued/
unrecognized/fee balances, incomplete rights or multiple expected physical paths
reject the **entire capture**. Pricing paths never become GL sources. Analysis
still retains these cases and all their source events; capture does not prune
economic events. Scheduled payoff without a fee/penalty remains supported.

Native recognition origins are FIFO assigned to actual interest settlements.
Splitting an origin preserves its original exact interval; amounts across all
assignments sum to the original recognition, retaining receivables after partial
interest cash. The explicit simple-interest segment amounts distribute uniformly
inside that original interval, and payment cash is posted once. Output includes
`DatedSchedule`, per-event origin/recognition segments, par opening values,
owner/run identity and explicit full scenario coverage, including `NoEvents`.
Capture schedule selectors/coverage use execution **run IDs**, as required by
the dated store; graph metrics retain their separate economic scenario IDs.
No reverse-severity or missing-source fallback is generated.

Root's later native mapper must construct complete dated-store owner/run/plan
inputs, verify ledger opening reconciliation and exclude duplicate monthly
capture, legacy stress/prepay/credit overlays, sales/pledges and incompatible
income policies. Default adoption must additionally map principal retirement,
accrued impairment, recovery receivable recognition and delayed cash through
the credit coordinator. A recovery cash receipt alone leaves defaulted principal
alive in the scheduled ledger and is therefore explicitly rejected here.
Independent immutable journal replay remains the publication gate.

## APIs, bounds and evidence

`AdvancedGraph::{new,request,snapshot,base_anchor,reprice,repriced,capture_scheduled}`
uses immutable references/`Arc` snapshots; `analyze` is the raw convenience route.
Admission allows 256 positions, 13 scenarios, 128 paths per role, 4,096 aggregate
native runs, 250,000 projected cash/state/recognition rows and eight million
conservative pricing/root/physical-reporting work units. Bounds are checked
before path creation, then actual projected rows are checked too. There are at
most 120 actual reporting periods. Core consumer money/date/action bounds and
native curve bounds remain additional. Canonical input is bounded at 32 MiB;
logical retained input/result/base identity uses conservative four-times
serialized charging within 128 MiB. Bounded counting writers precede identity
serialization. Cooperative checkpoints run across paths, scenarios and root
iterations. These are component limits, not aggregate process/RSS or complete
graph/solver/ledger scale guarantees.

Focused fixtures cover independent leap/month-end payment/interest/PV/risk,
separate P/Q and explicit bumped histories, base-anchor identity and frozen OAS,
auto collateral depreciation through repossession, signed unsecured recovery
cost, loss/retirement versus cash, full native capture/partial-interest origins,
revised immutable capture, expected-path rejection, fees/nonaccrual, zero-event
coverage, terminal/domain/work rejection and the persisted synthetic example.
The focused native suite passed all 16 tests, and the targeted Clippy check
passed with warnings denied. This evidence applies to this component's source
and fixtures; the release boundary must be rebuilt and validated separately.
Kernel fixtures do not establish public/API/cohort integration or empirical fit.
Full #12/#17/#18 acceptance retains native graph/cache/controller adoption,
consumer state-aware credit/daily journals, original effective-yield accounting,
stochastic policy/driver ownership with CRN, source-linked histories and held-out
product/cohort errors. Card, deposit, mortgage, indexed and funding dispatches
require their own native measure/state contracts.

# Transactional native aged preparation cache

`aged_units::cache::Cache` retains the canonical typed `AgedUnitsRequest` and
immutable native result. The public API is:

```rust
Cache::new(&AgedUnitsRequest) -> Result<Cache, String>
cache.update(&AgedUnitsRequest) -> Result<CacheWork, String>
cache.request() -> &AgedUnitsRequest
cache.snapshot() -> &AgedUnitsResult
```

`Cache` is `Clone`. Request, canonical identity bytes, shared identity bytes,
template pieces and combined result use immutable `Arc` buffers. Cloning copies
only the small template map and its labels; native metric/cash buffers are shared.
The decision actor can clone for staging, update the candidate, validate capital
dependencies and publish or abort without mutating its committed version. Cache
success itself is not actor publication, capital refresh or journal acceptance.

## Identity and selective preparation

Exact canonical serialization of the complete typed request is the unchanged
request identity. Repeating it returns `unchanged_request=true`, zero rebuilt
templates/units and zero pricing work. Revision labels alone never form a hit.
Canonical serialization is deterministic struct-field/input-array order, not a
lossy hash. Input domains and complete request dimensions are validated on entry.

A template piece key includes its complete typed terms, quote/original yield
anchors, weights, side/category/capital labels, and its ordered prepared and
validation purchases. Changed or new pieces prepare through the **same** native
`prepare_with_work` implementation as uncached preparation. This rebuilds all
purchase nodes and validation diagnostics for that template; it does not scale
old DV01, interpolate new risk, or replace coupon/principal cash with income.
Unchanged pieces share retained native values and events. Removed templates
require no pricing. Changing only global input/grid revision labels regenerates
current result/provenance metadata without repricing; merged contract source
revisions use the current immutable request revision.

Shared schema, model revision, CRN, valuation convention, curve-as-of/currency,
reporting grid, base/scenario ordering, complete curve content and source
identity, bump, or interpolation tolerance changes rebuild all templates. A
calendar, business-day adjustment or accrual-date policy change on an existing
template conservatively invalidates all pieces. A newly supplied template is
prepared under its own explicitly supplied calendar. Unsupported product
semantics remain rejected by the fixed-contract producer.

The merged result follows canonical **request purchase order** and scenario
order, even when template order or cross-template purchase order changes. It
copies exact dense `[S,N,10,H]` native slices. Validation diagnostics follow the
request's validation-purchase order, then scenario/metric order. Native cash
events are reindexed to global units and compiled through the shared funding
producer into a newly sorted **full-tail** union of reporting/purchase/settlement
dates. Stable same-day source order, side signs and source identities are retained.
No pricer runs during merging or coefficient-only consumption.

## Bounds, atomicity and work evidence

The existing one-million dense-value, full-tail funding and event bounds still
apply. The eight-million native pricing/replay/root work budget is checked
across **all** retained/prepared pieces, not restarted for every template.
Dirty preparation receives the remaining admitted budget before financial work.
`CacheWork.pricing_work` reports work actually rebuilt, while total retained
piece work controls admission. `units_rebuilt` counts prepared purchase nodes;
validation-node work is included in `pricing_work`.

Retained admission is 128 MiB, and logical old-plus-next staging admission is
256 MiB. Charging includes canonical identity capacities, four times serialized
request/result bytes as a conservative metadata/native-container charge, and
additional numeric-buffer, event, unit and opening-state capacities. Serialization
uses a bounded counting writer before allocating identity bytes. Template pieces
currently retain their result metadata, including repeated market descriptors;
those copies are charged and can cause admission to reject a request that an
uncached single result accepts. This favors explicit rejection over hidden
unbounded cache growth. Old and staged-clone buffers share `Arc` allocations;
staging charge conservatively counts logically retained pieces again.

These are component admission limits, not a global process/RSS guarantee.
Caller raw inputs, transport, temporary projection/serialization buffers,
solver state, other native caches and concurrently retained actor sessions are
additional. Actor/session count and aggregate runtime admission remain their
own contracts.

Updates build a candidate, checkpoint, then replace the committed cache once.
Invalid input, work/byte admission, projection/pricing failure and cooperative
cancellation return an error without changing its canonical request or result.
Immutable snapshots cannot mutate the cache's shared financial buffers.

Eleven focused Rust fixtures compare complete serialized cached results with
fresh `prepare` **exactly**, including quote/yield/weight edits, native contract
tail changes, purchase/template/scenario ordering, validation-diagnostic ordering,
input revision rebasing, shared-market/model/CRN/calendar invalidation, removals,
aggregate work and byte admission, failed updates and staged clone isolation.
Cloned request/snapshot pointers prove buffer sharing. All eleven and the
existing 23 aged analytical fixtures pass; strict all-target Clippy passes.
The 15 public aged-strategy tests subsequently pass against rebuilt native
artifacts, including coefficient-only execution and missing-input rejection.
Public actor and durable publication acceptance remain separate tests. Full
issue #23 scope in [aged-units.md](aged-units.md) remains.
docs/models/aged-funding-design.md:
# Quote-aware dated funding contract

The frozen `aged-units-1` fixed-contract result retains principal in metrics 8/9
to preserve the current ten-metric solver layout. `strategy-aged-1` now adopts
separate native funding rows, purchase-cost limits and allocated cash-event replay.
Nonpar quotes are admitted by that versioned route. The legacy solver contract
retains its historical economics. All 15 public aged tests pass against rebuilt
native artifacts, including independent allocated cash replay and actual quote
limits. The 23 native producer analytical tests also pass. Public release evidence
and its measured coefficient-only timing are recorded in [aged-units.md](aged-units.md).

## Native producer extension

Keep the ten financial metrics and add separately produced purchase/settlement
cash from the same `advanced_product::project_fixed` projection:

* `purchase_costs[N]`: actual positive quote in currency per face unit, with stable
  unit index and actual purchase date. Bank cash is `-side * quote`.
* `cash_events`: native unit index, ordinal, event/source identity, signed bank
  principal and coupon cash. Bank cash is `side * contractual_cash`. Preserve
  complete tails; these events are not NII recognition or market value changes.
* `funding_ordinals[F]`: sorted union of purchase, reporting and settlement dates,
  through the **full contract tail**, not only reporting horizon. Empty dates are
  unnecessary; same-day events net once under explicit end-of-day cash policy.
* `funding_demand[S,N,F]`: at date `d`, zero before purchase; otherwise
  `side * (quote - sum contractual_cash paid through d)`. Positive values consume
  starting cash, negative values are retained cash resources. Fixed contracts
  give identical cash under scenarios; keep explicit scenario dimensions for
  subsequent state-dependent products.

All these amounts must be native-produced. No Python financial construction,
caller-generated proxy, mark-to-market cash or double principal settlement is
allowed. Bound dense funding values/event transformation separately before
allocation, and preserve source identities/cancellation. A result lacking these
fields requires rebuilding before dated evaluation or solving. The explicit
funding policy declares gross pretax contractual cash retention, end-of-day
netting and full-tail coverage. Taxes, distributions, fees, collateral requirements, intraday order,
funding costs and discretionary reinvestment need additional explicit sources;
they must not be inferred from pretax NII or the existing regulatory weights.

## Native solver and evaluation adoption

1. Retain coefficient NII as the external objective and direct aged DV01 as risk.
   Metrics 8/9 remain principal exposure for existing KPI reporting; do not relabel
   them as purchase cash or silently change historic `strategy-library-1`.
2. Native cash-resource rows cover every admitted `funding_ordinal`, with
   `sum allocation_i * funding_demand[s,i,d] <= cash_budget`.
   The current incremental, baseline-free contract uses constant starting cash.
   Full saved-book adoption requires separately source-linked base cash.
   Do not let a future deposit issuance fund an earlier purchase.
3. Check all full-tail cash dates, or require an explicit source-linked terminal
   funding policy. Reporting-period checks alone can miss an early CD maturity
   funding a longer loan. A generic rollover assumption is insufficient.
4. For a purchase-cost asset cap, the row is
   `sum(asset allocations * actual_purchase_quote) <= max_purchase_cost_assets`.
   Keep notional-based limits explicitly separate. Report allocated face,
   initial purchase cash and principal exposure distinctly; changing the meaning
   of the existing `max_total_assets` field requires a versioned contract.
5. Replay allocated bank cash independently from native event/purchase streams,
   in chronological order, and reconcile it to every constructed funding row.
   Validate complete policy/source/grid/capital dependencies before a solve.
   Missing/stale native cash tensors require rebuilding. Constraint-only edits
   consume already prepared tensors and invoke no product models.
6. The additive version-1 funding coefficient FFI evaluates only retained
   `[S,N,F]` data; the existing ABI 8 remains unchanged. Interactive output
   separates actual `funding_gap` and full-tail ordinals from reporting-period
   `principal_exposure_gap`. Missing funding vectors require rebuilding.
   Daily candidate journal acceptance remains separate from coefficient funding
   feasibility, and saved snapshots require compatible dated source identity.

## Independent fixtures for the follow-through

* **Discount purchase:** face 1, quote .9, zero coupon, maturity cash 1. Starting
  .9 cash can buy exactly one unit. Initial bank cash is -.9, terminal +1; realized
  retained cash .1 reconciles original-yield income. The purchase date is not a
  new unexplained par gain. A premium 1.1 example reverses this result.
* **Actual future origination:** quote .9 on day 30 cannot use a day-60 CD receipt
  on day 30. Resource constraints before and at each purchase catch this.
* **Coupon settlement versus earning:** face 1, coupon .1 paid at maturity has
  zero funding benefit before payment, although frozen-yield NII accrues earlier.
  After maturity the .1 cash resource appears exactly once.
* **Funding tail:** issue par CD for 1 at day 0, repay 1 at day 365; purchase par
  zero-coupon asset paying 1 at day 730. A reporting horizon at day 180 must not
  hide the day-365 cash deficit. Explicit permitted refinancing requires its own
  dated cash-source event/policy; terminal inventing is rejected.
* **Matched maturity:** asset receipt and CD repayment on the same day net once
  under supplied end-of-day policy. Shift either settlement one actual day to
  expose the resulting liquidity deficit. This is not an intraday acceptance test.
* **Amortization/reinvestment:** native scheduled principal cash from a first unit
  funds a later actual purchase at its quote. Include coupon and principal
  separately, and verify no duplicate income or principal removal.
* **Signed CD cash:** issuance is positive bank cash; coupons and principal
  repayment are negative. Negative note rates remain explicit signed contractual
  amounts; original-yield expense and cash do not become two receipts.
* **Public adoption:** native full replay equals prepared cash-resource rows;
  a coefficient-only allocation evaluation invokes no pricers. Test discount and
  premium prices, a purchase-cost cap binding independently of face/cash limits,
  stale capital and missing funding data. Deadline/failed-publication and daily
  candidate journal gates remain distinct. Historical snapshots retain their
  existing economics.
docs/models/aged-units.md:
# Actual dated fixed-contract aged coefficients

`aged-units-1` prepares a bounded dense coefficient tensor in Rust. The initial
supported slice is fixed, nonoptional corporate contracts and fixed CDs with
disabled early withdrawal. `advanced_product::project_fixed` constructs their
actual calendars through the same `dated_term` producer used by standalone
contract analysis; `advanced_product` also owns remaining-right valuation,
purchase OAS solving and immutable-yield book replay. Future graph/cohort/aged
consumers can reuse those functions. There are no caller-prepared cashflow,
opening-state, risk or income tensors in the input.

The synthetic request is `examples/models/aged-units-1.json`. It contains a unit
zero-coupon asset purchased January 31, 2024, with reporting boundaries January
31, February 29 and January 31, 2025. These are actual Gregorian ordinals; there
is no 30-day month approximation. The native module does not automatically
replace historical `strategy-library-1` or the existing approximate forward
program path. Root integration uses the same dense vectors in a versioned dated
strategy route; publication/evaluation acceptance must be validated separately.

## Input and identity contract

The request contains a strict schema, model/input/grid/CRN revision labels,
currency, curve-as-of ordinal, `H+1` reporting ordinals, explicit base scenario
ID, ordered scenario collateral curves, fixed term templates, prepared purchase
nodes, optional off-grid validation purchases, a positive bump in basis points,
and supplied absolute/relative interpolation tolerances. Dates must increase;
purchases occur at reporting boundaries excluding the final boundary. Each
template's prepared purchase dates increase in input order, and `(template,date)`
identities cannot repeat across prepared and validation purchases. Stable input
scenario/unit ordering determines `[S,N,10,H]` tensor ordering.

Each template declares corporate/CD product, side, term in calendar months,
frequency, coupon, amortization, day-count, explicit calendar and payment/accrual
adjustment policies. Corporate side is `+1`, CD side `-1`. Native construction
sets unit face, rolls maturity from the **purchase** date with the shared clamp-day
calendar helper, preserves complete accrual/settlement tails, and disables calls,
puts, floating resets and withdrawal behavior. Corporate equal-principal legacy
`annuity` and true `level_payment` policies are distinct. Sinking schedules and
CD principal amortization are rejected. Frequency zero is only admitted for CD
single-payment conventions. Calendar and day-count assumptions retain the
limitations disclosed in [dated contractual terms](dated-term-contracts.md).

Each purchase supplies actual unit cash price, original annual effective yield
and its immutable source anchor. Price is an inception total-right quote with
zero opening accrual; it is not a percentage quote. The native yield must discount
the complete contractual cash schedule to purchase price within
`1e-10 * max(price,1)` at inception, and separately retire native book replay
within `1e-10 * max(total absolute contract cash,1)` at the terminal date. An inconsistent yield
fails instead of being refit. Original-yield anchor, quote, fixed base OAS,
actual purchase/full-tail dates, and replayed opening states accompany each unit.
Results retain full scenario curves and template policies, source revisions,
reporting dates, bump and native projection model `advanced-fixed-contracts-1`.
Consumers must hash/compare the immutable full request as well as labels for
collision-safe cache/session identity; a caller's label alone is not equality.

Accounting category and capital-policy revision are explicit dependencies;
the five supplied weights remain research/policy inputs. This module does not
infer regulatory eligibility, HTM sale rules, tax policy or credit RWA. A category
label in prepared output is not daily replay acceptance.

## Separate valuation and original-yield income

The supported valuation policy is explicitly `contractual_discounting`.
Contractual nonoptional rights are deterministic and measure-neutral. This slice
does not translate a physical deposit/state model into a pricing-measure model,
infer risk-neutral default/prepay hazards, or claim those behavioral models are
supported. Future state products need separate supplied physical/pricing inputs
with native validation of purchase-to-age prefix states before conditioning.
Clipping a pricing projection made at purchase does not establish an actual aged
state under a different physical history.

For curve anchor `a`, age date `v`, cash date `t` and continuous OAS `s`, the mark
is `sum cash(t) * D((t-a)/365)/D((v-a)/365) * exp(-s*(t-v)/365)` over `t>v`.
Log-DF interpolation and explicit tails reuse the native supplied market curves;
see [market model definitions](market-models.md) and the primary
[Strata log-linear definition](https://strata.opengamma.io/apidocs/com/opengamma/strata/market/curve/interpolator/CurveInterpolators.html).
Discount time uses ACT/365 independently of contractual coupon day-count.
Changing collateral curves changes marks, not already issued coupons or original
yield. Curves must be collateral-role, common-currency curves.

Base OAS is solved once at **purchase**, against the explicitly named base curve,
to the actual unit quote. All ages, scenarios and bumps retain that OAS. The
root solve uses positive remaining cash rights, log-sum-exp and a unique monotonic
`[-5,5]` spread bracket with 100 bisections. Signed intermediate coupon cash is
rejected by this initial solver; negative-rate single-payment CDs are supported
when their total final right remains positive. No scenario OAS refit occurs.
Age DV01 is the native remaining mark difference
`(PV(-bump_bp/10000)-PV(+bump_bp/10000))/(2*bump_bp)`, in unit currency per
basis point. It is recomputed at each reporting date, including full tails,
and is never origination DV01 multiplied by a balance ratio.

Book replay starts from actual purchase cash price. Between settlements, carrying
value compounds at frozen annual effective yield `y` using
`B_new=B_old*exp(log1p(y)*actual_days/365)`; contractual cash then reduces carrying
value and principal cash reduces unsettled principal rights. Same-day source
settlements retain stable order. A negative carry beyond numerical residual
admission fails. Once complete contractual rights retire, a roundoff-size terminal
residual alone can be cleared. Each reported opening state is generated by this
native purchase-to-age replay, not accepted from a provenance string.

The effective interest for an interval is
`carrying(right)-carrying(left)+cash_paid(left,right]`. Purchase cash is external
funding, not income; principal receipts are not income; integral/nonintegral fees
are absent because this fixed contract supplies no such policies. The same
fixed yield applies under all market scenarios. The
[dated IFRS 9 text](https://www.ifrs.org/content/dam/ifrs/publications/pdf-standards/english/2021/issued/part-a/ifrs-9-financial-instruments.pdf)
supports separating original effective yield and contractual cash as modeling
concepts; this simplified unit recurrence is not an automatic accounting policy
decision or standards compliance determination for a bank or CD liability.

## Reporting convention and vector layout

Each reporting boundary is **closing after settlement**. Risk excludes cash paid
exactly on the boundary; state includes its retirement. Column `m` contains the
state/risk at boundary `m` and income over `(boundary_m,boundary_(m+1)]`.
Before purchase every coefficient is zero. At actual principal settlement its
remaining balance and risk retire. A following convention can leave a payment
right after unadjusted maturity; a preceding convention can settle before the
contractual accrual end. Complete tails and actual settlement dates govern those
rights. This model publishes carrying/principal/cumulative cash states, not an
invented accrued-interest opening or whole-coupon daily NII. Full daily contractual
accrual/right posting remains the separate dated-store accounting responsibility.

For dense `values[((scenario*N+unit)*10+metric)*H+period]`:

| Metric index | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Side-signed frozen-yield effective income |
| 1 | Unsettled contractual principal magnitude |
| 2 | Side-signed native aged DV01 |
| 3–7 | Supplied HQLA L2A, 30-day outflow, ASF, RSF, RWA weights times principal |
| 8 | Asset principal magnitude, zero for liabilities |
| 9 | Liability principal magnitude, zero for assets |

The layout matches the existing solver's ten metrics. Quote price and cash replay
remain separate. `strategy-aged-1` replaces principal funding rows with explicit
full-tail cash-demand rows, accepts discount/premium purchase quotes and reports
allocated face separately from actual asset purchase cost. Its optional
`max_purchase_cost_assets` cap uses quotes; `max_total_assets` remains a face cap.
The historical solver route retains its existing contract. Source-linked saved-book
cash resources and category-aware candidate daily replay remain additional work.

The additive `funding` result now preserves native `purchase_costs`, stable
purchase/settlement `cash_events`, explicit `scenario_ids`, a sorted full-tail
union of reporting/purchase/settlement `ordinals`, and dense `[S,N,F]` cash-demand
values. Before purchase demand is zero; thereafter it is
`side * (quote - cumulative contractual cash settled)`. Positive demand consumes
starting cash; negative demand is retained cash. Purchase costs are bank cash
`-side * quote`, settlements are `side * (principal + coupon)`. These arrays
deliberately preserve coupon settlement independently of earned NII and include
cash obligations after the reporting horizon. There are no inferred taxes,
distributions, discretionary reinvestment, intraday phases, fees or rollover
sources. The returned policy explicitly states gross pretax contractual cash
retention and end-of-day netting.

Funding data is produced from the same native projection as risk/income, rather
than supplied by an adapter. Contract source per unit, whole input revision,
event IDs and unit indices retain lineage. Native dated solving consumes the
same prepared cash tensor, then independently replays allocated source events.
Coefficient-only evaluation reports actual funding demand and full-tail dates,
with principal exposure reported separately. Missing funding tensors require
rebuilding. The 15 public aged-strategy tests pass against the rebuilt native
artifacts with no skips. [The funding contract](aged-funding-design.md) specifies the native
rows and their full-tail/resource assumptions. Component funding bounds admit
one million dense demand values, 250,000 purchase/settlement events and the shared
32 MiB metadata cap; these are additional to ten-metric and pricing-work limits.

## Interpolation diagnostics, bounds and acceptance

No interpolation modifies prepared native nodes. Off-grid validation purchases
must supply their own actual quote/yield anchor and must lie strictly between
prepared purchases of the same template. Native full construction/replay at each
such purchase is compared with linear interpolation by actual ordinal of the
two dense coefficient rows. This intentionally exposes errors around purchase,
amortization and maturity boundaries rather than promising interpolation accuracy.
For each scenario/metric it reports maximum absolute error, peak period,
maximum relative error where native value is nonzero, and whether every cell meets
`absolute_tolerance+relative_tolerance*abs(native)`. Relative errors that cannot
be represented finitely fail; zero native values use the absolute test. Outside
grid tails fail instead of extrapolating flat. Interactive consumers use immutable
prepared coefficients only; no pricer is part of evaluation.

Admission allows 32 templates, 13 scenarios, 512 prepared purchases, 128 validation
purchases, 120 reporting periods, one million total dense scalar values including
validation work, and eight million aggregate event-pricing/replay/root work units.
Terms are at most 1,200 calendar months and full horizons at most 36,600 days.
Dates, bounded nonblank identities, directions, money up to `1e15`, finite yield
`[-0.99,10]`, coupon `[-1,2]`, weight `[0,100]`, positive quote and bump domains,
roles/currencies, scenario coverage and unsupported semantics are validated.
Inherited curve/calendar/schedule limits remain additional. Root and cash replay
are bounded; cooperative checkpoints run between rows/scenarios/marks. This is
component admission, not an aggregate RSS or combined 60,000-position guarantee.

The 23 analytical fixtures check actual purchase/maturity/leap dates, unchanged
principal with declining aged risk, scenario marks at frozen base OAS, original
effective income and native state conservation, equal-principal and true
level-payment behavior, CD signs and negative yields, preceding/late settlement,
stable scenario identity, actual off-grid error, strict admission, cancellation,
and persisted JSON against independent closed-form values. Quote-aware cash cases
cover discount/premium cost without a par gain, coupon cash after earning,
full-tail short-CD funding gaps, future issuance not funding an earlier purchase,
matched maturities, scheduled and partial amortization funding later origination,
cash/income conservation and large-quote yield rejection. Public engine tests
separately gate native solver/evaluation ownership and coefficient-only timing.

On October 2, 2026, the 15 public tests passed against rebuilt native artifacts:
discount/premium purchase cost and NII conservation, a cost cap binding separately
from face/cash caps, coupon settlement timing, future CD issuance rejection,
short-CD/long-asset full-tail infeasibility, same-day cash netting, input-derived
cash-event replay, missing-grid/metric/funding rejection, exact capital-refresh
dependencies and fresh-process Rust-default ownership. Pricers and coefficient
rebuilding are forbidden during interactive evaluation. The warmed one-unit,
two-period median across 128 evaluation samples is **41,500 ns (0.0415 ms)**.
This is measured fixture evidence, not a portable speed or large-book guarantee.
The product DLL SHA-256 is
`94841147112e7814e8db6c203eb058c9a4c3e2ffcc12957b87bad04cffac3da0`.
The decision DLL SHA-256 is
`6bc037bc8d9e5a02fd61c4042fd7899f4a17fd6f04fe2838532fd1a22e386b86`.
Actor/durable publication and independently verified candidate journals retain
their separate acceptance gates.

Full #23 remains open for mortgage/deposit/indexed/consumer physical versus pricing
state conditioning, quote/coupon rules from native projected indices, observed
behavior and credit, source-linked saved-book/reinvestment cash conservation,
state-dependent quote-aware solver limits, durable library/cache/dirty-row and
capital-refresh acceptance, coefficient
evaluation performance with no callbacks/pricers, solver allocation and independently
verified immutable candidate journals. Exact fixed-contract kernels do not close
those gates or establish empirical accuracy.
docs/models/card-credit-accounting-v2.md:
# Acquired card interest-basis ownership, schema 2

`portfolio_model_core::card_credit_accounting_v2` is a separate bounded native
component. Explicit `card-credit-accounting-2` selection is required. Schema1's
financial formulas, negative principal-basis rejection and wire contracts remain
unchanged. No fallback, mixed-ledger adoption, empirical fit or accounting-standard
approval is implied: the result's three corresponding flags are false.

## Raw source and reviewed assumptions

`Request` retains the actual native `CardRequest`, `Review` acquisition cost/face/date,
position/currency/source revision and immutable original-yield/review anchors,
`RightsPolicy`, termination, claim identity, reporting date and raw actual reviewed
interest-claim collections. Review explicitly requires
`accounting_basis="supplied_non_pcd_gross_cost-1"`. No financial state, journal,
fitted yield, probability weight or discount override is accepted.

Policy rule strings are mandatory:

- `actual_terminal_principal_transfer_to_unpaid_interest-1`;
- `frozen_original_yield_on_whole_live_carrying-1`;
- `proportional_basis_realization_separate_from_original_eir-1`;
- `stop_at_source_default_no_claim_eir-1`.

The admitted slice is acquired performing, physical, fee-free, non-grace, no draws,
zero opening interest rights and no allowance/PCD. Only exact full principal cash
is supported; subsequent default must have principal zero and a recognized unpaid
interest right. The native source's collection fraction and collection cost must
both be zero: actual interest collections use separately retained reviewed inputs.
Partial principal, default before principal retirement, negative contractual
coupon, early cash creating negative accrued rights, nonaccrual/cure, modifications,
fees, grace, CCF and new draws need separate policy owners and are rejected here.
Negative **original EIR** is distinct and can be admitted when carrying remains
valid. Supplied review identities are assumptions, not proof of outside approval.

## Channels, finance and actual source order

Let P be principal, A gross earned billed/unbilled interest, Bp principal basis and
Bi basis owned by the unpaid interest right. Carrying is `C=P+Bp+A+Bi`. Opening is
`Bp=cost-P`, `A=Bi=0`. The unchanged native card projector is the sole contractual
economic owner, preserving class/promo rates, statement/minimum/payment waterfall,
actual recognition intervals, source default and commitment evidence.

Each live actual-date interval uses unchanged native `dated_income::evaluate` with
one event and the original supplied annual effective rate y. Effective interest is
`e=C*expm1(log1p(y)*actual_days/365)`. Gross A increases by actual earned a; Bp while
P>0, or Bi after P reaches zero, changes by `e-a`. No complete future cash arrays,
re-fit, yield-change input or cash flow approximation is used.

Full actual principal cash atomically transfers remaining Bp to an **existing**
interest right with zero transfer cash/income, then settles P. The original shared
`P+Bp` guard is checked before and after; Bi is never hidden in principal basis.
Transferred `A+Bi` must be admissible. Actual interest q releases `Bi*q/A` (all exact
Bi for full cash), decreases gross A by q, receives q once and recognizes the
negative of released Bi as **reviewed disposal income**, separately from EIR.
Exact native cash is retained; rounded excess collection does not become owned cash.

Order is acquisition opening, live recognition, source interest-before-principal
cash, source default, then reviewed same-date claim collection. Every date index
preserves input order. Source-default recognition includes the actual default date,
then stops original EIR. Default claims receive no implied EIR. Gross A and Bi must
be paired under either transfer/transfer or reversal/recognition default policy.
Default and collection shared credit intents plus supplemental basis postings form
one atomic action. Individual gross claims and basis remain visible after default,
including when their net carrying is zero.

Reviewed closure requires the source's exact P, billed/unbilled interest, fees,
limit and undrawn to be zero, and owned channels/claims closed under existing
unchanged reconciliation tolerances. A source default can retain incomplete claims;
reporting does not prune them. No principal-zero payoff inference is made.

For each committed state, total live/default carrying equals original cost minus
cash received plus original EIR, reviewed disposal income and shared default income.
Postings use the existing debit-positive convention and balance within unchanged
`1e-9 + 1e-12*abs(reference)` reconciliation semantics. Interest carrying checks
retain the frozen proof's existing `-1e-9` bound. Nothing zeroes residual rights or
relaxes the shared principal-basis rule.

## Compact result and exclusive downstream owner

`ResultData` retains raw input and full native economic source once, then flat
`events`, `shared_intents`, `income_steps` and `actions` arenas. `Daily` holds only a
current `Snapshot` and action range. An `AtomicAction` holds event/intent/income
ranges, immutable source-recognition/cash/collection lineage and committed state.
Snapshots retain separate live Bi and claim-ID-to-Bi ownership alongside unchanged
`AccountingState`. Card balance classes are source classes; no new credit-state
origins are inferred.

**The event arena is the complete posting stream.** Shared intents and income
receipts are evidence referenced by action ranges; replaying their postings again
would double accounting. Source indices plus the retained raw/source and review,
yield, claim, date and atomic-action identities make replay deterministic. Atomic
staging clones only current state and newly proposed bounded receipts; failure
preserves all prior balances, earnings and arena cursors.

Downstream adoption still needs the existing Sim to own supplemental signed live
and default interest-basis accounts. Negative Bi is a contra receivable adjustment,
not deferred income. Gross rights cannot be netted away across paths. Allocation
and physical path weight belong to that exclusive outer owner and must apply once.
Treasury net-carrying mappings, capital verification, persisted independent replay,
publication/cancellation/lease fences and public transport remain separate gates.

## Admission and controls

`audit_request` returns full end date, conservative work, raw bytes, reserved bytes
and maximum action/event/income counts without card projection. It validates every
raw source action/review, including zero-allocation callers. `audit_request_with_check`
and `evaluate_with_check` accept caller-native cooperative control checks. Checks
surround the bounded source projector and run between serialization chunks, dates,
cash/default/collection actions and final retained verification. The existing
projector itself is unchanged and is limited here to 64 days and 64 source actions.

Limits are 64 actual days, 64 steps+cycles, 16 collections, 256 conservative events,
1MiB raw input, 16MiB component reservation/result and 2 million conservative work
units. Monetary values retain the shared 1e15 limit and EIR range -0.99 through10.
All byte/work/count admission arithmetic uses checked addition/multiplication.
Arena capacity is reserved/charged before projection. Every staged action and daily
snapshot is charged before retention. Final charging includes actual vector
capacities, conservative map-node space and full JSON-escaped numeric/identity
representation, then rejects overflow of the predeclared reservation. This is a
component capacity contract, not an aggregate process RSS guarantee.

Date/statement/source indices are built once. Income steps have exactly one native
input event and result row. Current states retain at most one default claim with16
settled IDs. Storage is linear in dates, source and flat evidence, with explicitly
bounded current claim snapshots; no daily cumulative history cloning remains.

## Validation and context

The tracked Core fixture contains 18 frozen typed proof cases, independently
raw-verified by 67 artifact reference checks. Twelve accepted cases expand exactly
to the same complete native card source, 492 daily states, ordered posting events,
dated-income inputs/results, default claims and action lineage; six invalid cases
remain rejected. Additional hand/bounds/cancellation/escaped-metadata/flat-retention
and atomic failure tests cover the compact representation. The evidence is
synthetic and does not establish empirical issuer fit or complete #19/#22/#25 scope.

The installed independent source suite passes 120 checks (79 pure and 41 actual
public-process checks) against the rebuilt official lifecycle. Explicit durable
primitive publication and final execution fences pass ten API checks. In the
[tagged mixed owner](product-mixed-product-credit.md), complete actions enter the
existing Sim and ordered GL; gross rights and signed basis close independently
before weights apply. The component result's own mixed/adoption flags stay false;
the outer mixed owner supplies its separate journal and verified closing evidence.
That outer lane passes 97 Ledger and 74 Decision tests with strict Clippy and 89
independent mixed-source checks against the rebuilt default workflow. The complete
installed bundle passes 1,842 engine tests (two reference-only skips), 493 API
tests and 40 browser cases. The final gates select no DEBUG override; identities
are retained in `artifacts/card-credit-v2-model-identities.json`, with
`deployed=false`. Wider issue scope remains required.

Signed live/default interest-basis adjustments are explicit asset accounts in
closing-capital preparation. Ten native and six independent journal/bridge hand
calculations preserve signed assets/RWA and distinct original-EIR/basis income.
Separate matching `closing_capital_eligible:true` native/independent/persisted
permission is required at the complete-tail date with supplied policies/weights.
`capital_ftp_eligible:false` remains; no interim capital or modeled FTP is inferred.

[CFPB payment-allocation rules](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/53/)
distinguish excess-payment allocation from minimum allocation. [CFPB finance-charge
rules](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/54/) address
grace-related charges. They motivate retaining actual card conventions and rejecting
unsupported grace ownership; neither source prescribes the supplied basis-transfer
or original-yield disposal policy in this component.
