# Acquired card runoff and reviewed credit intents

`card-credit-accounting-1` is an explicit native source contract for one acquired,
initially performing card account with a supplied physical runoff history.
`consumer_card::simulate` owns all principal, contractual interest, billed state,
payment/default and recovery economics. The adapter uses frozen original-EIR
income and the same reviewed `credit_accounting` operator as the installment
owner. No second principal/default projection or probability scaling runs.

Public Core export, native lifecycle dispatch and transport-only adapter are
implemented and pass 15 public native fixtures plus 93 independent/public DEBUG
process checks (55 pure source checks and 38 actual lifecycle cases). The official
product release is rebuilt, and all 93 checks pass against its default lifecycle.
Ten durable primitive publication/reopen/failure-fence API checks also pass.
The tagged installment/card mixed owner also passes independent source/ordered
journal, durable publication and full-tail closing-capital checks. The rebuilt
bundle passes 1,627 engine tests (two reference-only skips), 445 API tests and
37 browser cases, including primitive/mixed save and reopen. These local checks
do not establish deployment; the wider gates below remain required.

## Admitted source and explicit closure

The strict request retains raw `CardRequest`, path/economic-source identity,
purchase date/principal/cost/original yield and anchor, review policies, report
date, allowance and chargeoff instructions, and an explicit `Termination`.
Economic-source revision equals the raw contract revision. Aggregate opening
principal is positive and exactly equals purchase principal; purchase occurs at
as-of. The source must have zero opening billed/unbilled/unrecognized interest,
fees and grace shadow. Non-PCD gross acquisition cost and an independently
reviewed original annual effective yield are supplied, never inferred from Q.

The first lane accepts `Payment`, `Default` and one actual final `SetLimit0`
for reviewed nondefault closure. It rejects new draws, fees, rate/state changes,
other limit edits and as-of actions. Both purchase-grace switches are false.
ACT/360 or ACT/365 fixed contractual accrual, class rates, genuine promo expiry,
minimum/excess allocation, statement cycles and billed-only compounding remain
the card projector's supplied conventions. Unsupported events reject the whole
request; they are not pruned from the result.

`SourceDefault` requires the exact native source default. A nondefault
`ReviewedZeroRightsClosure` requires a reviewed date, one raw zero-limit action
on that date, no later actions, and zero principal/billed/unbilled/fees/limit/
undrawn at closure and full source end. Limit zero is not itself an inferred
legal closure; the review declares closure and the source proves financial rights.
Accounting status is retained separately from source `ConsumerState`: a zero
card balance is not relabeled as an installment `PaidOff` state.

## Interest, statements and original income

Native daily earned non-grace recognition is accounted once. A statement moves
earned unbilled interest into billed charges without recognizing income again.
Payments settle posted finance charges under the original card waterfall; they
do not settle unbilled charges prematurely. Recognition indices plus the retained
source identify lot/date intervals, because a card lot origin ID repeats across
days. `StatementReceipt` retains native index/date/due and explicitly records
`interest_recognized_again=false`.

The original EIR prefix uses purchase gross carrying value and the existing
ACT/365 fixed recurrence `C * expm1(log1p(y)/365)` on actual dates. Source coupon
day count remains separate. Principal and cash interest reduce carrying value;
earned interest updates the accrued right, and `effective - contractual earned`
updates basis. For reviewed closure, its day's final cash is excluded from the
prefix recurrence so actual ordered cash then reviewed signed basis retirement
can execute explicitly. Original EIR continues through an admitted interest-only
tail and stops at default or reviewed closure. The income operator's carrying
guards and shared accounting policy guards are unchanged.

For example, principal 100 at 36% ACT/360 earns 1 through day 10. A payment of 100
before the day 10 statement pays principal while leaving unbilled interest of 1,
which is subsequently billed and paid on day 11. Reviewed cost 101/original EIR 0
retains principal 0, accrued interest 1 and basis 0 between those dates, then
closes with total cash 101 and no income plug. Paying principal to zero on day 10
does not retire that accrued right.

**Current basis limitation:** cost 100/original EIR 0 in that same valid card history
leaves principal 0/accrued interest 1/basis -1 and total carrying 0 during the interest tail.
The shared accounting operator rejects negative principal-plus-basis. This source
retains an explicit rejection regression rather than skipping that guard. Positive
EIR can likewise leave a discount allocated to an interest-only asset; reviewed
basis-on-interest ownership is a required future extension. No asset/right is
silently zeroed, and an original EIR is not changed to force admission.

The admitted fee-free installment adapter has a different payment waterfall:
recognized and unrecognized coupon settle before principal. Its material
principal-zero/unpaid-coupon state is therefore unavailable in the current lane.
This distinction does not authorize relaxing the shared accounting guard for cards.

## Default, recovery and commitment

Prior-day recognition occurs before supplied same-day actions. A payment before
default reduces the exact source principal under the card waterfall. Default
then consumes actual remaining principal plus all recognized billed/unbilled
interest and current basis. The shared operator reverses or transfers accrued
interest and recognizes or transfers basis under the immutable reviewed policy.
Payment after default is rejected by the card projector. All balance classes
map to the performing credit origin in this lane; purchase/cash/promo classes
are never misidentified as performing/watch/delinquent credit states.

Gross principal-only recovery and cost are separated exactly as for the installment
adapter: shared claim loss is `P-gross`, gross cash reduces that claim, and a
separate reviewed same-date expense pays cost. Their net equals native source
recovery. Economic total loss is a retained diagnostic, not an extra provision.
The first policy requires `0 <= cost <= gross <= P`; it rejects surplus proceeds
and uncovered cost. If gross equals cost and the native model emits no net-cash
event, lineage retains the actual default coordinate rather than inventing a
recovery cash ID. Reviewed chargeoffs and allowance updates remain separate.

`Daily` retains source billed/unbilled arrays, limit and undrawn alongside accounted
monetary state. Undrawn is an unfunded source commitment under
`retained_source_undrawn_no_ccf_no_draw-1`; shared monetary undrawn/contingent draw
is zero. Its receipt retains the default/closure retirement coordinate and policy.
There is no implied CCF, additional funded draw, unused-line pricing or full
off-balance-sheet EAD claim. The current source lacks a predefault event-phase
commitment snapshot; wider CCF ownership needs that source and booking contract.

Reporting is an actual-date end-of-day snapshot. Full replay keeps all economic
recovery and reviewed chargeoff dates. Unpaid default claims retain principal,
accrued and signed basis instead of being written off automatically. The primitive
seeds acquisition monetary state but emits no acquisition cash/equity journal.

## Bounds, tests and adoption

Limits are 1080 days, 64 review instructions, 1 MiB raw input, 64 MiB retained
result, 2 million conservative adapter work units and the shared 1e15 monetary
bound. Native card's existing 250,000 lot/day/cycle admission also applies. Cash and
recognition are indexed by actual date, avoiding day×all-recognition scans.
Cooperative native control checks surround bounded projection/income stages and
daily accounting; failure returns no result. These are component limits, not an
aggregate process-RSS cap. Existing final/ownership tolerances are unchanged.

The focused native fixtures cover prestatement default, billed versus unbilled
recognition, interest-only rights, premium/discount/negative original EIR,
same-day payment/default/recovery/chargeoff order, class/promo behavior, gross/net
cost, retained claims/undrawn memo, unsupported ownership, cancellation and the
negative principal-basis rejection. Fifteen native fixtures and focused strict
Clippy pass for the public source, along with 93 independent/process checks and
10 durable primitive API gates. Shared mixed-owner and wider adoption still
require their separately documented publication and acceptance checks.

An exclusive mixed owner must acquire once, recognize initial allowance once
under its reviewed policy, apply allocation and physical weight once, post these
intents to the same pooled daily GL, and bypass duplicate legacy/monthly/default
ownership. Independent raw and persisted ordered journal/closing verification
remain publication gates. The primitive has no implicit mixed adoption or empirical claim.
General grace, fees, draws/CCF, nonaccrual, stochastic/empirical behavior,
solver/capital and combined scale scope under #19/#25 remain open.

## Primary context

[CFPB §1026.53](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/53/)
distinguishes excess-payment allocation from issuer minimum allocation; the
projector's supplied conventions remain authoritative for this supported policy.
[CFPB §1026.54](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/54/)
and [its interest explanation](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/how-does-my-credit-card-company-calculate-the-amount-of-interest-i-owe-en-51/)
make purchase grace and transaction APR distinctions material. This first lane
rejects the broader grace/fee boundary instead of treating shadow amounts as book
income. These references inform contract design; this supplied-source contract establishes
neither universal issuer terms nor regulatory/accounting compliance.

# Supplied revolving-card product graph

`card-product-graph-1` is an additive Rust analysis component for issue #19. It
adopts the existing `consumer-card-1` native daily state model into explicit
physical and pricing histories, collateral discounting, original base OAS and
paired scenario risk. It does not complete the consumer empirical, saved-book,
ledger, strategy, treasury or combined scale acceptance gates.

The [synthetic raw example](../../examples/models/card-product-graph-1.json)
starts with cash-advance principal 1,000 at APR 0.365 on ACT/365F. One day earns
exactly 1, the statement bills it, the supplied APR becomes zero and next-day
payment is 1,001 followed by a zero line limit. A collateral rate 0.05 and locked
OAS -0.05 cancel in discounting, giving PV 1,001; first-period gross recognition
is 1 and second-period interest cash is 1. This is a hand fixture, not observed
card performance or a trading recommendation.

The public API is `card_graph::analyze(&Request)` or immutable
`CardGraph::new`, `request`, `snapshot`, `base_anchor`, `reprice` and `repriced`.
Every position supplies a known opening `CardRequest` with contractual measure,
empty steps, exact position/currency/as-of identity and its complete native
contract/policy/source version. Each scenario supplies separate P, Q, Q-down
and Q-up action histories, explicit path IDs, weights and assumption IDs. The
graph generates native card requests with the selected measure, scenario run
ID and history identity. It retains all resulting daily states, statements,
recognition intervals, cash and default/recovery records, including the tail.

## Measures, rates and discounting

P histories can have independent IDs and probabilities. Every Q/Q-down/Q-up
collection across scenarios must have identical ordered path IDs and weights;
probabilities sum to one within `1e-12` and are never normalized. Even a
zero-weight path must pass admission and produce complete rights. The shared
randomness domain is explicitly `supplied_paired_histories-1`: this component
consumes supplied histories and generates no stochastic draws. Pairing provides
the same conditional history identity through scenario and curve bumps.

APR and changes in spending, payments, limits, delinquency, nonaccrual and default
are supplied actions. They are independent of the supplied collateral discount
curve. No three-month proxy, index projection, fixing publication assumption,
empirical behavioral response or transition law is inferred. If rates should
respond to a scenario, the caller must supply that scenario's reviewed APR
history. Supplied curves use their explicit collateral role, currency, source
revision, log-linear discount-factor interpolation and declared reject/flat-zero/
flat-forward right tail. No unused index curve is added.

PV is weighted Q lender cash (principal + interest + fees), discounted on the
scenario collateral curve and `exp(-base_oas * actual_days / 365)`. The explicit
`cash_timing=after_opening_actions` convention excludes same-as-of cash from PV
and `(left,right]` reporting; it retains those actions separately in
`opening_action_cash`. Native core actions execute after the preceding accrual
interval, before same-day statement/due processing, in supplied equal-date order.

`oas_target=locked` accepts an explicit source-linked spread in [-5,5].
`calibrate_positive_cash` solves the original positive Q future cash target by
bounded log-sum-exp bisection. Signed future Q cash requires locked OAS, including
signed rights on zero-weight paths. There is no target or backend fallback.
Repricing compares the complete serialized original base dependency: known
contract/opening, base Q histories, base scenario curve, target source and graph
model/paired-history identity. A changed dependency reports
`BASE_ANCHOR_CHANGED`; it requires a new explicit calibration. Reporting dates,
input revision, physical/down/up histories and nonbase scenarios can change
while preserving that anchor. No scenario re-solves OAS.

`supplied_history_dv01` is `(PV(Q-down,-bump)-PV(Q-up,+bump))/(2*bump_bp)` with
native spread-equivalent continuous curve bumps and the same original OAS.
This is risk conditional on supplied paired histories, not an empirically fitted
effective duration claim.

## Income, default and full rights

P reporting distinguishes gross contractual economic interest recognition from
collected interest, fees and signed principal cash. Recognition uses native
actual intervals, proportional overlap and explicit zero-length recognition at
grace loss or nonaccrual cash collection. Contingent grace interest is not earned
income. This is gross economic recognition, not effective-yield NII, accounting
income, reviewed allowance, charge-off timing or a journal.

Default reports principal, recognized and unrecognized contract interest, fees
and principal loss separately. Recovery cash is already net of collection cost
up to gross recovery; uncovered cost is negative fee cash. Gross recovery,
collection cost and net recovery are diagnostic fields and are never added to
cash again or charged a second time. Future recovery is retained through its
explicit date even when the reporting horizon ends at default. The separate
`physical_tail` covers all dates after the last report boundary through the
contract's supplied horizon.

The required terminal policy is `zero_rights_zero_limit_at_tail`. Every native
history must finish with exactly zero principal, billed/unbilled/unrecognized
interest, fees, contingent grace interest, limit and undrawn commitment. This
prevents an implicit balloon, truncated recovery or hidden commitment valuation.
It is a bounded modeling policy, not a legal assertion of account cancellation.
The caller supplies any terminal payoff/default/limit action; the graph does not
invent it. The native card model admits ACT/360 and ACT/365 Fixed; no ACT/ACT
consumer source adoption is implied.

## Admission and validation

Before projection, bounds cover 256 positions, 13 scenarios, 120 actual reporting
periods, 128 paths per role, 4,096 total runs, 4,096 steps plus cycles per path,
36,600 daily horizon and the core's 250,000 daily lot/cycle work per projection.
Worst-case daily points/recognition, statement/grace rows, action allocation and
sorting, calibration and report passes are charged against 250,000 generated
rows and 8 million work units. JSON input identity is streamed against 32 MiB
before canonical allocation; retained input/output/base identity uses a 128 MiB
component capacity estimate. This is not aggregate process RSS or combined
60,000-position workflow acceptance. Monetary values remain bounded by the
shared native limit and all unsupported states, incomplete paths, curve tails
and source/version mismatches fail closed. Cooperative checkpoints remain active.

`card_graph::audit_admitted_work` returns the exact conservative graph work
counter after graph admission and core input-domain validation for every explicit
measure/history request, before generating a schedule. The core public
`consumer_card::validate_request` forwards its existing private validator without
changing arithmetic. Chronological action feasibility (such as overspending or
overpayment after previous actions) still belongs to the native state replay.

`tests/card_graph.rs` includes hand daily interest/payment and curve-bump results,
independent closed-form OAS target, exact fixed-anchor repricing, independent P
weights, signed/as-of draws, default interest/principal separation, recovery
cost conservation, final-date tails and admission failures. Financial reference
tolerances stay `1e-12` relative and `1e-9` absolute.

## Sources and remaining scope

[CFPB Regulation Z §1026.53](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/2021-02-17/53/)
distinguishes minimum payment from excess allocation and gives deferred-interest
exceptions. The reused native card kernel supports supplied minimum ordering
and descending APR excess allocation; it supports genuine temporary promotional
APR, not deferred-interest retroactive charging or every legal exception. Product
agreements and jurisdiction must still supply applicable reviewed policy.

The [OCC Credit Card Lending handbook](https://www.occ.treas.gov/publications-and-resources/publications/comptrollers-handbook/files/credit-card-lending/pub-ch-credit-card.pdf)
discusses income/nonaccrual, charge-offs and recoveries as distinct practices.
This component retains economic states and supplied recovery assumptions and
does not infer an accounting or regulatory determination. Future spending,
payment/default calibration, empirical validation, pricing-measure construction,
commitment option valuation, effective-yield accounting and durable saved/mixed
book adoption remain explicit separate gates.

# Supplied CD sequence source publication

The proposed `/models/runs` selections `term-product-graph-2` and `term-product-reprice-2` run the actual native CD sequence/term graph owner and publish independently verified full source and risk tables. They do not select saved books, candidate libraries or empirical behavior. Historical graph1/single-election requests retain their parser, owner and economics. The selected public verifier admits CD-only positions and reviewed locked OAS; native indexed-term coexistence remains ineligible for this public route until its independent source gate is composed.

## Immutable originals and current sources

The raw submitted JSON is retained in the immutable queued manifest and bound by exact input hashing. Only schema-declared binary64 monetary/rate/probability cells normalize integer browser spelling into the native DTO. Dates, counts, boolean flags, enum string forms, source IDs/revisions and complete nested field sets compare with exact types and values. Immutable binary64 parents preserve signed zero. Repricing retains both complete original and current sources; current collateral curves and explicitly supplied histories cannot rewrite original known terms, authorized renewal/switch terms, paired Q/down/up path IDs/weights, original quote or OAS.

Original signed quotes reconcile against complete original Q cash at the declared original collateral curve and supplied original OAS with the existing 1e-12 relative/1e-9 absolute monetary tolerance. No OAS solver is called. Current PV and paired-history DV01 use the same supplied OAS and complete unsuperseded cash. Physical cash and penalty/renewal diagnostics remain separate. Full tails and post-principal-zero signed interest rights survive reporting cutoffs. Intermediate remaining-tail previews are verified evidence and are not priced a second time. The exact 8.881784197001252e-16 regression settles that retained right without a clamp or plug. The independent verifier separately rejects erasing a nonzero post-principal-zero cash/accrued right to zero; this source-ownership check does not change the monetary comparison tolerance.

## Runtime, storage and publication

A selected HTTP entry records its clock before raw body formatting. The accepted deadline is saved before enqueue; queue waiting and every retry consume that same deadline. Worker clocks and returned execution metadata cannot extend it. Each calculation captures one executable path/hash, checks the current source/code/workspace bundle, owns one child process and rechecks the captured path/hash after native return and JSON decoding. Missing or changed native artifacts refuse execution; no Python financial fallback exists.

The current selected public transport provides a process watchdog plus independent verification/publication cancellation probes. It does **not** expose a caller-cooperative native per-call control capability for these schema names. Contained native Control tests establish native cooperative behavior in the proof only; killing a child is not that evidence.

Selected raw input is capped at 2 MiB and native output at 32 MiB. Native graph preflight independently charges every original/current path, raw metadata, projection, price/risk array and complete tail under its existing 8M-work/128MiB component limits. Persisted replay admits at most 1024 objects and 250000 total table rows, 32MiB aggregate compressed objects, 32MiB encoded column components and 32MiB logical Arrow row components before full Polars decoding. Dictionary expansion is checked one row at a time. Identical content-addressed tables can share object bytes, but every decoded appearance is charged. These are component bounds, not an aggregate process RSS or scale-acceptance claim. Ordinary inherited workspace hydration remains the existing worker contract.

Every actual persisted Parquet source/metric table is re-read from checksum-verified privately captured bytes. The independent calendar/sequence/cash/curve/PV/DV01 verifier rebuilds the financial result from immutable raw originals/current inputs, including all action receipts and preview tails. Canonical table layouts and exact result/eligibility metadata are checked separately from calculated monetary tolerances.

Before SQL completion the selected guard privately captures request/output/source descriptors, queued identity and job state. Inside the repository transaction it freshly checks original deadline, STOP, owner/lease/token/attempt/revision, original queued request, current executable/source/bundle and every immutable object byte. Failed calculations, writes, rereads, drift or publication probes leave no successful result manifest. Paging/reopen use the ordinary immutable model table endpoints.

## Evidence and remaining scope

Contained tests exercise actual copied native financial owners, copied HTTP/worker/SQLite, real Parquet roundtrip and independent raw recomputation. Installed default native/process/API/browser tests are authored separately and remain pending root installation/rebuild. The contained harness is not an installed lifecycle or production deployment receipt.

Result and execution markers retain accounting, capital/FTP, saved/library/cohort, joint optimal exercise and empirical adoption false. The route supplies no observed depositor data, P-to-Q conversion, stochastic generator, optimal election tree, daily effective-yield journal, allowance or accounting-standard approval. Full issue16/25 criteria still require saved/library/cohort and mixed ledger adoption, joint credit/market/behavioral calibration, reviewable financial policies, and integrated held-out/scale acceptance.

See [term graph2](term-product-graph-2.md), [term enhancements](term-enhancements.md), and [existing term graph](term-product-graph.md) for contractual mathematics and supported policy domains. No new contractual convention is inferred by this publication layer.

that remains **not implemented or accepted** after the bounded local stages. The 0.29.11 supported
stage and its validation are recorded in
[the follow-through review](../reviews/2026-10-11-commercial-followthrough.md).

The local0.29.13 [holding-window foundation](commercial-continuation.md) implements

Local0.29.14 additionally implements [complete-origin native daily holding journals](commercial-holding-journal.md)
with a derived balanced cut opening, prior P&L rolled into equity and ordered

Local0.29.15 additionally verifies an authorized prior modeled holding publication
at its exact published cut through [the source-ID route](commercial-prior-opening.md).
Full independent source/journal replay, matching completed postings/opening and
source/object/current-job fences inside the final SQL transaction are implemented
and locally validated. Arbitrary closing or observed bank evidence, cut-started
mixed owners and broader seasoned/secondary integration below remain required.

## Seasoned holdings and acquired rights

Extend the native source/compiler and shared credit/coupon owners with a sealed
complete-origin continuation. Replay acquisition through the cut date, then
select the subsequent posting/reporting window from that same owner. Retain
original cost/EIR, canonical gross legal and recognized lots, P/U/B/G, draw-specific
anchors, nonaccrual/default/recovery progress and reviewed allowances/waivers.
Preserve the original latent waiting hazard and shared credit stream; restarting
CTMC at the cut changes paths. Derive opening from raw replay, rather than accept
caller monetary checkpoints or infer yield/payment from remaining balance.

An existing holding must not post a second acquisition or historical earnings.
Require identical observed cash, fixings, credit events and reviews through the
cut. Only explicit future revisions can change. Reuse complete-prefix comparison
and original-yield/opening-carry patterns while retaining commercial gross rights.
Admission includes prefix, continuation and every surviving recovery/rights tail.

Secondary midcoupon acquisition is a distinct required case. Separate contractual
origin from acquisition and supply conveyed earned rights and clean/dirty cost
allocation. Coupon entitlement can remain 100 when acquired live principal is 80;
pre-acquisition income must not become current income. Full versus cut replay
must match ordered cash, states, lots and recovery clocks. Test post-principal
rights, opposite signed lots, default/nonaccrual/draw/review prefixes, prefix
tampering, missing history and independent persisted opening/posting replay.

## Nonintegral fees

The supplied-history [fee component](nonintegral-fees.md) is locally implemented
and validated in0.29.16. Native credit binding, mixed GL, fee pricing/acquisition
allocation/units/capital/FTP and the full acceptance below remain open.

Add a separate source-owned fee entitlement/service/settlement/default-tail model.
Supply fee identity, sign/refund terms, earning event/period, payment date,
state/tranche eligibility and reviewed exercise/default/recovery dispositions.
Earned unpaid fees create receivables and fee income; prepaid unearned fees create
deferred liabilities released on the service event. Keep signed gross rights and
complete fee tails after loan principal settlement. Coupon recovery fractions or
modeled LGD cannot silently extinguish a fee claim.

Nonintegral fee cash stays outside loan G/EIR and enters total economics/funding
once. Integral fees retain their existing loan owner. Add explicit fee GL accounts,
snapshots, daily reconciliation, treasury lineage and independent replay. Purchase
allocation must distinguish fee rights from loan quote/OAS/EIR; do not silently
price a fee right inside the loan acquisition anchor.

Hand controls: a zero-EIR loan100 plus fee5 earned day10/paid day20 retains loan
G100 and recognizes a receivable/income5 once; fee paid day5/earned day10 retains
deferred liability5 before service. Cover opposite signed fees, reviewed fee
default/recovery tails, exercise with earned/unearned rights, mixed fee types and
graph/unit/persisted reconciliation. Additive GL/protocol changes must preserve
historical readability and require explicit compatible native rebuilding.

## Indexed coupons earned while fixings arrive

The present commercial credit owner requires every fixing influencing a cash or
partial-earning amount to be available by that payment or earning-segment start.
This prevents future information from entering exercise and recognized income.
It does not provide general daily earning for an in-arrears overnight coupon
whose fixings become available during its accrual period. The broader standalone
indexed cashflow calculation does not establish this credit/journal adoption.

Introduce native prefix coupon entitlement from the actually available fixing
sequence, with supplied lookback, observation shift, lockout, publication clocks,
day-count and compounding policy. Update earned/legal lots at those clocks and
retain the separately complete contractual settlement amount. Do not recognize
the final full-period coupon pro rata before its required observations exist.
Default/nonaccrual and exercise must act on the same observable prefix owner;
original acquisition EIR and current contractual reset policy remain separate.

Hand controls require changing daily fixings, unequal calendar weights,
simple/compounded conventions, publication delay, default before the last fixing,
and rights surviving principal settlement. Early cash that requires unavailable
fixings must reject or use a separately reviewed settlement policy. Independent
source, graph, income, ordered posting and persisted replay must agree without
weakening observability guards or financial tolerances.

## General generated original OAS

The bounded retained-Q graph and acquired-unit implementation is now present in
local0.29.12. Its [contract](commercial-generated-oas.md) and
[validation review](../reviews/2026-10-12-commercial-generated-oas.md) retain the
separate installed acceptance and convergence boundaries. The requirements below
remain the original design/acceptance contract; this stage does not establish
broad model convergence, empirical accuracy or all requested mixed adoption.

Introduce a sealed native calibration sample owner. Generate original Q training
and distinct evaluation tapes, observable features and native no-option cash once.
Every bounded OAS trial recomputes discounted backward targets and refits
continuation on the identical retained training sample; evaluate on the identical
distinct evaluation sample. Reusing stops fitted at a different OAS changes the
economics. Preserve reduction order and common random numbers.

Policy switches can make the finite evaluation objective discontinuous or
nonmonotone. A deterministic bounded bracket solver must accept only when final
actual native stopped Q cash reproduces the original quote at unchanged tolerance.
Unbracketed, ambiguous or unresolved quotes reject. Generate the original P
cost/EIR proof only for the accepted Q policy. Retain exact selected OAS bits in
all current scenarios/bumps; P never supplies the Q calibration target.

Preflight charges retained samples, all allowed trials, final stopped replay and
coexisting graph/proof receipts within the existing generated 4B work/128 MiB
limits. Test deterministic known-spread recovery, actual policy-boundary exercise,
unreachable/discontinuous residual refusals, repeatability, immutable original P
proof, independently rejected tampering and cancellation/no-publication.

## Generated candidate streaming and opening evidence

The current compiled journal borrows every full accounting owner. Materializing
all generated paths recreates the rejected capacity footprint. Add a sealed
compact journal source: materialize one genuine P recipe, copy native atomic
postings and absolute financial endpoints, intern identities, then drop its full
owner. Retain gross lots and snapshot fields as absolute f64 values; avoid
reconstructing money from repeated deltas. Finite and compact sources feed the
existing daily Sim posting/staging/reconciliation in the same total order:
scenario/day, global native year, binding index, native group index.

Keep ordinary candidate admission unchanged. An explicit generated route must
charge joined work within the existing 4B tier while retaining separate graph and
journal phase caps and combined 128 MiB capacity. Refine structural bounds for the
actual compact event/state passes within ledger 8M/32 MiB limits. Results beyond
the buffered envelope require bounded immutable partitioned emission, rather
than a larger JSON limit.

Compare compact versus borrowed ordered postings, gross daily/closing balances
and trial balances. Admit a minimum128-path control with at most one live full P
owner; cover real exercise/default/recovery/signed rights, zero allocation,
purchase offsets, foreign proofs, missing/duplicated/out-of-order records,
persisted tampering and cancellation at materialization/stream/publication.
Interactive evaluation remains coefficient-only.

Resolve opening evidence from an authorized immutable completed journal: replay
its raw source and persisted postings, bind exact closing date/currency/accounts,
reconcile signed opening, and retain all source/partition hashes through final
SQL publication. Cash/equity-only prior closing is a bounded first stage. Surviving
backbook principal/basis/allowance/rights need native prefix and future ownership;
closing scalar balances alone are insufficient. Modeled-journal verification is
not observed bank/custodian reconciliation; observed evidence remains separate.

## Empirical and integrated completion

Observed issuer/commercial histories and reviewed accounting/regulatory policies
must be supplied. Retain chronological fitting/holdouts, source lineage,
uncertainty diagnostics and independent verification. Synthetic mathematical
controls do not establish predictive accuracy. Complete saved-book/cohort/mixed
strategy and product capital/FTP adoption, original dependency gates and full
60,000-position mixed graph/credit/solver/journal acceptance remain required,
including deadlines, cancellation, immutable source/artifacts and final authority
fences. Completing the bounded stages above does not close these criteria.


Local0.29.16 adds the supplied-history [separate fee owner](nonintegral-fees.md).
It implements earning, signed gross rights, cash, prepaid refund, reviewed waiver/
cancellation and recovery intents with full supplied tails and independent replay.
The native event binding, mixed GL, graph/unit/acquisition allocation/capital/FTP,
observed and full-scale fee acceptance above remains required.


## Native loan and separate fee journal (local0.29.17)

`commercial-fee-journal-1` binds reviewed original-tranche fee earning/cash and
separate exit dispositions to one already generated physical commercial loan
owner. Native default/prepayment and explicit reviewed maturity events determine
waiver/refund/cancellation/recovery; fee LGD is not borrowed from loan policies.
Separate signed gross rights enter the same existing daily Sim once, with complete
fee tails, unchanged loan cost/EIR/carry and retained unweighted zero allocations.
Protocol7 adds fee lineage/daily/closing snapshots; historical6 is unchanged.
Actual fractional clocks cannot round into the preceding day. Independent raw
source, ordered shared journal, gross/report and persisted replay plus original
deadline/executable/object/final SQL authority fences gate durable publication.

This bounded lane does not yet adopt exercise/candidate/holding fee sources,
draw/secondary fee rights, fee acquisition allocation, Pricing graphs/units or
capital/FTP. In-arrears earning, generated streaming, saved/cohort/mixed strategy,
observed/reviewed histories and full60000 combined acceptance remain required
under15/25. See docs/models/commercial-fee-journal.md and the complete ledger.
Rebuild compatible native artifacts, restart deployed workers and explicitly
rebuild selected saved sessions/libraries before use; local validation does not
deploy or close the full issues.

## Reviewed earned-fee refunds (0.29.18 follow-through)

The standalone fee owner and native loan/fee journal now implement explicitly
permitted refunds of earned AND collected service, with separate cumulative
refund ownership, reviewed exit fractions, gross signed snapshots and reversed
fee income/cash. Refunds cannot recreate service/collection capacity or use
prepaid cash or waived recovery as collected earning. Loan original cost/EIR and
credit paths remain unchanged. Omitted selections retain historical layouts and
admission. Independent raw-source and persisted replay remain required.

This removes the earned-refund subtask from the earlier exclusion lists. All
other remaining engineering, data/policy and complete combined acceptance work
above stays open, including fee Pricing/acquisition/unit/capital/FTP adoption,
exercise/candidate/holding and draw/secondary rights, in-arrears coupons,
generated streaming/convergence and full saved/cohort/mixed adoption. It does
not establish observed accuracy, policy approval, deployment or issue completion.

# Complete-origin commercial holding continuation

Local 0.29.13 adds the explicitly selected `commercial-holding-continuation-1`
analysis contract. `analytics.model_contracts.continue_commercial_holding` sends
raw inputs through the native C ABI; `/models/runs` executes the same contract in
the durable standalone Rust process. Python performs independent verification
and storage. Neither transport computes opening money or restarts credit.

The request supplies `completed_source`, `revised_source` and `cut_ordinal`.
Both sources use the complete commercial compiler contract from original
acquisition through the complete contractual, reviewed-action and recovery tails.
The native owner replays each full history, requires identical completed atomic
groups and carry records through the cut, and constructs a non-deserializable
opening. It retains original acquisition cost and effective yield independently
of cut carrying value, live/default principal, undrawn commitment, tranche yields,
canonical coupon entitlement, signed recognized/legal lots and reviewed credit
state. It selects subsequent groups by their unchanged native indices. Summaries
reduce only subsequent cash, effective interest and basis realization, in source
order. Historical earnings and acquisition are excluded from that window.

There is no monetary checkpoint input. The revised CTMC starts at original
acquisition on the original stream and paths. Its latent elapsed waiting hazard
survives the cut and supplied calendar boundaries. For example, a supplied
exponential threshold corresponding to day 20 at hazard 10, with a cut at day 15,
defaults at day 17.5 when the future hazard becomes 20. Restarting the same waiting
draw at the cut would produce a different time. Defaults already incurred retain
their original complete recovery claims and reviewed book/legal state.

Original source/cost/yield, credit paths/stream, factor policy, contractual dates,
principal plan, draw terms and reviewed credit actions cannot change. Periods
already begun and observations with fixing dates through the cut cannot change.
Recognition, rates and hazards can change only in wholly future supplied intervals.
Future indexed projections can change when existing contractual observability
and original/current identity gates permit them. General contractual modification,
policy replacement and partial-interval editing require separate ownership.
A live holding cut requires an exact native earning boundary; a frozen default
owner can retain its latest action before the cut. No partial income is invented.

The example is a synthetic two-period100 loan. The original yield is 5%, its
purchase quote discounts actual day 35/day 65 cash, and the cut is day 15. An unpaid
legal coupon right of100*10%*15/365 survives the cut. Only the future period's
conditional projected coupon changes to 15%; original acquisition economics remain
retained. Other controls cover a funded draw with its 7% original tranche yield,
reviewed nonaccrual, reviewed chargeoff/waiver/recovery and signed rights after
principal has settled. These are numerical controls, not observed performance.

Admission charges both complete owners, prefix comparisons, opening copies,
suffix indices and raw transport before either source is generated, within 8M
work and 128 MiB retained capacity. Raw input is bounded to 1 MiB and output to 32 MiB.
These component bounds do not guarantee aggregate process RSS. Original native
execution controls cover decoding, generation, comparison and serialization;
durable jobs retain the original queue deadline through independent raw and
persisted replay, source/executable/object checks and final SQL authority fences.

This contract supplies a reusable holding-window foundation. It does not yet
consume a verified prior journal publication, run a cut-started mixed daily Sim,
prepare seasoned saved/cohort/strategy coefficients, or adopt option-stopped
acquisition proofs. `verified_prior_publication`, `mixed_ledger_adoption` and
`secondary_acquisition_adoption` remain false. Secondary midcoupon purchases,
conveyed earned rights and clean/dirty quote allocation remain distinct required
work. Nonintegral fees, daily in-arrears indexed earning, generated streaming,
empirical histories/policies and full mixed scale acceptance remain open under
issues 15/25. Historical schemas and receipts remain readable unchanged. New
execution requires matching rebuilt artifacts and explicit selected-session and
library rebuilding; this local change does not restart deployed workers.

Matching official local builds pass 1,216 native tests, 2,579 engine checks with two
reference-only skips and 1,091 API checks. Strict, contract and whole-output identity
checks pass. See [the accepted review](../reviews/2026-10-12-commercial-holding-continuation.md)
for exact source/artifact/log identities and the preserved superseded runs.

# Commercial contractual rights, credit carry and shared daily ledger

The explicit `commercial-credit-ledger-1` contract joins complete original/current
Physical term sources, one event-time credit path, coupon-level legal/recognized
rights, original-yield carrying value and the existing daily `Sim`. It requires an
explicit source selection and compatible native artifacts. It never changes a
historical saved contract or selects this model from an old `annuity` label.

## Financial owners

`term_enhancements/indexed.rs` owns principal and coupon cash, including supplied
fixings, observation/reset/payment dates, contractual day counts, caps, floors,
margins and compounding conventions. Its optional native segment capture retains
the actual pre-observation accumulator and exact full factor endpoints. Native
factor descriptors have no deserialization or caller restoration constructor.

`commercial_factor_source` resolves the captured segment at actual fractional
credit-clock endpoints under the selected reviewed clock policy. Legal earning is
the native factor difference times the native period entitlement principal, once.
That entitlement can remain nonzero after an early principal payment. Replacing
it universally with current live principal would erase delayed or prepaid rights.
Each coupon retains its own source event, audit, cash and earning-origin identities.

The actual-path factor owner requires every indexed fixing, source availability
and selection cutoff no later than actual payment midnight. Availability and selection
must also be no later than each interest-segment start midnight; term reset cutoffs
must be no later than the period start. Intraday contingent rate ownership is unsupported in
this selected owner. Retained-payment balances inherit prior indexed information
cutoffs, so later fixed cash cannot reveal a future indexed balance. Already
published lookback fixings remain supported. The broader supplied indexed
arithmetic analysis keeps its separate contract.

`credit_path_income` runs inside the existing CTMC event loop. It retains the
actual occupied state, transition clock and shared draws. On an occupied span
`dt`, effective interest is

```text
E = G * expm1(log1p(reviewed_annual_effective_rate) * dt)
G_next = G + E - actual_cash + funded_draw
financial_basis = G_next - principal - recognized_coupon_rights
```

Original acquisition cost and yield reconcile only to the complete original
cash source. A changed current source cannot refit them. Explicit prospective
recognition-rate reviews and stopped-income reviews are separate from that
immutable original anchor. A zero yield alone does not select nonaccrual.

`commercial_coupon_accounting` retains legal coupon earning/cash and recognized
coupon earning/cash separately. Actual cash selects a native coupon event; it
cannot settle all outstanding coupons using one aggregate fraction. Signed
recognized lots are classified before aggregation. A legal/recognized difference
remains visible rather than disappearing into a basis or terminal cash plug.

Default transfers the actual gross principal, basis and coupon lots. Economic
LGD and modeled recovery amounts are distinct from reviewed allowance, chargeoff,
legal waiver and book disposal. Unpaid claims remain explicit. Exact zero may omit
a posting; tolerances never authorize erasing a tiny outstanding right.

Integral fee cash is collected while live. It does not introduce an earned legal
fee claim at default. Optional reviewed prepayment premiums use actual live
principal. Opening undrawn commitments enter default EAD at the actual occupied
origin's supplied CCF. Explicit performing draw tranches retain their own actual
funding date, acquisition cost, original effective yield, principal and coupon
entitlements; eligibility is supplied and undrawn overspending rejects.
Issuer-credit debt and credit-free references are separate selected
identities, rather than an implicit spread interpreted as both reference and credit.

`maturity_basis_policy` may explicitly select
`dispose_financial_basis_after_exact_legal_close-1` with a reviewed identity.
After all complete source cash, a native zero-cash exit requires principal and
legal interest to be exactly zero and disposes the remaining financial carrying
basis through the reviewed exit policy. Default claims never enter that exit.
Absence retains the existing explicit closing claims. At every source clock,
canonical legal balance is native entitlement principal times the cumulative
source factor minus the actual coupon cash collected. This removes accumulation
drift without inventing terminal cash or waiving a legal right. Legal earning
and recognized earning retain distinct deltas and gross coupon identities.

Optional `reviewed_credit_actions` supplies separately identified provisions,
chargeoffs and legal waivers through the shared reviewed accounting primitive.
Book principal, allowance and legal principal remain separate from modeled
principal, gross carry and economic loss. A chargeoff does not cancel modeled
recovery cash or turn modeled LGD into a second provision. Complete later recovery
and reviewed action clocks extend replay beyond the contractual reporting date.

## One journal

`commercial_ledger` admits all original/current source, credit, coupon inventory
and daily work before source generation. It retains each source once and gives
borrowed accounting groups to `commercial_intent_owner`. That owner reuses the
shared account mapper and signed-right classifier, then enters `Sim::raw_post`.
It does not run another credit generator or concatenate standalone journals.

Monetary participation is `allocated_face / native_unit_face * source_weight`,
once. Native unit face must equal actual opening source principal. Every path is
validated, including zero participation. Scenarios retain identical original
source/cost/yield and complete draw-stream/path identities. Physical intensities
remain separate from a Pricing measure and an OAS calibration.

Opening account cash/equity is posted once by the shared specification. Commercial
acquisition uses that cash. Exclusive placeholders reject generic cash overlays,
position policies and collateral ownership; actual pooled cash floors remain
enforced. Capital, liquidity and HTM eligibility require separate explicit policy.
Acquisition is attributed to actual day zero. The raw reporting horizon remains
immutable; native preparation derives a separate complete calendar through the
contractual tail plus the maximum reviewed recovery lag, bounded to 1,080 days.
Other generic positions, netting, pooled fees/taxes and policies reject in this
selected independently verified publication tier. Sharing Sim does not imply
arbitrary mixed-book adoption.

Subday actions retain native credit years and stable chronological order under
`actual_credit_clock_order_day_end_journal_no_retiming_source-1`. Journal days use
the enclosing day end; exact integer source dates preserve their native bits.
The daily journal does not claim to record the precise intraday legal timestamp.

`commercial_source_lineage` retains complete native atomic groups and transaction
numbers, source acquisition offsets and explicit native source classes.
`commercial_daily` and `commercial_closing` retain unweighted gross book
and coupon lots alongside path/allocation identities. Historical `exposures`
placeholder rows are not commercial credit exposures. Protocol 6 identifies this
explicit journal; historical protocols remain separately readable.
This raw route retains the commercial-loan class. Issuer-credit assets require
the explicit amortized-cost security candidate owner; they cannot enter a loan
placeholder. AFS/HTM marks and institution funding liabilities need separate
owners and policies.

[Commercial treasury and candidate contracts](commercial-treasury-candidate.md)
describe the separate exact-closing capital, daily FTP and purchased-journal gates.

## Admission and verification

The source components retain their own 2M work/32MiB limits. Joined preparation
admits at most 512 source requests, 1MiB raw JSON, 8M aggregate work and 128MiB
retained component capacity. The bounded complete header/journal output is at
most 32MiB. These budgets do not promise aggregate process RSS or full 60,000
position mixed graph/credit/solver/journal acceptance.

The standalone native dispatcher retains the original input clock and inherited
cancellation. Raw duplicate keys, incomplete scenario coverage, changed original
anchors, changed CRN, missing source weights and unsupported owners reject.
Private preparation and journal execution finish before emission. Write/flush
failures and final checkpoints remain failures.

Durable publication requires independent raw source, credit/carry, coupon book,
ordered journal and persisted partition replay, with the original complete-job
deadline, lease/token and current input/executable/artifact fences. The native
receipt does not set its own independent-verification flag. Synthetic checks do
not establish observed predictive accuracy, accounting approval or deployment.
The exact current implementation and validation status is recorded in
[the issue implementation ledger](implementation-plan.md).

## Primary references and policy limits

The [ARRC technical appendices](https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/Microsites/arrc/files/2020/ARRC-Syndicated-Loan-Conventions-Technical-Appendices.pdf)
explain why simple/compounded interest and observation shifts need distinct
weights. The selected contract still supplies its own conventions.
[IFRIC's June 2021 discussion](https://www.ifrs.org/news-and-events/updates/ifric/2021/ifric-update-june-2021/)
distinguishes market-rate resets and other changes in estimated cashflows. This
supports a separate reviewed prospective rate rather than overwriting an original
quote/yield anchor. The [FFIEC 051 glossary](https://www.ffiec.gov/pdf/FFIEC_forms/FFIEC051_202412_i.pdf)
separates nonaccrual, cash recovery and collectibility judgments. Accordingly,
stopped recognition does not infer principal chargeoff or extinguish legal rights.
These references guide required policy fields; they do not approve supplied
research policies or certify an accounting methodology.

# Native commercial conditional exercise

An explicitly selected `commercial-native-exercise-1` policy in a commercial
product graph contains reviewed identities, permitted actual dates, call/put clean
factors and fees, and simultaneous-right priority. It contains no supplied
principal, coupon money, continuation values, membership partitions or decisions.
Before- and after-scheduled-cash decisions explicitly select their native phase.

Rust constructs native no-option Pricing contractual/credit paths, then forms
information sets from complete observed contract/rate and realized credit/event
prefixes. Future index rates remain hidden until both their fixing date and
selection timestamp. Path identifiers, future default draws and future outcomes
do not identify an information set. Initially observable contract/state data must
agree across the Pricing distribution. Each weighted path has one native credit
identity, and all positive weights sum to one.

For a decision date `t`, continuation is the conditional weighted mean of cash
strictly after `t` through the next decision, discounted at each actual event time,
plus the next decision value. Discounting uses the supplied collateral curve and
one immutable original OAS; a paired parallel bump enters separately. After-cash
redemption equals actual live principal times the contractual clean factor, plus
legal accrued interest and the explicit fee. The existing issuer/holder priority
determines the order of call minimization and put maximization. Exact ties retain
continuation or the preceding selected right. Defaulted or exited paths do not
exercise. A zero-principal contract with unpaid or future rights requires a
reviewed `settle_earned_cancel_future-1` termination owner. The native stop settles
actual earned rights and cancels future contractual cash without inventing principal.

The first reached decision becomes a private native stop. The same native credit
loop applies it at the selected phase and retires future source cash. Before-cash
decisions precede repayment, maturity and draw funding; credit events already
reached at that clock remain observable. A caller cannot deserialize or restore
a native stop. Default before
exercise retains the full default/recovery tail. Separately supplied Physical
paths use the Pricing policy only when their observed prefix has verified
coverage; uncovered states reject rather than guessing an action.

This conditional expectation is exact for an explicit finite path distribution.
It does not establish convergence for continuous stochastic market/credit models,
observed issuer exercise behavior or statistical accuracy. The distinction follows
the conditional-expectation requirement in
[Longstaff and Schwartz (2001)](https://escholarship.org/uc/item/43n1k4jb): a future
realized path payoff cannot be substituted for information available at exercise.
The finite-distribution implementation does not claim to fit their regression.

The graph keeps original OAS through current scenarios and paired risk bumps.
Acquired exercise coefficients additionally need the original stopped Physical
cash distribution and original cost/yield reconciliation. An analytical Pricing
receipt cannot supply that accounting anchor. Acquired units now retain and
verify the separately supplied complete original stopped Physical distribution
at the original purchase yield/cost before current scenario preparation.
Legacy threshold options and the supplied-DAG `conditional-exercise-1`
contract retain their existing meanings. This additive selection does not
reinterpret a saved contract or complete [issue #15](implementation-plan.md).

The separate [generated exercise contract](commercial-generated-exercise.md)
fits continuation on native observable joint market/credit training paths and
evaluates a retained policy on fresh paths. The finite-distribution contract keeps
its original exact conditional expectation; it does not approximate a continuous
state law by assigning each generated path its own future-aware information set.

# Native loan and separate fee journal

Local0.29.17 adds explicitly selected `commercial-fee-journal-1`, transported by
`analytics.model_contracts.analyze_commercial_fees` to `portfolio-strategy` and by
durable `/models/runs` jobs. It joins original-tranche service fees to the same
physical commercial loan paths and existing daily Sim. Loan principal, original
cost/EIR, contractual coupons, credit draws, allowance and LGD retain their own
owners. Separate fees are never silently included in the loan quote or basis.

The request supplies `loan` (the existing `commercial-credit-ledger-1` request)
and one `commercial-native-fees-1` policy per commercial source, in source order.
Each fee retains its exact position, original tranche, service, classification
review and source identity. Supplied events contain only service earning, cash
and permitted prepaid or explicitly reviewed earned refunds. Caller default/exercise/waiver/recovery money is
rejected. The complete supplied tape must be valid before loan generation.

Rust generates each loan owner once, then binds fee dispositions to that owner's
actual first default/prepayment event or explicit reviewed maturity event. A
performing contract without a reviewed maturity event does not invent one merely
because its principal settled. Sealed conditional exercise owners are recognized
by exact path/event identity in the binder; this public joint request does not
yet accept an exercise graph or acquired exercise candidate source.

Every exit category supplies a separate review and explicit cancellation,
unpaid-earned waiver, prepaid-refund and recovery policy. At the exit, let E be
signed earned service, W signed previously waived service and K net service cash.
With F the separately retained earned refunds and entitlement sign s, eligible
unpaid earning is max((E-F-W-K)s,0)s and eligible prepaid cash is
max((K-E+F+W)s,0)s. Apply separately supplied fractions to those
rights. Fee recovery applies only to the newly waived fee, with independent
fractions and actual-day lags; loan LGD and coupon recovery cannot supply it.
Recovery fractions total at most one. Refund policy must agree with fee terms.

Local 0.29.18 adds optional `refund_earned_fraction` (default0) to each reviewed
exit policy. Every affected fee must explicitly allow earned refunds. At the same
native exit, refund `max(min((E-F-W)s,Ks),0)s * refund_earned_fraction` through the
separate fee owner. Earlier supplied earned refunds reduce that remaining right.
The event reverses collected fee income and cash once without changing gross
service earned, loan carrying value/EIR, prepaid obligations or waived recoveries.
It retains the exit reason/review and the original fractional clock. Zero/omitted
selection adds no group or admission charge; selected policies reserve one extra
group per fee/path before loan generation. Historical output/protocols remain
unchanged. See [the fee owner](nonintegral-fees.md) for the signed hand controls.

The required `native_exit_before_coincident_service_cash-1` policy retires eligible
future events and posts reviewed dispositions before service/cash at the identical
native clock. Native years remain unchanged. Integer ACT365 dates retain their
exact calendar day; fractional events use the first day-end at or after their
native timestamp. A just-later floating-point year cannot round onto the preceding
day. Loan groups precede fee groups at an identical global clock; original group
and binding order then resolves ties. No timestamp nudges or tolerance changes
are used.

The one Sim posts separate fee receivable/payable, deferred income/prepaid expense,
income, writeoff and recovery accounts. It checks every absolute gross fee snapshot
against accumulated postings and reconciles them alongside loan stocks. Source
weight and face allocation are applied exactly once. Zero participation retains
the complete unweighted source policy. Separate signed fee rights remain gross.
Complete fee cash and recovery tails survive principal settlement and the original
report date. The root retains that reporting cutoff; the loan receipt resolves
the complete simulation horizon. Loan receipt admission covers the loan slice;

# Generated commercial exercise

`commercial-generated-exercise-1` explicitly selects supplied-law joint Gaussian
market and event-time credit generation with training-only least-squares
continuation and a fresh evaluation sample. This is an analytical contract.
It does not silently replace the finite-distribution graph or saved economics.
The example is synthetic; its separate evaluation sample is a Monte Carlo
holdout, not an observed borrower history or empirical predictive validation.

## Source and measure

The raw `commercial-source-credit-accounting-proof-1` prototype retains the
original contractual source, current source, original acquisition cost/yield,
actual dates, factor conventions and complete credit recovery tails. Both term
sources explicitly select Pricing. There is one prototype credit path; native
generation replaces its path identity and credit stream separately for each
sample. Native source owners calculate every earned right and cash event.
Neither caller continuation values nor caller-generated monetary checkpoints
enter the fit. Future performing draw tranches currently reject in this lane.
The separate source/ledger draw contract retains its own supported scope.

The discount curve is supplied and deterministic, with explicit interpolation,
tail and currency policy. Discounting is `D(t) exp(-(base_OAS + bump)t)`.
The original base OAS is supplied and retained; this operation does not fit it.
Repeating base/down/up with identical sample identities preserves common
random numbers, although exercise decisions can change. A supplied Gaussian
Pricing law is an assumption; this contract does not certify a calibrated,
arbitrage-free relationship between its coupon drivers and discount curve.

## Exact Gaussian transitions and credit coupling

For each observable coordinate, `dX_i = a_i(mu_i-X_i)dt + dW_i`, with supplied
instantaneous covariance `cov(dW_i,dW_j)=C_ij dt`. All coordinates are observable
at the supplied midnight UTC ordinal. Hidden future coordinates reject.
Conditional mean over actual elapsed ACT/365 time is
`mu_i + (X_i-mu_i)exp(-a_i dt)`; innovation covariance is
`C_ij (1-exp(-(a_i+a_j)dt))/(a_i+a_j)`, with exact zero-reversion limit `C_ij dt`.
A symmetric covariance square root maps independent shared native Gaussian
draws into the joint innovations. Covariance must be symmetric positive
semidefinite. The two halves of each market sample are antithetic.

Every future indexed observation requires an explicit coupon loading and a
generated state on its actual fixing date. Only conditional projected fixings
can be replaced; historical observed fixings remain supplied. The coupon law
uses `baseline + loading*(X_fix-X_initial)`, followed by the existing native
margin, compounding and cap/floor conventions. All future observations must
be mapped, rather than silently freezing an unmapped future rate.

Credit hazards are piecewise constant over the supplied credit intervals.
An explicitly mapped hazard uses `h_base exp(beta dot (X_start-X_initial))`,
conditioned on the observed state at the interval start. A zero baseline cannot
acquire an implicit hazard. Invalid or out-of-domain hazards reject rather than
clip. Native continuous-time credit transitions and complete source recovery
cash operate on those generated hazards. This interval-start approximation is
disclosed; the process does not integrate a continuously varying hazard within
an interval. LGD, CCF, interest recovery and recovery timing remain supplied.

## Observable contractual state and continuation

At each decision, regression state includes current observable market levels,
live principal, signed legal interest, Watch/Delinquent indicators, the current
stochastic hazard interval's observed anchor, already selected coupon fixings,
and separate coupon entitlement principal and remaining legal balances. Rates
fixed in the future are masked. Current market levels and net interest alone
would omit earlier fixings and gross coupon rights; they are not used as the
entire contractual state. The state is bounded to 64 features before generation.

Only the training sample establishes means, scales, active varying features and
the quadratic basis (intercept, linear terms and all quadratic cross terms).
Numerically constant features are removed from the basis using an explicit
`8*epsilon*max(abs(mean),1)` scale threshold. At evaluation, a change in a
training-constant feature rejects at the unchanged financial tolerance.
An evaluation live credit state absent from training also rejects.

The native SVD uses cutoff `epsilon*max(rows,columns)*largest_singular_value`.
Rank and singular values are disclosed; rank deficiency uses the minimum-norm
solution. At least twice as many live training rows as active basis columns are
required. Conditioning the continuation on observable state follows
[Longstaff and Schwartz](https://escholarship.org/uc/item/43n1k4jb).
Basis richness and path count must be considered together; the controlled
checks here do not establish general convergence, as discussed by
[Glasserman and Yu](https://business.columbia.edu/faculty/research/number-paths-versus-number-basis-functions-american-option-pricing).

Backward induction chooses Call/Put/Continue using the fitted conditional
continuation. Continue retains the realized discounted continuation target;
the fitted value is not substituted for actual policy cash. Simultaneous
priority, before/after scheduled cash, clean principal factor and fee remain
explicit native policies. Rights-only termination requires the reviewed
`settle_earned_cancel_future-1` disposition. No principal is invented after
principal settlement. Before-cash exercise precedes scheduled repayment,
maturity and draw funding; credit events at that clock remain observable.

## Fresh evaluation and numerical checks

Training and evaluation require distinct market seeds, credit seeds and stream
identities. Each sample contains an even 128 through 512 paths. Evaluation
outcomes cannot change the fitted policy. Every evaluation path is regenerated
under the same native streams and passed through the sealed native stopping
owner. Its complete stopped source cash must reproduce the retained policy PV
at `1e-9 + 1e-12*abs(PV)`. No final-output tolerance is relaxed.

The reported standard error uses independent antithetic pair clusters:
`Z_i=(V_i+V_(i+N/2))/2`, `SE=sqrt(sample_variance(Z)/(N/2))`.
It does not treat antithetic paths as independent. Controlled tests compare a
one-date Gaussian callable coupon with an exact normal integral at 128, 256
and 512 paths, test the zero-volatility option-free cash identity, separate
evaluation streams, correlated two-driver transitions, multiple exercise
dates and joint credit cash replay. Independent NumPy/SciPy verification
constructs raw paths, fits its own regressions and replays its own stopped
credit source. These are contained mathematical controls, not observed-data
evidence or proof of general policy/basis convergence.

## Admission, runtime and publication

The new explicitly selected `bounded_generated_1024_samples-1` tier admits at
most 1,024 aggregate training/evaluation samples, four drivers, 129 state dates,
64 observable features, four billion conservative aggregate work units and
128 MiB estimated retained compact capacity. The work estimate includes every
source and prospective stop plus bounded SVD work. Existing ordinary source
eight-million and graph 32-million work caps are unchanged. These component
bounds are not an aggregate RSS guarantee. Each source keeps its existing
admission. The request is at most 1 MiB and result at most 32 MiB, with small
outer protocol overhead; the historical process outer read remains 64 MiB.

The original byte selector checks every original schema field before routing
can erase duplicates. The native deadline starts at process entry before stdin
read and covers selected decode, generation, regression, native cash replay and
checked bounded serialization. The Python process transport adds cancellation,
watchdog and executable identity checks without financial calculation.
Durable publication additionally requires independently verified raw source,
persisted nested outputs and the original queue deadline, source/executable,
lease/token and final object-byte fences. Local testing does not restart deployed
workers; additive execution requires rebuilt artifacts and explicit saved model
or library rebuilding before adoption.

`convergence_established`, `physical_journal_eligible` and `empirical_validation`
remain false for this standalone analytical receipt. The separately selected
[generated graph](commercial-graph-strategy.md#generated-policy-graphs) now joins
Pricing policy, separately supplied Physical replay and acquired coefficients.
Physical model calibration, general Monte Carlo OAS calibration, path-specific
draw/review actions, full mixed candidate accounting and complete 60,000-position
joint acceptance remain required gates under issues 15 and 25.

Observed features mask each coupon's canonical entitlement metadata until its
accrual period starts or actual payment has already been observed. Earlier
floating resets can determine a later retained-payment principal balance; this
future balance cannot enter current regression features. The source owner also
requires every amount influencing actual cash and earned interest to be available
at that cash date or earning-segment start. This includes inherited indexed
balance dependencies. Rights-only eligibility uses observed legal rights and
known contract terms, rather than future realized coupon cash.

# Original generated commercial OAS

An explicitly selected `commercial-product-graph-1` position can now use
`oas_target.kind="calibrate_positive_cash"` with `generated_policy.oas_calibration`:

```json
{
  "policy": "native_retained_q_refit_bracket-1",
  "lower_oas": -0.02,
  "upper_oas": 0.06,
  "max_trials": 48
}
```

The target must exactly identify the original signed cash quote and retain its
source/revision. Controls require a finite increasing bracket within [-5,5] and
3..128 trials. Locked OAS requires no calibration controls. Historical omitted
controls retain their existing route and output. This is an additive explicit
selection, requiring compatible native rebuilding and selected-library rebuilding.

## Native sample and policy ownership

The native owner generates original Pricing training and distinct evaluation
tapes once. It retains native complete unexercised cash and observable states.
Each trial spread refits continuation using only the same training observations;
evaluation observations never enter the regression. Changing spread while retaining
a policy fitted at another spread would change exercise economics.

With the supplied original collateral curve D and spread s, discounted cash uses
`D(t) exp(-s t)`. Backward training targets include actual future native cash and
subsequent policy exercise values; regressions estimate conditional continuation
from observable state. Fresh evaluation uses that trial's fitted policy and
actual realized future cash. The calibrated objective is the mean present value
under that evaluation policy. Discount clocks retain actual settlement and complete
recovery/rights tails, including settlements after the accrual end.

The bounded solver evaluates both endpoints and then bracket midpoints. Matching
both endpoints is ambiguous and rejects. Unbracketed targets, sampled nonmonotone
values and unresolved final quote residuals reject. A finite evaluation objective
can jump when predicted continuation changes exercise while realized future cash
differs; bisection cannot turn a price in that gap into a converged quote.

Acceptance requires fresh native stopped-source replay for every selected
evaluation path, followed by the original quote tolerance
`abs(actual-target) <= 1e-9 + 1e-12*abs(target)`. No larger spread/price tolerance
or statistical confidence band replaces that residual gate. Sampled monotonicity
checks do not certify global uniqueness of every possible fitted-policy root.

The accepted fitted policy and actual stopped Q sources enter graph preparation
directly. Those original samples are not regenerated during preparation. Separately
supplied original Physical laws then construct the original stopped cost/EIR proof.
Physical outcomes do not calibrate the Pricing quote. Every current scenario and
paired Pricing bump retains exactly the selected original OAS bits; it can fit its
own current policy at that fixed spread. Original Physical cost/yield remain supplied
acquisition anchors, independently verified against complete expected cash.

## Acquisition coefficients and receipts

Commercial unit builds may select this original generated calibration. Native
graph preparation runs in the build; interactive strategy evaluation remains
coefficient-only. Units still require independently supplied Physical acquisition
cost matching the Pricing purchase quote, original effective yield, complete
physical cash and separate face/purchase-cost identities. Calibration never infers
a seasoned payment, missing history or original yield from remaining balance.

The graph's `generated_oas_calibration` receipt retains controls, original target,
trial spreads/evaluation values, selected spread, actual stopped cash and residual,
and original sample counts. Independent Python verification generates its own Q
sample, replays each recorded bracket step/refit and independently reconstructs
stopped cash before checking P acquisition, policies, graph metrics and coefficients.
Persisted nested receipts retain canonical JSON types and the existing final guards.

## Work, memory and execution

Admission charges native generation/final replay once and every permitted additional
discount/regression trial. Retained feature-derived column limits are checked against
the first fitted policy; an unexpectedly varying state rejects before further trials.
Existing source, graph and coefficient work limits remain. The generated aggregate
ceiling remains four billion work units and 128 MiB retained component capacity.
Calibration samples precede graph P/Q/proof preparation; only the accepted policy,
source receipts and trial receipt cross that phase boundary. These limits are not
an aggregate process RSS guarantee. Expensive brackets/scenario combinations can
reject even if a smaller permitted trial budget would converge.

The process and C ABI adapters select native execution controls for calibrated
requests. The original process-entry clock covers decode, generation, trial fits,
stopped replay and bounded serialization, including inherited caller deadlines.
The process transport also enforces cancellation/watchdog/executable identity.
Durable publication retains the original accepted queue deadline, source/executable
and object hashes, and SQL lease/token/revision/attempt/cancellation fences. An
expired or unresolved run publishes no accepted result.

## Controls and remaining scope

`commercial-generated-calibrated-graph-1.json` is a synthetic zero-volatility
control: accrual ends on day30, principal settles on day35, and original spread
0.017 is independently recovered from the complete day35 cash quote. The exercise
variant supplies a Gaussian law and quote at spread0.02; original Physical cost
uses its separately supplied original effective yield. Both call and continuation
occur in the Pricing evaluation sample. Their trial ceilings reserve the entire
joined graph within the unchanged work limit.

These controls do not establish observed accuracy, a calibrated arbitrage-free
joint law or general basis/path convergence. Generated path-specific draws/reviews,
seasoned holdings, nonintegral fees, daily in-arrears indexed earning, compact mixed
candidate streaming, verified opening evidence, full saved-book adoption and the
complete 60,000-position joint acceptance remain original #15/#25 gates.

Research context: [Glasserman and Yu's paths/basis convergence analysis](https://business.columbia.edu/faculty/research/number-paths-versus-number-basis-functions-american-option-pricing)
supports retaining a separate convergence boundary. A successful finite-sample
quote fit and a fresh evaluation sample do not prove broad convergence.
