# Commercial graphs, coefficients and allocation

The additive `commercial-product-graph-1`, `commercial-units-1` and
`strategy-commercial-1` contracts explicitly select the commercial source and
credit owners. They do not reinterpret historical corporate `annuity`, floating
quarter-rate proxies or threshold exercise. Rebuild native artifacts and selected
libraries/sessions when adopting them. Their numerical assumptions remain
separate from observed calibration and accounting or regulatory approval.

## Raw graph and original valuation anchor

Each graph identifies its input/model/grid revisions, CRN, currency, actual as-of,
reporting dates, original market scenario and complete current scenarios. Each
position identifies commercial lending, issuer-credit debt or a credit-free
reference. Credit-free references reject hazards and contingent commitments.
The selected commercial owner uses lender/holder receipt-side contracts and
asset units. Issuer-credit debt describes the borrower's credit, not an adopted
funding-liability owner for the institution's own issued debt. Currency labels
must agree; the contract does not infer FX conversion.

The original Pricing histories, original signed cash quote and explicit OAS target
establish one immutable original OAS. Current histories separately supply Physical,
Pricing, Pricing-down and Pricing-up sources and their weights. Native validation
requires compatible original contract/acquisition anchors, complete source tails,
path keys and shared draw-stream identities. A Pricing source does not generate a
Physical accounting policy or a Physical probability distribution.

For cash component total `C` at its native event year `u`, native valuation sums
the supplied Pricing path weights times `C`, discounted using the collateral
curve and `exp(-original_oas * elapsed_years)`. Reporting marks include only cash
strictly after the report boundary, using the curve ratio from that boundary.
Principal, coupon, fee and actual recovery cash remain separate source components.
Economic loss is not another cash payment. Subday defaults and recoveries retain
their actual valuation times. No complete-tail event is moved onto a report date.

The original quote either verifies an explicit OAS or selects bounded native OAS
calibration. Current scenario and down/up valuations retain that same OAS. With
parallel bump size `b` basis points, `DV01 = (PV_down - PV_up) / (2*b)` in currency
per basis point. Paired sources retain shared draws; an option policy can change
under a bump while its original OAS remains unchanged. The graph represents the
explicit supplied distributions; it does not fit their credit or market laws.

Optional [native conditional exercise](commercial-exercise.md) constructs its own
information sets and stopping decisions from native sources. Bellman value must
reconcile to independently generated actual stopped cash. Original and current
policies retain separate receipts. Physical replay requires covered observed
prefixes. Defaults before exercise retain complete recovery claims.

Admission precedes financial generation: at most 32 positions, 13 scenarios,
64 histories per role, 256 aggregate source requests, 32 million aggregate work
units and 128 MiB retained component capacity. The complete result has a 32 MiB
encoded bound. These limits do not promise aggregate process RSS or combined
60,000-position acceptance.

## Generated policy graphs

A position may explicitly select `generated_policy` with a
`commercial-generated-policy-1` request and
`admission_tier="bounded_generated_policy_replay-1"`. This selection is exclusive
with supplied finite histories and the finite exercise owner. The current tier
admits one position, within four billion conservative work units and 128 MiB
estimated retained capacity. Ordinary graph/source caps remain unchanged.

The request supplies original Pricing training/evaluation and original Physical
laws, plus complete current Physical and Pricing laws. Each current scenario has
base/down/up Pricing laws with the same training/evaluation stream identities.
Pricing training alone fits continuation; each separately supplied Physical law
applies that corresponding Pricing policy. Physical outcomes cannot refit it.
The stochastic assumptions and limits are documented in
[generated exercise](commercial-generated-exercise.md).

This tier requires a locked original OAS. Its bits must agree with the original
training request, whose generated Pricing cash independently replays the original
quote. General Monte Carlo OAS calibration is not implemented. Original Physical
acquisition generation uses the supplied original contract, independent of later
current coupons or scenarios. Its complete stopped weighted cash reconciles to
original cost and EIR; current assumptions cannot replace this proof.

Compact sealed raw recipes regenerate genuine native Physical accounting owners
one at a time. Reports retain source bindings, native stops and book coefficients;
they do not retain every expanded source owner simultaneously. Capacity charges
all retained recipes and original proof plus the peak temporary source/fit owner.
Independent verification regenerates raw Gaussian/credit paths, regression,
stopped cash and accounting points. Component capacity is not an aggregate RSS
guarantee. Generated path-specific draws/reviewed actions and generated mixed
candidate journals remain unsupported and reject before generation.

## Actual-purchase coefficients

Each acquired unit supplies its exact unit/template identity, positive
face, actual purchase graph, accounting category, explicit capital-policy revision
and research regulatory weights. Source opening principal must equal unit face;
face cannot be a denominator invented to rescale a different contract. Original
Physical source cash, purchase cost and original effective yield must reconcile.
An exercised unit supplies complete separate original Physical histories. Native
stopping selects their actual original acquisition cash under the original
Pricing policy, and their weighted full cash reconciles to original purchase
cost and original effective yield. Current scenarios cannot replace that proof
or refit the original yield. Per-tranche acquisition cash remains distinct.

The tensor layout is `[scenario, unit, metric, reporting_interval]`. Coefficients
are expressed per unit of allocated face. Physical `InterestIncome` postings in
`(interval_start, interval_end]` supply NII; contractual coupon cash is not used as
a substitute. The authoritative state at interval start supplies principal.
That state retains live or default principal claims, so a supplied RWA weight is
not a regulatory determination of default exposure eligibility. Paired Pricing
marks supply DV01. HQLA, outflow, ASF, RSF and RWA coefficients use explicit
supplied weights; no eligibility, capital requirement or FTP cost is inferred.

The funding grid contains reporting dates and every actual Physical cash date
through contractual, prepayment, default and recovery tails. Acquisition cash is
the original purchase quote per face; subsequent cash is separately weighted once.
Funding demand is the negative cumulative bank cash. Exact native integer dates
retain their dates; subday cash is attributed to the enclosing day end, consistently
with the [daily journal](commercial-credit-ledger.md). Funding does not stop at the
last NII interval and does not assume future reinvestment. Output admits at most
one million funding cells and 250,000 cash rows, within the result byte bound.

## Native allocation and retained sessions

`optimize_commercial` constructs HiGHS inputs from native prepared units, explicit
scenario baselines, constraints, actual-date funding and typed face limits.
HiGHS remains C++; Rust constructs and validates its financial problem. The
objective remains worst-case external NII. Total face and quoted purchase cost
have separate limits. A capital limit needs the exact corresponding preparation
identity; changed financial inputs require refreshed capital dependencies.

After solving, Rust independently reduces retained source cash and coefficients
for the complete ordered allocation, including zero allocations. NII, funding and
purchase amounts must reconcile to the solver replay at unchanged tolerances.
The caller cannot deserialize replacement prepared coefficients.

`create_commercial` retains that native preparation in an actor. Evaluation and
constraint-only updates use it without pricing or credit/accounting generation.
The native actor's coefficient evaluation also avoids raw-source cash replay;
source and allocation replay remain creation/solve publication gates.
Dirty unit edits reuse exactly equal native sources; changed identity/grid/count
requires preparation. Staging, publication and abort retain version/token checks.
Each commercial actor call receives its own control; the creation deadline is
not retained as the session's lifetime deadline.

## Durable analysis and remaining adoption

`POST /models/runs` admits the graph and unit schemas to the durable worker. The
worker independently reconstructs raw contractual/credit/exercise sources and
coefficients before and after lossless Parquet persistence. The accepted queue
deadline, raw request, source/executable identity and all uploaded objects are
checked again with the SQL publication lock and current lease/token/attempt.
Cancellation, changed authority or changed artifacts cannot publish a successful
result. Existing interactive Strategy Lab libraries and saved books are not
automatically converted by an analytical result.

Explicit performing draws, reviewed credit actions, acquired exercise anchors,
durable commercial cohorts/libraries and standalone finite candidate/treasury
routes now have their own supported gates. See
[purchased journals and treasury](commercial-treasury-candidate.md).
Seasoned prefixes, nonintegral fee claims, generated path-specific draws/reviews,
general generated OAS calibration, complete mixed candidate/saved-book adoption,
broader product capital/FTP integration, general exercise convergence and empirical
holdouts remain separate required gates under
[issue #15 and tracker #25](implementation-plan.md). The native finite distribution
and synthetic fixtures do not establish observed accuracy.

# Complete-origin commercial holding journals

Local 0.29.14 adds explicitly selected `commercial-holding-journal-1`.
`analytics.model_contracts.journal_commercial_holding` transports raw requests to
`portfolio-strategy`; `/models/runs` executes the same native contract as a durable
job. Python independently verifies raw economics, journal postings and persisted
tables. The existing monthly and commercial ledger schemas remain unchanged.

The request supplies `origin_ledger`, `revised_sources` and `cut_ordinal`.
The complete original ledger request supplies accounts, allocations, actual-run
path weights and complete acquisition sources. Each revised source pairs with
the corresponding original source through `commercial-holding-continuation-1`.
Both raw and financial completed prefixes must agree; original quotes, yields,
gross rights, draw anchors, reviewed credit state and credit streams remain retained.
Future changes require the existing complete-origin source conventions. No money
checkpoint or prior-publication identifier is accepted by this contract.

Rust transfers the sealed revised owners directly into one existing daily Sim.
The credit clock runs from original acquisition. The Sim executes actual opening,
acquisition, ordered recognition and settlement through the complete contractual
and recovery tail. It neither truncates that tail at the report date nor inserts
a terminal payoff. The result retains the complete source receipt, complete
ordinary daily reports and protocol-6 journal for independent verification.

The prospective journal is derived from that full native journal. Let B(g,i)
be the ordered sum of postings through the cut for GL account g and instrument i.
Non-P&L stocks retain B(g,i). Prior signed P&L is reduced in stable GL/instrument
order and added to the account's opening equity. One balanced opening transaction
per nonempty account is posted on the cut date. The window then contains only
original transactions strictly after the cut. Their values, dates, instrument,
account, event and order are retained; `origin_transaction_number` records their
full-journal lineage. Future transaction numbers are local to the window.

`window_tables` contains `journal`, `opening`, `retained_prior_pnl`,
`trial_balance`, `commercial_daily` and `commercial_closing`. The daily/closing
tables retain native gross legal and recognized rights and reviewed credit state
from the cut onward. Daily rows on the cut describe the opening state; journal
rows on that day are only the derived opening. Prior acquisition and earnings
are not reposted. Every non-P&L/non-opening-equity closing stock must reproduce
the complete-origin native GL with identical f64 bits. Independent verification
recomputes the full raw source and full daily journal before deriving the window,
then checks opening, ordered future transactions and published closing balances.
Existing final-output tolerances remain unchanged.

The example retains a day-15 unpaid coupon right on a synthetic100 loan with
5% original EIR. The stress source changes only its future default hazard. The
same original waiting draw survives the cut; original cost and yield remain
unchanged. Other controls cover stopped recognition, signed rights after principal
settlement, reviewed default/chargeoff/waiver/recovery, zero/half allocation and
a complete funded draw with its original tranche yield. They are numerical
controls, not observed predictive validation.

The joined preflight charges complete prefix owners/comparisons, sealed openings,
one full daily Sim, raw transport and retained full/window buffers before any
generator. It uses the existing joined32M-work/128-MiB tier. Inner continuation
and ordinary all-run ledger8M/128-MiB caps and per-source daily8M/32-MiB caps
remain unchanged. Raw input is bounded to2MiB and result encoding to32MiB.
A complete12-day zero-hazard draw control uses an explicit one-jump guard;
the larger draw control rejects at the unchanged ordinary cap. No reservation
is reduced to admit an unsupported contract. Component capacity bounds do not
constitute aggregate process RSS guarantees.

The original native deadline covers decoding, all sources, daily replay, window
derivation, bounded encoding and output writes. Durable jobs retain the original
queue deadline through independent raw and persisted verification, lossless
Parquet cells, source/artifact/executable hashes and final lease/token/revision/
attempt publication fences. Rehashed opening, prefix, prior-P&L, journal-order,
closing and adoption-evidence mutations reject publication.

`complete_origin_daily_sim_adoption` is true. `prior_publication_verified`,
`cut_started_mixed_sim_adoption`, `secondary_acquisition_adoption` and
`empirical_validation` remain false. This derives a window from one complete
origin run; it does not run a new mixed Sim starting at a previously published
opening, prove external bank reconciliation, prepare seasoned strategy/cohort
coefficients or allocate secondary conveyed rights. Those gates, nonintegral
fees, daily in-arrears indexed earning, generated draws/reviews and streaming,
observed histories/reviewed policies and complete60000-position mixed graph/
credit/solver/journal acceptance remain required under issues15/25.

Rebuild matching product, ledger and decision/workflow artifacts and restart
deployed API/workers before additive execution. Existing saved economics require
explicit selected-session/library rebuilding. Local validation does not deploy
artifacts, restart workers or close full issue15/25.

Matching official local builds pass1,220 native tests and strict checks,210
commercial engine and135 commercial API checks,2,598 full engine checks with two
existing skips and1,100 full API checks. Contract, source/artifact, independent
hand-control and four historical whole-output identity gates pass. See
[the accepted local review](../reviews/2026-10-12-commercial-holding-journal.md)
for exact source, artifact, log and snapshot identities.

# Verified modeled commercial prior openings

Local0.29.15 adds durable `POST /models/holding-journals`. It resolves an
authorized completed `commercial-holding-journal-1` job in the current repository
scope. The caller supplies `source_job_id`, the exact published `cut_ordinal`,
`revised_sources`, `expected_revision` and an optional timeout. The caller cannot
supply an opening ledger, balances, permission flags or object descriptors.

The API captures bounded source metadata. It materializes the new native request
from the stored source's original account/participation/allocation specification
and its actually executed revised sources. Native financial calculation uses the
existing `commercial-holding-journal-1` owner and daily Sim. No Python financial
generation, caller checkpoint, original-yield refit or credit-clock restart is
introduced. Before native execution, the durable worker reopens and independently
recomputes the complete raw prior source and its persisted full journal. A stored
verification flag alone grants no authority.

# Commercial closing capital, daily FTP and purchased journals

These are explicit additive contracts. Rust prepares the source, credit, coupon
book, journal and treasury amounts. Python transports immutable inputs and runs
independent raw-source and persisted verification. Compatible native artifacts
and explicit selection are required. Local fixtures do not establish observed
accuracy, accounting approval, deployment or complete issue acceptance.

## Source-linked capital and daily FTP

`commercial-treasury-1` takes `raw_commercial` containing the complete
`commercial-credit-ledger-1` request. Optional `capital` and `ftp` branches select
separate reviewed policy inputs; at least one branch must be configured. The
capital branch supplies `treasury`, account/scenario `policies`, an
`amount_multiplier`, reviewed identity and `exposure_policy`. The FTP branch
supplies `as_of`, policy identity, curves and explicit per-path reviews.

Rust first executes the commercial source and its protocol-6 journal. Closing
capital uses the complete-tail closing trial balance and requires the treasury
date and every account policy period to equal that exact closing date. It does
not substitute the requested earlier reporting date. Reviewed provisions,
chargeoffs, recovery income and retained P&L enter through actual postings once.
Economic modeled LGD does not become a second capital deduction. Legal memo
accounts are balanced and independently verified before being excluded from
regulatory amounts. Eligible capital, regulatory weights and adjustments,
denominators, requirements and management buffers remain supplied policies.

Daily FTP uses actual unweighted path stocks, actual cash dates and posted income,
with participation applied once. Separate channels retain live/default principal,
basis, signed recognized interest, gross legal coupon rights and actual undrawn
commitment. Reviewed paths additionally retain legal principal and allowance.
The supplied funding, channel-change and income reviews determine permitted
ownership. Remaining channel stocks require complete explicit termination;
neither a short reporting horizon nor a zero aggregate net right closes them.

Original effective-interest income, reviewed basis realization, reviewed credit
expense and recovery income use distinct posted earnings identities. Contingent
charges use actual undrawn commitment once. Internal transfers do not change
external NII or regulatory capital. Opening-day P&L with FTP is refused until a
separate opening earnings owner is supplied. Realized paths are not reinterpreted
as expected-flow FTP inputs. Supplied curves, reset tenors, option spreads,
operating costs, capital allocations and cost of capital remain assumptions.

The current bridge admits at most 16 paths and 64 complete FTP days, a separate
2-million bridge-work bound, 2 MiB raw envelope and 32 MiB output. Source and
journal admission limits remain in force. Capital-only requests retain the full
native ledger calendar. These component limits are not aggregate RSS promises.

The transport is `core.commercial_treasury_native.run`. The durable
`/models/runs` route independently recomputes sources, signed ordered postings,
closing reports and treasury outputs before and after persistence.

## Actual-purchase commercial candidate journal

`commercial-candidate-journal-1` takes a raw `commercial-units-1` request,
ordered `allocation`, actual `as_of_ordinal` and `reporting_end_ordinal`,
explicit `owners`, `run_mapping`, zero-placeholder ledger `specification` and
`verified_opening_identity`. The identity is supplied provenance; the native
receipt retains `opening_identity_verified: false`.

Unit preparation retains the original base OAS, separate Physical and Pricing
histories, actual purchase cash and original effective yield. Exercised
acquisitions require complete original Physical expectations and an independently
reconstructed stopped-cash acquisition proof. Performing draw tranches retain
their own conditional activation, original source, cost and EIR. Allocation
replays prepared coefficients and full-tail funding cash without repricing.

The native coordinator maps each exclusive source to an actual account and
position. Purchase offsets remain in source lineage and daily/closing rows;
local credit time and global credit time are distinct retained fields. Commercial
loans use `commercial_loan-1` and a loan placeholder. Issuer-credit assets use
`issuer_ac_security-1` and an AC security placeholder with zero duration and unit
opening market-price anchor. Issuer securities reject loan facilities, CCF and
performing draws. The selected candidate owner supports AC; AFS/HTM marks,
institution funding liabilities and arbitrary mixed owners need separate gates.

Opening account cash/equity is posted once, candidate acquisition uses actual
purchase cost, and source groups enter the existing shared daily Sim in stable
global chronological order. The minimum Sim calendar is 30 days; the caller's
earlier reporting date remains immutable. A separate full calendar covers every
contractual, recovery and reviewed action tail. No terminal payoff is invented.
Existing pooled cash-floor checks remain active.

The result retains complete native unit preparation, allocation replay,
normalized specification, protocol-6 tables and explicit reporting/full dates.
`shared_daily_sim_adoption` and `graph_exercise_source_adoption` disclose this
selected ownership. Independent persisted verification, opening evidence,
arbitrary mixed adoption and empirical validation are separate flags. Generated
policy graphs do not imply candidate adoption when complete native Sim retention
exceeds admission; such requests must refuse without increasing existing caps.

The candidate envelope/output are bounded to 32 MiB; native admission retains the
32-million aggregate work and 128 MiB component-capacity boundaries. The transport
is `core.commercial_candidate_native.run`.

## Immutable publication

Both durable routes preserve the original scalar deadline through raw parsing,
native execution, independent replay, persistence and final SQL publication.
Publication checks the exact queued raw request, native executable and source
identities, immutable artifact bytes, cancellation, input revision, lease and
attempt token. Nested monetary, integer and boolean identities are checked before
table conversion. Failed final checks remove only fresh owned unpublished output.
The API does not execute financial calculation in its request handler.

Focused tests cover raw cash/book/journal replay, reviewed capital without a
second loss deduction, incomplete FTP termination, mutation rejection and durable
publication adversaries. Their current execution evidence belongs in
[the implementation ledger](implementation-plan.md); rebuilding and restarting
deployed workers is a separate operator action. Full observed holdouts and complete
60,000-position joint graph/credit/solver/journal acceptance remain required.

The Capital & FTP panel can select one or two completed Card2 mixed or performing-deposit source1 jobs. Raw modeled-product inputs remain available in the existing mode. The selected-source route reconstructs each retained raw source and independently verifies its complete source and journal under the new job deadline; saved verification flags are evidence to reproduce, not permission.

Choose the source kind and completed job ID, then check its metadata. The helper reads bounded authoritative job/request metadata twice and returns owner/run/path indices and labels. It neither loads full journals nor executes financial calculations. Editing an ID or kind invalidates the checked selection. Journal verification, regulatory eligibility and accounting approval remain false on that metadata response.

Supply an explicit source alias, scope-review ID/revision and a complete reviewed funding policy. Policy indexed reviews must identify each declared path, and aliases must match its charges. Omit `source.sources` in this mode. Curves, repricing/liquidity tenor policies, cash assignments and contingent/option charges remain supplied inputs. The helper provides no financial or regulatory defaults. Card2 scope funds exclusive product owners while retaining inherited dated sources without funding them; deposit scope covers the isolated performing owner. Portfolio source2 is not yet a completed-source kind.

The new native preparation owns funding coefficients and FTP math. Source reproduction and immutable Parquet replay are publication gates. The panel waits through bounded job status, then pages reports and supports reopening/download; it never hydrates full result or journal manifests. The private source binding rechecks exact durable row, queued raw input, object hashes, current source/native identity, original deadline, cancellation, lease and token at publication. Failed publication produces no successful report.

Declared typed Rust DTO financial fields normalize integer spelling to binary64 only at their documented clone boundary. Raw `serde_json::Value` specifications retain integer/float/bool and signed-zero identity exactly. This is reviewed synthetic/source-linked FTP preparation, not empirical calibration, accounting-standard approval, regulatory eligibility or full saved-book/cohort/60,000-position adoption. Capital source eligibility remains distinct. Existing manual, legacy bridge and raw synthetic modes retain their contracts.
docs/models/consumer-card.md:
# Native revolving credit-card statement state

`portfolio_model_core::consumer_card::simulate` accepts strict `consumer-card-1`
requests. The model is distinct from installment amortization: purchase, cash
advance and promotional principal can grow with supplied draws and shrink with
supplied payments while an open commitment remains. It is the state mechanics
stage of #19; it does not by itself complete public product/graph/cohort,
unit-library, allowance, daily journal, or empirical validation acceptance.

## Source, state, and measure

The shared consumer identity retains account/original loan, position, cohort,
source revision, model/assumption/run identity and currency. Physical and pricing
policies are explicit; there is no inferred measure conversion or synthetic
reverse stress. Pricing state paths must not post physical GL. Spend/payment
behavior and credit transitions are supplied actions. An assumption identity
does not turn synthetic actions into fitted behavior.

All openings are explicit: three-class principal, billed interest, earned
unbilled interest, unrecognized billed interest, fees, pending statement rights,
minimum remaining and optional due date, plus contingent purchase grace
interest. Pending statement balances cannot exceed current billed debt. Missing
opening due dates with pending balances fail. Opening purchase principal is a
single aggregate lot: its supplied contingent interest is allocated
proportionally when that lot is paid. Accounts whose opening transaction lots
need distinct dates/rates require upstream lot-level state rather than claiming
this aggregate opening is exact for them.

Each new draw or fee creates a stable lot. Equal-day actions execute in input
order; draw-then-payment differs from payment-then-draw. Opening/draw lots are
FIFO at equal APR/class. The model does not infer spend from utilization or
infer borrower transactor/revolver type from a label. A transactor appears as
supplied full statement payments; a revolver carries unpaid principal.

## Daily accrual, statement posting, and payment

Dates are actual Gregorian ordinals. At each date the prior day's interest is
accrued before current transactions. A rate change on date `d` applies to
`[d,d+1)` rather than repricing the preceding day. APR inputs are periodic
accrual rates expressed annually, using explicit ACT/365F or ACT/360:

`daily_interest = (principal + optional previously billed interest) * APR / denominator`.

The `compound_billed_interest` switch is explicit. Newly earned **unbilled**
interest does not compound before posting, and fees do not earn interest. For
non-grace balances, daily interest is recognized as earned and retained as
unbilled until statement close. At statement close, unbilled interest becomes
billed without being recognized twice. Payments settle billed charges, not
earned unbilled charges that have not yet posted. These conventions must match
the selected issuer agreement; they are not universal card rules. The
[CFPB interest calculation explanation](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/how-does-my-credit-card-company-calculate-the-amount-of-interest-i-owe-en-51/)
distinguishes rates by transaction type and purchase grace.

The caller supplies statement and due ordinals. Each statement must precede its
due date; the next statement follows the previous due date. This version admits
ordered, nonoverlapping statement/due windows and rejects timelines it cannot
represent. It does not create a mailing/notice date or independently establish
regulatory compliance. In a date's order, transactions occur before due checks
and statement snapshots. Thus a payment on a due date is timely; a payment on
statement date occurs before that statement creates the new minimum.

At statement close, the configured minimum is:

`min(statement debt, max(floor, principal_fraction * principal + optional billed interest + optional fees))`.

The minimum remaining is reduced by supplied payments. The caller supplies a
permutation of the three classes for allocating the minimum portion. The excess
portion uses descending APR on the **payment date**, with stable FIFO ties.
Within each selected lot, payments settle fees, then billed interest, then
principal. This lot-based waterfall is a declared supported issuer policy;
different policies require a versioned extension. The minimum/excess
distinction and payment-date rate selection are consistent with the supported
case in [Regulation Z §1026.53 and its official interpretation](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/53/).
Deferred-interest exceptions and disputed/protected balances are not silently
modeled as ordinary APR balances.

## Purchase grace and promotions

Eligible purchase interest accumulates as **contingent shadow interest**, not
earned NII or billed debt. Cash advances and promotional balances have no
purchase grace. Principal paid while eligible proportionately waives that
lot's accumulated shadow interest. Consequently, full payment before the due
check waives the interest, and paid principal is protected even when a statement
is paid only partly. Lot-specific transaction dates prevent an early purchase
payment from incorrectly waiving a later purchase's interest history.

If pending statement rights remain at due, purchase grace is lost. The
remaining shadow amount on still-unpaid eligible purchase lots becomes billed
interest and is recognized **on that determination date**. The version supports
the supplied policy in which loss also applies to other outstanding eligible
purchase lots; issuer terms must permit that policy. Paid principal's shadow
amount has already been waived. There is no two-cycle back-billing. The
[paid-portion restrictions in §1026.54](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1026/54/)
are why the engine tracks shadow balances and waiver separately rather than
applying a blanket charge to original statement principal.

`regain_grace_after_full_statement_payment` explicitly determines whether a fully
paid due check restores eligibility for subsequent new purchase lots. Existing
non-grace lots are not relabeled retrospectively. Before a due check, closing
contingent interest remains visible in the result; a short analytical horizon
does not silently turn it into interest income.

Promotions are genuine temporary APRs. Before the explicit expiry ordinal,
promotional APR applies; at expiry and thereafter, post-promotion APR applies
to future daily accrual. Zero APR can therefore degenerate to no promo interest.
There is no deferred-interest retroactive catch-up. Unknown deferred-interest
fields fail. Supported supplied APR resets affect class rates going forward;
the model does not infer an index fixing or establish whether a rate change is
legally permitted. That permission and notice policy are source inputs.

## Limits, credit, recovery, and reconciliation

A draw requires a performing account and available limit after current
principal, posted finance charges and fees. Unbilled/contingent interest is
retained as rights but does not reduce this version's available credit before
posting. Limit reduction may leave existing debt above the line without
inventing a payment or negative draw. Utilization is billed debt/limit and can
exceed one after reduction. Zero limit returns unavailable utilization (`None`),
with zero available undrawn. The model does not create a CCF/default draw from
unused commitment. Upstream jointly modeled behavior must supply such a draw
before default, within the explicit limit policy, or introduce a reviewed
contingent-default-draw policy.

Delinquency/cure/nonaccrual are supplied live-state changes. Nonaccrual suspends
new daily contract interest in this version. If previously contingent purchase
interest becomes billed while nonaccrual, it remains unrecognized until cash
collection. Previously recognized accrual is not automatically reversed on
entry: that is the separate credit accounting policy's responsibility.

Default removes all principal once, closes the line, stops subsequent accrual,
and separately reports recognized accrued interest, unrecognized contract
interest, fees, and principal loss. Recovery is a supplied principal-only
collection fraction at an explicit lag, less supplied collection cost.
Costs exceeding gross collections produce negative expense cash, not a dropped
cost. An action after default, including a same-day later payment, fails.
Contingent grace interest not yet billed is extinguished at default under this
version's principal-only recovery policy; it is not fabricated as earned NII.
Agreements requiring collection of those contingent claims need a further
explicit default/grace policy. Mere zero balance is an open card account, not
an installment payoff exit.

The conservation identity is:

`opening principal + funded draws = principal payments + defaulted principal + closing principal`.

Recovery cash is outside that identity and never causes a second live-principal
reduction. Cash draws are negative principal from the lender's perspective;
payments/recoveries are positive. Fees, cash interest, and recognition are
distinct outputs. A downstream ledger must own draws/default/collections once,
preserve the account/run/lot lineage, reject legacy duplicate overlays, use
recognized-only accrued interest for GL, and retain full recovery and pending
statement/grace tails. Allowances, economic-versus-accounting recovery claims,
fee effective-yield amortization, capital/FTP and tax remain separate policies.

## Admission and validation evidence

There are at most 4096 supplied actions plus cycles, 36600 horizon days, and
250000 admitted daily lot/cycle work units. This bound includes the potential
lot/day recognition output, not merely input row count. Opening/closing total
rights, cash/principal totals and component amounts are finite and bounded by
`1e15`; rates lie in `[0,2]` and fractions in `[0,1]`. Each shared identity is
nonblank and at most 256 bytes. Unknown fields and terminal-state shortcuts
fail. Recovery dates must lie inside the full contract horizon; no tail is
clipped. A caller's transport/process budget remains additional to these
per-model bounds.

`tests/consumer_card.rs` provides 19 independent analytical fixtures. They
cover transactor/revolver limits, actual leap dates, issuer minimum versus
highest-APR excess, paid-portion grace, FIFO dated lots, promo expiry, statement
posting, billed-only compounding, pending opening rights, nonaccrual collection,
draw/limit/fee/default conservation, recovery costs/tails, zero-change/measure
identity, duplicate/unknown convention rejection and work/money admission.
These are controlled synthetic mechanics tests, not calibration evidence.
Chronological observed account panels, training-only fitting, forward holdouts,
payment/spend/utilization/default diagnostics, account-versus-cohort error
reports and stressed PV/DV01/NII/runoff validation remain required before any
empirical model claim or full #19 acceptance.
docs/models/consumer-credit-accounting.m:
# Acquired installment events and reviewed credit accounting

`consumer-credit-accounting-1` is a bounded native component for one purchased,
initially performing auto or personal loan with one supplied physical history.
It calls `consumer_installment::project` once as the sole economic owner and
feeds its default events into `credit_accounting::evaluate`. It does not compose
two daily ledgers or make the performing mixed-book route credit capable.

The request retains the complete raw contract, path and economic-source identity,
purchase principal/cost/date, original annual effective yield and anchor, income
review, accounting/recovery/cost policies and explicit allowance/chargeoff reviews.
The economic-source revision must equal the contract's source revision. Purchase
principal equals the contract's original and opening principal. The admitted
`supplied_non_pcd_gross_cost-1` convention seeds gross carrying value at purchase
cost. Supplied allowance is a separate contra-asset opening balance. No purchased
credit deterioration gross-up or acquisition equity/provision posting is inferred.

## Economics and original income

The contract must start performing with no opening accrued/unrecognized interest
or fees. Only explicit payment, payoff and default observations are admitted.
Original payment, actual payment dates, ACT/360 or ACT/365 fixed contractual day count and product recovery
assumptions remain the consumer projector's inputs. Its terminal scheduled payment,
payoff and default have distinct source state and intent identities. Contractual
interest in an interval is `principal * note_rate * actual_year_fraction`; daily
recognition apportions that exact interval amount by each calendar day's fraction
of the interval. A whole coupon is not counted as daily income a second time.

Before default or payoff, `dated_income::evaluate` advances gross carrying value
using the supplied frozen original annual effective yield:

```
effective_interest = opening_gross_carrying * expm1(log1p(original_yield) / 365)
accrued_change     = contractual_earned - cash_interest
basis_change       = effective_interest - contractual_earned
principal_change   = -cash_principal
```

This uses actual calendar days, including leap days; the annual EIR convention is
ACT/365 fixed. Contractual coupon accrual retains its separately declared day count.
The native prefix suppresses terminal payoff cash in its recurrence so it exposes
the carrying adjustment immediately before the explicit retirement policy. The
adapter then posts actual cash/principal/accrued settlement and recognizes the
remaining signed basis in earnings under `recognize_in_earnings_at_payoff-1`.
Default consumes the same predefault principal/accrued/basis; original EIR stops
at default, and the reviewed shared accounting policy transfers or reverses the
accrued right and transfers or recognizes the basis. Negative original EIR and
discount basis remain distinct from contractual negative coupon; the installment
projector admits nonnegative contractual rates only.

The original yield is supplied and retained, with no inference from a pricing
history, target price or risk-neutral recovery discounting. Incompatible negative
gross carrying value is rejected by the existing income operator. There is no
income, cash, principal or terminal basis plug.

## Gross recoveries and costs

`gross_recovery_with_credit_loss_cost-1` keeps costs outside the principal claim:

```
principal_only_loss = default_principal - gross_recovery
recovery_cash      = +gross_recovery
cost_cash          = -reviewed_recovery_cost
total_economic_loss = principal_only_loss + recovery_cost
```

The shared credit operator receives the gross principal-only recovery tail and
principal-only expected loss. Actual cost has a separate same-date debit to credit
loss expense and credit to cash, retaining its review and claim identity. The
consumer projector's net recovery and total economic loss are retained and
reconciled; economic expected loss does not create another journal provision.
The initial lane requires `0 <= cost <= gross <= default_principal`. It rejects
surplus collateral proceeds and costs exceeding gross recovery until ownership
of those cash obligations is explicitly supplied.

The synthetic example has principal 100, note 36%, ACT/360 and default after 10 days,
so accrued coupon is 1. Gross recovery 60 and cost 10 settle after 20 more days. The
principal-only loss is 40, net cash 50 and total economic loss 50. An independently
supplied opening allowance 40 and chargeoff 40 consume allowance once; cost 10 is
the remaining credit expense. Under original EIR 0, accrued reversal and signed
basis recognition offset; neither creates additional net coupon income.

## Order, rights and integration seam

`Daily.owned` is the state after that actual day's complete processing. Order is:

1. Original EIR and contractual recognition, followed by actual product cash.
2. Shared before-credit allowance review, default transfer and accrued/basis policy.
3. Reviewed chargeoffs, gross recovery cash and after-credit allowance review.
4. Separately reviewed recovery cost cash/expense.

`acquisition_opening` seeds live principal, cost-minus-principal book adjustment
and allowance only. It emits no acquisition cash/equity journal. An eventual
exclusive mixed owner must acquire and seed those balances once against its actual
opening account, apply each allocation and physical path weight once, retire future
generic contractual/default ownership atomically and process these intents in the
same daily GL. Standalone journal concatenation is not integration.

Every intent has source/policy/claim metadata; lineage retains path, original yield
anchor and source observation/origin coordinates. Reporting state is an actual-date
snapshot. Full replay retains all supplied recovery and review dates. Live contractual
tails must finish within the full source horizon; default claims with unpaid
principal, accrued interest or basis remain explicit unless reviewed actions retire
them. The primitive does not delete those claims or claim full-account publication.

## Admission and limitations

Limits are 1080 days, 64 review events, 2 million conservative work units, 1 MiB serialized
raw input, 64 MiB serialized result and the shared 1e15 monetary magnitude bound.
An optional native control closure runs before and between stages and daily steps;
it supplies no financial values. The existing consumer projector and income calls
are individually bounded and checked immediately before/after. Component budgets
are not an aggregate process-RSS limit. No fast math or final tolerance change is
introduced; ownership reconciliation uses existing `1e-9 + 1e-12 * abs(reference)`.

Modifications, nonaccrual, fees, prepayment penalties, seasoned/PCD acquisition,
interest recoveries, draws, migrations and negative contractual coupon are excluded.
Histories, recovery assumptions and review dates are supplied, with no empirical
hazard/recovery fit, stochastic CRN or measure conversion claim. Card and mortgage
economics require their own event adapters. Native mixed ledger ownership, independent
persisted verification, capital/solver adoption, empirical and combined scale gates
remain open.

## Primary references and evidence

[FASB ASU 2016-13](https://storage.fasb.org/ASU_2016-13.pdf), summary pages 2–4,
distinguishes an allowance from amortized cost and requires historical, current and
reasonable/supportable forecast information for expected losses. It also describes
different acquisition accounting for purchased credit deterioration. This component
keeps those judgments supplied and excludes that acquisition lane; its policy names
do not establish accounting compliance. The ASU communicates amendments and is not
itself the authoritative Codification.

The example and dedicated native fixtures independently check accrued coupon,
principal/gross/net recovery and cost conservation, original-EIR premium payoff,
retained default rights, same-day order, invalid ownership and cooperative cancellation.
The public component's native suite passes 10 tests, and strict all-target shared
core Clippy passes. The installed independent verifier and real debug and rebuilt
official `portfolio-lifecycle` processes pass 63 tests: 39 pure financial/source cases and
24 process cases, including 15 complete accepted results and unsupported-source
rejections. These retain exact ordered source/state/identity checks and the existing
financial tolerance. The explicit analysis adapter is `account_consumer_credit`;
the durable model worker checks sources before and after persistence. Ten focused
durable primitive publication and failure-fence checks pass against the rebuilt
official artifact. These component and application gates do not establish the
mixed-ledger, broader product or empirical acceptance gates.

# Native auto and personal installment paths

`portfolio_model_core::consumer_installment::project` accepts strict
`consumer-installment-1` inputs and returns a deterministic, versioned account
path. This is the contractual and supplied-policy calculation stage for issues
#17 and #18. It is not a calibrated consumer behavior model, an accounting-policy
approval, or evidence that cohort, public graph, unit-library, and journal
publication adoption are complete.

## Identity and source contract

Every request carries position, original loan, cohort, currency, source revision,
model version, assumption identity, and run identity. Currency is a label; there
is no conversion. A caller explicitly supplies a **physical** or **pricing**
measure. Identical cashflow mechanics can be run under either supplied policy
path, but the engine never converts a physical path into a risk-neutral one.
Pricing paths must not post physical GL. A contractual-only label is rejected
because this schema admits borrower and credit actions.

Original principal and original payment remain in the result. Current opening
principal cannot exceed original principal. Recognized accrued interest,
unrecognized contract interest, and unpaid fees are distinct supplied opening
balances. The model does not infer earlier payments, previous nonaccrual, or
origination fee economics from a current tape balance.

`payment_dates` are exact, already selected contractual ordinals. They are
strictly increasing after valuation and contained in the full horizon. The model
does not infer payment frequency, infer a holiday calendar, shift dates, or treat
months as 30 days. Users must retain the contract's original/adjusted date policy
in source inputs. All actions and recovery dates must fit this full horizon;
short reporting horizons belong downstream. Recovery tails are never truncated.

## Payment and interest calculation

This version supports fixed note-rate daily **simple** interest on the remaining
principal, with explicit ACT/360 or ACT/365F. For a half-open interval `[s,e)`:

`interest = opening interval principal * note_rate * (e-s) / denominator`.

The denominator remains 365 in a leap year for ACT/365F. Shared Gregorian/date
and accrual helpers perform date validation. There is no interest capitalization
into principal. Fees and accrued interest do not earn interest. Note rate and
disclosed APR are separate fields. Disclosed APR is retained lineage and does
not replace the note rate or compute a fresh disclosure APR from fees. The
[CFPB distinction between loan interest rate and APR](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-the-difference-between-a-loan-interest-rate-and-the-apr-en-733/)
supports keeping those concepts separate.

Each modeled date first accrues from the previous date using the previous
principal and credit state. It then applies at most one explicit action. An
explicit payment or payoff replaces the automatic payment on that date. Other
actions take effect before the automatic payment, when one is due. Only
performing accounts make automatic scheduled payments. Delinquent/nonaccrual
accounts require explicit collections or a supplied cure state.

The supported allocation order is unpaid fees, recognized interest,
unrecognized contract interest, then principal. It is an explicit versioned
policy, not a claim that all lenders use this order. Agreements with a different
waterfall require a different supported policy. The
[CFPB repossession bulletin](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/compliance/supervisory-guidance/cfpb-bulletin-2022-04-mitigating-harm-from-repossession-of-automobiles/)
emphasizes that actual payment application must follow the disclosed agreement.

Before the final due date, automatic cash is the current payment capped by total
payoff. At the final due date a performing account pays the full remaining
obligation: this includes any final adjustment or catch-up balloon caused by
earlier low/missed payments. It does not silently retain the original installment
when that would leave an unpaid balance. Delinquent accounts are not fabricated
as paid at maturity; unpaid principal and interest persist to closing. An
explicit partial final payment can also leave a supplied unresolved balance.

`ChangePayment` changes subsequent scheduled payments while retaining the
original payment. `Fee` adds supplied unpaid fees. `Payment` permits partial or
extra collections without recasting the original contract. `Payoff` pays accrued
obligations and all remaining principal, adds an explicitly supplied fraction of
principal as a prepayment penalty, and exits the account. Automatic or ordinary
extra principal payments do not receive that payoff penalty. If an agreement
penalizes all extra principal, this version's policy is unsuitable.

Precomputed-interest loans and unearned-interest refund methods are unsupported
and unknown fields fail, rather than being routed through this model. The
[CFPB simple-versus-precomputed explanation](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/whats-the-difference-between-a-simple-interest-rate-and-precomputed-interest-on-an-auto-loan-en-841/)
describes why early payment behavior differs between these contracts.

## Credit, nonaccrual, repossession, and collection

Performing, delinquent, and nonaccrual are live states. Supplied state changes can
represent delinquency and cure. Default and payoff require economic actions;
setting a terminal state directly is rejected. The engine does not fit cure,
default, or prepayment probabilities from FICO, DTI, vintage, or cohort labels.
These inputs need upstream calibrated or explicitly assumed scenarios. A path
cannot both default and pay off on the same date, and an action after terminal
exit fails. Original principal equals principal collected **before default**,
closing principal, plus defaulted principal. Recovery cash is tracked separately
and never counts a second time as pre-default principal amortization.

Nonaccrual suppresses accrual-basis recognition. The caller explicitly chooses
whether simple contract interest continues to accumulate as unrecognized debt.
Cash collected against that debt produces a cash-basis recognition record at
the collection date, with equal start/end ordinals. Cure does not automatically
recognize the uncollected nonaccrual balance or apply an allowance/accounting
reversal. Those decisions belong the reviewed credit accounting policy.

Auto inputs require new/used status, vintage, original LTV, channel, as-of
collateral value, annual depreciation, sale haircut, repossession cost, and an
integer recovery delay. Vintage and LTV are supplied domains, not fitted causal
coefficients. The recovery sale value is:

`gross = collateral_value_as_of * (1-depreciation)^((sale_date-as_of)/365) * (1-sale_haircut)`.

Depreciation runs through the **sale date**, including repossession delay. The
annual multiplicative decay with ACT/365 elapsed time is a disclosed supplied
assumption, not a vehicle-price forecast. Gross collateral proceeds are not
capped before deducting costs. Thus surplus collateral can cover repossession
cost before principal is capped, avoiding a false shortfall on an oversecured
loan. Principal recovery is `min(principal, max(gross-cost,0))`. Surplus belongs
outside the lender's principal recovery and is not invented as lender fee
income. Actual lawful repossession, redemption, notices and deficiency recovery
are jurisdiction/contract inputs, not automatic triggers. The
[CFPB repossession discussion](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-happens-if-my-car-is-repossessed-en-865/)
explains the distinction between vehicle proceeds, expenses, and remaining debt.

Personal inputs require vintage, DTI and its definition, channel, a supplied
principal collection fraction, collection cost, and recovery delay. There is no
collateral value or mortgage behavior proxy:

`gross = defaulted principal * collection_fraction`.

For both products, recovery net of cost is a principal-only policy. Default
recognized interest, unrecognized contract interest, and fees are reported
separately and are not silently included in principal LGD. Costs beyond gross
proceeds produce a negative fee/expense cash component at recovery, so they do
not vanish under a zero-recovery floor. Principal loss remains principal minus
principal recovery; the excess expense is additional economic cost. Multiple
collections, deficiency interest/fees, collateral liquidation uncertainty,
collection curves and recovery receivable recognition require explicit further
policies.

## Outputs, bounds, and independent evidence

The result retains dated lender-perspective cashflows, exact recognition
intervals, state/balance points, original due dates and payment lineage, closing
rights, and default/recovery records. Default principal removal is **not cash**.
Recognition is not another settlement. The graph/ledger adopter must retain
separate origins when allocating collections and defaults, map signed expense
cash, reject pricing GL, and prevent a second legacy credit/prepay overlay.
Allowances, effective-yield fee amortization, tax and regulatory classification
remain separate accounting functions.

Admission is at most 4096 total contractual dates/actions, 36600 horizon days,
bounded 256-byte nonblank identities, nonnegative finite amounts and aggregate
obligations/cash within `1e15`, note/APR rates in `[0,2]`, fractions in `[0,1]`,
and supplied DTI/LTV domain checks. Dates use shared ordinal validation. Requests
deny unknown fields, including tagged empty actions. Duplicate action dates,
payments larger than payoff, terminal-state shortcuts and truncated recovery
tails fail. There is no financial Python callback or silent fallback.

`tests/consumer_installment.rs` supplies 17 independent analytical tests,
including zero-rate principal conservation, leap-day actual interest, separate
APR, penalty payoff, delinquency/cure, cash-basis nonaccrual, default/accrual
separation, unsecured and auto cost/recovery, collateral surplus, depreciation
through sale, preserved tails, original-payment changes, monetary/domain
failures, and a direct payment/rate grid. Identical supplied paths serialize
identically. These synthetic/analytical checks are separate from empirical
validation. Auto and personal calibration need chronological observed borrower
histories, validated variable definitions, training-only fit, account/cohort
stress error reports, and held-out evidence; no such claim follows from these
fixtures or from cohort grouping.

# Fixed-rate contractual amortization

This is the contractual schedule stage of corporate debt and commercial-loan
enhancement issue [#15](https://github.com/beauschwab/model-portfolio-sim/issues/15).
It introduces explicit `amort_type="level_payment"` in the Rust term-deck request.
The existing `"annuity"` value retains its historical **equal-principal** meaning.
Saved instruments are never reinterpreted or automatically converted.

## Contract and scope

`level_payment` produces a constant scheduled total payment of principal plus
fixed-coupon interest, per unit of opening principal. The contractual frequency,
business-day adjustment and day count determine its actual accrual fractions.
The first stub receives the same total payment as the remaining periods; its
interest and principal split reflects its shorter accrual. An input must describe
the remaining fully amortizing contract starting at the valuation date. The
calculated payment is not a reconstruction of a seasoned loan's original payment.
If that payment must be preserved, a future explicit contractual-payment and
remaining-balance input is required.

The new value is supported for fixed-rate corporate/commercial instruments only.
Floating-rate contracts are rejected: a schedule prepared at valuation cannot
predict path-dependent reset rates or their payment-reset conventions. CD
contracts and simultaneous sinking schedules are also rejected. Corporate call
and put rules continue to operate on the resulting contractual balance, with their
existing threshold-exercise assumptions unchanged.

The actual adjusted payment dates must fit within the supplied market grid.
If any exceeds `months/12 - 1e-9` years from valuation, construction fails and asks
for a longer grid. This is deliberate for the new contract value: compressing
later payments into the terminal grid would change the contractual economics.
Historical bullet, equal-principal and sinking contracts keep their existing
terminal-grid behavior to preserve saved results.

## Financial equations

Let opening principal be `B_0=1`, annual fixed coupon be `c`, and actual accrual
fraction of payment period `i` be `tau_i`. Interest follows the existing term
kernel's simple-accrual convention:

```
g_i = 1 + c * tau_i
interest_i = c * tau_i * B_(i-1)
B_i = g_i * B_(i-1) - P
principal_i = B_(i-1) - B_i
```

For full payoff at the last payment, the level amount is:

```
D_i = 1 / product(g_k, k=1..i)
P = 1 / sum(D_i, i=1..n)
```

For equal `tau`, this reduces to `P=r/[1-(1+r)^(-n)]`, with `r=c*tau`.
At zero coupon it reduces continuously to `P=1/n`; interest is zero and
principal is equal across periods, including stubs. A negative coupon is permitted
when **every** `g_i > 0`; the coupon itself is not silently floored at zero.

The implementation calculates remaining payment annuities backward:

```
V_n = 0
V_(i-1) = (1 + V_i) / g_i
P = 1 / V_0
B_i = V_i / V_0
```

Logarithmic annuity values avoid overflow in a direct compounded-factor product
and avoid forward error accumulation on long amortizing contracts. `ln_1p` retains
accuracy near zero coupon. Principal is the difference of successive normalized
balances. The last remaining annuity is zero, so final principal pays exactly the
remaining numerical balance. No tolerance or fast-math relaxation is introduced.

Positive, finite accrual fractions and representable positive payment amounts are
required. The public shared helper `portfolio_model_core::amortization::
level_payment_principal(coupon, taus)` admits 1..=4096 periods independently of the
term-deck caller. It returns normalized principal repayments and owns validation
of the coupon, accrual factors and numerical domain. Extreme coupon/stub
combinations that imply increasing principal are
rejected as unsupported negative amortization; the existing principal kernel is
not a negative-amortization contract engine. A 64-machine-epsilon comparison
handles rounding at effectively zero principal without admitting an economically
increasing balance.

## Model interpretation and remaining assumptions

The CFPB describes a typical fixed-rate amortizing loan as a constant combined
principal-and-interest payment whose principal share increases over the term,
and a fully amortizing schedule as paying the loan off at the end of its term.
These primary sources inform the payment/payoff invariants:

- [How does paying down a mortgage work?](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/how-does-paying-down-a-mortgage-work-en-1943/)
- [How do mortgage lenders calculate monthly payments?](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/how-do-mortgage-lenders-calculate-monthly-payments-en-1965/)

The generalized irregular-period formula above is derived from the balance
recurrence, rather than asserted as a universal market stub convention. Real
contracts can instead have separately prorated stub payments, original seasoned
payments, cents rounding, interest-only periods, balloons, recasts, or negative
amortization. None of these is inferred by `level_payment`. Currency rounding is
not applied to intermediate normalized cashflows. Market discount factors and
OAS do not enter schedule construction.

This stage does not change credit/default/recovery, prepayment, floating-index
selection, exercise optimization, calendar conventions or accounting treatment.
It does not close issue #15. Rust remains the production calculation runtime;
the schedule helper calls no Python financial backend. Public application
validation and UI integration are separate rollout work.

## Validation

`packages/portfolio-risk-native/tests/amortization.rs` checks:

- Regular quarterly schedules against independent closed-form payments and a
  hand balance recurrence for positive, negative and near-zero coupons.
- Zero-coupon equal payments and exact full-payoff conservation.
- An irregular first stub and unequal calendar quarters using independently
  specified dates, compounded-discount payment calculation and forward balances.
- A 30-year monthly schedule, final residual payoff and constant total payments.
- Independently calculated rejection of a long, high-coupon ACT/365 contract
  whose first period would increase its principal balance.
- Exact preservation of historical `annuity` principal values and grid clamping.
- Explicit rejection of floating/CD/ambiguous-sinking terms, invalid negative-rate
  accrual factors, nonfinite inputs and uncovered new-contract payment dates.

Run `cargo test --manifest-path packages/portfolio-risk-native/Cargo.toml --test
amortization`. Existing term ownership and financial parity suites remain required
before production rollout; these schedule tests alone do not validate end-to-end
OAS, risk, income accounting or observed borrower behavior.

`packages/portfolio-model-core/tests/amortization.rs` additionally tests the public
shared helper's standalone admission/input validation, arbitrary accruals, and
all 4096 supported periods against a closed-form payment for zero, near-zero and
positive coupons. Run `cargo test --manifest-path
packages/portfolio-model-core/Cargo.toml --test amortization`.

# Explicit physical credit-accounting policy

`portfolio_ledger_native::credit_accounting::evaluate` applies one immutable
`credit-accounting-1` day step and returns balanced **journal intents**, closing
state and complete recovery claims. Adapters own account mapping, persistence,
independent journal replay and publication. This integration foundation does not
replace the historical daily credit engine or close the shared/product credit
issues.

The economic transition operator and accounting decisions remain separate.
`credit_operator` transports physical state probability, principal, undrawn
commitment, recognized interest rights and signed basis. The coordinator supplies
actual default-by-origin monetary deltas from its default-origin slots. This layer
does not rerun transitions, apply another survival ratio, infer a coupon allocation,
or convert a default CCF into ordinary scheduled commitment utilization.

## Scope and required identities

The request must specify `measure="physical"`, `monetary_unit="currency_units"`,
an uppercase currency code, position identity, today's `recognition_ordinal` and a
bounded `reporting_end_ordinal`. Pricing and contractual measures are rejected.
The supplied schedule represents modeled physical expected recovery cash; it is
not proof that an observed borrower actually paid. Recovery intents are explicitly
tagged `modeled_physical_recovery_cash`.

Opening live state has three origins in order performing, watch, delinquent:

```
live[3]: {principal, undrawn, accrued_interest, book_adjustment}
allowance: positive contra-asset balance
claims: complete conserved default/recovery states
```

Principal and undrawn amounts are nonnegative actual currency units. Recognized
`accrued_interest` is signed: a positive receivable or a negative deferred/prepaid
right supplied by the actual-date accrual owner. It is not reconstructed from a
whole contractual coupon. `book_adjustment` is signed premium/cost positive or
discount/deferred net fee negative. Principal plus basis cannot be negative.
Allowance is a positive balance; its corresponding debit-positive GL balance is
negative. No opening amount is silently recalculated.

The accounting policy includes immutable `{id,revision}` and explicit choices:

| Policy | Choices and effect |
|---|---|
| Accrued right | Reverse against interest income at default, or transfer until a separately reviewed reversal |
| Signed basis | Transfer until reviewed chargeoff, or recognize in earnings at default |
| Insufficient allowance | Reject a reviewed chargeoff, or recognize its uncovered amount as expense at that reviewed date |
| Cash above remaining booked default principal | Credit allowance, or recognize recovery income |

Claims retain the **full policy configuration plus identity**. Resuming a claim
under a changed treatment, even with a reused policy ID, fails. Configuration
choices are supplied research accounting policies; support for a choice is not a
claim that it is appropriate under a particular accounting standard.

## Economic default and cash-funded default utilization

Each `DefaultInstruction` supplies unique `claim_id`, economic-source identity,
reviewed recovery-schedule identity and three origin deltas:

```
by_origin[3]: {principal, undrawn, contingent_draw,
              accrued_interest, book_adjustment}
economic_principal_loss
complete_recovery_tail: [{payment_ordinal, amount}, ...]
```

Every delta must fit its supplied opening origin balance/right. Signed accrual and
basis allocations must have the same sign as, and not exceed the magnitude of,
their opening rights. Contingent draw must not exceed the explicitly defaulted
undrawn commitment. The entire defaulted undrawn amount leaves live availability;
the unused portion is terminated without a GL asset posting.

Let `D` be defaulted existing principal, `C` contingent draw and `G=D+C` gross
default EAD. Economic principal loss `L` must lie in `[0,G]`; all nominal recovery
tail points must sum to `G-L`. This loss definition excludes accrued interest and
premium/discount. No second LGD loss is applied to those balances.

Contingent utilization emits a cash-funded intent **before** default transfer:

```
Dr LivePrincipal C; Cr Cash C
Dr DefaultPrincipal G; Cr LivePrincipal G
```

The combined live-principal movement is `-D`, not `-G`; the new drawn exposure
enters the default claim after cash funding. CCF/default utilization is therefore
not an unrecorded EAD increase or an ordinary scheduled draw.

The default itself transfers gross principal to a separate default asset. Expected
loss does not automatically reduce that asset, debit allowance, expense a loss or
create an expected-recovery receivable. Accrued and basis rights follow their
explicit policies independently.

## Reviewed allowance and chargeoff timing

`ReviewedChargeoff` supplies review identity, claim identity, today's exact
recognition date, principal amount, signed basis amount and signed accrued-interest
reversal. Future reviews cannot be recognized today. A principal chargeoff is a
supplied accounting decision; it need not equal modeled expected principal loss.

With transferred basis, the reviewed net principal/basis chargeoff is:

```
W = reviewed_principal + reviewed_signed_basis
covered = min(W, available_allowance)
uncovered = W - covered
```

`W` must be nonnegative. The intent credits default principal and signed basis,
debits allowance for the covered amount and, only under the explicit shortfall
policy, debits credit-loss expense for the uncovered amount. Removing a negative
discount/deferred fee reduces net chargeoff; removing a positive premium increases
it. Reviewed accrued-interest reversal separately debits interest income and
credits its default accrued-right account, including the appropriate reversed
sign for a negative recognized right. It is not included in principal LGD or the
principal allowance calculation.

`ReviewedAllowance` has a review identity, today's date, explicit `target_amount`
and `before_credit` or `after_credit` phase. The target changes allowance through
credit-loss expense/release. A closing review cannot retroactively fund an earlier
chargeoff under the reject-shortfall policy. No allowance target is inferred from
PD, LGD, expected economic loss, remaining balance or a scenario.

Daily event order is deterministic:

1. Optional reviewed allowance target before credit.
2. Explicit cash-funded contingent draws, economic default transfer and independent
   accrual/basis policy intents, in supplied default order.
3. Today's reviewed chargeoffs/reversals, in supplied review order.
4. Due cash from supplied reviewed modeled-physical recovery schedules.
5. Optional reviewed allowance target after credit.

## Recovery claims and horizon treatment

An opening claim retains initial gross principal, principal-only economic loss,
initial accrual/basis, outstanding book balances, cumulative reviewed removals,
cumulative recovery cash and the full uncollected nominal recovery tail. Validation
independently enforces:

```
initial_principal = outstanding_principal + principal_charged_off
                    + recovery_applied_to_principal
initial_accrued = outstanding_accrued + accrued_reversed
initial_basis = outstanding_basis + basis_recognized
initial_principal - economic_principal_loss = recovery_cash_collected
                                             + remaining_recovery_tail
```

Due recovery cash first reduces remaining booked default principal. Excess cash
then follows the explicit allowance/income choice. No previously removed principal
is rebooked simply because a future recovery is expected. Fully charged-off loans
retain their economic recovery tails even when booked principal is zero.

If reviewed chargeoff differs from expected loss, the accounting principal can
remain after the last modeled recovery; it remains visible as an unresolved booked
default asset requiring further review. Basis/accrued balances can similarly remain
until their supplied recognition decisions. Nothing is silently cleared to make
the recovery schedule appear complete.

Same-day zero-lag recoveries execute after today's chargeoffs. Points after the
reporting end stay in `closing.claims[].remaining_recoveries` and contribute to
`recovery_tail_after_reporting`. No horizon truncation or terminal-date compression
is permitted. Passing a day that leaves unprocessed past-due schedule points in
opening claims fails rather than silently dropping cash. Resuming with today's
due points is supported; replay ownership must prevent applying the same state
twice.

## Balanced intents and validation

Posting amounts are debit-positive. The typed `AccountCode` also exposes stable
`numeric_code()` values for generic adapter mapping: cash, live/default principal,
live/default accrued right, live/default basis, allowance, interest income,
credit-loss expense, basis-recognition expense and recovery income. Adapters must
not treat intent account codes as a hardcoded production chart of accounts.

Every intent retains policy/source identity and position/claim identity. Inputs
are cloned; failure returns no result and never mutates caller opening state.
Final claims are checked against the original economic anchors. Numerical guards
allow f64 rounding only; existing engine/ledger tolerances are unchanged.

Standalone admission is at most 62000 opening-plus-new claims, 256 new default
events, 4096 reviewed chargeoffs and 32 points per complete recovery tail. Dates and
tails admit at most 36600 days; monetary components and reported totals admit
finite magnitudes up to `1e15` actual currency units. Identity fields admit at most
1024 control-free bytes each and 32 MiB aggregate metadata. These component limits
do not assert an aggregate RSS cap or regulatory exposure/chargeoff limits.

Ten independent native fixtures cover covered/uncovered allowance, rejected and
explicitly funded shortfalls, deferred reviews, full writeoff then recovery,
contingent funding before default, accrued reversal, signed premium/discount,
negative prepaid rights, closing allowance targets, same/final-day recoveries,
zero-credit exact state identity and invalid measures/units/tails/rights/policies.
They check hand-computed balanced postings and closing states. Run:

```
cargo test --manifest-path packages/portfolio-ledger-native/Cargo.toml --test credit_accounting
```

## Primary accounting guidance and limits

The [OCC Bank Accounting Advisory Series, August 2026](https://www.occ.treas.gov/publications-and-resources/publications/banker-education/files/pub-bank-accounting-advisory-series.pdf)
provides relevant distinctions: topic 2B separates accrued-interest reversal from
principal chargeoff decisions; topic 2D question 11 discusses deferred fees and
cost basis; topic 2F treats recovery recognition separately from hoped-for
collections and describes recoveries through ACL after chargeoff. These examples
informed the explicit separation and conservative default policy boundaries.

The [OCC allowance resources](https://www.occ.treas.gov/topics/supervision-and-examination/bank-operations/accounting/allowance-for-credit-losses/index-allowances-for-credit-losses.html)
identify allowance as a valuation account and link its measurement, documentation
and review guidance. This module executes supplied reviewed amounts; it does not
implement CECL, IFRS 9, regulatory chargeoff rules, collateral-dependent measurement,
off-balance allowance, return-to-accrual rules, tax, OREO, acquired-loan accounting
or observed borrower settlement verification.

Full native integration still requires coupled transition/accrual ownership,
product/default/prepayment replay, adapter state mapping, independent persisted
journal verification, production immutable publication, fixed base OAS/shared CRN
for pricing and the remaining issue acceptance criteria.
