# Native exact event-time credit paths

`portfolio_model_core::credit_path::evaluate(&CreditPathRequest)` implements `credit-path-1`. It samples the same performing/watch/delinquent/default/prepaid continuous-time state family as the deterministic operator. It retains migrations, cures, default origin, competing exits, earned interest, realized exposure, supplied contractual boundaries and full recovery tails. It does not turn the expected-exposure ledger into a stochastic ledger automatically. Legacy requests retain their existing model selection and economics.

## Contract and units

Every request declares `measure` (`physical` or `pricing`), `monetary_unit`, immutable source/revision/model policy IDs, an `origin_time` ordinal plus seconds-of-day, the complete piecewise supplied path, and path IDs/unique numerical CRN keys. The engine preserves the measure; it does not convert physical estimates into pricing hazards. Money is the actual amount of a single realized account. There is no survival/probability multiplier in the monetary state and no second default haircut. The caller aggregates paths and supplies any sampling weights outside this single-account contract.

Times are elapsed ACT/365 years from `origin_time`: one year is exactly 31,536,000 elapsed seconds. Exact event offsets remain `f64` and are not rounded to days or 30-day months. The origin timestamp is retained. Negative interest receivables/coupon accrual and signed carrying premiums/discounts are supported. Principal and undrawn commitment are nonnegative. Principal, undrawn, absolute accrued interest and absolute basis together are bounded by the shared 1e15 currency-amount limit per path state; closing aggregate counters and each origin's earned interest have that limit too. No currency conversion or implicit thousands multiplier occurs.

Each interval has a strictly increasing `end_year`, a 3 by 5 matrix of annual **continuous intensities**, signed annual simple `accrual_rates`, and per-live-origin LGD, CCF, interest recovery fraction, and a complete recovery lag/weight distribution. Diagonal hazards must be exactly zero; outgoing intensities sum to at most 100/year. LGD/CCF/recovery fractions lie in [0,1]. Interval coefficients are frozen over that interval. They are supplied assumptions unless independently supported and reviewed; annual cumulative PDs are not interpreted as intensities.

## Event algorithm and shared draws

For current live state i, let lambda_i = sum_j q_ij. Draw `E = -ln(U_wait)` and carry its unused internal waiting time across every term and monetary boundary. Consume `lambda_i * elapsed_years`; a jump occurs at the exact first time the accumulated intensity reaches E. Select its destination by `U_destination * lambda_i` and ordered cumulative destination intensities. A new pair is obtained after a jump; zero-intensity stretches consume no internal time. This handles default/prepay as mutually exclusive competing events and permits multiple migrations/cures before either absorbing exit. At equal times, credit transitions use the ending interval first, then contractual boundaries execute in supplied stable order, then the new interval applies. Events belong to the ending interval. Floating evaluation of a mathematically bounded jump time is limited to that interval endpoint; probabilities and hazards are never clipped or normalized.

The method is the direct event-time sampling construction applied to piecewise intensities. [Anderson's primary paper on integrated internal times](https://web.math.wisc.edu/~dfanderson/papers/AndNRM.pdf) explains why unused internal time can be retained when intensities change. [Vestergaard and Génois's temporal Gillespie paper](https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pcbi.1004579) develops total-intensity timing for time-varying networks. Their mathematical methods inform this implementation; no biochemical or network calibration is imported into credit.

Two explicit draw owners are supported:

- `supplied`: exact key coverage, finite open-(0,1) waiting/destination pairs, versioned stream identity. Exhaustion is an error; no fallback occurs. Unused trailing pairs are allowed. A partially consumed final waiting pair counts in `random_pairs_used`.
- `counter_splitmix64_v1`: caller seed and stream identity, stable wrapping-u64 counter generation keyed by path key and zero-based jump index. The constants and mix sequence in `credit_path.rs` are the versioned reproducibility definition. Waiting and destination lanes use separate domains. A 52-bit midpoint map makes both uniforms strictly interior. The stream is noncryptographic and has no claim of optimal statistical coupling or cryptographic randomness. Stream labels identify the caller's run; changing labels without changing the seed does not change numeric draws.

Reordering accounts, adding another account, splitting an unchanged interval, or changing a path label preserves another path's numerical stream when its seed/key remain fixed. Scenario comparisons use the same key/seed or supplied pairs; term edits retain the residual internal wait. Different realized migrations can change later event indices. CRN does not promise identical destinations across scenario coefficients or minimum-variance competing-channel coupling. Cross-platform transcendental functions may produce last-bit differences; byte-for-byte determinism is tested within the same runtime.

## Monetary conservation and boundaries

During a live sojourn, `earned_interest = principal * origin_accrual_rate * elapsed_years` adds to signed accrued rights. The result retains total earned interest and its actual live-origin allocation. A cure changes the state/rate prospectively; previously earned or nonaccruing rights persist.

At default from origin i, contingent funded draw is `undrawn * CCF_i`, EAD is current principal plus that draw, and the funding cash is negative. Undrawn is canceled. Economic principal loss is `EAD * LGD_i`. For each complete recovery weight w at exact default time plus lag, principal recovery is `EAD * (1-LGD_i) * w` and interest recovery is `accrued_interest * interest_recovery_fraction_i * w`. All tail entries are returned even after the report horizon. Only report-horizon recoveries reduce closing claims and enter report cash. Default basis remains a signed right requiring a separate reviewed accounting policy; economic loss is not an allowance or a write-off instruction. Accrual stops at default. Claim amounts and source origin are retained even when the report ends before recovery.

At prepay, principal and signed accrued interest are settled once, signed book adjustment is recognized separately, and undrawn is canceled. A repayment boundary settles supplied state-dependent fractions of actual principal/interest, recognizes the same principal fraction of basis, and cancels the specified commitment fraction. A draw boundary funds a supplied fraction of actual remaining undrawn. `maturity` settles actual remaining principal/interest, recognizes basis, cancels commitment and returns a distinct `matured` outcome. Maturity is never recorded as prepayment. Default/prepaid/matured accounts no longer receive loan boundaries; default recovery rights continue independently.

The general principal cash check per path is opening principal plus funded draws equals principal repayments/prepayments/maturity cash, in-horizon principal recoveries, and closing live/default principal. Economic loss remains part of the gross default claim until a separate accounting owner applies explicit charge-off policy. Interest opening plus realized earned interest equals interest settlements/recoveries plus closing rights. Opening signed basis equals recognized basis plus remaining basis. The module emits economic flows and rights, not balanced GL, taxes, CECL/IFRS9 allowances or accounting compliance claims.

## Bounds and evidence

Requests admit 1..10,000 paths, 1..4,096 intervals, at most 4,096 ordered boundaries, 32 strictly increasing recovery lags per interval/origin, horizon <=100 years and lag <=100 years. Complete tail weights sum to one within 1e-12 and cannot exceed one. Maximum jumps per path is explicit; path count times the maximum is <=250,000. Retained jump/boundary events are <=250,000, supplied pairs <=260,000, and actual interval/boundary/recovery work <=2,000,000 units. Labels contain 1..256 control-free bytes. Violations return errors with no partial accepted result. These are component admission limits, not an aggregate RSS or combined portfolio-scale claim.

Independent fixtures use supplied uniforms with hand-computed integrated hazard, two-stage waiting time, actual-origin cure occupation, negative coupons, contingent draw and recovery tails. Tests cover semigroup-style interval refinement, counter stream account ordering, reproducibility, missing uniforms, schema/domain rejection and maturity separation. [The synthetic example](../../examples/models/credit-path-1.json) defaults at year 0.3, earns 3 interest, funds 10, and retains recovery 66 principal plus 3 interest at year 2.3 beyond its one-year horizon.

Remaining #11 gates include empirical portfolio validation, wider observed severity/term models where justified, adoption by every product/scenario graph and daily stochastic accounting publication, correlated borrower/common drivers, Monte Carlo uncertainty and reviewed accounting policy. This component does not close those gates or replace the legacy model implicitly.

# Actual daily credit replay

`analytics.credit_ledger.run_credit_ledger` transports this explicit route and publishes
`credit-balance-partitions-1` after independent persisted verification. Python's
`credit_verification` uses SciPy matrix exponentials, explicit accounting-policy
replay, complete claim tails, once-only lineage and original posting order. It
checks all source states, journal entries, daily balances, closing trial balance
and summary. It is a publication gate, not a selectable financial execution backend.

The durable API exposes `POST /balance-stress/credit` with `expected_revision`,
`specification` and `large_book`; backend selection is absent. Native validation
enforces standard/large limits. Queued executable and validation-library hashes,
source identity, worker lease, attempt token and cancellation fence publication.
The raw input is retained as a storage-managed object reference and remains rooted
through restart and garbage collection. The partitioned panel supports credit
state/claim/lineage paging and reopening. It labels regulatory limits unevaluated:
this route does not infer capital policies from credit balances.

`credit-ledger-1` is an explicit native loan-credit execution route exposed by `portfolio-balance`. It compiles raw `balance-stress-2` accounts and loan opening anchors, complete run-specific physical credit contracts, actual dated boundaries and reviewed allowance/chargeoff decisions. It streams actual journals and independently constructed credit subledgers. The existing `dated-ledger-1` and legacy protocol-2 routes retain their existing economics and execution. The [synthetic example](../../examples/models/credit-ledger-1.json) demonstrates the exact wire schema; it is not empirical evidence.

The Rust API is `CompiledCreditReplay::compile_with_limits(request, max_positions, max_work)`, `normalized_spec()`, `admitted_work()` and `credit_replay::run(compiled, writer)`. `compile(request)` uses the explicit maximum 60,000-position/90-million-work tier. Callers cannot raise those limits. The ordinary API tier must pass its 2,000-position/3-million-work limits through the native compiler. There is a separate maximum of 62,000 run-position contracts across the supplied scenario grid. Thus a 60,000-position baseline plus a complete 60,000-position stress run exceeds this route's current contract tier. The module does not assert combined 60,000-position graph/solver/ledger scenario acceptance or aggregate process RSS bounds.

Requests require `schema`, `monetary_unit="currency_units"`, `as_of_ordinal`, `specification` and `runs`. Each run declares unique `run_id`, `scenario_id`, `severity` and complete `positions`. Each position declares `account_id`, `contract`, `opening`, `boundaries` and `reviews`. Baseline severity one, every named scenario severity one and every requested reverse severity must be supplied exactly; no interpolation or multiplication of hazards by scenario severity occurs. Duplicate severities collapse only when their economic identity is identical, including positive/negative zero. All native built-in credit coefficients are compiled once per position/run.

Opening live monetary arrays plus outstanding recovery-claim assets reconcile to the normalized position's principal, book adjustment and accrued-interest anchors. Allowance and live undrawn reconcile separately. Account opening equity is independently reconciled by native specification admission; no balancing plug is inferred. Claims retain unique position namespaces, economic and reviewed-policy identities and complete dated tails. The route rejects overlapping legacy default, migration, draw, runoff, floating repricing, marks, collateral, legacy cashflow/policy ownership and account fee/cost/tax/dividend policies. Only owned loan positions are admitted in this schema. Regulatory proxies, mixed funding books and capital/FTP reports require their separate integrated routes.

Every interval is exactly one actual day under ACT/365. The [joint state coordinator](credit-state.md) first transports live absolute probability and independently weighted money, including continuous earned-interest occupation, then emits reviewed default, recovery and accounting intents. Economic prepay settles only its own transported allocation. The replay then executes the supplied boundary events in stable input order. This documented closing-boundary approximation does not assign intra-day loan cash settlement times. Source and policy identities remain attached to every interval and boundary. Each credit policy review has its exact native recognition date, with allowance review before/after credit defined by `credit_accounting`.

Boundary actions are explicitly tagged objects:

- `repayment` declares three `principal_fraction`, `accrued_fraction` and `cancel_undrawn_fraction` values. Each is finite in 0..1 and applies to that state's surviving actual exposure. Book basis retires in the principal fraction, with signed recognition in earnings. The amount is not computed from opening scheduled notional and is not survival-scaled again. Principal can fully retire while accrued rights remain until a later settlement event.
- `draw` declares three nonnegative `amount_by_state` values. Each must fit its current surviving undrawn commitment. Cash funds once, principal increases and undrawn falls; the draw earns from the next interval. Default-contingent CCF draws remain separate and occur through credit accounting.
- `maturity` settles all live principal, signed accrued rights and signed basis and cancels live undrawn. It moves live probability to a separate `matured_probability` diagnostic. It does not increment prepaid probability, dispose of default claims or erase recovery tails. Every normalized in-report `maturity_day` anchor requires exactly one explicit Maturity boundary on that actual date. Missing, duplicate or mismatched boundaries fail native compilation; no reviewed term-modification override is admitted by this schema. Out-of-report maturity retains principal, rights and claims without inventing a payment. No legacy synthetic maturity is applied to these owners.

This is a supplied boundary model. Fractional repayments do not by themselves constitute a fitted consumer minimum-payment, amortization or utilization model. Full recovery of a previously charged-off default with negative retained book discount may require an explicit reviewed basis recognition; omitting that review can violate nonnegative carrying-value admission. The runner fails rather than infer a recognition policy.

Protocol 4 outputs bounded newline-delimited `{table, rows}` batches with at most 1,024 retained rows across tables, followed by `{complete:true, protocol:4}` only on success. Journal rows are explicit records rather than the protocol-2/3 dictionary-column representation. The transport must opt into this distinction; the old journal representation is unchanged. Transaction numbers are global, monotonically increasing and balanced per account/run. Cash has instrument `@cash`, opening equity `@equity`, live balances retain position IDs, and default assets retain claim IDs.

GL labels are `cash`, `asset_principal`, `credit_default_principal`, `accrued_interest`, `credit_default_accrued_interest`, `book_adjustment`, `credit_default_book_adjustment`, `allowance`, `interest_income`, `credit_loss_expense`, `basis_recognition_expense`, `recovery_income` and `equity_opening`. Signed journal values are debit-positive. Allowance and opening equity have credit balances; revenues have credit balances, expenses debit balances. Daily source assets equal live principal/basis/accrual plus retained claim principal/basis/accrual plus cash minus allowance. Daily equity equals opening equity minus the signed earnings GL balance. Both source-to-GL and asset-to-equity reconciliations gate successful execution.

Output tables retain these contracts:

| Table | Identity and financial contents |
| --- | --- |
| `journal` | transaction_number, run_id, scenario, severity, day, ordinal, account, event, gl_account, instrument_id, value |
| `credit_states` | run/day/account/position, contract_id/revision, absolute probability[7], matured_probability, live_principal/undrawn/accrued_interest/book_adjustment[3], allowance, default principal/accrued/basis totals |
| `credit_claims` | run/day/account/position/claim identity, economic source/revision, recovery review/revision, default ordinal, initial principal/loss, outstanding principal/accrued/basis, charged-off principal, collected/applied recovery cash, remaining recovery cash and tail after reporting |
| `credit_lineage` | run/day/account/position/event identity, source/revision, policy/revision, optional claim ID, earned interest, economic principal loss, contingent draw cash, prepay cash, recovery cash |
| `daily_balance` | run/day/account/entity/currency, cash, assets, equity, allowance, reconciliation_error |
| `trial_balance` | run/account/gl_account/instrument_id, final signed balance |
| `summary` | run/account, final cash/assets/equity and maximum reconciliation error |

The shared normalized specification retains its 30..1,080-day horizon and opening carrying-value constraints. Amounts reuse the 1e15 currency-unit bound. The replay admits at most one million boundary/review dates, shared bounded identity metadata and at most 62,000 retained recovery claims per run. Base work counts position-days, account-days and supplied events; actual retained-claim scans consume the same supplied work budget during execution. Cancellation/deadline checkpoints run between compilation batches, days, position batches and boundary batches. Failed writes, invalid dynamic draws, exhausted work, incompatible reviews and cancellation emit no final completion; immutable publication must reject every such partial stream.

Independent native tests hand-calculate competing exit flux, stopped coupon accrual, cash-funded EAD, signed basis recognition and maturity/recovery balances; cure timing; actual surviving repayment; delayed signed interest settlement after principal retirement; dated reviewed provision/chargeoff; scenario/reverse coverage; ownership/anchor admission and failed-completion behavior. Legacy dated tests run alongside the new tests. Python persisted-journal and credit-state economic verification, public durable API/UI adoption, complete scale acceptance and empirical calibration remain separate acceptance gates. Numerical tests and this synthetic example make no accounting-compliance or empirical-accuracy claim.

Primary modeling references and numeric equations are documented in [credit state](credit-state.md), [credit operator](credit-operator.md) and [credit accounting](credit-accounting.md). The supplied transition, LGD and CCF assumptions must retain calibration source/training/holdout evidence before empirical release.
# Native observed-panel credit calibration

`portfolio_model_core::credit_snapshot_calibration::fit(&SnapshotCalibrationRequest)` implements `credit-snapshot-calibration-1`. It estimates a declared bounded CTMC from individual interval-censored state snapshots using endpoint transition probabilities. It complements `observed-credit-calibration-1`, which requires exact transition times and exposure spells. Neither contract invents event times from monthly tapes. Python adapters transport raw observations and format results; likelihood, optimization, transition math and diagnostics execute in Rust.

## Observation and identity contract

Each snapshot supplies unique record/account/raw-source IDs, exact observation timestamps, observed origin/end states, named covariates frozen over the interval and a declared term level. Timestamps are ordinal dates plus seconds-of-day and use ACT/365 elapsed seconds. Intervals are within study windows and last (0,1] years. For an account, intervals are contiguous, nonoverlapping and endpoint states match. States are assumed observed without misclassification; observation schedules, entry and end of observation are assumed noninformative conditional on the supplied model. Missing covariates, unknown states/term levels, gaps and informative observation mechanisms are unsupported and require a separately declared model. A final known live snapshot contributes its endpoint likelihood without inventing subsequent exposure.

Mandatory request identities include source/revision, population/model policy, distinct training/holdout split IDs and `data_kind` (`observed` or `synthetic`). Ordinal windows obey `train_start < train_end < holdout_end`; the full study is <=100 years. All monetary outcome fields share mandatory `monetary_unit`; the unit is retained with no conversion or implicit multiplier. Individual record/account/source/partition provenance is returned. Marking a request observed is a caller declaration, not automatic evidence authentication.

Intervals ending exactly at `train_end` belong to training; intervals starting exactly there belong to holdout. An interval crossing the split has no observed boundary state and is rejected or excluded with its ID/diagnostic, according to explicit policy. It is not divided into invented state spells. Hidden-state propagation through a chronological split is a different model contract and is not silently inferred. The optimizer and observed-information calculation receive training cases only. Holdout changes affect diagnostics and never parameter search, active bounds or information.

## Declared hazard family and likelihood

Each performing/watch/delinquent row is either an explicit fixed row carrying assumption ID/rationale or a list of enabled log-linear edges. Omitted edges are declared structural zeros; diagonals are forbidden. For enabled edge i->j:

`q_ij(x,k) = exp(intercept_ij + sum_r beta_ijr*x_r + term_effect_ijk)`.

Term level 0 is the reference with exactly zero effect. The caller provides initial/lower/upper coefficients, named covariates and term levels; the engine does not choose drivers, center observations using holdout, or synthesize macro series. Candidate outgoing intensities must sum to <=100/year; excessive rows are infeasible, never capped. Covariates are in [-10,10], coefficients in [-20,20], and all supplied bounds are explicit. A log-linear origin with no observed training-start intervals is rejected and requires an explicit supplied fixed row. This conservative admission rule also avoids silently labeling evidence-free row coefficients as observed estimates.

For an interval with generator Q and elapsed time dt, likelihood contribution is `P_ij(dt)` where `P=exp(Q*dt)`. Default probability sums the three internal default-origin columns of the shared seven-state operator; prepay uses its separate absorbing column. Thus observed performing->performing includes unobserved migrations and cures, and observed performing->default integrates every compatible latent path. The native objective sums `-log(P_ij)` over training records, conditional on each observed starting state. This is not transition-count/exposure MLE, nor an annual cumulative-PD-to-hazard shortcut. Identical interval/covariate/term cases are grouped with endpoint counts as sufficient numerical work reduction, preserving observation provenance separately.

[Jackson's primary panel-model paper](https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v038i08) establishes the distinction between observed endpoints and unknown intermediate paths. [The author's model documentation](https://chjackson.github.io/msm/reference/msm.html) distinguishes panel observations from exact transitions and describes log-linear, piecewise covariate intensities. Those principles motivate this bounded schema; misclassified states, unknown terminal state, arbitrary mid-interval coefficient switches and general hidden-state models are not implemented here.

## Optimizer, convergence and identifiability

The deterministic native optimizer explores negative/positive coordinate directions within supplied coefficient bounds, accepts objective improvements exceeding the declared tolerance, and halves an unsuccessful mesh until the declared final mesh. It returns `coordinate_mesh_converged` only after a complete unsuccessful sweep at that mesh; interrupted/budget-limited sweeps return `search_budget_exhausted`. No derivatives, Python callbacks, external solver or randomness enter the search. `parameters` contains final estimates with stable origin/edge/covariate/term names; `declared_rows` retains original supplied templates and initial values. The latter must not be mistaken for fitted coefficients.

Coordinate-mesh convergence is a local numerical stopping criterion, not a proof of a unique/global statistical optimum. [Torczon's primary pattern-search paper](https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/S1052623493250780) is background on direct-search methods; this finite, constrained implementation does not claim all of that paper's theoretical convergence conditions. Independent starts, competing plausible model specifications and portfolio validation remain review duties. Coefficients near supplied bounds are listed and prevent adoption eligibility. A structural zero/no-event origin should use a reviewed explicit policy rather than a positive log-hazard forced against an arbitrary lower bound.

For an interior converged candidate, central training-objective differences with coefficient step 1e-3 construct the observed-information matrix. A bounded symmetric Jacobi decomposition reports its eigenvalues. `information_rank` counts positive eigenvalues exceeding `1e-5 * max(1,max_abs_eigenvalue)`. Missing information, negative/near-zero curvature or collinear/unobserved covariate effects prevent full rank. This finite-difference rank is a numerical identifiability diagnostic, not a mathematical proof, a confidence interval, or uncertainty calibration. No confidence interval is invented from an ill-conditioned inverse.

`adoption_eligible` requires observed caller data, mesh convergence, no active coefficient bounds and full numerical information rank. Synthetic requests always return false. Eligibility is a numerical admission result requiring model review, not empirical accuracy certification, accounting-policy approval or automatic activation. Missing observed bank histories keeps empirical issue gates open. Fixed supplied rows retain their assumption tags even when other origins are observed fits. All outputs declare `physical` measure; no observed-frequency fit is relabeled as a pricing measure or converted to it.

Holdout reports log likelihood, observed start/endpoint counts, predicted endpoint counts, impossible intervals, and rows outside the admitted hazard domain. Impossible events have null overall log likelihood, not an arbitrary epsilon probability. Domain-rejected cases are counted; their predictions are absent from numeric sums rather than fabricated. Holdout evaluation is separate from model selection and calibration. The diagnostics do not implement full censoring-adjusted calibration curves, bootstrap parameter uncertainty, subgroup fairness or causal driver effects.

## Observed severity and exposure outcomes

`SnapshotCalibrationResult::project_hazards(covariates, term_level)` evaluates final named coefficients in Rust, validates shape/identity/bounds and rejects out-of-domain projected rows. It is available for explicitly synthetic diagnostics too. It does not activate a model, authenticate observation provenance or imply that an ineligible estimate passed empirical review. Consumers must inspect the gates and retain model/source identities before any separately reviewed adoption.

Optional default outcomes supply unique account/outcome/raw-source IDs, exactly observed last live default origin, default timestamp, immediately-before-default drawn/undrawn, realized principal EAD, complete dated nominal principal recoveries, and an explicit complete resolution or right-censor timestamp. EAD must be between drawn and drawn+undrawn. Interest, costs, discounts, principal modification and product transformation are not silently inserted into these principal-only fields. An account has at most one absorbing default outcome in this study; repeated cured defaults need a richer explicit default-state contract.

Resolved training defaults enter training severity only when default **and full resolution** occur by train end. A training default resolved later is excluded with a distinct provenance reason, preventing future recovery leakage into historical training. Defaults strictly after the split with complete resolution by holdout end enter holdout diagnostics. Right-censored recovery processes require explicit reject or exclude-with-diagnostics policy; no unresolved remainder is inferred to be zero. Complete rows return pooled and exact-default-origin versions of:

`realized LGD ratio = sum(EAD - nominal recovered principal) / sum(EAD)`;

`realized CCF ratio = sum(EAD - immediately-before-default drawn) / sum(immediately-before-default undrawn)`.

Zero denominators return null. These are explicitly EAD-weighted/undrawn-weighted complete-case realized ratios, not regulatory long-run default-weighted LGD, a discounted workout estimate, a covariate severity regression or a downturn calibration. [The Basel Committee's working paper on validation](https://www.bis.org/publ/bcbs_wp14.pdf) discusses incomplete workouts and inconsistent recovery data; excluding unresolved cases can bias the remaining sample. [The current BIS credit-risk guidance](https://www.bis.org/committees/bcbs/basel-consolidated-guidelines/module/cri/30) distinguishes observed losses from regulatory parameters and economic recovery costs/discounting. The module exposes exclusions and raw IDs, and makes no Basel/CECL/IFRS9 compliance claim. Portfolio-representative censoring treatment, observed recovery timing/survival fits and justified richer EAD/LGD driver models remain separate empirical gates.

## Limits and independent evidence

At most 20,000 snapshot records, 20,000 default outcomes, four covariates, four term levels, twelve free parameters, and 512 distinct interval/covariate/term groups per split are admitted. Each default has <=4,096 recovery entries; aggregate recovery entries <=200,000. Monetary states/totals are <=1e15 and metadata <=32 MiB, with control-free 1..256-byte labels. Search evaluations are 1..2,000; total likelihood/diagnostic evaluations <=2,400, including information differences. Uniformization work is conservatively charged as 128 terms times bounded chunks for each group/evaluation and limited to 10,000,000. Group bounds and actual work checks remain component limits, not an aggregate memory or 60,000-account fitting acceptance claim. Failures produce no partial accepted result.

Independent fixtures prove a one-edge panel MLE `q=-ln(3/4)` for three survivors and one default in a one-year interval; separate covariate and term effects; performing/watch cure endpoint probabilities `2/3 + exp(-3)/3`; train-end inclusion; unchanged parameters/information when only holdout endpoints change; explicit split/censor exclusions; null unsupported severity denominators; and singular/boundary/nonconverged rejection gates. [The small synthetic JSON example](../../examples/models/credit-snapshot-calibration-1.json) is a numerical demonstration with no empirical accuracy claim. Native product/graph/daily adoption, observed representative datasets, external benchmark estimates, independent uncertainty/holdout review and durable publication remain necessary before #11 is considered complete.

# Joint native credit intervals

`portfolio-ledger-native::credit_state` compiles a `credit-state-1` contract and advances immutable `credit-state-opening-1` state with `CompiledCreditState::advance`. Contracts require physical measure, an explicit currency, `currency_units`, source/revision identities, reviewed accounting policy and complete recovery tails. A compiled operator is reusable; coefficients cannot be deserialized or mutated. Opening states retain contract identity and last actual ordinal. Repeating an already recognized date fails contiguous-interval admission.

The interval uses actual elapsed days divided by 365, independently of reporting months. Hazards have inverse-year units; state coupons are signed simple annual rates. The three live states are performing, watch and delinquent; default is retained by immediate exit origin and prepaid is absorbing. The shared operator permits migrations, cures and multiple jumps during an interval. Set the delinquent coupon to zero for nonaccrual; accrued rights already owned by the position continue to transport. A cure starts new earnings only for the time spent in an accruing state.

Probability is absolute population mass, with live/default/prepaid entries totaling at most one. Monetary principal, undrawn commitments, accrued rights and book adjustments are independently weighted aggregate currency amounts. They are never multiplied by population survival a second time. Matured or disposed population can be removed externally, leaving probability submass; maturity is not an economic prepayment.

For row vectors of live principal `B` and accrued rights `A`, the shared operator applies `B'=BQ` and `A'=AQ+BR`, where `Q` is the CTMC generator and `R` is diagonal signed coupon accrual. Earned income is calculated directly from the reward coefficients, avoiding subtraction of two large opening/closing accrued balances. Book adjustment and undrawn commitments use transition transport without invented fee amortization or ordinary draws.

After transport, each default-origin monetary bucket is used as the exact synthetic opening for `credit_accounting`. Separately conserved surviving live balances are merged into accounting's zero-live closing. This permits a surviving accrued right and default right in the same origin to have opposite signs after migration. Netting those rights before allocating default would reject valid signed economics. Origin transfers therefore also work when an origin had no opening exposure. Principal, undrawn, basis, accrued-plus-earned and probability conservation are checked independently; generated postings must reconcile live principal, accrued and basis movements.

Gross default EAD by origin is `D + CCF U`, where `D` and `U` are already transported aggregate default principal and undrawn exposure. The contingent draw funds cash once, increases gross default principal, and cancels all defaulted undrawn commitments. Principal-only economic loss is `LGD EAD`. The complete recovery amount is `EAD - loss`, distributed using supplied strictly dated lag weights. Default and recovery lags are recognized from the interval's closing day. This remains an explicit boundary-time approximation; it does not assign stochastic intra-day cash settlement times.

Default principal transfers to its separate asset account. Economic loss does not automatically create a provision, allowance, chargeoff or recovery receivable. Allowance targets and chargeoffs require the explicit dated reviews defined by `credit_accounting`; default accrued reversal and basis recognition follow its reviewed policy. Existing claims and full recovery tails are retained through principal maturity. Intervals crossing an unsettled recovery date must be split, so no scheduled recovery silently disappears. Daily use with `interval_days=1` naturally resolves every date.

Economic prepayment settles its transported principal and signed accrued right in cash, recognizes transported signed basis in earnings and cancels the prepaid undrawn allocation. This contract's prepayment policy is full settlement of those rights. It does not represent fees, retained contractual accrued rights or partial debt forgiveness; a producer requiring those economics must supply a distinct explicit boundary policy. Negative coupons and cash payable rights are admitted rather than clipped.

Bounds: outgoing row hazards and signed coupon magnitudes reuse the shared operator's 100/year limits. Intervals admit 1..36,500 actual days; daily integration uses one day. Each origin has at most 32 recovery points, lags at most 36,600 days and weights summing to one within eight machine epsilons. LGD and CCF are finite fractions in 0..1. Empty tails require LGD one. Currency amounts reuse the 1e15 limit; claims and reviews reuse accounting's 62,000 and 4,096 limits. Identity fields admit at most 256 UTF-8 bytes, claim namespaces 128, control characters are rejected, and metadata reuses the shared 32 MiB bound. These component limits are not an aggregate process memory guarantee.

Independent tests use analytic competing default/prepay flux and earned-interest integrals, a performing-to-watch-to-default chain, opposing signed migrated rights, zero-credit mass/money independence, exact retained absorbed probability, multi-day recovery claims, explicit allowance/chargeoff reviews and failed-input immutability. They validate numerical and accounting mechanics, not empirical calibration accuracy or accounting compliance. The native production replay and independent persisted-journal verification must separately prove adoption before issue #11/#12 acceptance.

Model references: the Federal Reserve's [2025 supervisory model descriptions](https://www.federalreserve.gov/publications/2025-june-supervisory-stress-test-methodology-descriptions-supervisory-models.htm) describe credit-state transitions and EAD including expected draws; its [January 2026 detailed credit documentation](https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/files/credit-risk-models.pdf) distinguishes model default thresholds and projected losses. These references motivate separate transition, EAD and severity components; they do not calibrate these supplied coefficients. The shared [credit operator](credit-operator.md) documents the block-exponential reward equations and primary numerical sources. [Reviewed credit accounting](credit-accounting.md) documents the distinct recognition and chargeoff policies.

# Next stage: dated schedules and native credit in daily replay

Version 0.29.7 implements the explicitly selected loan-only
[joint credit state](credit-state.md) and [credit replay](credit-replay.md) route,
with independent persisted source/accounting checks and durable API/UI publication.
It also connects verified credit closing journals to native capital preparation.
The mixed product/graph/candidate adoption and complete scale gates below remain
required; component execution is not their completion.

Current follow-through adds [realized event-time credit](credit-path-ledger.md),
[native consumer graph capture](graph-dated-ledger.md) and
[frozen covariate-driver replay](driven-credit-ledger.md). The modeled routes
retain raw model inputs, prepared economic sources and independent source/posting
verification through durable API publication. Consumer capture admits explicitly
reviewed performing par-note simple interest; the driver route is physical,
loan-only and preserves analytical versus adoption eligibility. These boundaries
do not replace the remaining mixed product, yield, candidate and scale gates.

This design preserves the full scopes of issues #11, #12 and the dependent
accounting/product issues. Version 0.29.6 delivers the explicit
[dated scheduled-recognition route](dated-ledger.md), [store](dated-store.md),
[credit operator](credit-operator.md) and separate [accounting intents](credit-accounting.md).
Automatic joint credit/product adoption and complete integrated acceptance remain
open; the full design below is not a claim of delivered coverage. The
[foundation checkpoint](../reviews/2026-10-01-model-foundations.md) documents
what is implemented and tested.

## Economic ownership and compatibility

Add a versioned dated-ledger route with an explicit Gregorian valuation date,
physical measure, scenario/run identities and exactly one source owner per
position: `legacy_monthly_overlay`, `contractual_dated_native_state`, or
`fully_scenario_generated`. Reject overlapping monthly/datetime schedules or
duplicate ownership of credit/behavior. Preserve old specifications and their
posting order without changing saved economics. Rebuild to adopt the new model.

The current `daily.rs` both applies credit/withdrawal behavior and rescales
scheduled cashflows by current/reference balance. Feeding it pre-adjusted scenario
events would double-count survival. Native-owned/generated positions must bypass
those branches, including generic interest. Reverse-severity scenarios require
regenerated state-aware inputs or explicit rejection; an unrelated baseline
schedule cannot stand in for reverse behavior.

## Shared transition and credit state

Implement a reusable bounded operator in shared core `credit_operator.rs`, then
ledger `credit_state.rs`/`credit_accounting.rs`. Maintain live state probabilities
separately from monetary principal, undrawn commitment, accrued interest and book
adjustment vectors. `CreditRequest` EAD is conditional per original account;
aggregate ledger balances cannot be passed to it as EAD without another survival
weight. Do not normalize surviving mass to one.

Transport migrations/cures, competing default/payoff flux and integrated interest
with one operator per complete hazard/scenario/interval identity. For principal
row vector B, accrued row vector A, generator Q and accrual-rate diagonal R,
propagate `B'=BQ` and `A'=AQ+BR` or an equivalent uniformized reward system.
Closing-balance interest or end-survival times a whole day's interest introduces
a new timing approximation. Nonaccrual/cure resumption is explicit policy.

Maturity/disposal are separate ownership exits; they are not voluntary
prepayment. Principal can terminate while delayed/deferred/recovery rights remain.
CCF estimates default-contingent borrowing; it is not ordinary utilization.
Default-contingent draws create cash outflow and loan principal before default,
with unused commitments canceled once. Ordinary draws need their own declared
dated plan/model and priced exposure schedule.

Economic default/LGD/recovery outputs do not set journal allowance policy.
Declare allowance horizon/discount/staging, charge-off timing, recovery-claim
recognition, accrued-interest reversal and premium/discount treatment separately.
Specify whether LGD includes accrued interest, preventing duplicate loss. Reviewed
opening allowances reconcile explicitly; no balancing plug is inferred. Physical
ledger inputs cannot relabel pricing hazards or multiply scenario-conditioned
credit terms by legacy stress multipliers again.

## Bounded dated scheduler and accrual rights

Add `dated_store.rs` and an accrual-plan module alongside legacy `FlowStore`.
Retain interned source/position/event IDs, five components, accrual endpoints,
scenario identity and stable same-day ordering. Support distinct same-day events
and day-zero settlement. Compile interval accrual separately from cash settlement;
the producer's whole-coupon `accrued_interest` is not daily NII.

Early coupons create deferred-income/prepaid-expense rights that unwind through
accrual end even after principal settles. Late coupons retain receivables with
declared credit treatment. Opening accrued balances require compatible anchors.
Split actual elapsed intervals at hazard/contract events. Version daily phase
ordering: opening rights, interval accrual/credit propagation, boundary credit
recognition, dated settlements, liquidity actions and closing verification.

Preserve the whole contractual/recovery tail beyond the reporting horizon. The
existing ledger's 1,080-day reporting cap does not permit clipping a longer
contract into a false maturity. Add dated native mapping/capture and workflow
dispatch; exclude these positions from `capture_cashflows=true` monthly capture
and `month*30` mapping. Candidates need actual origination dates in the new route.
The legacy monthly candidate route remains explicitly identified.

## Implementation ownership and gates

| Responsibility | Files |
|---|---|
| Shared transition operator | New core `credit_operator.rs`, independent CTMC/reward tests |
| Daily credit/policy | New ledger `credit_state.rs`, `credit_accounting.rs`, state/draw/claim tests |
| Dated event/accrual scheduler | New `dated_store.rs`, accrual-plan module and date/right tests |
| Native integration | Ledger `src/transport/types.rs`, `validation/specification.rs`, `replay/daily/mod.rs`, mapping and owned-workflow dispatch |
| Independent publication verification | `balance_stream.py`, `owned_workflow.py`, explicit test oracles and immutable lineage/report schemas |

Retain bounded batches, capacity/work admission, cooperative deadlines, process
watchdogs and final publication fences. Add immutable event lineage linking
transaction/run/position/event/source/model/input revisions. Balanced GL alone
does not prove contractual correctness: independently reconcile once-only events,
principal/draw/repayment/default conservation, allowance movements, recovery
claims, deferred interest rights and final credit subledgers.

Hand fixtures include competing one-day outcomes (100 opening, 80 live, 5 default,
15 prepay, LGD40%: 2 loss and 3 eventual recovery); cure/nonaccrual; default draw
100 drawn/40 undrawn/50% CCF; independently integrated pre-exit interest; maturity
with delayed interest; beyond-horizon recoveries; identical economics under
different allowance policies; leap/holiday/month-end dates; pre-as-of accrual;
early/late/day-zero/same-day settlement; coupon-day default/prepay/sale; mixed
legacy/dated books; source/scenario/measure failures; tampered lineage; and
cancellation at capture, execution, persisted replay and final publication.
The complete graph/credit/dated-settlement/solver/journal large-book acceptance
remains required; component tests are insufficient.

# Dated cashflow event model

`portfolio-model-core::cashflow` provides a Rust-owned, versioned event contract
for issue #12. It separates actual contractual settlement dates, accrual
endpoints, economic components, scenario identity and provenance. It is a shared
foundation for product generators and daily accounting. Existing monthly product
capture and daily replay have not yet been replaced by this contract: introducing
the type does not establish scenario-specific product repricing or end-to-end
publication acceptance.

## Dates and time

All dates are proleptic Gregorian ordinals with `0001-01-01 = 1`, through
`9999-12-31 = 3652059`. `payment_ordinal` is the actual settlement date supplied
by the source or product generator. `day_offset` is the exact number of calendar
days from the schedule's `as_of_ordinal`, and validation requires both fields
to agree. An event on the as-of date has offset zero. The horizon is inclusive.
There is no conversion from months to multiples of thirty days.

An optional accrual period is half-open `[start_ordinal,end_ordinal)`. Its end
must be inside the declared horizon, independently of settlement. It may follow
settlement when a preceding/modified-following convention moves payment before
an unadjusted contractual accrual endpoint; this is a negative settlement lag,
not a negative accrual fraction. Its start may precede as-of, as for a coupon
already accruing at the valuation date. Accrual endpoints are metadata; the type does
not smear accrued interest across a reporting month or automatically post
recognized income. The event date specifies when each explicit component is
recognized or settled by the downstream accounting policy. A producer needing
separate daily accrual recognition and later cash settlement emits separate,
uniquely identified events.

Calendar helpers implement Gregorian dates and actual month increments only.
`add_calendar_months` requires an explicit policy:

| Policy | Example from 2024-01-31 | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `clamp_day` | 2024-02-29 | Clamp an invalid day to the destination month's last day |
| `preserve_end_of_month` | 2024-02-29; 2024-03-31 from the original January anchor | Preserve month-end if the original anchor is month-end |
| `reject_invalid_day` | Error for February | Require the contractual day to exist |

Generate periodic dates from the original anchor plus the cumulative month
offset. Repeatedly adding to a clamped February date can introduce drift. These
helpers do not adjust business days or assume US holidays. A producer must
apply the actual contract's calendar, business-day convention and payment lag,
then provide the final payment date. No missing convention is inferred.

## Typed event and amount semantics

Each event carries `position_id`, stable `event_id`, scenario selector, currency,
date, optional accrual period, components, measure, provenance and adjustment.
The owner perspective is explicit: cash receipts are positive and cash payments
negative. Currency is a three-letter uppercase code, without FX conversion or
an embedded monetary multiplier. Currency-code validation is structural; it does
not infer settlement eligibility or validate against a changing ISO registry.

| Component | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `principal` | Cash principal receipt/payment; not an independently inferred outstanding balance |
| `cash_interest` | Cash interest receipt/payment |
| `fees` | Cash fees, separate from interest and principal |
| `accrued_interest` | Signed noncash interest-recognition change in the owner perspective |
| `book_amortization` | Signed noncash change in carrying value attributable to premium/discount/fee amortization |

`cash_total()` sums only principal, cash interest and fees. Noncash amounts are
never included in cash settlement. An accounting adapter must map signed
recognition changes onto asset/liability accounts; the event contract does not
assert that cash interest equals recognized interest or recompute a book yield.
All components and each event's signed cash total must be finite with absolute
value at most `1e15` actual currency units, using the shared monetary admission
constant. This is a numerical input bound, not a policy capital or exposure
limit. Financial calculations retain f64 precision without internal invoice
rounding.

## Scenarios, identity and provenance

`scenarios` declares the complete supported scenario names. The tagged selector
`{"kind":"all"}` makes an event apply unchanged to every declared scenario;
`{"kind":"named","scenario_id":"stress"}` selects one. All events must
be ordered by nondecreasing payment date. Same-day order is retained exactly.

Identity is `(position_id,event_id,scenario)`. The same economic `event_id`
may have separate versions in different named scenarios. It cannot occur
twice in one scenario, and an `all` version cannot coexist with any named
version of that identity, even if their dates differ. This prevents implicit
overrides and double-counting. Distinct IDs on the same date remain valid;
for example, one coupon and one fee. Distinct `all` and named IDs may combine
as explicitly supplementary events. Producers must preserve economic event
identity across scenario versions: the validator cannot discover two unrelated
IDs that describe the same payment.

Provenance is mandatory and uses one of:

- `contractual`: source ID plus immutable source revision; this describes an
  exact supplied contract event and requires contractual measure.
- `modeled`: model ID, model version and immutable input revision.
- `assumed`: assumption ID and a nonempty rationale.

`measure` distinguishes `contractual`, `pricing` and `physical` cashflows.
Contractual cashflows have no probabilistic measure. Pricing-model expected
cashflows belong to the declared pricing measure and are suitable for valuation
only with a consistent market/discount model and fixed base OAS. Physical or
conditional stress expectations are for forecasting or accounting under their
declared model, and cannot be silently substituted into OAS, EVE or derivative
valuation. Merely labeling a flow does not transform its measure or validate the
model producing it. Scenario identifiers are labels, not new random seeds;
product generators must preserve the shared-CRN risk contract.

## Actual accrual and overnight compounding

`actual_year_fraction` supports ACT/360, ACT/365 fixed and ACT/ACT ISDA. ACT/ACT
splits at calendar-year boundaries and uses 365 or 366 for each piece. ACT/365
fixed always uses 365. No helper silently selects a convention, and this helper
does not implement ACT/ACT ICMA or a 30/360 convention.

`overnight_compounded_factor(start,end,intervals)` returns the accumulation
factor, not an annualized rate or cash interest:

```text
F = product_i (1 + r_i * (end_i - start_i) / 360)
interest for unchanged principal P = P * (F - 1)
annualized period rate = (F - 1) * 360 / (end - start), when end > start
```

Rates are decimal annual values: `0.05` is 5%. Intervals must exactly partition
`[start,end)`, with no gaps, overlaps or zero-length pieces. A Friday observation
applying until Monday is one factor `1 + r*3/360`, not three daily compound
factors. The New York Fed methodology compounds on business days and applies
simple interest over intervening nonbusiness days using the preceding
business-day rate and actual/360 weighting. Observation/value dates differ
from publication dates. See the [New York Fed reference-rate methodology](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/additional-information-about-reference-rates).

The caller supplies interest-application intervals and the already-selected
rate. It must implement the contractual observation calendar, lookback,
observation shift, lockout, floor and spread policy before calling this helper.
The helper performs none of these choices, and has no implicit fixing fallback.
It supports negative rates when each accumulation factor remains positive.

The constant-principal rate-product identity does not establish correct
interest for principal changing within the accrual period. ARRC distinguishes
compounding the balance from compounding the rate, and notes qualifications for
rate compounding when principal is paid down. Loan lookbacks and derivative
payment delays may differ; floors and fallback spreads also require contractual
treatment. Those belong in dedicated product generators, which must emit exact
cash and accrual events. See the [ARRC bilateral business-loan conventions](https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/Microsites/arrc/files/2020/ARRC_SOFR_Bilat_Loan_Conventions.pdf).

## Surviving-principal overlay

`proportionally_adjust(fraction,rationale)` scales all five components by one
explicit fraction between zero and one. Fractions below one attach the
`proportional_surviving_principal` approximation marker and rationale. Applying
a second overlay to an already adjusted event fails. A factor of exactly one
returns the original event unchanged, including provenance and adjustment;
the zero-shock serialized identity is exact.

This is an optional approximation, not a credit or prepayment model. It may
misstate fees, interest already accrued, recovery timing, cure paths, option
exercise and effective-yield amortization. Full scenario integration must
regenerate product cashflows with joint credit/behavioral state and preserve
fixed OAS and CRN. An exact contractual source with this marker remains
traceable to its source but no longer asserts an unmodified contractual amount.

## Admission and validation

Schedules admit at most 250,000 events, 62,000 distinct positions, 256 declared
scenarios and 36,600 horizon days. Total supplied string metadata across the
schema, declared scenarios and events is bounded to 32 MiB; shared labels still
count each time supplied, and enum labels/JSON syntax are transport overhead.
Text fields also have explicit per-field byte limits and reject
empty/control-character values. Validation does not expand common events
across scenarios. `for_scenario` first validates and then creates one bounded
event vector, preserving order, amount and date. These are component limits,
not an aggregate process RSS guarantee. JSON transport must separately admit
request/output bytes before allocation and persist immutable request identity.
Structs and tagged enum payloads reject unknown JSON fields; unsupported schema
versions fail rather than reinterpret data.

## Validation and remaining delivery

`cargo test --manifest-path packages/portfolio-model-core/Cargo.toml --locked
--test cashflow` covers independently known Gregorian ordinals, leap centuries,
February/end-of-month policies, year-boundary ACT/ACT, a hand-computed coupon,
weekend SOFR accumulation, negative rates, interval gaps, strict JSON decoding,
duplicate/common-specific identities, scenario resolution, numeric overflow,
signed monetary bounds, aggregate metadata admission and exact zero-shock
overlay identity.

These tests validate the event foundation. They do not certify existing product
models, empirical behavioral fit, new production ledger integration, independent
persisted-journal replay, large-book acceptance or publication cleanup. Issue #12
still needs each product's actual-date scenario generation, transport/replay
integration, independent daily-output fixtures and removal of monthly-grid
mapping assumptions where contractual data is available.

# Actual-date effective-yield income

`dated-income-1` is an explicit amortized-cost analysis contract for lending
receipts. `portfolio-model-core::dated_income::evaluate` owns the financial
arithmetic; `analytics.model_contracts.evaluate_dated_income` transports it.
It does not automatically replace monthly accounting or the daily credit route.

Inputs retain contract, original-yield anchor, reviewed policy and cash-source
identities; physical/contractual measure, actual currency units and complete
contract dates are mandatory. Opening principal, signed accrued interest, gross
carrying value, original annual effective yield and reviewed current yield are
supplied separately. A seasoned loan is not refit from its remaining term.

For an interval of `d` actual days and current annual effective yield `y`, native
earned effective interest is `B * expm1(log1p(y) * d / 365)`, where `B` is opening
gross carrying value. Contractual interest earned is a separate supplied source
amount for this interval. Interest cash settles the accrued right. Principal cash
reduces contractual principal; integral fee cash reduces gross carrying value;
nonintegral fee cash is separately recognized as fee income. Basis amortization
is effective interest minus contractual interest earned minus integral fee cash.
Closing book adjustment is gross carrying value minus principal minus accrued
interest. The result preserves cash, effective interest, contractual interest,
basis amortization and reviewed modification gain/loss as separate values.

Settlement follows recognition, then an explicitly reviewed yield change:

- `prospective` supplies the reviewed new annual effective rate. It applies to
  subsequent intervals and does not reprice today's recognition.
- `catchup_original` supplies complete remaining revised cash rights. Their dated
  amounts must reconcile to the same admitted remaining source cash schedule.
  Native arithmetic discounts them at the immutable original yield, recognizes
  the carrying-value change separately, and retains that yield thereafter.

The model does not decide whether a change is a modification, derecognition,
floating-rate reset or credit impairment. The caller supplies that reviewed
economic policy. It does not generate an allowance, infer chargeoffs, introduce
an OAS into income, produce CECL/IFRS9 compliance, or convert pricing cashflows
into physical outcomes. Draws, borrowing directions and net-of-allowance interest
bases require separate explicit ownership and are rejected/not provided here.

Future cash is not a current recognition event. All supplied dated events are
returned, including tails, and residual principal/accrued/carrying values are
explicit. Missing terminal cash is not replaced by an invented maturity payment.
Event IDs are unique; dates are ordered (same-date phases remain in source order)
within the declared full tail. The model admits at most 4,096 events, 36,600 days,
32 MiB metadata, finite currency amounts up to `1e15`, and yields `-0.99..10`.
Exact terminal repayment can cancel machine-roundoff residuals only when both
principal and accrued rights have retired. These bounds are component admission,
not an aggregate RSS guarantee.

Independent fixtures cover a 100 principal/10 coupon one-year loan at 10% yield,
actual 29-day stub compounding, integral/nonintegral fees, historical anchors,
reviewed prospective and catchup changes, negative yields and invalid sources.
These analytical fixtures do not establish empirical predictive accuracy.

The dated [IFRS9 text](https://www.ifrs.org/content/dam/ifrs/publications/pdf-standards/english/2021/issued/part-a/ifrs-9-financial-instruments.pdf)
supports separating effective interest, contractual cash and modification
recognition as modeling concepts. The current [IASB amortised-cost project](https://www.ifrs.org/projects/work-plan/amortised-cost-measurement/)
contains tentative proposals as of this research pass; they are not treated as
effective requirements. A bank's applicable reviewed accounting policies are
required for production use. Full issue #22 still requires integrated yield/reset,
modification, fee, credit, reporting and independently verified journal adoption.

# Actual-date scheduled recognition and daily publication

Version 0.29.6 introduces an explicitly selected `dated-ledger-1` request and
`analytics.dated_ledger.run_dated_ledger`. Rust owns admission, active recognition,
settlements, daily GL reconciliation and closing reports. Python transports raw
inputs and independently verifies persisted source events and postings before
atomic publication. Existing `balance-stress-2` requests keep protocol 2 and their
historical economic/posting behavior. The dated route emits protocol 3.

This implements actual-date **scheduled** recognition. Shared credit propagation
and explicit credit-accounting intents exist as separate modules; their automatic
adoption into this daily route remains required. This is not a new credit,
prepayment, deposit-retention, reinvestment or accounting-standard calibration.

## Request and supported ownership

The strict request requires:

```text
schema: dated-ledger-1
monetary_unit: currency_units
recognition_policy:
  policy_id, policy_revision
  recognition_model: supplied_calendar_segments-1
  fees: immediate_earnings
specification: raw balance-stress-2 specification
dated: dated-store-1 source, owner, run and recognition plans
```

The recognition choice and immediate fee treatment are explicit supplied policies.
Fees requiring deferral, servicing allocation or effective-yield treatment need
their own supported policy; selecting this schema does not establish that all
fees should be immediately recognized.

Dated owners are opening positions with compatible account/currency/direction
and accrued anchors. Their generic interest, legacy default/migration, prescribed
draws, deposit flight/runoff, proportional survival and synthetic maturity branches
are bypassed. Other positions in the same book keep the legacy route. Overlapping
legacy cashflows, sale/collateral policies and opening pledged/eligible collateral
are rejected. Forward originations, active commitments/allowances/PD/migration,
floating-beta overrides and AFS/trading marks require explicit native integration
and are rejected by this initial route. These are remaining issue scopes, not
silent approximations or completed capabilities.

Runs must exactly cover baseline, each scenario and every reverse severity.
Regular and reverse executions at severity one share the same declared economic
source case; a reverse scenario cannot borrow an unrelated baseline schedule.
Full principal settlements cannot exceed opening face. New draws require explicit
state/exposure events and are not inferred from signed cash or CCF.

## Daily phases and gross rights

1. Post supplied opening principal, basis and accrued anchors; reconcile the
   source's earned rights at the valuation date before day-zero events.
2. Settle day-zero events once, apply the existing explicit tax policy to day-zero
   earnings, and close/report that day's activity before beginning day one.
3. For each actual elapsed day, execute disjoint legacy position-day events,
   recognize active supplied calendar segments, then settle that date's events
   in stable source order.
4. Execute remaining legacy cashflows, liquidity actions and closing checks under
   the existing policy sequence; a dated owner cannot also receive legacy economics.

The implementation currently executes legacy position-day events before dated
interval recognition on each day; they have disjoint ownership. A joint credit
coordinator must introduce its separately versioned interval/boundary phase order
before enabling credit or sale modifiers on dated owners.

Interest recognition posts the signed change in the appropriate right and
offsetting income/expense. Settlement posts signed principal/cash coupon/fees
without recognizing the whole coupon again. Basis recognition changes carrying
value and income separately. Principal may reach zero while interest rights
continue to accrue or await settlement.

Before cash settlement, positive/negative signed rights are receivables/payables.
After early settlement, positive/negative residuals are prepaid expense/deferred
income. Four distinct GL accounts preserve gross assets and liabilities rather
than netting early and late coupons. Closing statements derive solely from
replayed postings. The independent verifier classifies these GL accounts anew.

## Bounded runtime and immutable evidence

The active recognition cursor follows supplied segment boundaries; it does not
scan every cashflow each day. Owner/legacy overlap and coverage checks use indexed
sets rather than quadratic book scans. Position-day work and active segment-day
work are admitted together. Public transport keeps the existing 2,000-position /
3-million-work tier; explicit engine-only large-book transport allows up to
60,000 positions and 90 million combined work units. Reporting remains 30–1,080
days. Store/component limits are separate from aggregate process memory.

`event_lineage` links each dated recognition/settlement to run/input revision,
position/event/source/provenance, policy, date, transaction and five monetary
components. `dated_rights` retains all selected events, settled and future cash,
earned and unearned recognition, and the original full contract end. The raw
request is stored immutably as `dated-input.json` with a hash. DLL/executable and
Python verifier source identities are fenced before publication.

The independent publication gate verifies persisted balanced GL, once-only source
phases, exact calendar recognition, source/provenance identity, transaction-level
postings, principal/basis roll-forwards, gross rights, full tails and independently
classified closing/consolidated statements. A balanced but economically altered
transaction therefore fails. Cancellation/deadline checks cover native execution,
persisted replay and final publication; failure publishes no successful manifest.

Validation fixtures include leap/off-cycle/day-zero/same-day cash, early coupons
after principal maturity, delayed interest, mixed legacy ownership, immutable
source corruption and cancellation. Empirical credit/behavior validation, native
graph capture, saved-book/candidate adoption, API/UI exposure and complete
graph/credit/solver/journal 60,000-position acceptance remain open.

## Research and boundaries

The [Basel ECL guidance](https://www.bis.org/committees/bcbs/basel-consolidated-guidelines/module/pap/20)
supports separating credit-risk estimates from accounting measurement policy.
The [interagency allowance statement](https://www.federalreserve.gov/frrs/guidance/interagency-policy-statement-on-allowances-for-credit-losses.htm)
addresses accrued-interest treatment. These references inform explicit policy
boundaries; this scheduled-recognition route does not claim CECL/IFRS9 compliance.
Research was checked on 2026-10-01. See [credit accounting](credit-accounting.md)
and [the integration requirement ledger](daily-integration-plan.md).

Rebuild the ledger DLL/executable and dependent decision/workflow artifacts,
then restart API/workers before using the new schema. No services were restarted
and no production deployment is implied by local validation.
