# Revised physical deposit expectations at original yield

`deposit-revised-income-ledger-1` is an explicitly selected purchase-asof research lane. Rust projects the original and revised Physical deposit histories, preserves the original quote, purchase carrying value and annual effective yield, and posts the reviewed expectation revision and subsequent income in the existing daily Sim. Python transports immutable partitions and independently reconstructs source economics and the entire ordered journal. This route makes no accounting-standard, regulatory, empirical, saved-book, cohort, unit-library or full-product acceptance claim. Capital and FTP eligibility remain false.

The source schema is `deposit-revised-income-source-1`. Its `anchor` retains purchase ordinal, original principal, price per 100, gross carrying value, original annual effective rate, purchase quote identity and original yield-anchor identity. The `original` contract and every explicitly mapped revised run retain complete raw state requests. Only the named future driver dimensions in the reviewed policy may change. Contractual terms and opening economics cannot change. Every required baseline/named run has its own supplied Physical history; no global stress overlay runs again.

For original future liability cash amounts `cash_j` at actual time fractions `t_j`, original cost must reproduce `sum(cash_j / (1 + original_yield)^t_j)` using the unchanged dated-income owner. Revised expected cash is discounted with that same immutable yield. At asof, `basis_revision = revised_present_value - original_cost`. Original opening is posted first. The separate reviewed revision posts liability basis `-basis_revision` and `pnl:deposit_basis_revision = +basis_revision`, with zero cash. Subsequent original-EIR expense and contractual-earned interest remain distinct. There is no updated quote, new yield solve, Q reinterpretation, OAS recalibration or synthetic terminal cash. A zero revision preserves the original anchors.

Actual earning is allocated to native earned origins and actual cash retires those origins in FIFO order. A native full interest payment or contractual maturity retires all remaining eligible origins unchanged; its total must match unchanged native cash within existing tolerances. A partial withdrawal/closure retires eligible amounts by FIFO and never consumes future earning. Recognition periods explicitly include zero-earning gaps. Full-tail checks examine each gross payable/prepaid origin separately; offsetting balances cannot manufacture closure. Tiny source roundoff remains visible, without cash or income plugs.

The initial boundary is one zero-accrued liability acquired at asof. Original and revised complete tails fit 64 days; monetary inputs/components are bounded by 10,000, selected raw envelope by 1 MiB, joined native work by eight million units and retained/output component capacity by 32 MiB. These are per-component admission limits, not aggregate RSS, aggregate gross-money or guaranteed numerical-reconciliation claims. Existing runtime journal and reconciliation gates still apply. Migration, external inflow, fees, seasoned acquisition, changed contractual terms, negative coupon/yield, franchise value, reverse runs, added allowance/default/nonaccrual policies and automatic reinvestment are rejected.

The model-ledger executable first performs its bounded Value dispatch peek. Only the selected new branch re-deserializes the original input bytes with the strict typed parser; it preserves nested duplicates and rejects enum-object aliases and noninteger timeout values. Historical Value branches retain their existing parser behavior. The retained raw request preserves its original JSON types and signed zero separately from native declared monetary normalization.

The preparation header contains exactly `schema`, `model_schema`, `prepared_request` and `source_receipt`. The receipt retains original raw request, complete original/revised state outputs, original PV, original-yield income inputs/results, review and anchors, FIFO origins and admission. Actual native completion is persisted exactly as `{"complete":true,"protocol":3}` and reread through the frame facade. Neither table presence nor a legacy receipt marker supplies completion.

Independent preparation creates a private checked control; partition verification consumes bounded frames and returns `physical_deposit_source_recomputed`, `original_yield_revision_recomputed`, `ordered_deposit_journal_recomputed` and `complete_gross_cash_origin_rights_verified`. All four must be true. Approval, installed-adoption evidence and capital/FTP permission remain false. Persisted replay compares the original queued input and saved receipt with exact recursive type/value/signed-zero identity; financial outputs keep their existing tolerances.

Browser serialization may spell integral monetary inputs as JSON integers. The independent expected reports explicitly emit declared Float64 columns as finite binary64 values, including opening/inactive debit and credit zeros. This cast occurs only after complete raw admission and independent source/calendar replay. It does not normalize the queued request, metadata, review objects, dates or booleans, and it changes no financial comparison tolerance. The `product-adoption-0298-browser-identity-repair` regressions retain raw integer identity and reject changed types, signed zero and monetary errors.

Publication retains the original deadline before serialization. The runner and worker recheck raw/source/completion and current binary/library/source identity, cancellation, ownership lease and attempt token through final publication. Windows sharing retries repeat these checks; a late failure after rename removes only the proved new unpublished directory. No completed job or manifest is published after a failed source, journal, deadline or ownership gate.

The reviewed source and daily owner are applied locally in 0.29.8; matching official native builds and component gates pass. The revised-deposit process tests passed in the first full engine run, which failed a separate mortgage capital fixture. Full default engine, durable API and browser acceptance is being rerun under `product-adoption-0298-schema-repair`. Contained native/reference and copied-producer transport evidence remains distinct from complete installed acceptance. Restart matching deployed workers and explicitly select/rebuild the route before use; a local patch/build does not deploy it. Full issue 14/22/25 empirical, general ownership, joint model and scale requirements remain open.
docs/models/deposit-state.md:
# Daily native physical deposit state

`portfolio_model_core::deposit_state::simulate` accepts strict `deposit-state-1`
inputs and returns daily offered rates, cohort/segment balances, migrations,
earned interest, external cash, and closing rights. This is the supplied-policy
state foundation for #14. Its parameters are explicitly **supplied assumptions**.
It does not fit retention from paid-rate histories, establish observed account
accuracy, or complete pricing/ledger/FTP/public-product adoption by itself.

The existing production deposit fitter already supports logistic beta and
asymmetric adjustment. This version does not reinterpret it as a fixed-beta
model or silently replace saved monthly economics. Instead it provides a
separate versioned daily contract that can carry linear or logistic-beta offered
rate policies and one shared balance transition policy. Adopting it requires
explicit library/session rebuild and coordinated graph, daily stress, journal
and FTP ownership. The old monthly final payout and separate daily flight formula
must not be applied again to these generated balances.

## Research basis and evidence boundaries

The [OCC Interest Rate Risk handbook](https://www.occ.gov/publications-and-resources/publications/comptrollers-handbook/files/interest-rate-risk/pub-ch-interest-rate-risk.pdf)
treats deposit pricing sensitivity and runoff as separate assumptions. It calls
for documentation appropriate to model complexity, historical customer
behavior, competition and economic conditions, and review of key assumptions.
Recovering a synthetic rate-fit parameter therefore does not validate retention.

[Basel's current application guidance, SRP98](https://www.bis.org/committees/bcbs/basel-framework/standard/srp/98/inforce/2026-01-01/published/2024-07-16)
distinguishes contractual demand liquidity from behavioral stability, and
different runoff, constant-balance and dynamic-balance viewpoints. It also
distinguishes the information used for economic value and earnings. This model
accordingly separates withdrawals, internal migration, new business, residual
balances and continuation-value assumptions. It is not regulatory core-deposit
classification, prescribed standardized slotting, or proof of stability in a run.

## Identity, ownership and supplied policy

Every request supplies entity, cohort, currency, source revision, model version,
assumption ID and rationale, run identity and physical measure. Amounts are
actual monetary units without an implicit multiplier. Segment names are unique
and immutable within the request. The cohort's customers can migrate between
its deposit product/segment states without changing the bank's total principal.
External inflows explicitly enter that cohort; they are not inferred as payments
or renewal of lost balances. A request describes expected **balance mass**, not
account counts or a reconstruction of individual closures. Account lineage and
representative/cohort approximation must remain attached upstream.

`parameter_status` is always `supplied_assumption`. No caller can set a boolean
claim that this kernel fitted retention. The optional `ObservedRange` carries a
caller-declared dated history revision, reference-rate range and whether a
logistic plateau was identified. It is support metadata, not an audited fit.
Each daily point reports whether that segment's selected observation is outside
the declared range, and whether a range was supplied at all. Unknown regime
support does not mean an in-regime pass. The caller must decide publication
policy for unsupported extrapolation and retain parameter-sensitivity scenarios;
the kernel neither fabricates a confidence interval nor suppresses the flag.

Only physical measure is admitted. Economic-value pricing can consume these
same conditional physical state cashflows under its explicitly selected
discount/valuation convention, but that does not convert the probabilities or
policy into pricing measure. There is no separate kernel-side stress-flight
multiplier. The same function and inputs determine state for runoff, paid-rate
NII and liquidity projection. Full integration must verify that consumers do
not post the principal reduction, interest or migration a second time.

## Actual observations and offered repricing

Drivers are daily exact Gregorian rows, strictly contiguous from
`as_of - maximum_observation_lag - 1` through `horizon_end - 1`. The extra
previous day supports actual reference-rate velocity. Each row supplies
reference rate and per-segment competitor rates, offered-spread stress,
confidence stress, and external inflows. Historical rows must have zero
external inflow because opening balances already reflect history. Missing
history/forecast days, dimensions or dates fail. There is no forward filling,
interpolation, guessed fixing, calendar adjustment, or future observation used
before its lag expires.

For segment `i` on date `d`, repricing observes the complete row at
`d - lag_i`. A linear target before floor/ceiling is:

`intercept + beta * observed_reference + competitor_weight * (observed_competitor - observed_reference) + observed_offered_spread_stress`.

The logistic variant replaces beta with:

`beta_min + (beta_max-beta_min)/(1 + exp(-steepness*(observed_reference-midpoint)))`.

The sigmoid uses a numerically stable branch in extreme regimes. Beta bounds,
midpoint and steepness are supplied and validated. Logistic target economics
are not claimed to be identified when rate history never reaches a plateau.
Competitor premium and offered spread affect the **actual paid target**, not
just a withdrawal score.

The target is clamped to the supplied floor and ceiling. The applicable
upward/downward response half-life is selected against the previous paid rate:

`adjustment = 1 - exp(-ln(2)/half_life_days)`;

`paid_today = previous_paid + adjustment * (bounded_target-previous_paid)`.

Zero half-life is explicitly immediate adjustment. Positive half-life uses real
calendar days, and the final paid rate is bounded again. The model carries the
actual offered rate at each point. Floor/ceiling policies can be negative within
admission; signed expense/cash rights then remain signed. This is a policy for
administered rate changes, not an inferred market-rate fixing contract.

## One competing daily transition

The date's current competitor gap and reference velocity enter retention after
the offered rate has changed. For one origin segment:

`gap = max(current_competitor - paid_today, 0)`;

`velocity = abs(reference_today-reference_yesterday)`;

`stress_exposure = uninsured_coefficient*uninsured_fraction + concentration_coefficient*concentration + digital_coefficient*digital_fraction - relationship_protection*relationship_fraction - operational_protection*operational_fraction`;

`withdrawal_intensity = max(0, base_withdrawal + gap_sensitivity*gap + velocity_sensitivity*velocity + confidence_stress*stress_exposure)`;

`closure_intensity = base_closure + closure_stress_sensitivity*confidence_stress`.

Each named internal migration has supplied base intensity plus a sensitivity to
the positive destination-minus-origin offered-rate gap. Migration destinations
past a true contractual maturity are unavailable. Their intensity is zero, and
is not reassigned as an external withdrawal or synthetic reinvestment.

All active origin exit intensities compete once. Let `H` be withdrawal, closure
and migration intensity summed for that row:

`daily_exit_fraction = 1-exp(-H/365)`;

`fraction_to_cause = daily_exit_fraction * intensity_to_cause/H`.

When `H=0`, all exit fractions are exactly zero. The implementation uses
`expm1` for small intensities. The retained share is `1-daily_exit_fraction`.
Annual intensity time uses ACT/365 elapsed days; it is distinct from the selected
contract interest denominator. The admitted combined row intensity is at most
100 per year; an extreme driver/policy combination that exceeds it fails rather
than being silently clipped to an arbitrary runoff cap.

Rows read the same opening vector and accumulate a new vector simultaneously.
Newly migrated principal cannot migrate, withdraw or close a second time that
day. Accrued rights move in the same fraction as origin principal; withdrawals
and closures settle their fraction of accrued interest. Internal migration is
a transfer report, not external bank cash. Withdrawals, closures, true maturity
and assumed horizon payout have distinct cash event identities and totals.

This is a **daily single-transition convention**, not an exact continuous-time
multi-jump process or an intraday withdrawal model. In particular, migrating
balances cannot traverse several product states within a day. Its daily timing
is an explicit approximation to observed intraday behavior. If data require
multiple jumps, the transition engine must be replaced or refined under a new
policy/version rather than described as continuous-time exact.

## Event timing, interest, maturity and horizon

At date `d`, the model settles any true contractual maturity, adjusts offered
rates, allocates the competing transition, and adds separately supplied inflows.
Transitions are placed at the **start** of `[d,d+1)`. New inflows enter after
those transitions and do not immediately run off in the same daily step.
Post-transition balances accrue simple deposit interest at their destination's
new offered rate over `[d,d+1)` using supplied ACT/360 or ACT/365F. Interest is
not added to principal. A supplied end-of-day settlement date pays accumulated
interest as cash and clears that payable without recognizing it twice. No
monthly interest-payment date is guessed. Opening accrued rights, daily expense,
cash interest and closing accrued rights independently reconcile.

Cash uses the bank's perspective: new deposits received are positive principal;
withdrawals, closures and maturity payouts are negative principal; interest
expense settlement is normally negative cash interest. Recognition amounts use
the depositor's accrued-right/expense sign. Negative paid rates therefore create
negative expense and positive interest cash when settled.

A true contractual maturity is a separately supplied exact ordinal, never
inferred for an NMD. It stops that segment's remaining principal/interest and
disables later inflows. Maturity at the closing horizon still settles explicitly.
This schema supplies no automatic rollover/renewal fraction; a renewal model
must define its source and new contract separately.

Terminal treatment is mandatory:

| Policy | Physical closing behavior |
|---|---|
| `retain_residual` | Leave principal and unpaid accrued rights visible; no invented final payout. |
| `assumed_liquidation` | Explicitly repay remaining principal/interest at horizon with a supplied rationale and distinct assumed event. |
| `franchise_value_only` | Retain physical balances and report a supplied continuation value separately; no cash settlement or inferred discounting. |

A continuation value's sign/unit matches the caller's valuation convention and
currency label. It is not an added physical deposit liability or income. Full
horizon-sensitivity work must compare actual residuals, cash, NII and the
selected continuation convention across horizons. Extending a horizon does not
alter the prior state when policies, drivers and cash-payment dates retain the
same prefix.

## Conservation, admission and acceptance

The principal identity is:

`opening balance + external inflows = withdrawals + closures + contractual maturity payouts + assumed terminal payouts + closing balance`.

Migration does not appear as external loss. The independent rights identity is:

`opening accrued rights + earned interest expense + bank-perspective cash interest = closing accrued rights`.

The engine checks conservation without renormalizing state or relaxing published
portfolio output tolerances. It admits at most 16 segments, 36600 calendar days
subject to 250000 daily segment/migration/work units, and at most one named
migration rule per distinct pair. Segment IDs are at most 64 bytes; other
identity/history labels are at most 256 bytes and supplied rationales 1024.
Observation lag is at most 366 days. Driver dimensions/history, payment dates,
rate/coefficient/fraction domains and opening/closing/cumulative monetary
admission are validated. Amount and gross accrued/interest/cash-interest bounds
use shared `1e15`. Work counts include potential output rows. Component bounds
are not an aggregate process RSS guarantee or regulatory capital admission.

`tests/deposit_state.rs` contains 21 independent analytical fixtures. They cover
actual leap interest, residual without payout, competing withdrawal/closure/
migration, simultaneous two-way principal/accrual transfer, destination-rate
interest, explicit new inflow, lag coverage, asymmetric half-lives, floor/ceiling,
competitor/spread-driven offered rates, logistic midpoint/extremes, regime
flags, gap/confidence/velocity retention, true maturity, residual/franchise/
liquidation, horizon extension, exact same-policy replay, signed interest rights,
and invalid source/domain/money/work/overlap admission. The persisted
`examples/models/deposit-state-1.json` also checks two actual days of interest:
`1000 * 0.365 * 2 / 365 = 2`, bank cash interest `-2`, and retained principal `1000`.

These tests do not establish fitted account-level retention, stress-run accuracy,
cohort representativeness or regulatory stability. Required follow-through is
observed dated retention/migration/inflow/closure histories with customer/source
linkage, jointly identified paid-rate behavior, chronological training and
held-out regime diagnostics, parameter uncertainty and plateau identification,
account-versus-cohort PV/DV01/NII/runoff error tables, full graph/daily/FTP
single-ownership integration, and independently replayed immutable journals.
Those are retained #14 acceptance gates; no paid-rate synthetic fitter test can
substitute for them.

# Explicit derivative accounting intents

`portfolio_risk_native::derivative_accounting::evaluate` consumes an immutable
`DerivativeAccountingRequest` and returns a `DerivativeAccountingResult`.
The schema and model version are both `derivative-accounting-1`. It is an additive
component: the saved `derivative-contracts-1` and `derivative-contracts-2` valuation
contracts retain their own admission and economics. MPOR requests still require
an explicit V2 selection; enabling accounting does not upgrade a saved derivative.

This component prepares balanced journal **intents for one modeled Physical
scenario**. It does not claim observed settlements, a complete financial reporting
standard, persistence, saved-book adoption or verified publication. The immutable
request must accompany the result when a coordinator publishes it.

## Supported reviewed policies

The caller supplies an accounting policy identity/revision and one reviewed
designation per mapped position. `undesignated_trading` and
`undesignated_economic_hedge` are supported with
`clean_value_changes_in_earnings`. Formal cash flow, fair value and net investment
hedge designations are rejected: there is no effectiveness assessment, hedged-item
accounting, OCI recycling or designation history in this component.

Coupon presentation is explicit:

* `settle_derivative_carrying` transfers the signed contractual right from
  derivative carrying into cash or an unpaid receivable/payable.
* `contractual_income_at_due_with_mark_offset` records signed income at the due
  date and independently marks the remaining derivative. Its mark offset prevents
  counting the same coupon in income and derivative value. This policy is due-date
  presentation, not a daily earned-interest accrual or effective-yield policy.

`reviewed_modeled_closeout_shortfall_in_earnings` recognizes the native reviewed
counterparty closeout loss and posted-collateral return loss separately.
`segregated_custodian_memo_only` records received IM principal as equal custody
asset/obligation memo balances. Received IM is not entity income, cash or a source
of funding; native custodian interest is retained as a third-party diagnostic.
Posted IM remains a financial asset, and its actual native return/remuneration
affects entity cash. Signed VM becomes received VM liability or posted VM asset;
crossing zero uses the gross accounts and never silently nets presentation.

XVA and modeled funding costs are `report_only`. An optional raw Pricing
derivative request is independently evaluated for XVA diagnostics; it must share
the exact opening clean value, CRN, entity/currency and legal trade mapping.
Its CVA/FVA never change the Physical journal or automatically adjust carrying.
Actual Physical default recovery/loss is recognized through the closeout waterfall
once. A supplied spread cost diagnostic is not an observed financing transaction.

These are reviewed model policies rather than an inference of accounting rules.
[IAS 32](https://www.ifrs.org/issued-standards/list-of-standards/ias-32-financial-instruments-presentation/)
sets requirements for financial offsetting; a supplied enforceable netting flag is
not by itself a financial statement offsetting conclusion.
[IFRS 9](https://www.ifrs.org/issued-standards/list-of-standards/ifrs-9-financial-instruments/)
requires designation and qualification for hedge accounting. The
[March 2019 IFRIC discussion](https://www.ifrs.org/news-and-events/updates/ifric/2019/ifric-update-march-2019/)
also distinguishes physical settlement from reversing previously recognized
fair-value results. The component therefore retains prior mark earnings and
requires an explicit delivery-recognition review rather than erasing them.

## Input and early admission

The raw `derivative` operation must be a native `netting` lifecycle. Standalone
swap/option snapshots lack the daily path and cannot be silently expanded.
Admission requires exactly one Physical path with probability exactly one,
`modeled_physical_scenario`, actual `currency_units`, matching entity/currency,
complete reviewed trade coverage and every calendar-day raw node from opening
through the full contractual/default/collateral tail. Missing daily marks are
rejected; no interpolation, extrapolated coupon source or report-horizon tail
truncation is introduced. Each native node retains its exact valuation cutoff,
curve/source identities, payment timing and legal mapping.

Opening anchors explicitly provide settlement cash, every mapped clean carrying
value, posted VM, received VM, posted IM, received IM custody and an equity credit
balance. Financial opening debits must reconcile to that equity anchor, and
carrying/collateral must reconcile to native opening marks/CSA stocks. Cash may be
signed; its financing or overdraft treatment is not inferred. Nonzero opening
collateral cannot be allocated across independently reviewed buckets implicitly.

Normal coupon cash is derived from raw contractual legs. Floating cash requires
observed fixings or a declared Physical path with information available by the
node cutoff. `physical_index_paths` supplies immutable observations keyed by
mapped position and contractual period, using the same reviewed reset/calendar
conventions as the raw leg. A Pricing projection cannot become Physical cash by
changing an output label. Unknown, duplicate, unused or late fixing inputs fail.
Publication/reset cutoffs and rate bounds are validated by shared native indexed
arithmetic; calendar/source mapping remains supplied rather than independently
verified against a fixing provider.

MPOR uses V2's native retained obligations and identity/date-only settlement
instructions. Physical MPOR observations belong to the MPOR policy in the raw
derivative request; normal accounting observations belong to the accounting
request. Raw cash/exposure overrides are not admitted. A cash European election
uses its selected native contractual settlement price; physical delivery changes
the carrying owner to the admitted delivered swap and retains future leg cash.
Short delivery uses the explicitly reversed underlying contract required by the
native legal mapping. No intrinsic cash is added to physical delivery.

The initial tier admits 256 trades, 4,096 daily nodes and 250,000 combined native
work units. Before schedule allocation it charges raw Physical and optional
Pricing paths, observations, native MPOR work and each independent due-right
repricing, with saturating work arithmetic. Requests are limited to 32 MiB;
journal output to 250,000 intents. Finite monetary values and cumulative account
balances retain the native monetary domain. These component bounds do not claim
an aggregate process RSS limit or acceptance of the full 60,000-position workflow.

## Replay and output contract

Each dated signed-debit event balances within its financial or custody ledger.
Positive amounts are debits and negative amounts credits; generic typed account
codes require a reviewed adapter mapping before persistence. Every intent retains
run/scenario/entity/currency, Physical measure, policy, source identities, mapped
position, current contractual owner and legal bucket. Zero events do not create
empty postings. The returned native result still retains zero/raw marks.

Daily replay first retains native collateral flows, reconstructs the clean mark
including any same-day contractual due right, recognizes or retains signed cash
rights, and marks the remaining derivative. Before/after scheduled payment
snapshots partition the same due cash explicitly. An option delivery transfers
carrying between owners with balanced book postings and no settlement cash.
MPOR settlements clear individual retained rights by identity; aggregate native
movement is independently reconciled instead of being posted a second time.
Closeout removes future carrying, unpaid claims and collateral once, recognizing
native entity cash and both types of shortfall. Subsequent marks/rights remain
extinguished.

`cash_rights` reports Physical amount separately from the Pricing amount excluded
from clean carrying, selected fixing/model sources, recognition sources, current
contractual owner, due date, settlement date and closeout inclusion. `native`
retains raw clean trade marks, reviewed mapping, collateral/call records, default
waterfall, MPOR policy, obligations and exercises. `daily` reconciles independent
gross rights/cash/collateral state to the replayed financial and custody trial
balances. The full tail ends with no derivative or unpaid rights and exactly the
native residual collateral stocks; unsupported residual rights fail publication
preparation rather than being dropped.

## Independent fixtures and example

The native tests independently sum every intent and replay its signed postings
from explicit opening balances. Hand fixtures cover payer/receiver coupons,
negative actual rates, coupon-income offsets, before/after marks, delayed/outage
VM calls, custody and posted IM, negative collateral remuneration, long/short
physical delivery, cash European settlement, retained/settled signed MPOR rights,
default recovery and posted-return losses, report-only nonzero CVA, finite/source/
policy/measure/calendar/work rejection and unknown cash overrides. The existing
derivative valuation fixtures continue to run unchanged.

[`derivative-accounting-1.json`](../../examples/models/derivative-accounting-1.json)
is synthetic: N=360, ten ACT/360 days, fixed 5%, observed floating 10%, DF=1.
Fixed cash is -0.50 and floating cash +1.00, so net settlement is +0.50.
Opening cash 100 and derivative asset 0.50 reconcile to equity 100.50.
The twelve daily snapshots end with cash 100.50, zero derivative/VM/IM and zero
net mark earnings; VM receipts and returns cancel. This is a component fixture,
not a market calibration or production book.

Remaining #20 gates include raw saved-book mapping, durable daily-ledger adoption,
independent persisted replay/publication verification, reviewed account mapping,
actual transaction ingestion, journal-to-capital/FTP reconciliation, production
scale/deadline acceptance, empirical option/XVA validation and legally supported
closeout/hedge-accounting scope. This component does not close those gates.

## Independent raw-source verification

`portfolio_risk.analytics.derivative_verification.verify_derivative_accounting(raw_request,
result)` runs after native calculation. It returns an immutable
`derivative-accounting-verification-1` receipt only after the complete result
passes; unsupported conventions or mismatches raise `DerivativeVerificationError`
and return no receipt. The module has no native callbacks, application pricer
imports, backend selection or financial execution route.

The verifier reconstructs actual-date year fractions with Python's independent
calendar, fixed and indexed cash from supplied raw observations, exact discount
PV, conditional European intrinsic/cash carry, explicit delivery and election,
Physical MPOR obligations, signed lagged/failed margin calls, custody/principal
returns and the reviewed closeout waterfall. It then independently constructs
reviewed recognition events, sums signed postings and reconciles all daily gross
rights, cash, collateral and trial balances. Producer clean marks and reported
cash are checked against raw arithmetic rather than accepted as economic truth.
Optional raw Pricing XVA references are separately reconstructed and remain
report-only. All supported accounting policies, day counts, coupon/margin
conventions, legal buckets and European/MPOR modes are checked; there is no
approval for a partially supported result.

Financial comparisons preserve the existing 1e-12 relative / 1e-9 absolute
tolerance. Identity, revision, date, cutoff, measure, enum, event order and field
coverage comparisons are exact. Because both implementations post any nonzero
change, a last-ulp difference in a near-zero carrying value (an at-market swap
after a settlement, or exactly offsetting legs) decides whether a mark intent
exists at all; the verifier therefore treats an intent whose postings all lie
within the 1e-9 absolute tolerance of zero as a zero event on both sides and
renumbers the remaining intents in order before comparing
(`normalize_intents`). Daily balances are still compared in full. The canonical raw-request SHA-256 in the receipt
binds the reviewed source; checked day/journal/right/path counts and the optional
Pricing diagnostic check are reported. Unknown output fields and duplicate,
omitted or balanced-but-economically-wrong entries fail.

The test suite invokes fresh native artifacts for independent source cases and
tampering cases, including amounts, dates, sources, policy reviews, default,
exercise/delivery, margin and diagnostic CVA. A fresh subprocess forbids Python
financial callbacks and disables the independent oracle during native calculation,
then enables the verifier afterward. Verification failure is tested before any
publication write. No fixture is a market calibration or accounting qualification.

Persist variant-bearing nested data as lossless canonical JSON cells (or an
equivalent immutable JSON payload) and decode it before re-verification.
`RateSource` and MPOR settlement instructions have heterogeneous tagged fields;
automatic Polars struct union can add undeclared null fields. Those additions are
intentionally rejected rather than silently normalized into a different source
shape. Every JSON serialization must reject nonfinite values and retain exact
integer date/cutoff types.

The receipt explicitly reports `persisted_journal_verified=false`. Verifying the
native model JSON, and later re-verifying a decoded persisted model-result cell,
is **analysis-source verification**. It is not independent persisted mixed/saved
ledger replay, account-mapping approval, immutable ledger publication or adoption
into daily capital/FTP. Those gates require the corresponding coordinator and
persisted financial journal verification, and remain separate.
docs/models/derivative-contracts.md:
# Explicit derivative contracts and collateral paths

`derivative-contract-1` with original `derivative-contracts-1` or explicitly selected `derivative-contracts-2` adds an opt-in Rust analysis component. It does not reinterpret historical swap/swaption economics or close enhancement issue #20 by itself. The full production graph, saved hedge mapping, daily journal, FTP, scenario calibration and scale/publication gates remain separate integration work.

The protocol envelope is `{schema:"derivative-contract-1",threads:1,request:{schema:"derivative-contract-1",model_version:"derivative-contracts-1",operation:{kind:"swap"|"european_swaption"|"netting",request:{...}}}}`. Public native functions are `derivative_contract::evaluate`, `swaps::value_swap`, `options::value_european`, and `csa::evaluate`. Modules separate clean swaps, European contracts, collateral types, raw-trade handoff, and the collateral timeline. Python transports requests/results; it is not a financial backend.

## Clean actual-date swaps

Fixed and floating legs have independently supplied frequencies, accrual/payment dates and day counts, with common contractual start/maturity and constant nonnegative notional. There is no notional exchange. Floating coupons use the shared `term_enhancements::indexed` contract: explicit term, daily simple or daily compounded observations, index/calendar identities, reset/selection cutoffs, shifts, floors/caps and spread treatment. Observed fixings retain publication/revision identity. Conditional projections retain model/path/measure identity and their information timestamps cannot follow the exact UTC valuation cutoff. Arithmetic does not verify externally supplied calendar mappings or generate future forwards.

The collateralized discount curve is separate from the index basis and projected rate path. It carries an immutable source/revision, collateral-discount policy, currency, exact asof, information timestamp, and exact positive discount factors for every admitted payment date. The asof factor is exactly one. Intraday information must be available by the supplied valuation cutoff. Interpolation and extrapolation are rejected. Rates and factors need not be positive; discount factors must be positive, allowing negative interest-rate environments. Shared coupon-factor domains still apply.

For fixed coupons `N k tau_i` and floating amounts `F_j`, `A=sum(N tau_i D_i)`, `PV_fixed=k A`, `PV_float=sum(F_j D_j)`. Payer clean value is `PV_float-PV_fixed`; receiver clean value is its negative. Par rate is `PV_float/A` when `A>0`, otherwise unavailable. Signed dated cashflows independently reconcile the clean value. Payment timing explicitly includes or excludes coupons on the valuation date. Paid coupons are removed once; unsettled coupons retain their contractual accrual intervals. These pricing schedules are not daily accounting journal instructions.

## European cash or physical settlement

A European contract supplies a complete set of terminal conditional states, risk-neutral probabilities summing to one, asof-to-expiry discount factors and source identities, conditional-model/exercise-policy identities, and CRN identity. Every state revalues the raw underlying swap at expiry. The strike is the underlying fixed rate; payer/receiver is its contractual side. Contractual leg descriptors must agree across states. Forward/index information may be known at the terminal node, never after that node's exact valuation cutoff. No volatility surface, empirical tree, stochastic path, or exercise boundary is inferred.

Terminal intrinsic value is `max(clean_underlying_at_expiry,0)`. Long option value is `sum(probability * expiry_discount * intrinsic)`; short is its negative. Zero intrinsic expires. Cash settlement supports the **collateralized swap-value policy**: terminal cash equals intrinsic divided by the supplied expiry-to-settlement collateral discount factor. Thus delayed cash carries the same expiry PV. This is an explicit policy, not a claim to reproduce every ISDA settlement matrix or par-yield/realized-annuity convention.

Physical settlement at expiry emits only the exercised, mapped underlying future legs, weighted by the supplied conditional probabilities. It emits no intrinsic cash payment. Delivered position and legal netting-set IDs are mandatory. The output legs remain Pricing projections; a physical observed election or realized cash settlement requires separately supplied evidence and integration. Bermudan/American exercise is unsupported.

## Raw exposure and European expiry handoff

Each CSA scenario/date node contains every raw mapped trade and uses exactly the same clean swap/option pricers. Quoted exposures or sensitivity-only substitutes are not accepted. Native admission checks contractual descriptors across nodes, exact scenario/currency/time, payment timing and complete maturity/settlement tails.

A pre-expiry option is `Trade::EuropeanSwaption`. At expiry it becomes `Trade::ExpiredEuropean` with one complete, immutable supplied terminal state, an election source/revision, and the same option mapping slot. The expiry node is mandatory when crossed during the run. The selected state and election cannot change subsequently.

For physical exercise, the handoff carries the raw delivered swap with its mandatory delivered position ID, unchanged contractual legs/notional/strike, and the declared netting-set ID. Short physical options reverse the delivered swap side. Clean exposure is replaced by the current raw underlying swap value; the original option is not valued a second time. Unexercised options cannot deliver a swap. For cash settlement, no underlying is allowed; the outstanding cash claim uses its exact current collateral discount curve and disappears according to explicit before/after settlement timing. A cash discount route on physical delivery is rejected.

## Legal buckets, margin and collateral conservation

Every trade maps explicitly to entity, counterparty, currency, contract revision, netting set and reviewed legal identity. `enforceable_netting=true` permits signed aggregation within that reviewed bucket. Otherwise each trade remains an independent bucket, even if netting-set labels match. Mixed legal reviews in one bucket fail. Opening collateral cannot be guessed across multiple buckets: supply separate requests or zero opening balances.

VM is signed cash collateral: positive means received, negative means posted. Received and posted segregated IM are separate nonnegative balances. Static opening IM is a supplied reviewed policy input; this component does not calibrate or dynamically recompute IM. Segregated received IM is not reusable for funding and is excluded from unsecured exposure until the reviewed default waterfall applies it. Received VM reuse for funding is an explicit boolean.

VM target is `V-receive_threshold` above that threshold, `V+post_threshold` below the negative post threshold, and zero otherwise. Calls equal target less settled VM and outstanding pending calls. MTA, calendar-day settlement lag, exact due date and per-node settlement availability are explicit. Outstanding calls prevent duplicate calls. An outage leaves due calls pending until an admitted available node. Collateral remuneration settles in cash using each interval's opening balances, supplied signed rate and day count; it does not silently capitalize or convert IM into VM. Received-IM interest and returns are recorded separately as custodian cash.

Complete tails require final collateral return or explicit default closeout. Tail return cancels remaining open calls and returns VM/IM; unavailable final settlement fails. At each bucket, opening stock plus every signed collateral movement must equal residual stock. Default cancels unsettled calls before margin settlement on the default date. No business-day calendar, collateral securities, FX, cross-currency setoff, collateral rehypothecation right or legal opinion is inferred.

## Default waterfall and separate clean/XVA output

Only counterparty default is supported. Default date, closeout date, legal/replacement-value policy, unsecured recovery, posted-VM return recovery, posted-IM return recovery, posted-collateral setoff and received-IM availability are explicit. Default/closeout nodes and complete tails are mandatory. Closeout revalues raw trades at the closeout node.

Original v1 requests remain readable and executable under their prior supported scope. Selecting `default.mpor` requires `model_version="derivative-contracts-2"`; v1 with that new policy fails with an explicit selection/rebuild error. Without the reviewed policy, the original strict-intermediate-payment/exercise rejection remains. Neither version infers legal early termination or own-default/DVA mechanics.

### Native unpaid obligations and exercise during MPOR (v2)

`DefaultPolicy.mpor` is a reviewed `MporPolicy` with its own identity/revision, `claim_measure` equal to the path measure, `carry_policy="nominal_no_interest"`, and `exercise_rights_policy="preserve_contractual_european_to_closeout"`. Nominal no-overdue-interest carry and preservation of exercise rights are explicit legal/contract choices, not inferred universal bankruptcy rules. Overdue interest, penalty accrual, pre-default arrears, alternative termination/exercise rules and own-default remain outside this policy.

Every coupon, exercise and settlement date within default-to-closeout must be an admitted raw-trade node. Each cash event is identified by mapped `position_id`, native `event_id` and `payment_ordinal`. Event IDs are `fixed:<period_id>`, `floating:<period_id>`, and `option_cash:<selected_state_id>`. Instructions contain **no cash amount**: they declare either `retain_to_closeout`, or `settle_on_node` with an admitted due-or-later date and settlement-evidence identity. Settlement requires declared availability and occurs once before that node's closeout waterfall. Missing, duplicate, unmatched or unused instructions fail. A failed settlement must remain an explicitly retained claim; the engine does not invent a receipt from the scheduled date.

The native pricer reconstructs due cash from the mapped dated contracts. Fixed cash follows notional/rate/day count; indexed cash uses the supplied reset/observation arithmetic. For Pricing paths, captured claims retain the Pricing rate-source identity. For Physical paths, Pricing projections cannot be relabeled: actual coupon arithmetic must use observed fixings or a supplied `physical_index_paths` entry containing **index observations, source revisions and a Physical path identity**, with unchanged mapped coupon terms. Physical conditional observations must explicitly declare Physical measure and information available at the due-node cutoff. Publication/reset/coverage/calendar domains still apply. Physical cash-settled option amounts are contractual calculations on the reviewed single-state expiry clean value; retained election, exercise and discount identities disclose that valuation basis rather than claiming an observed market transaction.

Signed unpaid receipts and obligations survive contractual maturity and are retained through closeout. At a Before-payments node, due Pricing cash embedded in the raw clean mark is subtracted from remaining replacement value. The captured measure-specific claim is then added once, unless an explicit settlement instruction paid it. At an After-payments node, the raw clean mark already excludes the due cash. Default-day After timing excludes payments processed before default; default-day Before permits their capture. This preserves the distinction even when Physical fixing amounts differ from Pricing projections.

Exposure and closeout output explicitly partition `clean_value`, `replacement_after_due_obligations`, `unpaid_obligation_claim`, and `total_closeout_claim`. The waterfall receives only remaining replacement plus unpaid signed claims. `PathResult.obligations` retains native amount, dates, contract/source/measure, disposition, actual settlement date or inclusion in closeout. After closeout, neither old contractual rights nor unpaid claims generate a second exposure or cash payment.

European exercise inside MPOR uses the existing single-state native handoff under the declared rights-preservation policy. `mpor_exercises` records the reviewed election, selected state, calculated Pricing intrinsic, delivery identity and netting mapping. Cash exercise creates only the contractual settlement claim; physical exercise transfers the underlying rights once and creates **no intrinsic cash payment**. Subsequent delivered-swap coupons can become unpaid obligations under the original option mapping slot, retaining delivered position and election identity. Legal bucket rules govern whether signed obligations offset across trades; no netting is inferred from matching dates.

The complete native event/observation work remains bounded at 250000 across raw pricing and MPOR capture, with aggregate 32 MiB immutable metadata admission. Compiled maps avoid repeated linear instruction/date searches. Full maturity, coupon, option-settlement and recovery/closeout tails remain required.

For positive replacement value, received VM is applied first, then legally available segregated received IM; the residual is an unsecured counterparty claim. Excess received VM is returned once; excess received IM is returned by the custodian. Posted collateral return claims use their own supplied recovery fractions. Received VM already held is not emitted again as closeout cash. For negative replacement value, reviewed posted-collateral setoff reduces the obligation; unused posted collateral has separate return recoveries. All remaining posted/received stocks are closed once. Subsequent exposure rights are extinguished.

Pricing paths produce separate `clean_value`, discounted counterparty/posted-return credit loss (`cva`), and a supplied-spread funding adjustment (`fva`). Funding cost is the left-endpoint settled posted VM plus posted IM, less explicitly reusable received VM, multiplied by supplied signed spread, exact year fraction and endpoint discount. This is a disclosed deterministic interval convention, not a market-calibrated total-XVA model. Own DVA, dynamic IM/MVA, nonlinear funding and capital/KVA are unavailable. Physical scenario paths retain modeled movements and losses but do not become risk-neutral CVA/FVA values. No allowance, chargeoff, accounting designation, GL posting or regulatory-capital consequence is derived.

## Bounds, identity and compatibility

Actual `currency_units` are mandatory; currencies are three uppercase letters. Monetary values are finite and bounded by the shared `1e15` domain. At most 4096 periods per leg, 8192 exact discount points, 256 European states, 256 legal trades, 256 scenario paths and 4096 nodes per path are admitted. Combined raw-leg/observation work is at most 250000 per derivative operation. Direct swap, option and CSA immutable raw metadata is capped at 32 MiB; identities are control-free and at most 128 bytes. Date domains are at most 36600 days. These component bounds are not an aggregate process RSS guarantee.

Model/schema changes require explicit input/cache identity rebuilds. Contract, index basis, path, collateral discount policy/source, exercise model/policy, CRN, legal review, opening state, scenario and valuation ordering are preserved in typed requests/results. Integrators must include the complete immutable request in graph/cache identity, preserve fixed base OAS and shared CRN, retain full final-date tails, and independently verify persisted journals. No legacy default, existing saved economics or Python fallback changes are made here.

## Independent examples and checks

`examples/models/derivative-contract-1.json`: N=360, ACT/360 over ten days, fixed 5%, indexed 10%, DF=1. Fixed cash is -0.5, floating cash +1; payer clean value=0.5 and par rate=10%. Principal exchange is zero.

`derivative-option-1.json`: equal terminal weights, expiry DF=.99. Payer underlying at 10% has value=.5; at 2% has value=-.3. Long European value=`.5*.99*.5=.2475`. Only the positive state settles. The fixtures separately verify delayed cash carry and physical future-leg conservation.

`derivative-mpor-2.json`: default on January 3, contractual coupon on January 11, closeout on January 12. Native fixed cash -0.5 and floating cash +1 remain unpaid after maturity. Remaining replacement value is zero; unpaid claim is 0.5. With supplied 40% recovery, closeout cash is 0.2 and credit loss is 0.3. V1 policy selection rejects; explicit v2 succeeds.

`derivative-netting-1.json`: the same payer swap calls +.5 VM immediately and returns it when coupons settle. Net margin cash/stock changes are zero; clean=.5, credit loss=0 and supplied funding cost=0. Other independent tests cover unequal leg frequencies, exact intraday information, negative coupons/remuneration, lag/outage/pending calls, gross margin without legal netting, both closeout directions, segregated IM, complete-tail admission and European expiry replacement.

## Primary sources and scope

- [ISDA 2021 Interest Rate Derivatives Definitions](https://www.isda.org/2021/10/04/2021-isda-interest-rate-derivatives-definitions/) distinguishes confirmed economic terms and conventions. This component requires explicit terms rather than inventing a convention.
- [ISDA collateralized cash-price settlement practice](https://www.isda.org/2018/11/26/market-practice-change-for-settlement-of-eur-swaptions-to-collateralized-cash-price/) motivates an explicitly named alternative to older cash-settlement approximations; the implementation's delayed-cash carry policy is separately disclosed above.
- [ISDA settlement matrix](https://www.isda.org/book/isda-definitions-settlement-matrix-for-early-termination-and-swaptions/) reinforces that legal settlement method is a declared contract choice. Full matrix replication is not claimed.
- [QuantLib rate-curve material](https://www.quantlib.org/slides/rate-curves.pdf) describes distinct discounting and forwarding curves. Exact supplied factors are used here; no bootstrapping is added.
- [BCBS counterparty-credit-risk guidelines](https://www.bis.org/bcbs/publ/d588.pdf) motivates reviewed legal netting, collateral operational risk, exposure and counterparty-loss separation. This is not regulatory compliance or an automatic capital engine.
- [Bilateral closeout research](https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.3355) identifies replacement closeout and settlement conventions as material choices. This component limits own-default and requires an explicitly reviewed MPOR obligation/exercise policy rather than inferring it.

# Frozen covariate drivers to realized credit ledger

`driven-credit-ledger-1` is a native preparation contract. It composes the frozen `credit-covariate-1` physical hazard projection with explicit realized path/accounting policies and a raw `credit-path-ledger-1` specification. Rust performs the projection and ledger admission. Preparation emits no financial journal rows; protocol 5 execution evaluates each financial batch once in staged output. Existing supplied-hazard path, protocol 4 credit and legacy daily routes retain their own economics.

The public Rust interface is `driven_credit::prepare(&Request) -> Result<Prepared,String>`, with `prepare_with_limits` for a caller's smaller native position/work tier. `Prepared` contains the raw protocol 5 `ledger` request and a `receipt`. Compilation validates full baseline/scenario/reverse coverage, ownership, opening anchors, account reconciliation and ledger admission before preparation returns. Per-batch accounting domain, conservation and claim checks remain the execution gate. A structurally prepared request is not an independently verified published ledger.

## Inputs and ownership

The strict request contains schema, execution use policy, currency unit, as-of ordinal, raw specification, deadline and explicitly identified runs/batches. Each batch contains exactly one position/path/binding, its account, a frozen projection request and an accounting template. This initial preparation tier does not group heterogeneous hazards into a shared multi-position path contract.

`AccountingTemplate` uses the existing `DayMapping`, `PathBinding`, `DrawStream`, `PathOpening` and `PathBoundary` types. Its `PathTemplate` retains source revision, original opening amounts and live state, boundaries, CRN stream and path key. Its `PolicyInterval` contains an exact end date/time, three signed accrual rates, LGD, CCF, interest-recovery fractions and complete per-origin recovery tails. There is no hazard field. Unknown fields reject, so a caller cannot substitute, multiply or overwrite native projected hazards.

The position, scenario, physical measure, as-of midnight, reporting endpoint, model-policy ID and interval counts must match the projection. Every policy interval must end at precisely the corresponding driver endpoint; missing driver intervals, unavailable covariates and incomplete paths reject in the shared projector. Projection uses supplied frozen feature transforms and parameter identities. The fitted model checksum and the raw driver vintage are retained. No P-to-Q conversion, driver forecast, missing feature substitution or clipping of excessive projected hazard is inferred.

The shared projector produces annual continuous intensities. For driver interval ending at time `b`, the path end is `(b - as_of) / (365 * 86400)` years under ACT/365 elapsed seconds. The existing path engine integrates the competing hazard clock across those boundaries without redrawing at a driver change. A realized account's principal, commitment, accrued rights and basis remain absolute amounts; no second probability factor is applied. Scheduled repayment/draw/maturity and reviewed allowance/chargeoff/recovery policy continue to belong to their explicitly supplied path/accounting contracts.

The complete serialized CRN stream and opening account state must be byte-identical for a position across baseline, scenarios and severity-reverse runs. Both supplied uniforms and the versioned counter stream are preserved, including stream revision, seed and integer path key. Driver paths may change hazard/event timing, while common draws remain common.

## Execution use and evidence

`use_policy.kind = adoption` requires every projector to request adoption output and pass its native model eligibility gate. `research_analytical_only` requires a nonempty reviewed identity and rationale, and every projector must request analytical-only output. Mixing these modes rejects. Research preparation explicitly reports `research_only=true` and `adoption_output=false`; it cannot silently become an adoption result.

Every receipt retains the complete normalized typed raw request, every projected interval and its driver/model revision, plus run/severity/account/batch/position/path identity. It reports preparation bounds, actual shared projection work and admitted ledger work. `empirical_validation` and `regulatory_compliance` remain false in both modes: numerical adoption eligibility does not establish that caller-supplied histories are authentic, representative or independently approved. Production publication must retain raw inputs and receipt, independently recompute driver hazards and realized/accounting outcomes, replay persisted GL, and pass immutable publication/deadline/cancellation gates. Prepared hazards alone are not source truth.

The shared estimation likelihood and feature transform assumptions are documented in [credit covariate calibration](credit-covariate.md), with the [ETH piecewise constant hazard reference](https://www.stat.ethz.ch/CRAN/web/packages/eha/vignettes/tpchreg.html). Exact event-time integration follows the shared [credit path model](credit-path.md) and its [temporal Gillespie reference](https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1004579). These modeling references do not establish regulatory accounting approval.

## Bounds and validation

The initial preparation tier admits at most 4,096 generated batches across all runs, 50,000 aggregate driver intervals, 64 MiB serialized input/prepared request, and a conservative 20 million preparation work bound (`serialized input bytes + 256 * driver interval count`). Actual shared projection work also cannot exceed 20 million. These are component ceilings, not measured 60,000-position portfolio acceptance. The underlying ledger's 60,000-position/90-million-work maximum remains a separate upper bound; caller limits may be smaller. Full recovery tails, source metadata and common-draw payloads count in input admission before projection or receipt cloning.

Local deadline checks cover serialization, per-batch projection and preparation stages. Each projector receives the smaller of its valid supplied timeout and the remaining request budget. Existing native cooperative control checkpoints remain active. The root execution and publication watchdog must include preparation, streamed replay, verification and final publication; this module does not establish a process-wide RSS cap or interrupt arbitrary arithmetic inside every shared primitive.

Independent native fixtures cover the synthetic macro fit with hazards 0.25 and 0.5 per year, a common half-day-baseline default draw, contingent EAD draw and complete recoveries. Baseline/stress final cash and equity are 66.05 and 66.025, with no extra modeled-loss deduction. A separate two-interval hand case crosses a driver boundary using one waiting draw and reconciles exact earned interest. Fixtures reject injected hazard fields, altered coefficient checksums, unavailable drivers, calendar/policy/measure mismatch, scenario CRN changes, missing reverse coverage, opening reconciliation failure and bounded/cancelled requests. The example is explicitly synthetic research input; fixtures are not empirical model validation or full publication acceptance.
