# Supplied-fixing floating coupons

`portfolio_model_core::floating_rate::evaluate` implements the bounded,
versioned `floating-rate-1` arithmetic stage of
[corporate/commercial issue #15](https://github.com/beauschwab/model-portfolio-sim/issues/15).
It calculates contractual interest from immutable **supplied observed fixings**.
There is no default index, hidden three-month mapping, rate projection, inferred
missing fixing, benchmark fallback or Python financial backend.

This stage does not integrate the new model into the existing corporate graph,
strategy unit library or ledger. Future forward-rate emission remains work under
[market-model issue #10](https://github.com/beauschwab/model-portfolio-sim/issues/10).
Existing saved floating contracts retain their historical model until explicitly
converted and rebuilt; this analysis helper never reinterprets them.

## Inputs and provenance

`FloatingRateRequest` contains `schema="floating-rate-1"`, `position_id`, an
uppercase three-letter `currency`, `monetary_unit="currency_units"`, and
`direction="receipt"|"payment"`. Principal amounts are nonnegative actual currency
units. The direction determines the interest cashflow sign; negative interest
rates can reverse that cashflow economically.

Required identities include `reference_calendar:{id,revision}` and
`fixing_snapshot:{id,revision}`. The index descriptor has `index_id` and one of:

| Kind | Required descriptor | Supported calculation |
|---|---|---|
| `term` | Explicit `tenor_months` | `term_simple` |
| `published_average` | Explicit `average_calendar_days` | `term_simple` |
| `overnight` | Neither tenor nor averaging window | `daily_simple` or `daily_compounded` |

Index tenor and the interest/payment period are independent. The supplied fixing
determines the rate; the descriptor identifies what that fixing represents. This
helper cannot certify that a supplied benchmark rate actually corresponds to its
declared tenor or administrator.

Each fixing has `fixing_id`, `revision`, matching `index_id`, `value_ordinal`,
`publication_unix_seconds` and a decimal annual `rate` (`0.05` means 5%). The
request supplies an exact `publication_cutoff_unix_seconds`. Future value dates,
unavailable publications, duplicate fixing IDs, wrong indices and missing fixing
references fail. Only one selected immutable revision may exist per fixing ID.
The result retains the snapshot, calendar, cutoff, index descriptor and each
selected fixing/revision in observation order.

Each `FloatingPeriod` has `period_id`, half-open accrual dates `[start_ordinal,
end_ordinal)`, an independent `payment_ordinal`, a calculation, actual day count,
margin, margin treatment and optional index/all-in bounds. Payment may precede an
unadjusted accrual end under a supplied preceding/modified-following convention;
the arithmetic does not move either date or change interest for that reason.

For `term_simple`, `reset_cutoff_unix_seconds` is mandatory. It must be at or before
both period start and the valuation cutoff, and the selected fixing must have been
published by that exact reset time. A fixing published at 08:00 is unavailable for
a 07:00 reset on the same day. Overnight periods must leave the term reset cutoff
null and use their individual observed fixing publications.

The principal path and observation mapping are separate:

```
principal: [{start_ordinal, end_ordinal, amount}, ...]
observations: [{interest_start_ordinal, interest_end_ordinal,
                observation_start_ordinal, observation_end_ordinal,
                fixing_id}, ...]
```

Principal intervals and interest intervals must each fully and contiguously cover
the period without overlaps. Overnight fixing value dates match observation-start
dates. Observation dates cannot be after their corresponding interest-start date.
The caller supplies `lookback_business_days`, `observation_shift`, and
`complete_observation_coverage=true`. Shifted observation intervals must themselves
be contiguous. Weekend-start periods can use the preceding business day's fixing.

**Calendar/lookback mapping is supplied, not verified here.** The helper checks
dates, identity, availability and coverage. It does not generate government
securities business days, verify calendar content, or prove that a declared
business-day lookback produced the supplied observation dates. The result
explicitly returns `calendar_mapping_verified=false`. Production calendar mapping
needs its own native validation and source identity before integration.

## Arithmetic and contractual choices

Use `act360`, `act365_fixed` or `act_act_isda` explicitly. The shared actual-day
fraction helper handles real dates and ISDA year-boundary splitting. No reporting
month is interpreted as thirty days.

For each observation, select the annual rates in this order:

```
index = apply(index_floor, index_cap, supplied_rate)
all_in = apply(all_in_floor, all_in_cap, index + margin)
adjusted_index = all_in - margin
```

Bounds apply to annual interval rates; they do not constrain the final compounded
effective period rate. No bound is inferred when its value is null. This ordering
keeps index bounds distinct from all-in bounds and makes the treatment of margin
under a binding all-in cap/floor explicit.

`term_simple` holds one selected in-advance term/average fixing over the complete
period. `daily_simple` applies each selected daily fixing to the principal actually
outstanding within its interval, including principal changes inside a weekend.
Without observation shift, both methods calculate:

```
interest = sum(principal_on_subinterval * all_in_rate * interest_year_fraction)
```

With observation shift, daily simple uses constant principal and:

```
interest = principal * sum(adjusted_index * observation_year_fraction
                           + margin * interest_year_fraction)
```

For `daily_compounded`, principal must remain constant within the period. Only
**rate compounding** is supported. The `balance_compounded` calculation is
explicitly rejected. Rates are compounded over each business-day interval; a
three-day weekend interval has one factor `1+r*3/360`, rather than three separate
one-day factors. No implicit capitalization of accrued interest or compounding
across payment periods occurs.

Let `w_i` be interest-date weights without shift and observation-date weights with
shift; let `a_i` always be actual interest-date weights. Then:

```
simple margin:     interest/principal = product(1 + adjusted_index_i*w_i) - 1
                                       + margin*sum(a_i)
compounded margin: interest/principal = product(1 + all_in_i*w_i) - 1
```

The simple margin remains uncapitalized and accrues over actual interest dates,
even when the index's observation weights shift. Each compound factor must be
positive and finite. The implementation accumulates `ln_1p(rate*weight)` and
uses `exp_m1` for the resulting interest factor, preserving interest near zero
where subtracting one from a rounded product would erase it.

Changing principal is rejected for compounded rates and shifted daily-simple
calculations because allocating shifted/cumulative interest across changing
principal requires further contractual rules. Separate balance compounding and
noncumulative rate implementations can be added under explicit model identities.

`effective_annual_rate` equals unsigned-direction interest divided by the sum of
principal times actual interest year fractions. It is null for zero principal.
Cashflow direction affects `interest_amount`, not the reported annual coupon.
Internal calculations are unrounded; invoice/ledger rounding remains a downstream
explicit policy.

## Admission and failure

Standalone validation applies before result calculation:

- 1..=4096 periods; 1..=250000 fixings; at most 250000 combined principal and
  observation intervals across the request.
- Actual dates in Gregorian years 1..9999; each interval and payment displacement
  is bounded to 36600 days. Lookback metadata admits 0..=366 business days.
- Each identity is nonempty, control-free and at most 1024 bytes; aggregate checked
  metadata is at most 32 MiB. Supplied UTF-8 IDs/revisions retain their exact text.
- Principal and each result interest amount are finite and at most `1e15` actual
  currency units in absolute value; no hidden monetary scaling is applied.
- Publication cutoffs are UTC Unix seconds in 1970..9999. Nonfinite rates/margins,
  inverted bounds, nonpositive compound factors and numerical overflow fail.

These are component/work limits, not an aggregate process RSS guarantee.
Calculations intersect two ordered interval lists in linear work; no path-by-day
tensor or new random draws are created. Failure returns no successful result.
The surrounding native transport retains its own JSON/input and deadline bounds.

## Independent validation and sources

`core/tests/floating_rate.rs` checks hand-calculated simple and compounded coupons,
Friday/weekend weights, observation shifts, distinct index/all-in caps and floors,
simple/compounded margin, principal changes inside an observation interval, term
tenor/provenance retention, intraday reset availability, payment before accrual end,
negative/near-zero rates, zero principal, coverage/source failures and independent
metadata/monetary/work admission. Run:

```
cargo test --manifest-path packages/portfolio-model-core/Cargo.toml --test floating_rate
```

Primary sources informed the explicit conventions and limitations:

- [ARRC in-advance term/average conventions](https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/Microsites/arrc/files/2021/Term_SOFR_Avgs_Conventions.pdf)
  distinguish forward-looking term rates from published averages and explain
  in-advance observation and independent interest-period/benchmark tenor choices.
- [ARRC syndicated-loan arrears conventions](https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/Microsites/arrc/files/2020/ARRC_SOFR_Synd_Loan_Conventions.pdf)
  distinguish simple, compound-balance and compound-rate methods, describe
  lookbacks without observation shift, daily floors and principal-change limits.
- [ARRC technical appendices](https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/Microsites/arrc/files/2020/ARRC-Syndicated-Loan-Conventions-Technical-Appendices.pdf)
  describe interest/observation date weights and alternative compounding methods.
- [NY Fed SOFR methodology](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/additional-information-about-reference-rates)
  distinguishes value/publication dates and specifies business-day compounding,
  weekend/holiday simple weights and ACT/360 for its published averages/index.

Conventions are contractual choices, not a claim that every supported combination
is an ARRC recommendation. These tests validate arithmetic, not empirical rate
projection, administrator data authenticity, full graph/ledger behavior or issue
#15 completion. New production coupon models require explicit cache/model identity,
library rebuilds, historical compatibility, fixed base OAS, shared CRN and separate
end-to-end ownership/publication validation.
docs/models/funding-contracts.md:
# Dated funding and exclusive repo collateral

`portfolio-risk-native::funding_contract::evaluate(&FundingRequest)` implements
schema `funding-contract-1`, model version `funding-contracts-1`. The native JSON
route uses `{schema, threads, request}`; the inner request has the same schema.
Rust owns the arithmetic. The module is split into immutable `types`, admission
`validation`, collateral arithmetic, a chronological `timeline`, and orchestration.

This is an explicit contractual/scenario capability. It preserves the legacy
spread-to-short, constant-principal rollover model under its existing identity.
Adoption requires new contract inputs and a rebuilt graph/unit library. A
successful component test is not deployment, empirical calibration or full #21
integration acceptance.

## Dates, direction and rates

Each contract identifies its entity, counterparty, currency, contractual source,
rate path, lending/borrowing direction, funding kind, start and actual maturity.
Supported kinds are interbank, unsecured funding and repo. Currency must equal
the request currency; FX conversion and same-entity counterparties are rejected.

`New` produces an initial cash advance and an explicit lender-perspective
origination fee. `Opening` receives existing principal without repeating that
advance or historical fee. Opening contracts supply only remaining interest
periods; their first remaining accrual anchor can follow original origination but
must be at/before asof. Historical settlements are rejected rather than replayed.
Remaining full coupons retain their original accrual anchors. They are cash
settlements, not automatically the current day's earned interest.

Interest periods reuse `term_enhancements::indexed::ContractPeriod`. Fixed coupons
and explicitly supplied observed/conditional projected index paths therefore
share actual day counts, index tenor, exact UTC reset/selection cutoffs, immutable
source revisions, lookbacks, compounding, margin and cap/floor conventions.
Observed publications cannot follow the declared valuation snapshot. Projected
information must be available at its selected reset/observation. No future
published fixing, front-quarter index proxy, or rate fallback is synthesized.
Indexed business-day mappings remain supplied and are explicitly reported as
unverified. See [term-enhancements.md](term-enhancements.md) for exact equations
and supported conventions.

Funding principal is a bullet: final principal and the last coupon settle at
actual maturity. Intermediate coupon cash and fees are separate. From the lender
perspective, a new advance has negative principal cash, later repayment positive
principal and interest. Borrowing reverses these cash signs. Signed and zero
interest are supported; principal and total claim-factor domains remain bounded.
There is no OAS solve or random-number generation here.

## Partial rollover and funding access

A maturity election can request a positive principal amount no larger than the
old principal. Available access requires separately identified `New` replacement
terms starting at the old maturity, with explicit replacement coupon/spread,
counterparty and collateral policy. Entity, currency and lending/borrowing
direction remain compatible; counterparty switching is explicitly represented by
the replacement input. Old principal is repaid in full, then the new principal is
advanced. The same-day net funding reflects those two distinct contracts.

One replacement generation is supported. Recursive future rollover is rejected.
An unavailable-access election omits executable replacement terms and reports the
requested amount as a funding-access shortfall. It does not remove, delay or
reduce the old contractual maturity obligation. Automatic constant-balance
extension is absent. Rollover is a modeled election and rejects `Contractual`
measure; its scenario/assumption/source must be explicit.

## Collateral inventory and margin

Repo requires a collateral agreement, eligible asset classes, owned inventory,
exactly dated valuation/haircut snapshots and initial pledge quantities. Unsecured
and interbank rows reject attached repo collateral semantics. Negative haircuts,
haircuts of one, and implicit initial-margin ratios are unsupported. This policy
uses haircut `h` as a discount from collateral market value:

```
eligible collateral credit = sum(quantity * market_price * (1 - haircut))
required exposure = principal + (include_accrued_interest ? supplied_accrued_right : 0)
```

The accrued right and its immutable source come from the state-aware coordinator;
the collateral module does not infer them from a whole coupon or haircut.
Required exposure must be nonnegative. Initial eligible credit must cover it.

Global inventory records owner, currency, asset class, quantity and quantity
encumbered outside this request. That external encumbrance is never released by
one of this request's contracts. Pledges belong to the cash borrower: own entity
for a borrowing book, counterparty for a lending/reverse-repo book. Received
collateral is rejected as pledgeable inventory. No legal title transfer,
rehypothecation permission or re-use right is inferred.

All contract actions run on one chronological timeline. Opening holdings are
established first; old maturity release/liquidation occurs before separately
supplied new pledges on the same date; later margin transfers follow. This allows
explicit same-day refinancing while rejecting incompatible overlapping pledges.
Each asset's pledged quantities plus outside encumbrance cannot exceed its owned
remaining quantity. Report-horizon encumbrance is captured independently from the
complete tail closing inventory.

Margin snapshots explicitly supply changed prices, haircut and eligibility.
Every held/delivered asset requires a mark. Ineligible held collateral contributes
zero credit; new deliveries must be eligible. Positive quantity transfers deliver
owned collateral; negative quantities return that contract's existing pledge.
Substitution is an explicit delivery/return pair. Releases execute first within a
failure-atomic request, followed by deliveries and a final coverage check. No
cash funding is generated by these security movements.

The minimum transfer value controls whether a deficit creates a material call.
The audit retains required exposure, before/after eligible credit, call value and
unmet value even when a small gap falls below the transfer threshold. `Reject`
fails a material unmet call; `Report` retains the explicitly disclosed breach.
With management access unavailable, proposed transfers remain pending and do not
change encumbrance. Future maturity payment and contractual release remain in the
projection. Management outage is not automatically a settlement-system failure
or borrower default. Same-date margin/default ambiguity is rejected: margin
actions must precede default.

Snapshot ID/revision pairs cannot be reused with different contents in one
request. Stable inventory-index reduction and movement ordering preserve
repeatable output. No collateral cash, external fee, or funding principal is
added for an ordinary pledge, substitution, margin transfer or release.

## Counterparty default and realization

The separate default policy supports `Physical` cash-lender counterparty claims
before maturity. New origination and default on the same day are rejected. An
opening already-defaulting claim can be recognized at asof with its explicit
initial holdings. Own-entity borrowing default, counterparty-lender default,
cross-contract legal netting and closeout enforceability are unsupported.

The default source supplies actual nonnegative accrued-interest claims, separate
economic principal/interest loss amounts, immutable recovery review and complete
dated residual recovery schedules. Unsupported signed prepaid accrued rights at
default are rejected; ordinary signed coupons remain supported. Whole future
coupons are stopped, including principal at contractual maturity; scheduled cash
through the declared default date survives. No allowance, chargeoff timing,
accounting P&L or legal liability extinguishment is inferred.

A defaulted repo requires explicit collateral realization. All held collateral
remains encumbered until realization. A supplied liquidation mark, sale discount,
cost and principal-first or interest-first waterfall determine the retained
recovery:

```
gross_sale = held market value * (1 - sale_discount)
net_sale = gross_sale - sale_cost
retained = min(net_sale, principal_claim + accrued_interest_claim)
surplus_to_owner = net_sale - retained
```

The contractual haircut is not applied a second time to actual modeled sale
proceeds. Sale cost cannot exceed proceeds. Immediate same-date surplus return is
required; a delayed custodial payable needs a separate reviewed state/policy.
The chosen waterfall allocates the retained amount between principal and
interest, capped by each claim. Funding cash records that retained recovery once.
Gross sale, cost and surplus fields are explanatory audit amounts marked
`cash_already_in_funding_schedule=true`; consumers must not add them as another
funding cash event. The asset inventory is disposed, not merely released for reuse.

Separate conservation holds over the entire declared tail:

```
principal_claim = collateral_principal_recovery + residual_principal_recoveries + economic_principal_loss
accrued_claim = collateral_interest_recovery + residual_interest_recoveries + economic_interest_loss
```

Principal LGD does not include accrued interest and is not an accounting allowance.
Recovery tails may extend beyond both original maturity and report horizon, but
must fit the explicit full-tail domain. The result distinguishes live principal,
gross unsettled default claim, and expected principal recovery after reporting.
The gross default claim still includes economic loss until separate reviewed
accounting/legal recognition; it is not silently written off here.

## Admission, identity and integration

The book admits 1..256 total old plus replacement contracts, at most 4096 assets,
4096 margin steps per contract and 4096 points per principal/interest recovery
tail. A combined 250,000-item budget counts periods, index observations, snapshot
values, allocations, recoveries and timeline actions. Complete dated domains are
bounded to 36,600 days within Gregorian years 1..9999. Monetary/quantity/price
inputs use the shared finite 1e15 admission; products and sums are admitted again.
Metadata IDs/revisions are 1..128 control-free bytes with a combined 32 MiB budget.
The native JSON layer adds its own request/output bounds. These limits do not
constitute an aggregate process RSS cap.

Every contract, rate path, source revision, collateral snapshot, eligibility
policy, loss/recovery review, election, entity, currency and measure belongs in
cache/model identity. Results retain the complete coupon-source audits. Saved
legacy constant-balance economics stay under their historical identity. Model
changes require explicit source preparation and native library/worker rebuilds.
Pricing callbacks or Python financial execution are not used.

The result's schedule is complete through `tail_end_ordinal`; report horizon does
not clip obligations or recoveries. Entity/counterparty lineage, margin calls,
inventory, realization and market-access diagnostics are separate typed outputs.
Native risk, liquidity, NII, daily accounting, capital and FTP must consume these
outputs through their own declared policies. Persisted journal replay remains a
publication gate. This component does not by itself establish those integrated
gates, optimal funding management, empirical rollover calibration or legal rights.

## Independent example and evidence

`examples/models/funding-contract-1.json` is a complete native protocol request.
It advances 100 on January 1, 2026 at 0.36 ACT/360, settles 100 plus interest 1
January 11, then explicitly advances replacement principal 60 at 0.72 until
January 21. Same-day January 11 net lender cash is `100 + 1 - 60 = 41`;
replacement interest is `60 * 0.72 * 10 / 360 = 1.2`. Total net cash is 2.2 and
all cash principal advances/repayments sum to zero.

Initial collateral quantity 112 at price 1 and haircut 0.1 gives credit 100.8.
On January 3, price 0.9 and haircut 0.2 give credit 80.64; supplied accrued claim
0.2 makes the call `100.2 - 80.64 = 19.56`. Explicit delivery of 40 adds credit
28.8, leaving pledged quantity 152 and credit 109.44. The old pledge is released
at maturity before the replacement pledges quantity 70. All tail encumbrance
returns to zero; report-horizon encumbrance remains 152.

`tests/funding_contracts.rs` contains twelve independent fixtures covering
funding signs/fees/zero/negative interest, no re-advance of opening balances,
partial roll and outages, collateral haircut changes/substitution/exclusivity,
outside encumbrance, deterministic output, default losses and delayed tails,
sale/waterfall/surplus and no duplicate cash, strict domains, and the checked-in
example. Existing indexed-coupon fixtures independently gate the reused reset,
compounding and observation-availability arithmetic.

## Primary sources and supported-policy limits

[ICMA's haircut explanation](https://www.icmagroup.org/market-practice-and-regulatory-policy/repo-and-collateral-markets/icma-ercc-publications/frequently-asked-questions-on-repo/21-what-is-a-haircut/)
distinguishes the collateral-value haircut from an initial-margin ratio. The
implementation explicitly chooses the haircut convention and separately models
valuation changes, transfers and realized sale proceeds.

The [Federal Reserve's repo margining research](https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/notes/feds-notes/proportionate-margining-for-repo-transactions-20250214.html)
describes cash/securities exchange, haircuts and variation margin. Negative
haircuts exist in practice; this supported subset rejects them rather than
reinterpreting the sign. Its margin method is a supplied contract policy, not an
assertion of universal market practice.

The [New York Fed collateral schedule](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/domestic-market-operations/monetary-policy-implementation/repo-reverse-repo-agreements/TOMO-Repo-Collateral-Schedule)
contains specific eligibility/margin terms and can change. This model does not
hardcode that facility's terms for arbitrary private repos; callers supply
reviewed, versioned eligibility and haircut snapshots. The
[reference-rate methodology](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/additional-information-about-reference-rates)
distinguishes observation and publication and allows revisions, motivating exact
available-time and immutable fixing identity.

Issue #21 additionally requires native graph risk/runoff and scenario adoption,
daily journal/liquidity/FTP integration with verified publication, supported legal
collateral/closeout policies, scale gates and observed conditional funding-access/
rollover evidence. Those criteria remain open until their own evidence exists.

# Supplied funding and repo product graph

Rust `funding_graph::analyze(&Request)` and immutable `FundingGraph` own the
`funding-product-graph-1` analysis stage of #21. They replay whole-book supplied
P/Q/Q-down/Q-up `funding_contract::FundingRequest` histories, price native cash,
retain the original whole-book OAS and report physical funding/collateral flows.
Whole-book replay preserves the component's exclusive global owned-collateral
inventory; pricing individual contracts through isolated inventories would not.
Public methods are `new`, `request`, `snapshot`, `base_anchor`, `reprice` and
`repriced`. No Python financial execution or backend fallback is introduced.

## Known state and supplied history boundary

`known` is immutable contractual opening/term metadata using `FundingRequest`:
explicit actual currency units, asof/tail, owned inventory, original contracts,
and their initial collateral agreement/pledges/snapshots. It has contractual
measure, maturity exits without elections and empty future margin actions. It
is an anchor template, not an implied financial projection. Indexed conditional
observation slots can retain explicitly Physical/Pricing source metadata; every
executable history supplies its own compatible declared measure and rate sources.
No future observed fixing is synthesized for that template or any history.

Each history includes the full executable native request and its probability and
path ID. Graph scenario IDs and native run IDs are separate retained identities;
history `scenario_id` equals the graph scenario's `run_id`. Measures must be
explicitly P for physical and Q for all pricing roles. No measure is converted
from observed/default behavior. P IDs/weights can differ from Q. Ordered Q path
IDs/weights are identical across all scenarios and both bumps; each role's
probabilities sum to one within `1e-12`, without normalization or path pruning.
Zero-weight paths are still validated and executed. The randomness domain is
`supplied_paired_histories-1`; this graph consumes supplied paired histories and
generates no draws or fitted funding-access/default/rollover behavior.

Every history preserves known static contract identity, opening principal,
origination terms, entity/counterparty, currency, lending/borrowing direction,
funding kind, actual period/payment dates/daycounts/fees, fixed coupon rates and
initial collateral policies/inventory/pledges/marks. Explicit future margin
snapshots/transfers, exits and one separately specified rollover replacement
generation can vary. Indexed conditional observations preserve geometry,
selection/reset convention, descriptor, margin/bounds and calendar policy while
their declared conditional rate/source/path can vary. Observed fixing content
is immutable. Snapshot and observed fixing source ID/revision pairs cannot be
reused with different content anywhere in the graph. Fixed coupons cannot be
quietly treated as scenario-dependent floating rates.

The reused component admits fixed and explicit indexed coupons with observed
publication or conditional information cutoffs. An indexed business-day mapping
is supplied and retained as unverified; arithmetic acceptance does not prove a
calendar/fixing mapping. See [funding-contracts.md](funding-contracts.md) and
[term-enhancements.md](term-enhancements.md) for exact coupon, collateral,
settlement, default and supported-policy conventions.

## Signed funding cash and immutable OAS

PV includes only native Q schedule cash `principal + cash_interest + fees`,
strictly after asof, discounted by supplied collateral DF and
`exp(-base_oas * actual_days / 365)`. Lending receipts are positive; borrowing
liability payments negative. Signed and negative-rate coupon cash remains signed.
The required `after_opening_actions` timing retains asof advance/fee/security
actions in a separate opening report and excludes them from future PV and
`(left,right]` cash reports. Opening contracts are never re-advanced.

The graph's single `book_id` identifies one whole-book base spread.
`oas_target=locked` is required for mixed-direction books or signed directional
future cash. For a homogeneous lending or borrowing book,
`calibrate_positive_cash` targets the positive **magnitude** of future cash in
that direction; borrowing still produces negative signed PV and DV01. The
solver rejects any future event whose net contractual cash opposes the book
direction, even on a zero-weight path. It does not net an old repayment and new
advance into an artificial positive calibration instrument. Bounded log-sum-exp
bisection uses the original base Q histories/curve and [-5,5] OAS interval.

The retained base key contains the complete known dependency and base Q raw
requests, original target/source, base scenario/curve, book/model/paired-history
identity and explicit cash/tail policies. Repricing checks exact dependency
equality, reports `BASE_ANCHOR_CHANGED` when it changes, and never solves a
scenario OAS. Nonbase scenarios, P/down/up histories, input revision and report
boundaries can change while preserving that anchor. The raw request's final
report date must match the graph; report dates are excluded from calibration
identity. `supplied_history_dv01` is a signed central finite difference using
paired Q-down/Q-up cash and native +/- curve bumps with original OAS. It is
conditional supplied-history risk, not an empirical funding spread or legal
collateral-option valuation.

## Cash, collateral, default and full tails

P reports expose signed principal/interest/fees, new advances, maturity principal,
retained/residual recoveries, explicit default claims and reviewed separate
economic principal/interest losses. Margin call/unmet values and rollover
requested/executed/access-shortfall amounts are separate diagnostics. Security
quantity movements are grouped by asset, owner and disposition; quantities in
different assets are never added into a single monetary cash balance.

Ordinary pledge, margin, substitution and release never generate cash/PV. Native
collateral realization cash already contains the retained principal/interest
recovery once. Gross sale proceeds, sale cost, net proceeds and surplus returned
are explanatory amounts, never a second sale cash flow or a second haircut.
Physical reports preserve those audit explanations distinctly from recovery cash.
Failed management-access transfers remain pending, retain the margin breach and
do not erase maturity or collateral release. Rollover requires complete separately
identified replacement terms; unavailable access does not invent new funding or
remove old maturity principal.

The required `complete_economic_cash_collateral_tail` policy retains all explicit
maturity, replacement, recovery and collateral disposition through the supplied
tail, independent of reporting horizon. The native component reconciles each
default's principal and accrued claim separately to recoveries plus supplied
economic loss; it preserves report-date gross default claims rather than
pretending an economic loss is legal/accounting extinguishment. Inventory remains
conserved and tail encumbrance is released/disposed; outside encumbrance is never
released by these contracts. The graph retains full raw/native sources and a
separate physical tail beyond the final report boundary.

Default is inherited as **Physical cash-lender counterparty default only**.
Pricing-measure default requests, own borrowing default and unsupported legal
netting/closeout fail closed. Supported P defaults can be paired with explicitly
different Q maturity histories; their empirical or risk-neutral probability
relation is never inferred. This restriction is not full credit-risk pricing.

Cash interest is truthful native settled cash. Full coupon audits and original
intervals are retained. Uneven overnight compounding and default supplied accrued
claims are not prorated into a claimed daily earned-income measure. Gross daily
recognition plans, effective-yield NII, reviewed allowance/charge-off/journal and
treasury/liquidity/FTP adoption remain separate integration gates.

## Bounds and independent fixtures

Preflight charges every supplied full book before projection: up to 256 old plus
replacement contracts, 4,096 owned assets, 4,096 periods/observations/margin steps/
recovery points per supported component field, 13 scenarios, 128 paths per role,
120 actual report periods and 4,096 runs. Worst-case native cash/audit/source rows
are bounded to 250,000; coupon/observation work, registry scans, action/asset
sorting, calibration passes and ordered per-period security aggregation are
charged against 8 million graph work units. Input byte counting precedes canonical
dependency allocation at 32 MiB; retained raw request/source/result/base identity
uses a 128 MiB capacity estimate. These are component admission bounds, not an
aggregate process RSS or 60,000-position combined workflow gate. Native source
domain/chronological feasibility remains authoritative and failures publish no
successful result.

The [raw synthetic example](../../examples/models/funding-product-graph-1.json)
uses initial repo principal 100, ten-day ACT/360 rate 0.36 and a separately
supplied 60-principal replacement at rate 0.72 for another ten days. Initial
advance -100 is asof; old maturity 101 and replacement advance -60 are distinct
events, followed by final replacement payment 61.2. Collateral discount rate
0.05 and locked OAS -0.05 cancel, so future PV is 102.2. First-period margin call
is `100.2 - 112*0.9*0.8 = 19.56`; delivery of 40 produces report pledge 152.
Both maturity releases remain in the complete tail. This is a hand fixture,
not observed market access, a quote or an empirical calibration.

Focused tests cover cash/sign/fees, original opening anchors, closed-form OAS,
fixed-anchor reprice, separate P default/Q maturity, final-date recovery, sale
cost/surplus once-only cash, margin outage, explicit rollover/no access, supplied
index measures/reset cutoffs, Q pairing, immutable sources and preprojection
work/tail admission. Reference tolerances stay `1e-12` relative and `1e-9` absolute.

[ICMA's haircut explanation](https://www.icmagroup.org/market-practice-and-regulatory-policy/repo-and-collateral-markets/icma-ercc-publications/frequently-asked-questions-on-repo/21-what-is-a-haircut/)
distinguishes collateral-value haircuts from initial-margin ratios; the reused
component chooses the former explicitly and does not apply it again to sale cash.
The [New York Fed reference-rate methodology](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/additional-information-about-reference-rates)
distinguishes publication/observation and revisions, motivating exact cutoffs and
source identity. Those sources do not establish private repo enforceability,
reuse/netting rights or empirical scenario probabilities. Full #21 saved-book,
verified daily journals, liquidity/FTP, legal scope and joint scale acceptance
remain open until independently integrated and validated.

# Native supplied product graph cohort audit

`graph-cohort-audit-1` compares an explicitly supplied representative with an
ordered set of explicitly supplied individual members. Rust invokes the existing
consumer installment, revolving card, mortgage and deposit native product graphs.
It never derives a representative state by averaging member contracts, calibrates
OAS, fits behavioral models, or authorizes cohort publication. A passing diagnostic
demonstrates the requested numerical comparison under the supplied histories;
synthetic histories do not demonstrate observed predictive accuracy.

The complete synthetic example is
[`examples/models/graph-cohort-audit-1.json`](../../examples/models/graph-cohort-audit-1.json).
It compares a two-unit representative deposit with two one-unit members, each with
1000 principal, a supplied .365 annual paid rate and a two-day maturity. The resulting
representative and member-sum liability PVs are 2004, bank cash PVs are -2004, and
full physical earned interest is 4 currency units. The one-day reporting period
contains 2 of that interest; the remaining 2 and the maturity settlement remain in
the full tail. This is an intentionally synthetic mechanics fixture.

## Contract and ownership

`Request` contains mandatory `schema`, `source_revision`, `monetary_unit` and
`cohorts`. `monetary_unit` must equal `currency_units`: amounts are in the native
graph's explicit currency, not implicitly USD or a scaled thousands convention.
Each cohort contains `cohort_id`, one `representative`, ordered `members`, and
`tolerances`. A row has `row_id`, a positive `amount_multiplier`, and a tagged
`graph` with `kind` and the entire raw native `request`. Kinds are
`consumer_installment`, `card`, `mortgage`, and `deposit`. All fields use strict
versioned serde contracts; unknown fields are rejected.

Each row identifies exactly one native position and requires `oas_target.kind`
`locked`, with its original supplied OAS and provenance. Members may have different
locked original OAS values; no representative OAS is imposed on them. The audit
compares amounts, not OAS labels or an average of member OAS. Core monetary/state
quantities remain owned by the selected native product graph. The multiplier
scales only the final signed reported amounts; it does not alter the contract's
state, default intensity, migration mechanics, rate or path probability. Member
amounts are summed in their supplied order without normalization.

Within a cohort the product, currency, as-of date, reporting endpoints, base
scenario, curve/bump contexts, ordered scenarios and applicable terminal/cash
policies must match exactly. The model and paired-history source/revision/randomness
domain must match, as must the ordered path IDs and weights in every scenario and
physical/pricing/down/up role. Consumer subtype and mortgage agency/whole-loan
ownership kind must match. Contracts and supplied behavioral histories can differ
between rows: comparing their effect is the purpose of the diagnostic. Each
component's native admission additionally verifies physical versus pricing measure,
calendar/currency/run ownership, complete source obligations and paired bumps.
The audit does not infer physical hazards from pricing histories or transform P to Q.

## Metrics, signs and tolerances

All native monetary metrics are compared, including PV, the supplied-history
finite-difference DV01 and every reported physical-period/tail field. Names are
deterministic JSON field paths, with zero-based array ordinals, for example
`physical_periods/0/interest_expense` or
`gross_physical_contract_interest/0`. ID fields are retained in source identity
and are excluded from monetary reductions. Every metric label must have exactly
one tolerance; missing, unknown or duplicate labels fail. A single label policy
applies to that metric across the explicitly matched scenarios.

The audit additionally sums every physical-source cash and recognition event,
including opening-date cash, beyond-reporting tails and recoveries after principal
has ended. These metrics are `source_full_cash/principal`,
`source_full_cash/interest`, `source_full_cash/fees`, and
`source_full_gross_interest`. Consumer/card outputs also report
`source_full_default/principal` and `source_full_default/principal_loss`.
These supplementary metrics retain complete physical source coverage where the
component's ordinary period reports end before the source tail. They do not create
extra cashflows or an additional economic loss charge. Mortgage-specific default,
agency advance/buyout and recovery metrics are retained from its complete native
reports. Deposit principal/interest are bank-perspective signed cash; liability PV
and bank cash PV retain their opposite signs.

For representative amount `R` and original-order sum of weighted members `M`,
the signed error is `R-M`, the absolute error is `abs(R-M)`, and a metric passes
when `abs(R-M) <= absolute_amount + relative*abs(M)`. `relative_error` is
`abs(R-M)/abs(M)` when `M != 0` and null at zero; a nonfinite ratio fails admission.
The tolerance is absolute-plus-relative, not an implicit OR between separate
tests. Negative coupons, signed bank flows and zero member sums keep their signs;
no absolute value is applied to source amounts. Tolerances must be supplied,
finite, nonnegative; relative tolerance is at most 1. Absolute amounts and all
reduced monetary quantities obey the shared 1e15 currency-unit bound.

## Bounds, work and retained evidence

At most 4096 total rows, 256 rows including the representative in a cohort, 10000
tolerance labels per cohort, 32 MiB serialized raw input, and 32 million admitted
work units are accepted. All component domain validators and admitted-cost helpers
run before the first financial generation. Aggregate work charges serialized
input bytes, each component's native generation/reporting cost, and conservative
scenario/tolerance reductions. Component ceilings alone do not imply aggregate
acceptance. A fixture uses structurally admitted but dynamically invalid behavior
and excessive aggregate work to prove the aggregate gate precedes simulation.

Complete native results, raw sources, immutable locked OAS anchors, scaled row
amounts, cohort errors and stable row order remain in `ResultData`. Retained JSON
size is checked incrementally and at completion with a conservative factor of four
within a 128 MiB limit. These are admission budgets, not measured process-wide RSS
limits. Existing cooperative cancellation/deadline checkpoints apply during input
serialization, preflight, rows, native graph work and output serialization. There
are no additional dependencies, normalized survival factors, reseeding operations
or Python financial callbacks.

The result always declares `diagnostic_only=true`, `empirical_validation=false`
and `cohort_publication_allowed=false`, even when every metric passes. Durable
publication, independent persisted comparison, selection/rebuilding of cohorts,
observed predictive validation and 60000-position aggregate scale acceptance are
separate integration gates. This module changes neither legacy product selection
nor existing cohort economics.

## Validation

Dedicated native tests cover independent two-day cash/accrual/PV/bump hand math,
heterogeneous pricing histories with unchanged physical histories, negative
coupons, original per-member OAS retention, exact tolerance and pairing identities,
aggregate admission before generation, cancellation, deterministic replay and all
four native product dispatches. A separate default hand fixture reconciles 2000
defaulted principal, 1100 loss and 900 recovery cash after the reporting endpoint;
a EUR fixture verifies that currency units are not relabeled USD. Product pricing
equations and their independent
validation fixtures remain in the respective product graph/model modules.

# Native consumer graph to dated daily ledger

`graph-dated-ledger-1` connects the admitted scheduled consumer graph to the
existing native dated store and streamed daily runner. It supplies complete
physical event sources and explicit recognition segments. It does not change
saved monthly books, manufacture accounting policy, publish a manifest or adopt
consumer defaults into credit accounting.

## Raw input and native APIs

The request contains `graph: advanced-product-graph-1`, `owners`,
`capture_policy`, `run_mapping`, `monetary_unit`, `recognition_policy` and a raw
`balance-stress-2` `specification`. All are required. Unknown typed fields reject.
Owners and capture policy use the graph's existing source contract; the ledger
recognition policy must explicitly select `supplied_calendar_segments-1`, with
its policy identity/revision and `immediate_earnings` fee policy. Capture admits
no fees, so this latter ledger convention has no financial effect on these
sources. The policy remains recorded rather than silently inferred.

`advanced_ledger::prepare(&Request) -> Result<Prepared, String>` builds a native
graph, captures the complete scheduled source, maps it into a typed
`DatedLedgerRequest` and calls `CompiledDatedLedger::compile`. It returns that
fully validated request plus `SourceReceipt`. `run(&Request, Box<dyn Write +
Send>) -> Result<SourceReceipt, String>` prepares the same source, invokes
`daily::run_dated` and returns the source receipt only after successful streaming.
A failed validation or writer returns an error; the component publishes nothing.

The synthetic request is
[`examples/models/graph-dated-ledger-1.json`](../../examples/models/graph-dated-ledger-1.json).
Its zero-change run is explicitly supplied because the daily specification
requires at least one scenario in addition to baseline. No identity scenario
is invented by the adapter.

## Ownership, measures and run identity

Capture requires one realized physical history of exact weight one for every
position/run. The graph's pricing histories and fixed base OAS remain separate
valuation evidence. No pricing-measure cashflow is posted. Native generation
consumes supplied paired histories; it does not claim fitted behavior or shared
stochastic draws merely because histories have matching path IDs.

`run_mapping` explicitly maps every graph execution `run_id` to a daily
`ledger_scenario_id`. The graph base alone must map to `baseline`, with severity
one. Other mappings preserve each graph scenario's supplied severity. Different
graph economic scenario IDs can explicitly map to one daily scenario at distinct
reverse severities. The daily compiler checks that the resulting economic run
set is exactly baseline, every named daily scenario and every requested reverse
severity. Missing coverage, extra coverage and duplicate economic executions
reject; no reverse-stress interpolation or severity fallback occurs.

The source schedule and accrual-plan selectors retain execution run IDs.
`RunIdentity` retains the mapped ledger scenario name and graph input revision.
The source receipt preserves the original graph economic scenario IDs, curves,
P/Q histories, original loan/cohort identities, raw ledger input, both policies,
owner mapping, native graph results and complete capture.

## Opening anchors and accounting admission

Every graph position must already name an explicit raw ledger position with
`kind="loan"` and the owner's account. Accounts, currency, classification,
research weights, costs, tax, policies and equity remain raw ledger inputs.
The adapter adds omitted `balance`, `opening_accrued`, `book_adjustment` and
`source_id` from the captured native opening. An explicitly supplied value must
match exactly. It neither rescales principal nor plugs equity. The raw request
retains the omitted or supplied original fields; the prepared dated request
contains the derived anchors. Other raw specification defaults and all opening
reconciliation execute in the existing native ledger compiler.

The supported policy is `consumer_simple_interest_par-1` with
`book_basis="par_note_simple_interest"`, `fees="reject"`, performing opening
state, zero opening earned/unrecognized interest and zero fees. Principal and
gross carrying value are par. This is explicitly selected contractual simple
interest recognition, not an effective-yield claim for arbitrary purchase
prices, fee deferral or credit-impaired loans. Full native interest recognition
and settlements are retained for scheduled payments and admitted penalty-free
payoffs. Default, recovery, nonaccrual, delinquency, unrecognized income, fees,
day-zero cash or ambiguous rights reject the entire source. No invalid event
is pruned to make capture succeed.

`CompiledDatedLedger` also rejects overlap with legacy cashflows, credit/default
fields, draw/runoff/floating overlays, sale/collateral policies and unsupported
mark conventions on dated owners. Its existing daily route suppresses legacy
coupon/maturity processing for owned positions. Other unowned ledger positions
can retain their existing processing in the same book.

## Actual-time recognition, rights and lineage

Each captured segment carries an explicit actual ordinal interval and interest
amount. Native simple note interest is `principal × note_rate × selected
day-count fraction`. Cash and recognized interest are separate: a paid interest
amount is assigned FIFO to complete native recognition origins. Partial interest
payments split an origin amount across event plans without duplicating total
income or moving the original earning interval. The dated store distributes
each explicitly supplied segment uniformly within its original calendar
interval, and settlement cash is posted once on the event date.

`CaptureSegment.origin_id` is preserved in `SourceReceipt.capture`, along with
position, run and settlement event identity. The numeric dated-store segment
layout omits that text; the immutable receipt is the retained lookup for origin
lineage. A reused origin ID across runs or positions must be interpreted with
those identities, not globally deduplicated. Full raw sources and policy
revisions must be published alongside generated journals and reports.

The final reporting ordinal minus valuation ordinal must match the raw ledger
horizon. Full contract schedules remain intact beyond that cutoff. Closing
rights distinguish accrued interest receivable and future interest/principal
settlements. Reporting dates are not converted to 30-day product periods;
legacy daily report cadence remains the existing ledger convention.

The existing runner emits detailed postings/lineage for baseline and ordinary
scenarios. Reverse-severity executions retain full source coverage and produce
the runner's existing summary output rather than a new detailed reverse journal.
This adapter does not broaden that reporting contract.

## Bounds, reproducibility and validation

Canonical raw input is admitted with a counting writer before additional owned
copies and is limited to 32 MiB. Prepared request plus full source receipt uses
a conservative four-times serialized retained charge within 128 MiB. Native
graph run/event/work limits and dated-store capacity limits remain additional;
the existing daily tier remains 60,000 positions and 90 million combined work
units. These are component budgets, not an aggregate RSS cap. `run` validates
again when building its executable compiled store. Cooperative checkpoints
remain active in graph paths, source anchoring, compilation and daily execution.

Source regeneration is deterministic for the same complete typed request.
Publication can hash the canonical serialized raw request and receipt; the
adapter supplies complete content rather than a label-only identity. It does
not substitute hashes for collision-safe raw model identity.

Focused tests independently calculate the leap fixture: 1,000 principal at
36.5% ACT/365F earns 29 over January 31–February 29; payment 529 retires 500.
The remaining 500 earns 15.5 over the next 31 days, with final cash 515.5.
Closing cash is 1,044.5, principal is zero and recognized interest is 44.5.
At a day-30 reporting cutoff, cash is 529, principal is 500 and accrued interest
is 0.5, while the complete final settlement remains in the tail. Tests also
check partial-interest origin conservation, explicit scenario/reverse mapping,
zero-change identity, equal-date positions, mixed legacy ownership, conflicting
anchors, policy/domain/overlap rejection and failed streaming. An independent
test decodes and sums emitted journal postings to every trial-balance key and
checks transaction balance. This proves posting/report consistency separately
from the hand-calculated raw source economic fixtures.
The focused native suite passed all 14 fixtures; targeted Clippy passed with
warnings denied. This is source/component validation. Matching release binaries
and public worker/API publication require their separate integration checks.

Full issue acceptance still requires public worker/API immutable publication

# Opt-in per-call native graph execution control

This successor is applied locally as part of 0.29.8; matching official native builds and component checks pass, while complete installed-default acceptance remains pending. It follows the immutable market-indexed book and month-360 proposals. It adds execution control to explicit pricing-only indexed graph owners; it does not change product ABI 8 numerical IDs, layouts, prior `portfolio_term_request` payloads, financial formulas, OAS, CRN, cache keys or tolerances. The standalone analytical adapter keeps its existing caller-Control branch.

Python `runtime={schema:"graph-call-control-1",timeout_ms:integer,cancelled:optional callable}` is execution IO, separate from the graph financial request. Timeouts are 1..3,600,000 milliseconds. A cancellation callback must return bool, must perform bounded IO and must tolerate invocation on a helper thread. The monotonic transport deadline starts before the first lease read; native receives floor remaining milliseconds after initial callback readiness. No graph retains a deadline or callback. Every call needs a fresh token and deadline. An expired creation call cannot make future warm calls expire.

The native-owned execution registry permits 256 one-shot tokens. A token starts Fresh, transitions atomically to Running, and becomes Finished on success, failure or unwind. Signalling Fresh or Running sets its shared atomic flag. Reusing a token, signalling Finished, releasing Running or using unknown tokens refuses. IDs never recycle. Unreleased finished tokens still count toward the cap. This small separate registry has a conservative 128 KiB retained allowance; it does not loosen any graph/cache/work/output budgets. Callers must release tokens after completion.

New capability symbols are `portfolio_graph_runtime_version()->u32` (1), `portfolio_graph_cancel_new()->u64` (0 is refusal), `portfolio_graph_cancel_signal(u64)->i32`, `portfolio_graph_cancel_release(u64)->i32` (1 success, 0 refusal), and `portfolio_term_graph_controlled(const u8*,size_t,u64 token,u64 timeout_ms)->char*`. The input range must remain live for the synchronous call. Result allocations must be freed exactly once by unchanged `portfolio_term_free`. No callbacks or pointers survive the call. All calls use the same captured loaded artifact as the actor. Missing symbols or wrong capability version raise `NATIVE_GRAPH_CONTROL_REQUIRED`, requiring rebuild/restart; no uncontrolled fallback is permitted.

Controlled operations admit only typed indexed creation, matching indexed price, info and clear. Wrong-owner requests, legacy financial requests and controlled drop refuse before acquiring the owner lock. Drop remains an unconditional bounded resource cleanup using the existing entrypoint. Initial generation remains outside the global owner registry lock. Control propagates into the actual Rayon worker scope, existing financial checkpoints, a 1 ms owner try-lock wait loop, bounded output serialization writes and final CString allocation/handoff. JSON parsing, individual allocation and finite mathematical kernels are not interruptible inside a single operation; checks before/after retain bounded cooperative scope. There is no hard interrupt or aggregate RSS guarantee.

A creation result is not handed off until the last check succeeds. Any error or late cancellation/deadline retires its registered unpublished handle; existing actors remain owned on pricing failure. Python polls lease IO every 50 ms during native execution and performs fresh bounded reads after native return and after JSON decoding. Exceptions, non-bool returns and reads exceeding 250 ms fail closed. A stalled daemon IO reader cannot be forcibly stopped; callers must provide bounded IO, and the existing worker/watchdog and final atomic publication checks remain required. Native cancellation tests and process watchdog termination are separate evidence. Python cleanup retires only this invocation's newly created actor through its captured library and frees its response once.

Contained native tests cover token cap/state/reuse, pre-cancel, invalid timeout, actual owner-lock cancellation/deadline, independent concurrent tokens, late handoff rollback, fresh warm deadlines and response compatibility. Installed-default control process tests passed in the first full engine run; that run failed a separate mortgage capital test fixture, so complete default acceptance is being rerun. Durable indexed-book publication remains a separate unapplied proposal. This successor adds no saved-book/library/cohort, Physical, accounting, capital, FTP, empirical, calibration or joint stochastic adoption. Source/reference identities remain exact; runtime fields do not rewrite original supplied OAS or financial parents.

Integration documentation must append these exports to `docs/models/native-contracts.md` and `docs/contracts/native-abi-layouts.md` (additive capability, not new buffer ABI). The schema/architecture checks should inventory the new execution module and Python IO-only helper. Numeric ABI-8 manifest remains unchanged.

A cold public book call may create and then price through two native calls; each receives a fresh per-call runtime. A whole-job deadline/lease must remain enforced by the outer durable worker and final publication guard. This change does not add RunConfig financial fields or automatically transport worker controls where no explicit caller opts in.

Tokens and graph handles are scoped to their originating loaded library. Bare u64 IDs can coincide in two libraries; direct C callers must never pass a foreign token/handle, and native rejection of such collisions is not claimed. Python captures the actor library for token creation, invocation, signal, release, cleanup and response free; path/artifact stamp drift rejects financial actor operations before invocation. Cleanup continues through the captured library even when the environment changes.

# Explicit ASC 815 interest-rate hedge accounting (initial lane)

`portfolio_risk_native::hedge_accounting::evaluate` consumes an immutable
`HedgeAccountingRequest` (schema and model version `hedge-accounting-1`) and
returns a `HedgeAccountingResult`. It is an additive, explicitly selected
component of issue #35. It does not reinterpret saved economics, upgrade a
saved derivative, or close the issue's saved-book, portfolio-layer,
net-investment, treasury or 60,000-position gates.

The owner binds formal fair-value and cash-flow hedge relationships to one
complete reviewed Physical derivative source (`derivative-accounting-1`) and
to explicit hedged-item or forecast-exposure sources. It produces dated
assessment evidence, an append-only relationship lifecycle, and one ordered
journal in which every derivative mark, coupon, collateral and hedge entry is
recognized exactly once. A legacy `fvh`/`cfh` saved-book label is not an input.

## Rule matrix and activation

| Rule area | Treatment in `hedge-accounting-1` |
|---|---|
| Designation and documentation (815-20-25) | Relationship identity, risk-management objective, documentation, instrument, hedged item/exposure, designated proportion, hedged risk and inception date are mandatory retained inputs. Missing or unsupported values reject. |
| Hedged risk | `benchmark_interest_rate` only. The benchmark coupon component of a fixed-rate instrument (FVH) or the variability of forecast index-linked interest (CFH). Credit, FX, price-component, total-cash-flow and prepayment risks reject. |
| Effectiveness assessment (815-20-35) | `cumulative_dollar_offset` with explicit reviewed `lower_bound`/`upper_bound`. The band is policy input; no universal band is coded. Regression, qualitative and shortcut methods reject. CFH without a supplied hypothetical requires reviewed `matched_critical_terms_evidence` and exact native term matching. |
| Fair-value hedge recognition (815-25-35) | Instrument marks stay in earnings. The hedged item's benchmark-component clean value change is posted daily as a basis adjustment with the offset in earnings. Discontinuation freezes the basis; it is amortized straight-line by actual days to the item's principal date, or derecognized on sale. |
| Cash-flow hedge recognition (815-30-35, post ASU 2017-12) | The designated share of every instrument mark change goes to OCI while qualified; nothing is split as ineffectiveness. OCI is reclassified to earnings when each hedged forecast period affects earnings, by the hypothetical settlement for that period. After discontinuation frozen OCI is released pro rata by period accrual weight; `probable_not_to_occur` releases all remaining OCI immediately. |
| Discontinuation (815-25-40, 815-30-40) | Reviewed `discontinue` events (dedesignation, hedged item sold, instrument terminated) and failed assessments discontinue prospectively. Partial discontinuation removes a fraction of the remaining designated proportion. Redesignation is a new relationship with `predecessor_relationship_id`; history is append-only. |
| ASU 2022-01 portfolio layers | Not implemented; `asu_2022_01_portfolio_layer` must be `false`. |
| ASU 2025-09 | Adoption identity and date are retained. Every election (`similar_risk_grouping`, `selectable_rate_debt`, `swap_written_option_exception`, `dual_hedge_basis`) must be `false`; `true` rejects as unimplemented. |
| Net investment, nonfinancial components, options as instruments, counterparty default | Rejected explicitly. |

`policy.rule_version` must equal `asc815-asu2017-12`. The implemented rule
matrix is this document; accounting policy approval, auditor judgment and
entity-specific qualification are outside the engine.

## Request

```json
{
  "schema": "hedge-accounting-1",
  "model_version": "hedge-accounting-1",
  "run": {"id": "...", "revision": "..."},
  "entity": "bank", "currency": "USD", "monetary_unit": "currency_units",
  "policy": {
    "identity": {"id": "...", "revision": "..."},
    "rule_version": "asc815-asu2017-12",
    "adoption": {
      "asu_2025_09": {"adopted": false, "adoption_ordinal": null,
        "elections": {"similar_risk_grouping": false, "selectable_rate_debt": false,
                      "swap_written_option_exception": false, "dual_hedge_basis": false}},
      "asu_2022_01_portfolio_layer": false
    },
    "assessment": {"identity": {...}, "method": "cumulative_dollar_offset",
                   "lower_bound": 0.8, "upper_bound": 1.25},
    "fvh_basis_amortization": "straight_line_actual_days_to_principal",
    "cfh_reclassification": "hedged_period_hypothetical_settlement"
  },
  "derivative": { ...complete derivative-accounting-1 request... },
  "hedged_items": [{
    "item_id": "loan-1", "source": {...}, "carrying_source": {...},
    "kind": "fixed_rate_instrument", "direction": "asset",
    "notional": 100.0, "contractual_rate": 0.06,
    "periods": [{"period_id": "p1", "start_ordinal": 738886, "end_ordinal": 738896,
                 "payment_ordinal": 738896, "day_count": "act360"}],
    "principal_ordinal": 738896
  }],
  "forecast_exposures": [{
    "exposure_id": "float-1", "source": {...}, "probability_evidence": {...},
    "direction": "payment", "notional": 100.0, "index_id": "term-1m",
    "periods": [{"period_id": "e1", "start_ordinal": 738886, "end_ordinal": 738896,
                 "payment_ordinal": 738896, "day_count": "act360"}]
  }],
  "relationships": [{
    "relationship_id": "fvh-1", "predecessor_relationship_id": null,
    "designation": "fair_value_hedge",
    "hedging_instrument_position_id": "swap", "designated_proportion": 1.0,
    "hedged_item_id": "loan-1", "hedged_notional": 100.0,
    "hedged_risk": "benchmark_interest_rate", "benchmark_rate": 0.05,
    "inception_ordinal": 738886,
    "risk_management_objective": {...}, "documentation": {...},
    "hypothetical": null, "matched_critical_terms_evidence": null
  }],
  "events": [{
    "event_id": "assess-1", "relationship_id": "fvh-1", "ordinal": 738896,
    "sequence": 0, "kind": "assess", "review": {...}
  }]

```

A `cash_flow_hedge` relationship names `forecast_exposure_id` instead of
`hedged_item_id`/`hedged_notional`/`benchmark_rate`, and either a `hypothetical`
(`evidence` plus one `nodes[]` entry `{ordinal, request}` holding a complete
`SwapRequest` for every path node from inception) or
`matched_critical_terms_evidence`.

Events are `assess`, `discontinue` (`reason` in `dedesignation`,
`hedged_item_sold`, `instrument_terminated`; optional `proportion` in (0,1]
of the remaining designated proportion, default 1) and `forecast_status`
(`status` in `no_longer_probable`, `probable_not_to_occur`; CFH only). Events
are globally ordered by `(ordinal, sequence)` with unique ids and reviews.

## Admission

- The derivative request is a complete `derivative-accounting-1` Physical
  netting lifecycle with one path, no default policy, matching entity,
  currency and unit. Every hedging instrument is a mapped `swap` trade whose
  raw review designation is `undesignated_economic_hedge`; CFH instruments use
  `settle_derivative_carrying` coupon recognition. Options, expired options and
  defaulted paths reject.
- Hedged item periods are contiguous and chronological; `principal_ordinal`
  is at or after the last payment. `hedged_notional` is positive and at most
  the item notional; the sum over relationships cannot exceed it. The sum of
  designated proportions per instrument over relationships cannot exceed 1.
- `inception_ordinal` is a path node at or after the opening date and an
  accrual-free boundary: a `start_ordinal` of some fixed and some floating
  period of the instrument and (FVH) of the item, or (CFH) of the exposure.
- `assess` requires an accrual-free node: `end_ordinal` of some fixed and
  floating period of the instrument and of the item/exposure, with
  `after_scheduled_payments` timing, after inception and before the
  instrument's final payment date. Other events can occur on any node at or
  after inception. Events on discontinued relationships reject except
  `forecast_status` for CFH frozen OCI.
- Every item payment date and principal date after a node must have an exact
  discount point in the instrument's node discount curve; no interpolation.
- A supplied hypothetical covers every node from inception to the tail with
  `asof_ordinal` equal to the node, the node's timing, the exposure's currency
  and exactly the exposure's periods on its floating leg; its clean value at
  inception must be zero within the shared tolerance. Matured hypothetical
  floating periods must carry observed or Physical observations.
- A `predecessor_relationship_id` must name an earlier relationship on the
  same instrument that is fully discontinued at or before the new inception.
- Bounds: 64 relationships, 1,024 events, 64 items/exposures, 4,096 periods
  per item/exposure, 32 MiB raw input, 32 MiB output, saturating 1,000,000
  combined hypothetical work units in addition to the derivative owner's own
  admission. Component bounds are not aggregate RSS guarantees.

## Valuation and recognition

Let nodes be the derivative path nodes `t_0 < ... < t_n`. For a relationship
with designated proportion `p`:

**Instrument change.** `dV_t` is the instrument's clean mark change at node
`t` as posted by the derivative owner (`clean_mark` intents, excluding coupon
settlements); it drives recognition. For assessment the instrument change is
measured clean of accrued periodic interest: `D_t = sum(p_s * (V_s - V_{s-1}))`
over nodes after inception through `t`, where `V_s` is the after-payment
carrying value at node `s`. At an accrual-free date this is the clean fair
value change since inception; settled net coupons are excluded on both sides.

**FVH hedged item.** With `N_h` the hedged notional, `r_b` the benchmark
rate, `tau_i` the period year fraction and `D_t(d)` the exact discount factor
from the instrument's node-`t` curve:

```
B_t = sum_{active i} N_h r_b tau_i D_t(pay_i) + [principal active] N_h D_t(principal)
A_t = N_h r_b * yearfrac(start_j, t)   for the period j containing t (zero after
      its end with after-payment timing, the full coupon with before-payment timing)
C_t = B_t - A_t
```

A period is active with before-payment timing when `pay_i >= t`, otherwise
when `pay_i > t`. `C_t` is continuous across coupon payments. The daily basis
adjustment is `dC_t = C_t(before payments) - C_{t-1}(after payments)`, starting
from the inception node's after-payment `C`, so settled coupons and the
principal repayment are excluded exactly as the derivative owner excludes
settled coupons from marks. Posting (direction `dir` = +1 asset, −1 liability):
`hedged_item_basis_adjustment` debit `dir * dC_t`, `hedged_item_basis_gain_loss`
debit `-dir * dC_t`. The hedged item's contractual interest is not posted here.

**CFH hypothetical.** `H_t` is the hypothetical swap's after-payment clean
value at node `t` (native `swaps::value_swap`), or the instrument's own
after-payment carrying value when matched critical terms are elected.
Cumulative `E_t = sum(s * (H_t - H_{t-1}))` after inception, the same clean
measure as `D_t`. Matched critical terms additionally require the instrument's
fair value at inception to be zero; a supplied hypothetical must itself be at
market at inception.

**OCI.** While qualified, each node's `p * dV_t` moves from
`mark_gain_loss` to `cash_flow_hedge_oci`: the derivative owner's `clean_mark`
intent is re-owned with the `mark_gain_loss` posting split into
`cash_flow_hedge_oci` (`p` share) and `mark_gain_loss` (`1-p` share). The
derivative asset/liability postings are unchanged.

**Reclassification.** At each exposure period payment date on or after the
inception node, `R = p * S_t` where `S_t` is the hypothetical's net
settlement due at `t` (the instrument's Physical cash right when matched).
Posting: `cash_flow_hedge_oci` debit `R`, `hedged_forecast_reclassification`
debit `-R`. After discontinuation the frozen OCI balance `F` is released at
each remaining period `k` by `F * w_k` with `w_k = N tau_k / sum N tau` over
periods remaining at discontinuation; the last release clears the balance
exactly. `probable_not_to_occur` posts the entire remaining balance at the
event node.

**Assessment.** At an `assess` event, `ratio = D_t / E_t` where for FVH
`E_t = -dir * sum(dC)` since inception (the clean benchmark-component change,
with the principal settlement excluded). `qualified` iff
`lower <= ratio <= upper`. Assessment dates must precede the instrument's
final settlement; at or after it nothing remains to measure.
`E_t = 0` with `D_t = 0` rejects the event (nothing to assess); `E_t = 0` with
`D_t != 0` fails. Failure discontinues the whole relationship at that node
with reason `failed_assessment`.

**Discontinuation.** For fraction `q` of the remaining proportion: FVH freezes
`q * basis_balance`; `hedged_item_sold` derecognizes it at once
(`hedged_item_basis_derecognition`), otherwise it amortizes per node by
`frozen * (t - t_disc) / (principal - t_disc)` cumulatively
(`hedged_item_basis_amortization`), fully at or after the principal date.
CFH freezes `q * oci_balance` for pro rata release. Proportion becomes
`p * (1 - q)`; zero means fully discontinued and later marks stay in earnings.

**Node order.** For each node: the derivative owner's intents for that node in
their original order (with CFH mark re-ownership using the status at the end
of the previous node); then hedge postings (FVH `dC`, amortization, CFH
reclassification/frozen release); then that node's events in sequence order;
then the daily closing. Relationships become active at the end of their
inception node, so inception-node marks stay in earnings.

## Output

`HedgeAccountingResult` retains `schema`, `model_version`, `run`, entity,
currency, unit, the policy, the complete `derivative` result (evidence, not a
second journal), `relationships` (closing status, proportion, balances,
frozen schedules), `lifecycle` (ordered inception/assessment/discontinuation/
forecast events with proportions before and after), `assessments` (cumulative
amounts, ratio, bounds, outcome), `daily` (per node, per relationship:
instrument designated value, hedged clean value or hypothetical value,
cumulative changes, basis and OCI balances, status; plus the financial trial
balance), `intents` (the single ordered journal), `closing` roll-forwards and
explicit flags: `accounting_standard_approval=false`,
`empirical_validation=false`, `persisted_journal_verified=false`,
`saved_book_adoption=false`, `portfolio_layer_supported=false`,
`net_investment_supported=false`.

Journal accounts are the derivative owner's accounts plus
`cash_flow_hedge_oci`, `hedged_item_basis_adjustment`,
`hedged_item_basis_gain_loss`, `hedged_item_basis_amortization`,
`hedged_item_basis_derecognition` and `hedged_forecast_reclassification`.
Every intent balances; hedge intents carry `relationship_id`. Each node's
trial balance equals the derivative owner's balances for every derivative
account except `mark_gain_loss`, which is reduced exactly by the OCI share.

## Independent verification

`portfolio_risk.analytics.hedge_accounting_reference.verify(raw, result)`
independently reconstructs the derivative result with the existing raw
derivative reference, the item benchmark values, hypothetical values, the
relationship state machine, assessments, intents, daily balances and closing
roll-forwards, then compares with the existing 1e-12 relative / 1e-9 absolute
financial tolerance and exact identity for every nonfinancial field. It uses
no native callbacks. A receipt is returned only when the whole result passes.

## Scope statement

This lane admits single-currency fixed/floating swaps against fixed-rate
assets/liabilities and forecast index-linked interest. It does not establish
accounting-standard compliance, observed effectiveness, portfolio-layer,
net-investment, option or nonfinancial coverage, saved-book or shared daily
journal adoption, treasury/capital feeds or complete-scale acceptance. Those
remain open under issue #35 and are listed in `implementation-plan.md`.

# Product model enhancement implementation and evidence

Tracking scope: [GitHub issue 25](https://github.com/beauschwab/model-portfolio-sim/issues/25).
This document records implementation stages, not a reduced definition of completion.
Every child issue's acceptance criteria remain required. A numerical implementation
is not an empirical calibration, a regulatory methodology approval or a deployment.

## Formal ASC 815 hedge relationships (local 0.29.19; initial lane validated)

`hedge-accounting-1` implements issue #35 stages 0-4 and the durable part of stage 7
for the initial interest-rate lane: fair-value and cash-flow relationships on one
reviewed `derivative-accounting-1` Physical source, explicit hedged items/forecast
exposures, append-only lifecycle, cumulative dollar-offset assessment under reviewed
bounds at accrual-free dates, mark re-ownership into OCI, hedged-period
reclassification, frozen OCI release, basis amortization/derecognition and one
ordered journal. See [the contract](hedge-accounting.md). The rule matrix is
`asc815-asu2017-12`; ASU 2022-01 layers, ASU 2025-09 elections, net investment,
options, defaulted paths and seasoned openings refuse explicitly.

Evidence (worktree `claude/hedge-accounting-35`, Windows, rebuilt release binary):
six native hand/lifecycle/refusal/protocol tests plus the unchanged 45 derivative
contract/accounting tests and strict all-target Clippy; 20 engine checks (hand
values, partial dedesignation, sale, forecast outcomes, failed assessment, supplied
hypothetical, eleven tamper refusals, eight native refusals, fresh-process ownership,
cancellation and strict scalar categories) with the derivative accounting suite
unchanged; ten durable API checks (original deadline, independent receipt, seven
persistence tampers, expired deadline, listing). The independent Python reference
replays the derivative source, item/hypothetical values, lifecycle, assessments,
journal and roll-forwards. Both oracles now treat rounding-level intents as zero
events; the previous derivative verifier dropped native floating-noise marks for
exactly offsetting legs, so at-market fixtures use a par rate with distinct legs.

Not closed by this stage: accounting-standard approval, observed effectiveness,
ASU 2025-09 lanes, portfolio layers, net investment, options, saved-book and shared
daily journal adoption, treasury/capital/AOCI policy feeds (#24/#30), browser flow
beyond the generic model-analysis page, PostgreSQL parity and the 60,000-position
joint acceptance. Local validation does not deploy or restart workers.
