## Research basis and design decisions

Research checked 2026-10-01, with FTP and model-validation sources refreshed
2026-10-03. Primary sources guide model structure; the project
does not copy supervisory parameters or claim supervisory suitability.

- The Federal Reserve's [2025 detailed model descriptions](https://www.federalreserve.gov/publications/2025-june-supervisory-stress-test-methodology-descriptions-supervisory-models.htm)
  motivate product-specific delinquency transitions and competing exits. The
  [2026 methodology](https://www.federalreserve.gov/publications/files/2026-february-supervisory-stress-test-methodology.pdf)
  documents the subsequent annual scope and adjustments. We use these as dated
  modeling references, not substitutes for a bank's data or applicable policy.
- The [Basel credit/ECL guidance](https://www.bis.org/publications/201512-guidelines-guidance-credit-risk-and-accounting-expected-credit-losses)
  supports keeping credit risk estimation, expected cash shortfalls and accounting
  policy explicit. A supplied economic hazard is not an accounting staging rule.
- Current [SR 26-2 guidance](https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602.htm)
  supersedes SR 11-7. Validation records must use the current, risk-based framework
  while preserving independent financial reference tests and documented limits.
- The [interagency FTP guidance](https://www.occ.treas.gov/news-issuances/bulletins/2016/bulletin-2016-7a.pdf)
  distinguishes funding from contingent liquidity risk and calls for granular,
  transparent allocation. Its inception perspective motivates retaining the
  original funding policy/curve identity separately from a later closing source.
  The [BIS liquidity-transfer-pricing research](https://www.bis.org/publications/fsi-paper-10-liquidity-transfer-pricing-guide-better-practice)
  motivates matched maturities and marginal funding costs; it is research, not
  approval of this application's supplied policies. Product source reconstruction
  alone grants no permission to infer a liquidity tenor, set an optionality charge
  to zero, relabel basis/credit/revision P&L as recurring external interest or count
  modeled economic loss again in FTP. Contractual reset and liquidity tenors stay
  separate, consistent with the [OCC interest-rate-risk handbook](https://www.occ.ustreas.gov/publications-and-resources/publications/comptrollers-handbook/files/interest-rate-risk/pub-ch-interest-rate-risk.pdf).
- [New York Fed SOFR methodology](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/additional-information-about-reference-rates)
  distinguishes actual value-date day weights and overnight compounding. Contracts
  therefore require explicit observation intervals; no hidden conversion from
  three-month simulated forwards to contractual overnight fixings is permitted.

The shared deterministic credit stage uses explicit continuous-time hazards and
absorbing default/prepayment states, with cures among active states. This is a
project design choice: it prevents independently applied exit probabilities from
spending the same surviving exposure twice. Piecewise intervals, exposure inputs,
loss severity and recovery timing are supplied assumptions until calibrated.

default runtime, durable worker and browser acceptance remain pending. This
does not opt saved `/run` pricing, what-if, strategy or cohort books into a new

# Joint product funding: modeling rationale and acceptance evidence

This companion to [modeled-product FTP](modeled-product-ftp.md) records design
requirements for issues #12, #14, #20 and #24. Source2 funding and joint derivative
ownership are isolated continuations under review. Their acceptance remains
separate from the installed CD/source2 source freeze and from complete issue #25.

## Research basis

The interagency FTP guidance separates ordinary funding from standby liquidity,
requires transparent aggregation and independent review, and illustrates separate
reset and liquidity tenors for floating exposures. It calls for documentation when
FTP and stress behavioral assumptions differ, and consideration of derivative
collateral rights and stressed outflows. Its methodological examples are
illustrative; they do not prescribe one formula. See principles 1–3 and the
non-trading and trading attachments in the
[Federal Reserve's interagency guidance](https://www.federalreserve.gov/frrs/guidance/interagency-guidance-on-funds-transfer-pricing-related-to-funding-and-contingent-liquidity-risks.htm).

The Basel liquidity principles call for granular dynamic cashflow analysis,
behavioral funding sensitivity, derivative exercise/maturity and collateral
demands, currency analysis and collateral availability by entity and location.
They discourage assuming automatic overnight rollover and require realistic
transfer timing and restrictions. See LQY 10.34–10.35, 10.45, 10.48,
10.96–10.102 and 10.131 in
[Liquidity risk management and supervision](https://www.bis.org/committees/bcbs/basel-consolidated-guidelines/module/lqy/10).

The FSI better-practice study supports central treasury oversight, marginal
funding costs matched to product maturity, blended treatment for amortizing or
non-maturing products and explicit contingent usage. It is a survey-based
author paper, not a certification of this implementation or a binding formula.
See [Liquidity transfer pricing: a guide to better practice](https://www.bis.org/publications/fsi-paper-10-liquidity-transfer-pricing-guide-better-practice).

## Application to the native model

The following are repository design conclusions drawn from those sources and
the production contract. Numerical and accounting choices still require explicit
reviewed policies; the sources do not supply missing customer histories,
original yield, legal netting permission, curves or regulatory weights.

| Requirement | Implementation and validation obligation |
|---|---|
| Separate reset and funding life | Retain rate-reset dates, complete physical principal and gross coupon tails, and explicit funding curve/policy identity. Test an exposure whose next reset precedes final runoff; do not replace both tenors with one scalar. |
| Exclusive economic ownership | Preserve entity, currency, canonical position and account lineage across selected source jobs. A second job ID cannot authorize a second allocation to the same economic owner. Test duplicate-owner refusal and distinct-owner acceptance. |
| Complete cash and gross rights | Retain original/current histories and each earned/cash origin through settlement. Check original-EIR recognition and revision catchup separately. Do not fund settled cash again or erase small signed residuals. |
| Joint cash availability | Execute deposit and derivative events in one chronological journal with one reviewed opening cash/equity source. Independently reconstruct ordered postings and closing balances; adding standalone closing reports cannot prove this requirement. |
| Derivative and collateral scope | Exercise the existing complete admitted standalone domain, including options/delivered legs, seasoned openings, collateral and closeout policies. Verify custody and legal mapping independently. A vanilla swap fixture alone cannot establish this coverage. |
| Explicit contingent liquidity | Retain supplied draw, flight, collateral and haircut policies with scenario and measure identity. Disclose differences between funding and stress assumptions. Expected funding calculations do not establish observed withdrawal prediction or intraday availability. |
| Conservatively bounded generation | Admit aggregate source preparation, full tails, parser/encoding staging, journal work and retained capacity before generation. Preserve the original deadline and cancellation through routing, parsing, child preparation, replay and publication. Component capacity limits do not guarantee total process memory. |
| Immutable publication | Verify raw source, model identity, reviewed policy, exact receipt counters and independently persisted postings before successful publication. Repeat ownership, artifact, deadline and private lease/token checks at final commit. Late failures must publish no successful result. |

## Evidence required before completion

The selected source2 tier's 365-day input-shape ceiling is distinct from admission
of every possible tuple and from general long-tail deposit coverage. Current
40-day multi-owner and 90-day single-owner examples establish those examples
only. Joined work and retained capacity remain charged without relaxing source
or journal ceilings. Broader portfolio capacity requires explicit implementation
and the original combined 60,000-position graph/credit/solver/journal gate.

Historical Card2/source1 byte controls protect those exact inputs and outputs;
they are not independent financial validation. New source2 validation requires
native financial execution, independent original-source reconstruction and
persisted journal/funding replay. Browser evidence must use actual durable
workers and private publication checks, including failed-publication cases.
Contained artifacts must be rebuilt and checked again against the final installed
source before default execution is accepted.

Observed deposit, borrower, repayment and credit histories with chronological
holdouts remain necessary to establish empirical accuracy. Supplied scenarios,
synthetic fixtures and numerical parity cannot substitute for that evidence.
The original [implementation plan](implementation-plan.md) and child issue
criteria remain the completion authority. No financial tolerance, fixed base OAS,
shared random-number or coefficient-only interactive contract changes here.

## Shared derivative replay work reservation under review

The proposed raw structural reservation must serve both standalone saved
derivative replay and joint deposit/derivative replay. Charging only the native
source's 250,000-unit ceiling does not reserve the mapped journal's complete-tail
scans. The correction is an isolated successor; earlier receipts remain evidence
for their original source, and corrected final-source gates remain required.

For each admitted Physical source, let `N` be its supplied daily nodes, `B` its
distinct legal buckets, `T` its opening trades, `U` the sum of all node trade
slots, `C` a conservative count of raw potential cash rights and `D` the complete
mixed replay days, including as-of. `C` includes fixed/floating schedules in
every node, option states and expiry/terminal events, and delivered underlyings.
Optional Pricing XVA inputs are reserved separately and create no physical GL.

The reviewed posting-line upper is

```text
L = (7 + 2T) + 10U + 20NB + 8B + 2T + 6C
replay_upper = L * (1 + 6D) + 16N
```

Every arithmetic operation must check overflow before financial generation.
The terms correspond to current native emission branches:

| Term | Structural argument |
|---|---|
| `7 + 2T` | Explicit cash/equity, VM/IM/custody opening lines and both gross carrying sides per opening trade. |
| `10U` | At most two three-line marks and one four-line physical delivery per node/trade slot. |
| `20NB` | Across a complete path, at most one generated VM call per node/bucket, each settled once; collateral interest has at most seven financial/custody lines per node/bucket and tail return at most six per bucket. Twenty is a conservative whole-path bound. |
| `8B + 2T` | At most one reviewed closeout per bucket, its six financial and two custody lines, and both gross carrying reversals per trade. |
| `6C` | At most three due lines, two later MPOR settlement lines and one default unpaid retirement line per potential right. |
| `L * (1 + 6D)` | Source/intents validation plus the existing complete mixed-day historical-line scans, including days after a shorter derivative source closes. |
| `16N` | All sixteen current financial/custody account kinds can remain in each derivative daily closing; zero-value/netted output cannot reduce admission. |

Multiple delayed VM calls may settle on a single day. Consequently the `20NB`
argument applies to the full path and cannot be interpreted as a per-day
movement-count limit. Actual delayed/unavailable settlement and catchup cases
must verify this property without dropping historical calls.

The joined admission charges the dated base once, each complete source
reservation, raw transport work and retained/staging capacity before projection.
Observed mapped work must compare against the dated-plus-derivative reservation.
A field containing complete mapped work must retain that disclosed meaning;
it cannot be compared to a derivative-only upper or used to double-charge the
dated base. Native and independent references must agree on raw cardinalities,
complete replay days, overflow refusal and exact source/receipt identity.

Required validation includes admitted option/delivery/default/CSA branches,
longer mixed tails, zero-generator aggregate refusal, unchanged historical
streams and refreshed original-source/persisted-journal gates for both routes.
This posting bound does not by itself establish aggregate process memory,
empirical accuracy or the required combined 60,000-position acceptance.

# Joint stochastic market and credit generation

`joint-market-credit-1` composes two explicit native stages for analysis:

1. `model-market-1` generates a bounded PSD Gaussian tape for named rate,
   mortgage-spread and regional-HPI drivers. The tape retains the declared
   covariance, factor truncation, driver order, source revision and common
   random-number identity.
2. The annualized innovation for each path and period enters supplied hazard
   elasticities. For a positive baseline hazard `h` and coefficient vector
   `beta`, the resulting hazard is

   `h(path, period) = exp(log(h) + beta · z_annualized(path, period))`.

   A zero baseline requires a zero coefficient vector. Hazards above the
   admitted domain are rejected; they are never clipped. Behavioral exit,
   credit default and prepayment then use the shared competing-exponential
   state machine from `joint-state-1` with the caller-owned uniform pairs.

The period policy supplies actual dates, discount factors, recovery fraction
and recovery lag. The generated rate shock is retained as a market driver; it
is not silently converted into a discount curve, pricing measure, OAS or P/Q
mapping. The state output therefore remains an analysis receipt, not a saved
product valuation, accounting journal, CECL/IFRS 9 result or regulatory model.

The request binds market source revision and shared-draw identity to the joint
identity, requires market durations to equal the declared actual-date periods,
and requires one random pair per position-period. Rust validates dimensions,
driver domains, dates, hazard coefficients, positions and work before output.
The market generator and state loop accept cooperative cancellation; no partial
result is returned after a failed checkpoint.

The checked-in example is synthetic and deliberately reports
`adoption_eligible=false`. Observed market/borrower calibration, uncertainty,
product-specific policies, cohort/saved-book adoption, daily journal/FTP
integration and full mixed-book scale acceptance remain separate gates. This
boundary follows model-risk guidance that implementation tests and synthetic
fixtures do not establish predictive or regulatory validation.

# Joint market, behavioral and credit state

`joint-state-1` is a bounded Rust coordinator for a product that already has
explicit market, behavioral and credit drivers. It provides one event-time
state path per position and preserves the caller's common-random-number (CRN)
identity across competing exits. The Python adapter
`analytics.model_contracts.evaluate_joint_state` only serializes the request;
it does not calculate probabilities or provide a fallback.

## Inputs and identity

The request carries `source_id`, `source_revision`, `assumption_id`,
`common_random_numbers_id`, and an explicit `measure` (`contractual`,
`pricing`, or `physical`). The measure is a label. The coordinator never
converts physical probabilities to a pricing measure, solves an OAS, or
derives a market curve from a cashflow stream.

Each period is an actual-date interval with a supplied market discount factor,
three annualized competing hazards, a recovery fraction, and a recovery lag.
Each path supplies a unique position and path key, principal, and exactly one
caller-owned pair of uniforms per period. The same pair can therefore be sent
to a sibling product graph while preserving scenario parity.

## Competing event math

For an interval of length \(\Delta t\), let

\[
  h = h_b + h_c + h_p,
  \qquad p_{exit} = 1 - e^{-h\Delta t}.
\]

The behavioral-exit, credit-default, and prepayment probabilities are,
respectively,

\[
  p_b = p_{exit}h_b/h,\quad
  p_c = p_{exit}h_c/h,\quad
  p_p = p_{exit}h_p/h,
\]

with all three equal to zero when \(h=0\). The waiting uniform selects the
first event in that stable order: behavioral exit, credit default, prepayment,
then continuation. The destination uniform is retained in the input for CRN
identity and future state-specific destinations; this bounded coordinator does
not invent a destination transition.

An exit consumes the live principal once. Credit default records recovery
`principal × recovery_fraction` and economic loss as the residual. The market
discount factor is reported on every event and is used only for the supplied
live-balance diagnostic. Recovery lag is retained on every event as an explicit
policy input; actual recovery-date cashflow and journal posting require a
downstream accounting owner.

## Bounds and validation

Rust rejects unknown fields, non-contiguous actual-date periods, duplicate
position/path identities, out-of-range hazards, invalid discount factors,
negative principal, missing CRN pairs, and non-finite values. The route admits
at most 4,096 periods, 10,000 paths, and 2,000,000 path-period work units.
These are component limits and do not constitute an aggregate process RSS
guarantee. Native request/output size and thread limits remain those in
`native-contracts.md`.

## Adoption boundary

This contract supplies a reusable joint state frame; it is not empirical model
validation, interval-censored fitting, LGD/EAD calibration, or a CECL/IFRS 9
allowance calculation. It does not automatically alter saved-book economics,
the daily ledger, FTP/capital, a Strategy Lab library, a cohort audit, or a
complete mixed-book graph. Those integrations must retain fixed base OAS,
shared CRN, independent Python reference checks, persisted source/journal
verification, and their issue-specific observed-data and scale gates.

This separation follows current interagency model-risk guidance: validation
must assess conceptual soundness, limitations, ongoing monitoring and outcomes
analysis, and extending a model beyond its original use requires analysis of
the new use and its limitations. See [SR 26-2](https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602a1.pdf).
The contract therefore treats supplied hazards and synthetic CRN paths as
implementation fixtures until observed outcomes, chronological holdouts and
product-use monitoring are available.

The current tests prove schema/domain validation, exact competing-hazard math,
CRN identity preservation, and public native dispatch. Synthetic fixtures do
not establish predictive accuracy. Production use requires rebuilding the
native product and dependent workflow artifacts and explicitly rebuilding any
saved library or session that elects this route.

# Observed market-driver calibration

`market-driver-calibration-1` is the explicit analysis boundary for fitting
four supplied market-driver columns. It estimates training moments in Rust and
reports diagnostics on a later chronological holdout without allowing holdout
rows to change the fit. The Python function
`analytics.model_contracts.fit_market_drivers` is transport only.

The request retains model, input, source, training-split and holdout-split
identities. `training_end` partitions the strictly increasing actual-date
history. At least 30 training and 10 subsequent holdout observations are
required, and the split identities must differ. Optional scenario selection
uses only training rows and is deterministic under equal-distance ties.

For training rows \(x_i\), the native fit returns the arithmetic mean

\[
  \bar{x}=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i
\]

and unbiased covariance

\[
  C=(n-1)^{-1}\sum_i(x_i-\bar{x})(x_i-\bar{x})^T.
\]

Holdout diagnostics report component bias, RMSE and the fraction outside three
training standard deviations. The fit is never re-estimated on the holdout;
changing only holdout observations must leave the training moments byte-stable.
The optional selected stress rows are ranked by the training covariance
Mahalanobis distance and are bounded to the declared driver domains.

The optional `uncertainty_lag` requests a Bartlett HAC standard error for each
component of the training mean. With centered observations (y_t), the native
diagnostic uses

\[
\widehat{\Omega}_j=\gamma_{0,j}+2\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}
\left(1-\frac{\ell}{L+1}\right)\gamma_{\ell,j},\qquad
SE(\bar{x}_j)=\sqrt{\max(\widehat{\Omega}_j,0)/n},
\]

where each autocovariance uses the training-row count as its denominator. A lag
of zero is an explicit iid estimate; lags above 64 or the training-row count
are rejected. The method and lag are retained in the result so uncertainty is
not mistaken for empirical validation or a calibrated pricing parameter.

This contract is deliberately narrower than a pricing calibration. It does not
bootstrap curves, estimate a risk-neutral drift, fit a smile, infer mortgage or
deposit behavior, or authorize a product graph/cache. A result is always marked
`adoption_eligible: false`; a production model requires reviewed source vintage,
parameter uncertainty, chronological outcomes analysis and explicit adoption.
Synthetic fixtures validate leakage controls and arithmetic only.

The distinction follows current interagency model-risk guidance: conceptual
soundness, limitations, ongoing monitoring and outcomes analysis must be
separately evidenced before extending a model beyond its intended use. See
[SR 26-2](https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602a1.pdf).

# Supplied curves and conditional indexed-product analysis

`market-indexed-adapter-1` is an explicit analytical source. Rust converts supplied
named index and collateral curves into conditional term-index observations, then
calls the existing `term_enhancements::indexed::build_path` and
`derivative_contract::swaps::value_swap`. These are actual product owners; the
transport does not calculate cashflows or discount factors. This schema does not
enter the saved-book incremental pricing graph.

The outer lifecycle request contains `schema`, `threads`, and the typed `request`.
The canonical example is `examples/models/market-indexed-adapter-1.json`, whose
`request` member is the typed raw request. The adapter retains that complete request
as `cache_parent`, including both complete original/current supplied markets, all
source/revision/currency/date fields, named roles, curve nodes/tails, contract/reset
dates, margin, index tenor, calendar and review identities. A result from this source
is unsuitable for a coefficient library, accounting publication, capital or FTP.

For actual-date year fraction `tau`, the simple projected index is
`F = expm1(log(P_index(start)) - log(P_index(end))) / tau`.
Supplied pseudo-discount factors use the existing native log-linear interpolation
and explicit `reject`, `flat_zero`, or `flat_forward` tail. Curve time is ACT/365
from as-of; contractual fixed and indexed accrual may independently use ACT/360 or
ACT/365. A parallel index shift changes the index factors by `exp(-shift*time)`.
Collateral discounting and its bumps use the separately named collateral curve.
Both may include negative rates within admitted coupon/factor domains.

The clean swap is constant notional, with no principal exchange. Payer fixed cash
is `N*(F+margin)*tau_index - N*fixed_rate*tau_fixed`; receiver signs reverse.
`swap_result.clean_value` uses pure collateral discounting. The separately labeled
`spread_adjusted_swap_pv` applies the retained original reviewed OAS to those actual
dated cashflows. This OAS is supplied, never solved or refitted on current/bumped
curves. The indexed illustration returns principal at maturity; its principal cash
is deliberately separate from the swap and must not be added to swap value.

Eight deterministic cases retain complete product DTOs, native cash/result receipts
and source identities: original, current, and down/up collateral, index and parallel
bumps. Their contract/calendar/reset/OAS parents are identical. There are no random
draws; this deterministic paired case is not a proof of stochastic shared CRN or
joint market dynamics. The original/current comparison is not quote calibration.

Only same-as-of Pricing sources are admitted. Every source must be available before
its declared information time, and information must be at/before each exact reset
cutoff on the supplied reset calendar date. Past resets, missing named index/role,
currency/as-of mismatch, missing complete maturity tail, unsupported coupon factors
and unadmitted curve tails fail before product generation. Generated observations
are explicitly `conditional_projection`, never observed fixings. Calendar identities
and caller dates are retained; business-day mapping is supplied and unverified.
Availability is explicitly supplied Unix seconds and may precede 1970, down to
the beginning of calendar year 1. Information and actual product selection cutoffs
retain their existing 1970..9999 UTC domains; availability cannot follow information.
Publication/observation lookup, overnight reset conventions, actual observed fixes,
joint drift/numeraire dynamics, smile, exercise and behavioral/credit paths remain
separate work. See [floating-rate.md](floating-rate.md),
[term-enhancements.md](term-enhancements.md), and
[derivative-contracts.md](derivative-contracts.md) for the product foundations.

Preflight admits at most 1 MiB serialized typed raw adapter input, 512 periods,
16 curves per original/current market, and 4096 nodes per curve. Let `I` be the
adapter serialized byte length, `B` the bridge byte length, `M` the total original
and current curve node count, and `R=8*periods`. Adapter work is `4*M+320*R`, capped
at 2 million; retained/output capacity is `8*R*(I+16384)+4*I+65536`, capped at 32 MiB.
The nested bridge additionally admits `4*M+64*R` work and
`R*(B+4096)+B+16384` bytes capped at 8 MiB. These conservative repeated-metadata
bounds use actual serde escaped byte lengths and checked arithmetic before output
vectors. Parsing, transport, source hashing and separate caches are additional
bounded stages; these figures are not an aggregate process RSS claim.

The new curve boundary accepts tail enum strings only. It rejects singleton-object
aliases, extra fields and duplicate typed fields in direct lifecycle JSON bytes.
An earlier caller parsing JSON into a dictionary/`Value` loses duplicate occurrences;
the native boundary cannot reconstruct that lost information. Historical shared
curve parsers, saved schemas and their economics are unchanged.

`market_indexed_reference.verify` independently reconstructs raw named-curve
projections, generated DTOs, complete native product cash/PV and retained source,
review, clock, admission and flag fields. It uses unchanged final tolerances of
`1e-12` relative and `1e-9` absolute for financial numbers, exact nonfinancial
identity/date/policy comparison, and stable log-ratio/expm1 for near-zero forwards.
Python is an independent verifier only. Durable ModelJobs require this verification
before formatting and again after immutable Parquet reload, with original deadlines,
lease/cancellation checks and queued/executed/current source/executable fences before
publishing a manifest. Retained raw/source/OAS parents and descriptor source fields
use exact recursive typed identity, including float signed zero; financial tolerance applies only to calculated
outputs. Neither identity alone nor producer results certify economics.

When a Rust caller supplies an active compute Control, this new analytical branch
captures it before Rayon dispatch and scopes it on the worker through calculation
and result conversion. Legacy branches retain their existing behavior. The standalone
`portfolio-lifecycle` CLI does not create a Control from this envelope; durable CLI
deadline/cancellation is enforced by the process watchdog and publication checks.
This patch introduces no broad envelope or process-control ownership change.

Result flags `production_adoption`, `observed_fixings`, `physical_accounting`,
`joint_dynamics`, `calendar_mapping_verified`, `accounting_adoption`,
`capital_ftp_eligible`, and `empirical_validation` are all false. Source verification
does not certify observed data, an accounting standard, a persisted journal, an
incremental graph cache, held-out calibration, or 60,000-position acceptance.

The source changes are applied locally and require a matching native rebuild.
Isolated copied-target/native and independent-reference tests are distinct from the still-required installed default
lifecycle, full regression, durable API, Parquet-tamper and browser execution gates.

# Raw-book supplied-index native owner

This explicit owner selects actual dated indexed pricing for bound loan rows inside one native portfolio/cache owner. Unbound loan/debt rows continue through the existing native incremental pricer. Python transports the raw request and formats the native row union; it does not calculate a second financial union. The owner, month-360 successor and per-call runtime control are applied locally in 0.29.8, and matching official native builds and component gates pass. Complete installed-default acceptance is being rerun after a separate test-fixture repair. Saved libraries/cohorts, physical accounting, capital/FTP, empirical validation and joint market dynamics remain unsupported. Local source application and builds do not deploy this owner.

`graph-1` operations `create_market_indexed_books` and `price_market_indexed_books` carry `market-indexed-books-1`. Complete original/current normalized rows and complete `market-indexed-graph-1` sources are supplied per binding, together with `original_native_pv_quote_reconciliation-1` review identity. Original native PV at the retained supplied OAS must equal original quote times face / 100 at unchanged 1e-12 relative and 1e-9 absolute money tolerances. A conflicting quote rejects. Initial creation and warm/cold/scenario indexed nodes never call the OAS solver. The old unbound calibration policy remains unchanged.

The first opt-in slice supports price-only loans/debt, at most 16 bound bullet floating Corporate loans and 64 total rows. Actual dates, named index tenor, currency, complete current/original curve/source identities and base row ownership must match. Current displayed quote stays validated on warm calls; it cannot rewrite the original. Calls/puts/sinks, nondefault contractual caps/floors, nonzero spread edits, analytics/KRD/NII, generic balance-sheet extras, MM/deposits/CD/MBS/hedges, forecasts, book yields and accounting anchors reject explicitly. Coupons generated in every admitted case must remain within the unchanged default row cap/floor. Shared curve keys exclude position-specific parents only in this new portfolio branch; cash/mark keys retain complete product and original parents. Existing standalone graph keys remain unchanged.

Admission checks cardinalities before aggregate serialization/generation. Let S be the larger current/retained original typed JSON length, C the larger paths*months*forwards grid, R the larger raw row count, and L=C*max(R,1)*128. Work is L+64*S+sum(individual indexed preflight work at zero cache); retained/transient byte admission is 32*S+configured cache+4*L+262144+sum(individual indexed preflight bytes at zero cache). Checked arithmetic admits at most 60M work and 128MiB, with 2MiB typed request and 32MiB output bounds. Shared cache is charged once and limited to 16MiB/4096 entries. Legacy grid caps are 8 paths, 360 months, 512 forwards, 4 factors. The copied dispatcher harness separately caps input at 1MiB/8 operations. Parser, transport and the legacy separate market cache are additional; this is not an aggregate RSS or 60,000-position acceptance claim.

Active Control reaches the real dispatcher branch and polls admission, source generation, row/case and output boundaries. Bounded serialization is not a byte-by-byte cooperative writer; process watchdog scope remains separate. Failed creation registers no successful owner; wrong-owner financial calls reject, and drop/info/clear remain owner-specific.

Evidence: seven new native tests, one cold/warm nonempty legacy serialization control, strict all-target Clippy, eleven independently reconstructed complete source/native union results, twelve real process rejections, seven pure transport/owner/artifact checks. Seven actual standalone predecessor/successor dispatcher results (cold, warm, curve edit, info, clear, cold rebuild, drop) compare byte-for-byte. Native calculated money tolerance remains unchanged. The focused legacy hand oracle uses an unchanged one-day par stub; general changed legacy-market calibration continues to require existing legacy acceptance gates.

The successor patch includes the frozen real-registry predecessor, preserves its golden JSON missing final newline with a proper patch EOF marker, and adds this portfolio owner. `freeze.py` applies only to a disposable baseline, compares every applied file's bytes to proposed content, checks exact inventory and parses all JSON/Python/Rust files. Installed apply is check-only. Complete installed source hash snapshots cover Core/Risk/Ledger/Decision/control/engine/API/web with dependency/build/output/binary files excluded. Their comparison window is this final artifact assembly, not a claim about unrelated preceding root work.

Next adoption gates are fresh default release process tests with Python financial callbacks forbidden, real `price_books` transport acceptance, complete independent retained source publication rules, cancellation/eviction/identity adversaries, and existing saved/candidate/library/cohort full-flow gates. This patch does not satisfy those gates by itself.

The locally applied default-grid successor admits the unchanged application 360-month grid under the same aggregate budgets. Its copied target passed three default-grid/control fixtures. The first full installed-default engine run passed the indexed owner tests but failed five setup cases in a separate mortgage capital fixture. That fixture is corrected; full default acceptance is still pending under the distinct `product-adoption-0298-schema-repair` receipt. The durable indexed-book publication proposal is a separate, still-unapplied successor.

# Unapplied named-index incremental registry branch

This candidate adds an explicit `market-indexed-graph-1` owner to the **existing** Risk `incremental.rs` handle registry. It invokes the actual indexed-contract and vanilla-swap owners and caches their dependencies. It is not a renamed analytical response. Installed sources, native libraries, and official targets remain unchanged.

The frozen predecessor at `../market-indexed-graph-stage` remains unchanged. This successor removes its artifact-only OAS solver counter. Acceptance instrumentation which compiles the untouched legacy registry is confined to the copied target and is excluded from the prospective patch.

## Public entry and ownership

The outer protocol remains `graph-1`. New operations are explicit:

```json
{"schema":"graph-1","threads":2,"request":{"op":"create_market_indexed","max_bytes":8388608,"max_entries":1024,"request":{"schema":"market-indexed-graph-1","product":"vanilla_swap","source":"complete typed market-indexed-adapter-1 request"}}}
```

The illustrative `source` string above must be replaced by the complete typed object in `market-indexed-registry-1.json`. Creation returns `{handle,owner,initial}` after successful actual pricing. `price_market_indexed` requires that handle and a complete typed graph request. `info` and `clear` dispatch by owner; market info returns `{owner,cache}`. `drop` retains the historical idempotent behavior for both owners.

Legacy `create`, `price`, and `compare` retain their original request types and financial implementation. The registry stores `Legacy(Arc<Mutex<Cache>>)` or `MarketIndexed(Arc<Mutex<Graph>>)`. A market handle rejects legacy `price`/`compare`; a legacy handle rejects `price_market_indexed` with `GRAPH_OWNER_MISMATCH`. It never casts an actual-date request into legacy quarterly `Flow`.

Pricing is outside the global registry lock. Creation checks the common 128-handle limit before expensive work and again during registration. Failed admission, pricing, cancellation, and full-registry creation leave no registered new owner. New branch caller Control is captured before Rayon dispatch and scoped on the worker. A final scoped creation failure removes the unpublished handle. Existing branches retain their None behavior. The CLI retains its existing external watchdog scope; this patch does not invent a universal CLI deadline envelope.

## Exact originals and financial owners

The graph pins product/schema, complete known contract, date/reset/calendar/index binding and review policies, full immutable original curve source and supplied original OAS. Each warm request is admitted before lookup. Current market edits are allowed; changing original input requires rebuilding the handle (`BASE_ANCHOR_CHANGED`). Float signed zero participates in native serde-byte key identity. Hashes accelerate lookup; complete serialized key and parent equality decide a hit.

`market_indexed_adapter::requests` mechanically extracts only DTO construction from the existing case function. The original case still invokes the same actual owners in the same order. The graph invokes `indexed::build_path` for complete actual-date contractual cash and `swaps::value_swap` for clean swap value. Its indexed-loan reduction calls **`term_product_graph::pricing::price` with supplied original OAS**. It does not call `TermGraph::new`, `Graph::build` calibration, or `pricing::solve`. Swap spread adjustment uses the adapter's same cash/OAS convention. Graph counters report actual projection/cash/clean/spread/loan node computations and hits. The frozen predecessor's calibration counter evidence and this branch's actual call graph establish zero OAS refits; no global instrumentation is proposed for production.

Projection and collateral curves have separate parents. Collateral-only edits reuse cash and reprice marks. Index edits change cash; a source-revision change invalidates source-dependent nodes. Original and current/bumped results keep the original OAS. All active Arc request/results survive through risk even when cache insertion is refused or eviction occurs.

## Admission

Per graph: 1 MiB serialized typed input, at most 512 periods, 16 curves per market, and 4096 nodes per curve. Cache capacity is at most 16 MiB /4096 entries. Original and current full curve/date validation occurs before serialization or generation; source validation polls active Control between admitted groups and retains the deadline reason.

Let `a` be the existing adapter admission, `b` the existing bridge admission, and `r=max(serialized current graph request, serialized retained initial graph request)`. Each call charges:

* bytes: `4*a.retained_bytes + 3*b.retained_bytes + 16*r + configured_cache_bytes + 262144`, at most 128 MiB;
* work: `a.numerical_work + b.admitted_work + 64*r`, at most 60 million;
* serialized graph result: at most 32 MiB.

The maximum initial/current metadata term retains the original anchor budget even when later current inputs shrink. Cache bytes include retained nodes/identities; the formula additionally reserves pinned product results, raw originals and transient projection/risk arrays. Registry/parser/allocator/process overhead remains separate; this is not an aggregate RSS or 60,000-position acceptance claim. Old legacy cache limits are unchanged.

## Acceptance and patch boundaries

`new/tests/market_indexed_registry.rs` covers real dispatcher/registry ownership, creation admission/cancellation/deadline, warm/current validation, curve invalidation, clear/drop, original product/version/OAS including signed zero, and real-byte nested aliases/duplicates. A separate copied-target-only test executes the unchanged installed legacy registry and proposed registry side by side, comparing serialized create/info/price/compare/clear/drop outputs and unknown-handle errors. Its captured golden output is versionable; it does not add a second production pricer.

`run_reference.py` independently reconstructs contractual cash, forward projections, swap/loan PV and risk, exact raw originals, and admission for 30 complete real-registry results and 9 raw process failures. It uses the existing independent reference, never a native financial callback. `check_transport.py` exercises the proposed additive `NativeMarketIndexedGraph` with mocked library transport and verifies captured binary identity, close/drop and no extra callback. The acceptance sequence harness buffers each record through Value, so duplicate-byte admission is established by the direct native dispatcher tests, not that harness.

The prospective patch owns narrow changes to Risk `incremental.rs`, `term_protocol.rs`, module exports/DTO helper visibility; a new graph module/tests; additive pure transport in `core/graph_native.py`; an independent reference module; and documentation. It contains no solver instrumentation, acceptance-only cloned registry, installed artifact executable, API durable publication, or UI changes.

## Remaining adoption

This is a reviewable actual registry branch proposal, not installed production adoption. It supports supplied Pricing curves for an indexed lending asset and a vanilla payer/receiver swap, with deterministic paired curve bumps. `stochastic_crn`, `physical_accounting`, `production_adoption`, `saved_library_adoption`, and `capital_ftp_eligible` remain false. The deterministic pairing policy is explicit; it does not describe stochastic LMM or joint-driver dynamics.

Root would need to apply/rebuild/version this branch, add default native/process callback-forbidden gates, and separately bind raw books to complete typed sources before the generic `price_books` dispatcher can select it. Existing saved numeric rows cannot supply missing original curves/reset/calendar parents implicitly. Saved books, candidate/library/cohort reconstruction, decision dirty/source refresh and persisted independent verification must preserve those exact parents and original OAS; they remain open. Physical observed fixings, income/accounting, conditional stochastic histories, smiles/options, behavioral/credit coupling, empirical calibration, capital/FTP and combined scale acceptance are also outside this slice.

# Supplied multi-curve, smile and joint market analysis

`model-market-1` is a bounded Rust analysis contract implemented in
`portfolio-risk-native::model_market`. The native transport accepts the same raw
JSON shown in `examples/models/model-market-1.json`. Source revisions, currency,
as-of ordinal, model and assumption identity are explicit. All parameters are
supplied inputs; a synthetic example is not a fitted or observed market.

## Curves and basis

Collateral discount factors and index pseudo-discount factors have distinct typed
roles. A caller supplies positive factors with exact `(time=0, factor=1)` anchors,
strictly increasing times and an explicit right-tail policy. Negative interest
rates are admissible: factors can exceed one. The contract does not bootstrap
par instruments, infer collateral agreements or create an index curve from the
collateral curve. Separate discount and forward curves follow the distinctions
in [OpenGamma's multi-curve research](https://quant.opengamma.io/Multi-Curves-Variations2.pdf).

Between nodes, `log D(t)` is linear. Thus for `w=(t-t_i)/(t_j-t_i)`,
`D(t)=exp((1-w) log D_i+w log D_j)`. This is the log-linear definition in
[Strata's interpolation documentation](https://strata.opengamma.io/apidocs/com/opengamma/strata/market/curve/interpolator/CurveInterpolators.html).
Exact nodes return the supplied factor. The right tail is one of: reject,
flat continuously compounded zero rate (`log D(t)=t log D(T)/T`), or flat
instantaneous forward (`log D(t)=log D(T)+(t-T) last_log_slope`). Tail use is
returned independently for collateral and index. A left tail is unnecessary
because the time-zero anchor is compulsory and negative times are rejected.

For a caller-supplied contractual accrual fraction `tau`, the simple forward is
`F=(D(start)/D(end)-1)/tau`, evaluated using `expm1(log D(start)-log D(end))`.
The result reports the index forward, collateral-implied forward, their difference
as index basis, and collateral discounting at the payment endpoint. Times and
accrual fractions are separate: no implicit 30-day/calendar/day-count assumption
converts between them. Queries enforce typed roles and common currency.

## Quote surfaces and option values

A complete rectangular grid has axes expiry, underlying tenor and **absolute
strike**, with row-major `[expiry, tenor, strike]` values. Strike-dependent quotes
represent supplied smile/skew rather than an ATM label applied to all strikes.
Normal volatility uses absolute rate units per square-root year; shifted-lognormal
volatility uses relative units per square-root year and a supplied nonnegative
shift. Normal conventions permit negative forwards and strikes. Shifted-lognormal
requires strictly positive shifted forward and strike, including at zero
volatility. Normal and Black formulas/conventions are described in the primary
[finmath Bachelier](https://www.finmath.net/finmath-lib/apidocs/net.finmath.lib/net/finmath/functions/BachelierModel.html)
and [analytic formula](https://www.finmath.net/finmath-lib/apidocs/net.finmath.lib/net/finmath/functions/AnalyticFormulas.html)
documentation.

Interpolation is multilinear in total variance `v=sigma^2*expiry`, including the
strike and tenor axes. Returned `sigma=sqrt(v/queried_expiry)`; the zero-expiry
price is intrinsic. Each axis has an explicit reject or flat-volatility tail.
For an expiry tail, boundary volatility is held flat and variance grows with
queried expiry. Tail and interpolation flags accompany every result. This is a
representation/interpolator, not an arbitrage-free calibration: arbitrary inputs
may violate calendar monotonicity or call-price convexity, and interpolation does
not enforce those conditions. No SABR, local/stochastic volatility dynamics or
quote fit is inferred.

Let `U` be supplied payoff unit, `s=sigma sqrt(T)`, `phi` the standard normal
density and `Phi` its CDF. A normal call is
`U*((F-K)*Phi((F-K)/s)+s*phi((F-K)/s))`. Shifted Black uses `f=F+shift`,
`k=K+shift`, `d1=log(f/k)/s+s/2`, `d2=d1-s` and
`U*(f*Phi(d1)-k*Phi(d2))`. Put-call parity is `call-put=U*(F-K)` in both
conventions. Implementation evaluates out-of-the-money time value plus intrinsic
to avoid in-the-money subtraction; small Black ATM values use a centered CDF.
The caller owns the economic annuity/discount/notional behind `U`; this analysis
does not silently infer swaption or caplet settlement conventions.

The native Gaussian CDF evaluates a convergent centered power series for small
arguments and the error-function/Mills-ratio continued fraction for larger ones,
consistent with [NIST DLMF 7.9](https://dlmf.nist.gov/7.9). The series has a
128-term bound and the fraction 512 levels. Beyond a standardized option argument
of 38 the numerically negligible tail is zero; this is an explicit option
numerical guard, not truncation of simulated regional HPI innovations. A negative
time value within a machine-roundoff bound is set to zero; a larger discrepancy
is an error. Monetary values above the shared `1e15` bound are rejected.

## Joint rate, mortgage spread and regional log-HPI innovations

Drivers have stable ordered identities and coordinate units: rate factors and
mortgage spread in decimal rates, regional HPI in log changes. At least one of
each type is required. The input is an annual covariance matrix, positive actual
year fractions per step, path count, retained eigenfactor count and either native
seed words or an exact supplied standard-normal tape. The output contains additive
zero-drift Gaussian increments, cumulative terminal changes, and diagnostics.
There is no inferred mean reversion, market price of risk, forward-measure drift,
LMM, mortgage discount path or HPI-level conversion in this contract. The shock
analysis alone is not a physical- or pricing-measure product projection.

For diagonal standard deviations `S`, form correlation `R=S^-1 C S^-1`.
Symmetry is exact at the supplied covariance boundary. A zero-variance row must
be identically zero. Correlation bounds and PSD are checked in normalized units
so an invalid small-variance coordinate cannot be hidden by a large coordinate.
Negative eigenvalues below `-8*machine_epsilon*driver_count` reject the input;
only roundoff-size negatives are zeroed for the square root and reported.
Diagonal correlation is exactly one for nonzero variance. A computed off-diagonal
correlation outside one by at most four machine epsilons is bounded to one and
the adjustment is reported; larger violations fail. This is no nearest-PSD
repair of materially invalid covariance.

For sorted correlation eigenmodes, let
`L=S*V_k*sqrt(Lambda_k)*V_k^T`. Each step is `delta=L*z*sqrt(dt)`, with `z`
still having the full number of named driver coordinates when factors are
truncated. Full rank reconstructs the supplied covariance to floating-point
accuracy. Explicit truncation is of **correlation** eigenmodes, not necessarily
the largest raw rate/log-HPI covariance eigenmodes; returned retained covariance
`L L^T` and Frobenius discarded error make that approximation measurable.

Native draws reuse the existing `random::SharedDraws` PCG/SeedSequence/Ziggurat
Gaussian machinery, using its full rate tape as the joint driver tape. Antithetic
paths negate all joint coordinates together. Complete seed, ordered driver list,
path/step shape and duration grid identity must be retained by consumers. Changing
covariance or retained factors keeps these standard normals unchanged; changing
dimensions does not promise the same CRN sequence. Supplied tapes allow
independent controlled-covariance and timestep fixtures. No simulated Gaussian
tail is clipped. The legacy helper additionally allocates its unused spread and
HPI tapes; these component allocations remain additional to the joint result.

Diagnostics report means and population covariance of `delta/sqrt(dt)` pooled
over paths and steps, and theoretical retained covariance. They assess this
simulation; they are not held-out statistical calibration diagnostics. Historical
regime, source, sampling frequency, covariance estimation, forward drift and
regional dependency calibration must be supplied/validated by a separate stage.

## Admission and validation scope

There are at most 64 curves, 4,096 nodes per curve and 4,096 combined queries.
Curve times are in `[0,100]`, factors in `[1e-100,1e100]`, and query simple
forwards in `[-100,100]`; overflow fails instead of clipping. The smile allows
128 expiries, 128 tenors, 256 strikes and at most 65,536 complete quotes. Expiry
and tenor are bounded by 100 years; strikes/forwards by `[-2,2]`, normal volatility
by `[0,2]`, shifted-lognormal volatility by `[0,5]`, and shift by `[0,2]`.
Joint requests have at most 16 drivers, 4,096 steps, 100,000 paths, one million
scalar increments, and eight million transform-work units per matrix pass.
Variance is at most four in declared coordinate units; total duration is at most
100 years. Supplied standard normals outside `[-100,100]` fail admission. Sources
and identifiers are bounded to 256 bytes and rationale to 1,024 bytes. Unknown
fields, missing source identity, duplicate curves/drivers/regions, mismatched
currency, non-finite domains, and malformed shapes fail. These are component
work/size bounds, not an aggregate RSS guarantee or complete graph deadline gate.

`tests/model_market.rs` has 19 independent fixtures: exact curve nodes and
log-DF midpoint, distinct tails and basis, negative rates, hand total variance,
normal/shifted-Black ATM and out-of-the-money price/parity, small-volatility
stability, controlled exact covariance, rank deficiency, invalid tiny-axis PSD,
nonbinary variance roundoff, native seed golden draw and antithetics, covariance
CRN scaling, Brownian timestep aggregation, explicit factor error, admission and
strict JSON checks, and the persisted synthetic example. The companion deposit
example retains physical measure and two actual-day interest expense independently.

Remaining #10 acceptance includes source-linked quote bootstrapping and residuals,
arbitrage diagnostics/calibration, observed joint-driver estimation and chronological
held-out tests, uncertainty and regional stress validation, product/native graph
and cache adoption with full curve/quote/grid/CRN identities, discretization and
factor-convergence reports on real product outputs, and combined runtime limits.
The analysis route does not automatically change legacy built-in economics or
establish empirical accuracy. Those acceptance gates remain open.

## Retrospective published-rate diagnostic artifact

`artifacts/observed-market-driver-stage/` contains an isolated Rust diagnostic
and independent reference over a hashed Treasury history download. It is not an
installed native model or pricing calibration. Six nominal/real par-yield series
have 2,750 complete dates from 2015–2025, with 1,999 training intervals through
2022 and 749 later holdout intervals. The interval crossing Treasury's declared
2021-12-06 methodology change is excluded; values are not filled or interpolated.
The source is a latest-download retrospective vintage, not a point-in-time archive.

Rust fits constant calendar-time drift/covariance and reports holdout normalized
bias, RMSE and three-sigma exceedances. Eight native hand/admission/cancellation/
leakage tests and strict all-target Clippy pass; five numerical result fields match
independent NumPy calculations, and holdout mutation leaves the training fit exactly
unchanged. Nominal 2y holdout exceedances are about 8%, so this pooled covariance
does not establish predictive adequacy. No production, pricing-measure or empirical
predictive acceptance flag is set. See the artifact README, retained request/raw
source hashes and `observed-validation.json` for equations, bounds and limitations.
Holdout bias/RMSE have units decimal yield per square-root year; they are not
dimensionless sigma-standardized scores.
Product/factor adoption, publication vintages, regime/uncertainty diagnostics and
the full issue #10 criteria remain required.

The isolated successor `artifacts/observed-market-regime-stage` diagnoses eleven
supplied calendar-year periods without changing the pooled training fit. Six
native tests and strict Clippy pass; independent references verify every period,
exact predecessor output identity and exact held-out training-fit invariance.
Nominal two-year three-sigma exceedances are 15.6% in 2023, 4.8% in 2024 and about
4.0% in 2025 under the frozen training moments. This descriptive instability
assessment does not select regimes or establish statistical/predictive acceptance.
The retained source, vintage and pricing/product limitations above still apply.

The isolated `artifacts/market-smile-diagnostics-stage` additionally audits
supplied strike rows with the existing native option arithmetic. It reports
intrinsic/shifted-underlying bounds, vertical-spread bounds and nonnegative
butterflies with explicit rate/slope thresholds. Six native tests, strict Clippy,
36 independent normal/shifted-Black CLI rows and seven raw rejections pass.
Quotes and financial comparison tolerances are unchanged. This does not certify
calendar, interpolation or wing behavior and does not calibrate/repair the smile
or adopt it into production pricing. The complete #10 criteria remain required.

# Native option price and risk comparison

This synthetic study executes the unchanged Rust shifted-lognormal LMM and
cash-settled European swaption kernels. It publishes timestep, path and factor
comparisons required by issue #10; it does not admit a new volatility model,
establish observed calibration or complete that issue.

The accepted local predecessor passes 2,227 engine tests (two reference-only
skips), 590 API tests and 45 scoped browser checks. Its immutable receipt is
`artifacts/product-adoption-0298-capital-browser-repair-acceptance.json`.
The study uses an exact separate copy of its Risk DLL, SHA-256
`0bc08f27a264c07887478cc82f60b8371fda2a4224edbe6fd171f919507eaa42`.
It changes no production settings, source, saved economics or artifacts.

## Method and financial meaning

Thirty-two quarterly initial forwards are flat at either 3% or -0.5%, with a
4% displacement and supplied 25% volatility. The supplied correlation is
`exp(-0.10 * quarter_years * abs(i-j))`. One/two/three-factor loadings are fitted
by the actual native fitter and independently checked. Eight/full-rank factors
are independently supplied reference loadings; the production fitter's three-
factor limit remains unchanged. Truncated loading rows are normalized to retain
individual forward variances, so factor truncation changes cross-forward
covariance. Full-rank covariance Frobenius error is approximately `1.83e-14`.
Volatility is held fixed across factor counts; each representation is not
recalibrated to observed swaption quotes. These differences therefore measure
this supplied covariance approximation, not empirical pricing error between
separately calibrated production models.

The 24 option contracts cover payer/receiver, one/two-year expiries, two/five-
year swap tenors and ATM/plus/minus 150 bp strikes. Grids use 12/24/48 annual
steps. Coarse Brownian increments sum matching fine increments. All price and
rate-bump comparisons retain the same draws. Nested 64/1,024/2,048 paths consist
of complete antithetic pairs, with 1,024 independent pairs at the largest size.
Means and estimated standard errors use pair averages as independent units.
Paired differences against the finest full-rank result report their own standard
errors; overlapping standalone error bars do not establish equal prices.

Reported DV01 is `(PV(-1bp)-PV(+1bp))/2` per unit face. It shifts every initial
simple forward by one basis point with volatility, covariance, strike, shift
and draws fixed. It is not a bootstrapped market-quote or key-rate sensitivity.
Native option marks and this paired risk are independently recomputed from
pathwise discounted payoffs. Four small scalar LMM controls compare complete
discount, swap and short-rate output at the unchanged `1e-10` checks.

## Recorded findings

For the ATM two-year-expiry/five-year payer at 48 annual steps and 2,048 paths,
the three-factor representation remains measurably different from the full-rank
reference. Amounts below are per 100 face; standard errors are paired differences.

| Initial forwards | Three-factor PV | Full-rank PV | PV difference | Difference standard error |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3% | 3.870259 | 3.747406 | 0.122853 | 0.006630 |
| -0.5% | 2.274601 | 2.204173 | 0.070428 | 0.004360 |

The full-rank monthly-to-48-step PV difference is -0.013017 per 100 face for
the positive curve, and -0.001331 for the negative curve. Finer stepping does
not remove the factor approximation. Risk differences have separate uncertainty:
the three-minus-full-rank DV01 difference is approximately +0.000050 and
-0.000192 per 100 face respectively, with paired standard errors approximately
0.000093 and 0.000114. These two risk cases do not support an equally strong
claim about factor sensitivity as their corresponding PV comparisons.

The complete 2,160 comparison rows, pair counts, seed, covariance errors,
scalar controls and source/artifact identities are in
`artifacts/option-product-convergence-study/results.json`, SHA-256
`8922f9f55df4f0bd10a2e63d7f493d04268fa447c855f8cb24aed3a819330e23`.
The scientific figure and its identity are retained alongside it. All finite-
sample results belong to this supplied configuration and seed; no automatic
convergence threshold, empirical accuracy or new-model acceptance is inferred.

## Preserved assumptions and remaining work

The legacy discount output is recorded after its same-index discount update,
while swap rates are recorded before the rate step. The existing cash-annuity
negative-rate floor remains. Grid comparisons therefore include those existing
clock conventions, and cannot certify actual-date or multicurve settlement.
No tolerance, reduction ordering or financial default is changed by the study.

Quote-calibrated smile/skew, joint rate/spread/HPI generation, actual-date
settlement, independent settlement references, observed calibration/vintages,
holdouts, model admission and full product/cohort/saved-book/scale adoption
remain separate requirements. A three-factor legacy price must not be described
as full-rank convergence on the strength of native/reference implementation parity.

Coarse/fine Brownian coupling follows page 22 of
[Giles's multilevel Monte Carlo lecture](https://www2.maths.ox.ac.uk/~gilesm/talks/imperial_15.pdf).
The separation of process grids and product conventions is also explicit in
[finmath's Brownian motion interface](https://www.finmath.net/finmath-lib/apidocs/net.finmath.lib/net/finmath/montecarlo/BrownianMotion.html).
Here these ideas support paired numerical diagnostics; the study does not
implement a multilevel estimator or claim a theorem's convergence order for
the existing shifted log-Euler implementation.

# Source-linked par-quote bootstrap

`market-quote-bootstrap-1` is a bounded analytical contract for turning
source-linked fixed-leg par quotes into a discount-factor curve. It is
implemented in `portfolio-risk-native::market_bootstrap` and exposed through
`bootstrap_market_quotes`. The request retains source and curve identities,
every payment time, every accrual fraction, and separate bootstrap versus
validation quotes. The result is adoption-ineligible until a reviewed market
configuration binds its curve, collateral, currency, calendar and quote
vintage to production pricing.

Each bootstrap quote adds exactly one new maturity pillar. For a quote with
rate `c`, payments `(t_k, alpha_k)`, known earlier discounts `D_k`, and final
discount `D_T`, the unit-notional par condition is

```text
1 = c * sum_k(alpha_k D_k) + D_T
```

The final discount is solved in closed form after the caller supplies the
complete schedule. Every non-final payment must match an earlier bootstrapped
pillar; the contract rejects an unseen intermediate date rather than silently
interpolating it. All payment times and accrual fractions are explicit. No
annual, 30/360, business-day, holiday, collateral or compounding convention
is inferred by the adapter.

For each quote, the result recomputes

```text
c_model = (1 - D_T) / sum_k(alpha_k D_k)
residual = c_model - c_observed
unit_par_pv = c_model * sum_k(alpha_k D_k) + D_T
```

Bootstrap residuals must be within the closed-form numerical tolerance. A
validation quote must use already-created pillars and is allowed to show a
nonzero residual; this provides an independent quote-fit diagnostic rather
than a false claim that every source quote was an exact input to the fit.

The result reports a deterministic convergence receipt for the sequential
closed-form method, but this is numerical convergence only. It is not a proof
of quote quality, arbitrage freedom, collateral consistency, or predictive
market calibration. Smile dynamics, basis construction, risk-neutral drift,
observed quote-vintage backtesting and product adoption remain separate issue
#10 gates. Negative par rates are admitted where the supplied schedule produces
a positive discount factor; invalid denominators, nonpositive factors,
duplicate identities, unseen intermediate dates and malformed schedules fail
closedly without clipping.

Controlled native and independent adapter tests cover exact pillar recovery,
validation residuals, identity and schedule rejection, public dispatch and
cancellation. The synthetic example is arithmetic evidence only; it does not
close the empirical or production acceptance requirements.

Independent publication verification also checks the exact admitted payment
work count, bootstrap quote count type and unchanged residual gate. Nonfinite
quote diagnostics and altered tolerances reject. Verification retains the
original deadline/cancellation callback through quote replay.

This separation follows current model-risk practice: [SR 26-2](https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602.htm)
calls for validation to assess reliability and limitations, while [Strata's
market-quote sensitivity documentation](https://strata.opengamma.io/apidocs/com/opengamma/strata/pricer/sensitivity/MarketQuoteSensitivityCalculator.html)
identifies par-rate quotes as calibration instruments whose quote mapping and
sensitivities should remain inspectable. The contract therefore publishes
source identities and residuals without treating a synthetic fit as approval.

# Reviewed performing-deposit portfolio FTP source

The explicit `deposit_portfolio` source kind selects the complete
`deposit-performing-portfolio-ledger-2` owner and the separately bounded
`modeled-product-ftp-source-channels-2` funding tier. It does not relabel or change
historical `deposit_performing` or Card2 source behavior. Funding and charge
formulas are common to both tiers; the additional tier admits complete longer
histories and multiple exclusive owners only when their joined work and capacity
reservations fit.

## Inputs and economic ownership

Select compatible completed performing-deposit portfolio jobs in Capital & FTP,
check their bounded metadata, and supply a source alias, scope-review identity,
complete indexed owner/run/path reviews and the full reviewed funding policy.
The whole-portfolio scope is `whole_performing_deposit_portfolio-2`; path index is
zero for each supplied owner/run. Metadata checking establishes compatibility,
never permission, regulatory eligibility, funding assumptions or empirical fit.
The raw synthetic-example mode remains available separately.

The source retains supplied original cost, principal and original yield anchor,
complete original and revised physical histories, observed prefix, paid-rate lag,
revision policy, actual native principal atoms and gross FIFO earned/cash origins.
The actual source journals are independently regenerated and replayed before FTP
publication. No new draw, inflow, migration, unknown prefix, seasoned-anchor,
negative-EIR or credit policy is inferred. Historical source-domain refusals remain.

Funding is built from native source-owned daily principal, signed basis and gross
rights. Actual cash is retained with explicit exclusion from a second funding
roll-forward. Original-EIR earnings and reviewed expectation-revision P&L have
separate labels and user-supplied inclusion rules. Rate-reset/reference tenor stays separate from behavioral funding/liquidity life.
Contingent, option, collateral and haircut inputs require their own explicit
reviewed policies; no new draw or collateral model is supplied by this deposit
route. If reviewed FTP and stress behavior differ, that difference must be
retained and disclosed. Internal business and treasury transfers offset; they do
not create external NII or regulatory capital.

A completed job ID is lineage, not an economic owner identifier. New-tier sources
require explicit raw account entity/currency identities and must have disjoint
`(entity, currency, canonical position ID)` identities across
selected portfolio jobs, even if their accounts or source aliases differ. Every
original/current owner/run tail is checked before participation; job selection
cannot omit an unused run or a gross origin to gain admission.

## Bounded native admission

The new primitive tier has a 365-day shape ceiling, 368 origins per state, 366
resets, 8M preparation work and 8MiB per primitive input/output. These are ceilings,
not a guarantee that every tuple fits. The source compiler independently retains
8M joined work and 32MiB component capacity; the outer source adapter retains
48M/256MiB and the complete FTP coordinator 62M/384MiB, with a 32MiB output limit.
All complete source histories, output staging and reviewed paths are charged
before source generation. Historical tier1 keeps its 64-day/2M/1MiB contracts.

For horizon H, one-segment no-inflow/no-migration ownership has I<=H earned origins
and C<=3H+1 cash events. Counted FIFO creates at most I+C fragments. The conversion
indexes those fragments once, retains native subtraction order and emits all
applicable gross origins. Conservative conversion work includes the historical
`state_count*18*256`, plus `(H+1)*(H+3)*96` and
`(H+1)*review_count*64` per review. Each portfolio source additionally reserves
16 work units and 10 capacity bytes per serialized typed-request byte for bounded
serialization/reparse staging. This restores the standalone selected Rust DTO
allocation boundary without changing raw identities or financial comparisons.
The existing active deadline remains in force; no nested Control or renewed
budget is created. Component capacity is not an aggregate RSS guarantee.

## Publication and remaining gates

The completed-source binder rechecks exact queued raw and declared Rust DTO
clones, current source/object descriptors, complete source journals, actual
producer completion and bounded Parquet frames. The new FTP job retains its
original accepted deadline and private authority through upload/reopen. Its
final SQLite guard rechecks queued request, current code/native bundle, source
objects, STOP, lease and token within the publication transaction. Calculation
receipts alone cannot grant permission or substitute for these gates.

The contained proposal demonstrates two-owner/two-run 40-day and one-owner/two-run
90-day cases through actual workers, the selector, native FTP, persisted replay,
private SQL, paged tables and reopen; corresponding late SQL refusals publish no
result. It is not installed-default acceptance, PostgreSQL validation, empirical
calibration or complete #14/#24 adoption. Full joint 60k scale, broader products,
saved-book/cohort mapping and all empirical gates remain required. Accounting
standard approval and regulatory permissions remain explicit and ungranted.
