# Source-linked modeled product FTP

The explicit `modeled-product-ftp-preparation-1` contract reconstructs selected
Physical product sources, prepares reviewed daily funding balances, and invokes
the existing native Treasury owner. It keeps actual cash, earned income, carrying
adjustments, credit accounting and internal transfers separately traceable.
This is one implementation stage of issue #24; all original issue #25 gates remain
required. Applied source and successful acceptance of a particular source bundle
are separate facts.

## Owners and inputs

`portfolio-model-core::modeled_product_funding` owns the common state-channel,
cash-assignment, reset and daily-averaging contract. The shared
`modeled_product_ftp_policy` module contains typed bindings and review identities.
`portfolio-decision-native::modeled_product_ftp_source` rebuilds raw sources through
their existing product/journal owners, then maps their evidence into that contract.
`modeled_product_ftp` admits the combined problem and invokes native Risk Treasury.
`portfolio-risk-native::modeled_ftp_policy` owns the two explicit comparative-cost
formulas. Python transports inputs, stores tables and independently verifies raw
sources and persisted output; it does not generate the production financial result.

Each source has an immutable `source_id`, declared scope and review identity.
The selected variants are acquired mortgage mixed accounting, acquired installment
or Card2 mixed accounting, revised deposit income, and performing deposit source
continuation. The native source journal and actual producer completion survive
preparation. Reviews bind exactly to `(source_id, owner_index, run_index, path_index)`;
missing, duplicate and surplus bindings fail. Inherited dated backbook owners are
retained as evidence but do not automatically become funded product exposures.

The first durable API route accepts explicit raw sources. Selection of completed
Card2 or deposit jobs needs a separate source-binding integration; a job identifier
alone cannot supply the original raw source, policy or journal authority.

Every path requires entity, currency/unit, source/anchor identity, full start/end
dates, physical weight, unit face, allocation, reviewed funding policy and reset
schedule. Paid rates, original effective yield, reviewed allowance/credit policy,
recovery cash and collection cost remain owned by the source model. No source
permission becomes accounting-standard or regulatory approval by passing through FTP.

## Funding state and complete rights

The common state retains eighteen ordered channels:

- Active, pending-default, pending-prepay and default-claim principal.
- Live and default interest receivables/payables.
- Principal, live-interest, default-principal and default-interest basis.
- Borrower and economic principal/interest memos, undrawn commitments and allowance.

Each channel has complete source-origin lineage and an explicit reviewed coefficient
in `{-1, 0, 1}`. Borrower/economic memos, undrawn memo and allowance require coefficient
zero: they cannot be converted into funding exposure. Gross channels stay nonnegative;
the four carrying-basis channels retain their signed source amounts. The selected
funding balance at checkpoint `d` is

`F_d = sum(channel_coefficient_i * source_channel_i,d)`.

Ordered cash assignments and separately reviewed noncash reallocations must reproduce
every subsequent checkpoint. An assigned cash event changes funding by
`-side * bank_cash`, where asset side is `+1` and liability side is `-1`; an event
instead excluded from funding requires an explicit exclusion review. A cash event
cannot be assigned twice or both assigned and excluded. Noncash reallocations
cannot invent cash.

Source-weight and allocation scaling occurs once:
`scale = allocated_face / unit_face * source_weight`. Funding, cash and earnings
are scaled after the complete unweighted source has been checked. Zero participation
does not excuse missing tails or contradictory source state.

Policies explicitly choose opening-daily or trapezoid-daily averaging:
`average_d = F_(d-1)` or `(F_(d-1) + F_d) / 2`. This tier uses ACT/365F, with daily
fraction `1/365`. Supplied reset schedules independently retain reference/repricing
and liquidity/funding tenors; the last reset strictly before the ending day applies.
Tenors are not inferred from repayment cash or account labels.

Principal reaching zero does not terminate interest rights, basis, recoveries or
commitments. The terminal checkpoint must close every unweighted channel and each
individual origin. Complete tails cannot be replaced with synthetic maturity cash.
The common research contract can retain signed funding under an explicit policy;
the existing Treasury-position bridge rejects negative funded exposures.

## Earnings, acquisition and internal transfers

Seven distinct signed bank-profit channels are retained: original EIR, reviewed
basis, incurred credit, recovery income, recovery cost, initial allowance and deposit
revision. Original EIR is earned income supplied by the accounting source, not
coupon cash. Cash repayment, gross recovery and a carrying-basis realization cannot
silently become a second copy of recurring income.

The selected acquisition phase retains actual source-owned purchase cash and initial
allowance postings once. These opening amounts are separately reconciled to the
native ordered journal; deposit continuation does not receive an invented purchase
cash flow. The mandatory policy is
`actual_owned_purchase_and_initial_allowance_once-1`.

The existing native Treasury owner computes matched-tenor reference and liquidity
charges, entity/currency/scenario/period elimination, profitability, economic profit
and annualized RAROC. Its linear curve interpolation and disclosed flat tails remain
unchanged. Reviewed operating costs and allocated capital are explicit inputs.
Daily Treasury positions carry original EIR; the accompanying accounting-scope
reconciliation adds the other six earnings channels exactly once. In that complete
scope, `business_profit + treasury_profit = source_earnings - operating_cost`.
Internal transfers do not alter external earnings, OAS or regulatory capital.

## Explicit comparative charges

This stage implements reviewed Physical-scenario incremental costs. They are not
pricing-measure option fair values. Each selected path requires compatible complete
benchmark paths, reviewed annual rates and the exact rate vintage.

`option_amount_d = max(funded_average_d - benchmark_average_d, 0) * rate * 1/365`.

`contingent_amount_d = max(native_undrawn_d - benchmark_undrawn_d, 0) * rate * 1/365`.

Undrawn amounts come from reconstructed source commitments, not caller-supplied
surrogate balances. The positive part belongs only to the stated cost methodology;
source cash, carrying amounts, income and regulatory exposures are not clipped.
The option amount converts to the existing Treasury spread only against a positive
funding/accrual basis. A nonzero amount at zero basis rejects. Annual comparative
rates and derived spreads are bounded to one.

Optional closing capital is currently the separately reviewed mortgage complete-tail
bridge. Its raw mortgage source must match the FTP source exactly, with explicit
capital policy, monetary multiplier and closing date. Interim/report-date capital,
automatic eligibility and jurisdiction-specific regulatory inputs are separate work.
Dirty retained unit dependencies require refreshed capital preparation; this route
requires `clean_frozen_units-1`.

## Durable execution and verification

`POST /treasury/modeled-product-ftp` queues `modeled_product_ftp.run` on the durable
worker. The example is synthetic. The request retains its original raw JSON and
finite queue-time deadline, workspace revision, code/source identity and executable
bundle. Selected JSON admission rejects duplicate keys, including nested variants.
Missing or mismatched native artifacts fail without fallback.

Independent verification reconstructs raw source state, source journals, complete
funding/earnings channels and comparative charges before storage. Publication retains
the complete native result plus strict typed FTP reconciliation, source-journal and
actual completion tables. Persisted output is reread and independently compared,
including exact source/metadata identity and unchanged financial tolerances.
Object-body and partition hashes, original deadline, cancellation, revision, attempt,
lease and token are fenced through the final scoped SQL transaction. Reopening,
paging and downloading use immutable published artifacts.

The separate reviewed successor adds
`POST /treasury/modeled-product-ftp/sources` with an explicit
`modeled-product-ftp-completed-selection-1` specification. It requires one or two
distinct completed source jobs, exact tagged scopes/reviews and the existing FTP
policy template with source records omitted. The server captures raw source records
from completed Card2 mixed or performing-deposit jobs; the worker independently
replays those records and reconciles fresh native FTP source preparation. Original
completed-job deadlines remain provenance; the new job's original deadline begins
before metadata reads and covers reopening, native execution and publication.
Completed source status or a saved verification flag never supplies funding policy
or eligibility. Source request/result descriptors, executed identities, owner/token/
attempt and raw state are rechecked during persistence and inside final SQL completion.

The successor separately checks original typed input clones exactly. A monetary
comparison is not input identity: a preserved predecessor case accepted an original
yield clone changed by `1e-16`. New declared DTO normalization rejects that change
while retaining the original raw JSON types, signed zero and unchanged computed
amount tolerances. The helper's own file hash joins the queued/current code bundle.

## Bounds and current acceptance

The selected raw FTP body is at most 1 MiB; native complete output and joined stored
output are each bounded to 32 MiB. The shared channel tier admits up to 64 complete
daily intervals, 4,096 cash/change/earnings events, 65 resets and 128 origins per
checkpoint. Source composition admits at most four sources and sixteen selected
reviews. Preparation reserves source generation, channel conversion, acquisition
scan, charge work and optional capital replay before generation. Its combined work
ceiling is 62 million units and charged retained-capacity ceiling is 384 MiB.
The retained journal transport admits 250,000 rows. These component reservations
are not aggregate process-RSS guarantees or 60,000-position acceptance.

The reviewed 49-file public integration is applied under
`modeled-product-ftp-public-adoption-0298`. Its frozen 851-file source set has aggregate
SHA-256 `998d3fee404fde63dcfe3c27f801b8e2afa143d273c8774f6fb7b93a9d7874bd`.
All eleven matching official native build/check gates pass, with 923 native tests
and four strict crate checks. Fresh installed-default engine acceptance passes
2,237 tests with two reference-only skips. The API gate is terminal with 676
passing tests and one initial API-health startup failure in the actual restart
test; browser acceptance was not reached. Its original temporary process log is
no longer available, and the cause remains unproven. A retained reproduction
exposed a real local Windows long-path publication/read failure. The subsequent
852-file `modeled-product-ftp-public-adoption-0298-windows-storage-repair` has
aggregate `b82dd0a2458459ca3783faf9b48967ea8f5ea0b463d8acce395719e3a465ca2b`.
Its storage helper preserves relative object keys, checksum and scope; the exact
preimage fails and the helper passes on the same 415-character object path.
Twenty-five focused checks and the exact actual process restart case pass with
the existing timeout. Its API gate passes 679 tests and the existing browser scope
passes 47 cases. The required FTP browser failed on two full-result requests during
saving/reopening a paged report, so the storage source set is not accepted. Native/engine
results are explicitly reused because their source and artifacts are unchanged.
The missing original process log prevents a confirmed original-cause claim. The earlier
accepted deposit bundle does not establish acceptance of
this new financial source set. Evidence lives in the distinct application, native
gate and acceptance receipts under that prefix; failed receipts must be preserved.

The coherent 17-file selector/identity/UI correction is now applied under
`completed-product-ftp-ui-public-adoption-0298`. Its 859-file freeze aggregate is
`db900cf5b82d2371fa0ce9346b6049e37bb482ec0323e2d8849100a53d93ce9b`.
It retains the storage repair, reads strict real Codec descriptors, preserves
opaque raw Value fields, bounds logical table expansion, independently binds
declared source DTO clones and uses status-only polling for modeled reports.
All 22 official-default source-worker/metadata cases pass; architecture and
HTTP/native contract checks pass. Complete fresh validation passes 2,252 engine
tests with two reference-only skips, 701 API tests, 47 existing browser cases and
four FTP browser cases. The application receipt is complete. The unchanged
native financial source/artifacts explicitly reuse the 923-test build/check gate;
these results belong to the 859-file source set. The subsequent applied CD/source2
successor is undergoing separate fresh builds/default gates and inherits no
financial acceptance from these counts. Source2 multi-owner deposit funding/FTP remains a
separate additive native contract rather than a relabeled historical source1.
The contained successor now passes two actual completed-source browser flows and
two late-private-SQL refusal browser cases, with complete source comparison and
independent persisted replay. Final successor source freeze/application/default
acceptance remain required. See [joint funding validation](joint-funding-validation.md)
for the primary-source rationale, separate reset/funding tenors, exclusive owner
identity and required full-tail, collateral and empirical acceptance evidence.

The completed-source successor's frozen seven-file delta passes 105 contained
native/source/Codec/Parquet/SQL/HTTP checks and exact isolated patch roundtrip.
Manifest SHA-256 is `eb00338cffc9de01c22af7380afba083c33742b5eb97583da87814f97886bd11`.
It changes no Rust source, artifacts or numerical tolerances. At that predecessor
freeze, four actual default source-worker/selected-publication tests were authored
but unexecuted. Actual UI
source selection, installed acceptance and PostgreSQL evidence are separate gates.
The root application review passes, but application is held for matching predecessor
acceptance and a separate actual-source transport/identity repair. Real source-worker/
browser checks found normalization applied to opaque raw Value fields, missing
declared numeric DTO fields and unsupported Codec ObjectReference nodes. Preserved
standalone-versus-nested source receipts also require exact separately declared
raw/DTO clone binding. The operational-fixture suite does not establish that missing
actual source-worker/browser coverage. No financial tolerance or Rust calculation
change is authorized by these repairs. The unapplied delta is not evidence of
installed completed-source support.

Remaining full issue gates include completed-source bindings, broader product and
long-tail coverage, product/cohort/saved-book/strategy adoption, report-date capital,
observed behavioral/credit holdouts, reviewed regulatory policies and combined
60,000-position graph/credit/solver/journal acceptance. Supplied histories and
synthetic numerical checks cannot establish empirical predictive accuracy.

persisted verification and final publication. Retry does not extend it.

Rust rebuilds the complete raw mortgage source and its actual ordered journal.
It admits complete unweighted seven-slot principal, interest, signed basis,
borrower rights and default/economic claim tails, including zero allocations.
It checks authoritative native journal/trial/closing coverage and exact dates
before using the Risk crate's existing treasury bridge. No saved trial balance,
closure boolean or Python financial option supplies native authority.

Reviewed per-account/scenario capital inputs, monetary multiplier, risk weights
and negative net-carrying exposure policy remain explicit. Signed accounting
balances, including tiny negative basis, remain unchanged. The reviewed
nonnegative-group policy changes only the separate exposure used for supplied
risk-weight calculations. Research signed contributions are disclosed and an
aggregate negative credit-RWA denominator is rejected. The reject-negative
policy rejects negative groups rather than silently treating them as zero.

The independent Python verifier reopens original source, completion and bounded
partitions, reconstructs source economics and ordered GL, then verifies the
native capital result. It encodes normalized DTO types independently under
`typed-json-binary64-identity-1`: UTF-8 sorted keys, binary64 float bits, signed
zero and distinct integer/float/boolean domains. Original queued input identity
is retained separately from typed normalization.

The selected native operation reparses original request bytes after the
historical CLI peek. Its body limit is 2 MiB; historical whole input admission
remains 128 MiB, so this is not a preparse 2 MiB or aggregate RSS guarantee.
Source work retains its independent 8M admission and the bridge separately
reserves up to 2M work. Complete serialized source/control limits are unchanged.

Publication seals queued inputs, source and code bundle, executed binary,
owner/token/revision, original deadline and independent receipt. It rereads
checksummed source and capital-output bodies after replay and inside the final
SQL guard. The guard rechecks source metadata, current job, lease and workspace
revision in the publishing transaction. Failed native rebuild, cancellation,
expiry or changed evidence publishes no completed result reference.

Whole-number policy amounts and rates may arrive with integer JSON spelling.
The independent verifier retains their exact original reviewed input, then
constructs a private copy with only the declared native f64 policy fields typed
as floats. This covers weights, exclusions, capital inputs and minimum/buffer/
management requirements; it does not infer eligibility or requirements. Null
advanced RWA remains unavailable. Boolean money, unknown policy fields and
changed output weights reject; metadata, inclusion booleans, signed zero and

The reviewed route is applied locally in 0.29.8; matching official native builds
and component gates pass. Earlier setup/transport failures and their immutable
receipts are retained. The latest full engine/API gates pass 2,220/589 cases,
while browser acceptance exposes the financial policy spelling defect described
above. Its repair passes 18 focused engine and 11 durable API/source/capital/
publication-fence cases. Fresh full acceptance runs under
`product-adoption-0298-capital-browser-repair` now passes 2,227 engine tests
(two reference-only skips), 590 API tests and 45 scoped browser checks. Contained
proof, focused process checks and complete installed acceptance are distinct.

# Acquired whole-loan mortgage source and accounting carry

`mortgage-credit-accounting-1` is a bounded Rust analytical contract. It retains an immutable original mortgage source, a supplied current Physical scenario, one actual acquisition cost and original effective yield, exact interval carrying transport, and complete economic/book claim closeouts. It does not produce balanced journal entries or a daily mixed-book ledger. A review identity is supplied provenance, not accounting approval or certification of an observed balance.

The implementation is `packages/portfolio-model-core/src/products/mortgages/sequential_carry/mod.rs`, with private source, coupled-transport and default-interest helpers. The actual native mortgage loop remains in `mortgage_state.rs`; `mortgage_receipts.rs` provides borrowed observations from that same loop. The [synthetic request](../../examples/models/mortgage-credit-accounting-1.json) has explicit policies and complete original/current sources. It is an arithmetic example, not a calibrated loan or approved accounting policy.

Read this alongside [the native mortgage state contract](mortgage-state.md), [the shared credit/earned-interest operator](credit-operator.md), [actual-date income](dated-income.md), and the [Rust production contract](../rust-production-contract.md). Their respective financial ownership and compatibility contracts remain in force.

## Public API and schema versions

```text
mortgage_sequential_carry::admit(&Request) -> Result<Admission, String>
mortgage_sequential_carry::admit_with_check(&Request, check) -> Result<Admission, String>
mortgage_sequential_carry::evaluate(&Request) -> Result<ResultData, String>
mortgage_sequential_carry::evaluate_with_check(&Request, check) -> Result<ResultData, String>
mortgage_sequential_carry::run[_with_check](&Request, writer[, check]) -> Result<(), String>

mortgage_state::project(&MortgageRequest) -> Result<MortgageResult, String>
mortgage_state::project_with_receipts(&MortgageRequest, sink, check)
    -> Result<MortgageResult, String>
```

`check` is a cooperative `FnMut() -> Result<(), String>`. A sink implements `MortgageReceiptSink`. Callback values borrow actual native data and cannot outlive the callback; the interface supplies no setters or generator, rate, cash or state overrides.

| Layer | Schema |
|---|---|
| Public acquisition/source owner | `mortgage-credit-accounting-1` |
| Original and current raw mortgage contracts | `mortgage-state-1` |
| Captured interval DTO | `mortgage-loop-interval-1` |
| Borrowed callback contract | `mortgage-loop-receipts-1` |
| Private exact carrying operator | `mortgage-coupled-carry-1` |

The earlier artifact's `mortgage-sequential-carry-draft-1` remains a distinct proof-tool schema. It is not an alias accepted by this public owner. Schema/model changes require explicit selection and rebuilding; historical inputs are not silently relabeled or refitted. Python may independently verify results or transport raw requests but is not the production financial backend.

## Required raw inputs and admitted ownership

The typed request rejects unknown fields.

The new owner also rejects duplicate JSON object keys and extra fields in a fixed
rate object: its complete wire form is `{"kind":"fixed"}`. Unit enums use their
documented string forms; singleton-object aliases are rejected. These checks apply
to both original and current contracts and the reviewed interest policy. They are
confined to this new owner; historical mortgage parsing and financial formulas
retain their existing behavior.

Its required groups are:

| Field | Ownership and meaning |
|---|---|
| `contract` | Complete current native Physical mortgage request, including actual payment/reset/path dates and full native recovery tails. |
| `original_contract` | Complete immutable original Physical request used to validate the original acquisition quote. |
| `economic_source`, `original_economic_source` | Separate explicit source `id`/`revision`; each revision must match its corresponding raw mortgage source revision. |
| `path_id` | Explicit outer supplied-path identity. No source generation or empirical probability estimate is inferred. |
| `pairing` | Reviewed identity, exact original/current run IDs and `supplied_physical_original_contract_unchanged-1` selection. |
| `acquisition` | Acquisition identity, original-yield anchor, income-review identity, purchase ordinal, actual cost, original annual effective rate, opening gross carrying `[3]`, and `supplied_non_pcd_gross_cost-1`. |
| `policy` | Explicit supported accounting, cash, economic-right and full-tail policies, each with its required review identity. |

The initial slice admits whole loans only, with `remittance_lag_days=0`, equal opening borrower/investor principal, zero acquired borrower/investor/contractual accrued interest, purchase on the source as-of date, and actual `currency_units`. Opening gross carrying is nonnegative, belongs only to origins with nonzero opening principal, and sums to actual acquisition cost under the unchanged financial reconciliation tolerance. Cost is positive and respects the shared monetary domain; original annual effective yield is finite in `[-0.99, 10]`. Negative yield is supported without clipping. Signed basis is retained separately.

Both sources must have a complete contractual/payment/live-right tail. The owner does not infer an opening allowance, PCD adjustment, fee, nonaccrual-income convention, legal disposition, funding transfer or agency guarantee. The source's whole-loan recognized-accrual fractions remain supplied assumptions; a zero fraction stops new recognized contractual accrual but does not itself change the selected original-EIR policy.

## Original versus current source

Pairing requires exact typed equality of contractual terms, original loan/cohort/currency/model/source identities, as-of and opening state/probability vectors, ownership, day count, payment calendar and reset terms. Only these differences are admitted:

- Supplied `path` points, including current credit and prepayment drivers.
- Borrower collection fractions, LGD and complete native recovery tails.
- Explicitly paired run and assumption IDs.
- ARM reset `input`, while reset dates, index descriptors, calendar identities, margins, caps/floors and payment-recast rules remain unchanged.

Both complete fixing/projection inputs are retained. Availability/publication and selected observed-versus-projected semantics remain those of `mortgage-state-1`; no future fixing is inferred. Its calendar-mapping disclosure also remains in force.

Let original effective yield be `y`, `k=log1p(y)`, purchase date `d0`, and original actual cash rows be `(dj,Cj)`. Quote validation is

```text
original_quote_PV = sum_j Cj * exp(-k * (dj-d0)/365).
```

`Cj` includes original native principal/interest cash and separately reviewed original default-interest collections on their actual dates. Economic disposal is not cash and is not added to this quote. Quote PV must reconcile to the supplied actual cost. The policy is recorded as `complete_immutable_original_actual_cash_only-1`.

The current scenario never fits cost, yield or opening gross carrying. Original receipts do not post into current cash. Neither yield nor OAS is solved by this contract, and the Physical quote is not a pricing-measure conversion. Pricing-graph adoption still requires its separate fixed-original-OAS and paired-history gates.

## Exact coupled interval transport

Use row vectors and seven states: performing, watch, delinquent, default from each of those three origins, and prepaid. Let `Q` denote the actual same-loop transition generator, not a pricing measure. Exit states are absorbing. Probability and monetary vectors are distinct; expected monetary amounts already contain their population weighting and are never multiplied by probability again.

For one interval of `t` ACT/365F years, let `P` be principal, `A` recognized accrued interest, `G` gross carrying, `E` accumulated earned original-EIR reward, `R` the diagonal native recognized-contractual accrual rates, and `K=diag(k,k,k,0,0,0,0)`. The selected `stop_at_exit-1` policy gives

```text
probability' = probability Q
P' = P Q
A' = A Q + P R
G' = G (Q+K)
E' = E Q + G K
signed_basis = G-P-A.
```

The shared credit operator supplies

```text
T = exp(Q t)
F = integral_0^t exp(Q s) R exp(Q(t-s)) ds
P_out = P_in T
A_out = A_in T + P_in F.
```

Gross carrying and accumulated reward use the augmented exponential of

```text
[ Q+K  K ]
[  0   Q ].
```

Rust evaluates a bounded uniformized exponential. For negative `k`, it evaluates the corresponding nonnegative `|k|` reward block and restores the signed reward. It does not use Euler steps, closing-principal/full-period interest or proportional basis allocation. The independent reference uses a separate scaling-and-squaring matrix exponential; the [Al-Mohy–Higham paper](https://eprints.maths.manchester.ac.uk/1300/) and [official SciPy `expm` documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.linalg.expm.html) describe that reference numerical method, rather than this Rust uniformization implementation.

The owner carries one `G` and cumulative live `E` continuously through all source intervals. Ending default/prepay reward slices and completed live-origin rewards are retired exactly once into a conservation accumulator. Intervals cannot receive new caller cost, yield or carrying anchors. Native principal/accrued transport must match the captured source exactly at every interval, including origin-specific default slices and the post-boundary live state.

For an independent one-state hand check with default intensity `h`, no prepayment/migration and recognized rate `r`, define `phi(z,t)=expm1(z*t)/z`, with `phi(0,t)=t`. Before the boundary's contractual settlement,

```text
live_P = P0*exp(-h*t)
default_P = P0*(1-exp(-h*t))
live_A = P0*r*t*exp(-h*t)
default_A = P0*r*((1-exp(-h*t))/h - t*exp(-h*t))
live_G = G0*exp((k-h)*t)
default_G = G0*h*phi(k-h,t)
new_EIR = G0*k*phi(k-h,t).
```

At zero hazard, default `P/A/G` are zero by their continuous limits; at `k=h`, the carrying/reward integral uses `t` rather than a division by zero. These formulas illustrate exact occupation/exit transport, not a new event-date convention.

The canonical zero-credit example has principal 100, a 3.65% ACT/365F note rate and one actual 30-day remaining maturity settlement. Native contractual cash is 100.3. With original effective yield 2%, original cost is `100.3*exp(-log1p(.02)*30/365) = 100.13688317735347`; earned EIR is `100.3-cost = 0.16311682264652935`. Contractual accrual is 0.3, so basis runoff differs from earned EIR. Actual cash closes carrying without a new terminal plug or scenario yield fit.

## Native dates, settlement and boundary approximation

The receipt observes actual native operators/rates, source clocks, opening/transported monetary states, default claim ranges, cause-specific payoff fractions, scheduled collections, ARM resets, final state and entitlement-to-cash IDs. The existing order is

```text
interval transport → default capture → turnover/refinance payoff
→ scheduled collection → ARM reset → snapshot.
```

A payment on an ARM reset date uses the preceding interval's rate; the reset applies to later accrual. Turnover/refinance shares come from the actual native source, without reimplementing its seasoning, incentive or burnout formulas.

The native source assigns expected default/payoff events to the interval end and measures recovery lags from that ending date. Continuous-time occupation and original-EIR transport are exact for the frozen interval coefficients; borrower exit cash/default birth timing remains this explicit interval-end approximation. Refining supplied boundaries can change behavioral coefficients, cash timing and recovery dates. This is not a continuously timed realized-borrower simulation.

Scheduled actual principal plus interest reduces live `G`. At complete native live-origin settlement, remaining signed carrying is disposed under the reviewed exit policy, with signed accounting gain/loss and no added cash. A partial settlement that produces negative live gross carrying rejects. Prepaid carrying is split by the source's actual turnover/refinance fractions; each exit recognizes actual payoff cash less exact exit `G` once.

The result contains interval endpoints, not complete daily states or arbitrary report-date income snapshots. Absorbing default/prepay monetary slices exist inside a multi-day interval before the native source creates its boundary claims or payoff cash. A future daily owner must explicitly retain those pending exit rights and derive exact subinterval cumulative rewards from the same captured generator. It cannot interpolate endpoints, discard pending assets, move claim birth dates or post both daily rewards and full interval income.

## Explicit accounting and economic-right policies

| Request selection | Supported value |
|---|---|
| `policy.original_income` | `stop_at_exit-1` |
| `policy.remittance_float` | `reject_nonzero_remittance_lag-1` |
| `policy.live_cash` | `actual_native_cash_reduces_carry-1` |
| `policy.exit_basis` | `signed_native_exit_cash_minus_exact_carry-1` |
| `policy.default_basis` | `dispose_signed_basis_at_default-1` |
| `policy.default_principal_book` | `chargeoff_native_loss_at_default-1` |
| `policy.tail` | `reject_unclosed_gross_rights-1` |
| `policy.interest.accounting_accrued` | `reverse_income_at_default` |
| `policy.interest.economic_remainder` | `reviewed_economic_disposal` |

For each actual default-origin claim, the owner separately retains gross contractual principal/interest, recognized accrued interest, exact default `G`, signed basis, native loss, complete native principal cash, reviewed interest cash, accounting actions and dated economic dispositions.

The admitted book policy reverses recognized accrued `A`, disposes signed basis `G-P-A`, and charges off the native principal loss. These are distinct signed accounting-income actions. They do not retire the borrower's gross economic debt. Native principal recovery is owned exclusively by the native mortgage cashflow source; no second recovery, generic survival haircut or recovery-cost lane is added.

Default-interest cash is generated from the native contractual interest claim, a supplied origin-specific collection fraction and complete dated weights. Accounting interest reversal does not prevent separately reviewed later collection income. Remaining contractual interest requires its own economic-disposal review/date. Principal economic disposal likewise has its own review/date and must follow every native principal recovery. For gross claim rights `Pclaim` and `Icontract`,

```text
principal_disposal = Pclaim - sum(actual native principal cash rows)
interest_disposal  = Icontract - sum(actual reviewed interest cash rows).
```

Economic disposal is neither cash nor accounting income. Amounts use actual emitted sums, not normalized weights or an intended collection target. Negative disposal from overcollection rejects; a waiver policy cannot silently become a refund policy. The original economic-only quote receipts may close reviewed rights after actual cash while the current book still has unpaid principal. Such current book claims reject full-close execution; no extra writeoff, cash or terminal plug is inferred.

The native principal-tail unit-sum domain remains eight machine EPSILONs; reviewed interest weights use `1e-12`. They are not normalized. Final financial reference/reconciliation tolerances remain `1e-9` absolute plus `1e-12` relative. Exact economic residual and complete live-right closure checks remain exact where the implementation requires them. Scale-aware native principal conservation remains a separate source rule; it does not relax book claim closure.

## Result, full tails and identity

`ResultData` retains the complete typed `raw_request`, admission receipt, `source` and `original_source`, source intervals/boundaries/cash links, exact carry requests/operators/transport, ordered analytical `actions`, current and original reviewed interest cash, current book/economic closeouts, and separate original economic closeouts. Actions are scalar analytical receipts, not balanced posting instructions. Stable ordering uses actual ordinal and interval index.

It separately reports original quote PV, acquisition cost, cumulative earned EIR, total signed accounting income, actual current cash, original/full end ordinals, closing live gross carrying and conservation errors. Original and current raw/receipt hashes are separate SHA-256 values of compact, sorted-object, native-typed JSON. Retained normalized raw inputs, original/current immutable contract metadata and original-EIR/policy copies require exact type/value identity; dates and order remain exact. Financial tolerances apply to calculated results. A hash establishes receipt identity, not correctness by itself.

Full end is the maximum of both original/current source ends, all native recovery cash, reviewed interest collection dates and reviewed economic-disposal dates. Live contractual principal, borrower/investor principal/accrued and live `G` must fully close; every current claim must close its book and gross economic rights individually. Net-zero carrying is not permission to hide a gross claim. Each native entitlement must have one actual cash owner. No tail is truncated at a report horizon or replaced by terminal liquidation.

The result explicitly retains `sequential_carry_adoption=false`, `production_adoption=false`, `installed_independent_verification=false` and `mixed_ledger_adoption=false`; the private carrying receipt also retains `native_mortgage_generator_verified=false`. These markers do not negate the native source linkage, but they do prevent treating source-generated receipts as independent acceptance. A public independent analytical verification receipt is a separate publication gate. Mixed journal, capital, FTP and empirical eligibility remain false by scope; no accounting-standard approval or observed-source certification follows from successful arithmetic.

## Compiled generator hash and None behavior

`BASE_FINANCIAL_SOURCE_SHA256` labels the reviewed preinstrumentation body as provenance. The instrumented generator has different bytes. `generator_source_sha256()` hashes each file name and compiled file bytes with separate little-endian u64 length prefixes, in this order:

```text
mortgage_state.rs
mortgage_receipts.rs
consumer_contract.rs
credit_operator.rs
credit.rs
amortization.rs
cashflow.rs
floating_rate.rs
limits.rs
```

The declared scope is `length-prefixed-core-mortgage-generator-and-dependencies-1`. At this reviewed Core checkpoint, the encoded hash input is **141,669 bytes** and the digest is `cb467bb6260f6882d84a55a335c7bc91d377e228791b09a8a38d68c79d2e583a`. Rebuilding different source bytes changes these values. This nine-file digest does not claim to hash the full acquisition owner or executable: queued, executed and current bundle/source/artifact identity fences must independently bind public execution.

`mortgage_state::project` calls the same native loop with no receipt sink/check. The None path does not compute this digest or allocate receipt DTOs. Existing monetary formulas, reduction/event order, domains and guard errors remain unchanged. Versionable historical fixtures compare complete None and sink serialized native output bytes, including fixed/ARM, Physical/pricing and agency source cases. The analytical owner still rejects agency ownership and pricing measures; receipt compatibility does not extend its admitted accounting policy.

## Admission, capacity and cancellation

Admission finishes before either heavy original/current capture begins. Both native raw sources are validated without generating schedules, then their complete calendars, paired terms, policy identities, actual escaped metadata and output cardinality are admitted together. Limits are:

| Boundary | Limit |
|---|---:|
| Complete typed raw request | 1 MiB encoded bytes |
| Current intervals / original intervals | 16 each; aggregate work can be tighter |
| Aggregate owner work | 9,000,000 work units |
| Conservative retained/output capacity | 64 MiB |
| Contractual source horizon | 1,080 days each |
| Reviewed interest collection tail | 32 points per origin |
| Reviewed economic disposal lag | 1,080 days, after the respective complete cash tail |
| Explicit review/source/path identity text | 256 bytes, nonempty and control-free |

Each native mortgage projection retains its separate two-million-work/component domains. Those source bounds do not substitute for this combined admission. These are small admitted analytical slices, not 360-payment mortgage or 60,000-position workflow acceptance, and not an aggregate process RSS guarantee.

Let `I/Io` be actual current/original calendar interval counts, `RP/RPo` their summed native recovery-tail cardinalities, `IR` the summed reviewed interest-tail cardinality, `M` the sum of encoded JSON string-leaf lengths in the complete typed request, `Eraw` the complete encoded request length, and `Hcode=source_code_bytes()`. The checked conservative bounds are

```text
Rrows = I*(8*RP + 4*IR + 128) + Io*(8*RPo + 4*IR + 128)
Bbytes = Rrows*(M+4096) + (I+Io)*(M+65536) + 4*Eraw
Wwork = 4,000,000 + I*(140*14^3 + 4096) + Io*4096 + Hcode.
```

The fixed four-million source allowance charges both native projections; `Hcode` charges the compiled generator digest once even when cached. Numeric matrix/output overhead and source/cash/action/closeout replication are charged before generation. Arithmetic overflow, over-budget metadata/cardinality, invalid dates/amounts or unsupported policy return errors. The completed serialized result is checked again against its admitted byte bound. For the canonical public example, work is 4,534,021 and retained/output bound is 2,323,814 bytes.

Cancellation checks run during request counting, between admission/source stages, each actual source interval, native recovery/cash-conversion loops, sequential intervals/default claims/recoveries, and final output fences. Matrix exponentials, validation, hashing, some bounded short scans and final JSON serialization have boundary checks rather than an inner check for every arithmetic or byte operation. Each such phase remains bounded by the admitted contract; the public process watchdog handles a blocking transport/write. Writer/newline/flush errors or the final cancellation check return failure. Partial bytes may have reached a failed writer, but they cannot count as a complete result or authorize immutable publication.

## Validation and remaining adoption gates

The acquired-source Core stage passed 281 all-target native tests; the additional shared instruction guards bring the current Core total to 286, with strict Clippy. Its 23 acquired-source hand/domain fixtures cover original=current identity, changed default/prepayment/refinance/ARM with fixed anchors, signed yields and basis, migration/cure/default-origin conservation, sequential semigroup, actual cash/tails, large-scale near-unit weights, cancellation and failed writes. Four receipt tests cover historical eight-source None/sink byte equality, all 32 corrected accepted/error snapshots and compiled generator hashing/admission. Eight additional native cases cover strict new-owner fields, enum forms and duplicate keys. Official-default artifacts pass 185 independent/public-process mortgage checks and 34 durable mortgage checks, including exact retained-input tamper rejection. The complete bundle passes 788 component native, 2,066 engine (two reference-only skips), 531 API and 41 browser tests. The separate frozen artifact's 57 native and 206 independent-reference checks remain component evidence; they are not public persisted-journal acceptance.

Public analytical execution must be independently reconstructed from raw original/current sources, then reverified after immutable persistence with current bundle/executable and request fences. Existing mortgage valuation guards remain until their separate supported cash/claim valuation gates are implemented. Daily same-Sim adoption additionally needs acquisition cash once, complete balanced atomic P/A/basis/default transfers, explicit pending-source-exit ownership, exact interim/report-date native checkpoints, and independent ordered/persisted journal replay.

Unsupported policies include agency guarantees/advances, remittance float, acquired accrued rights, PCD, allowance, state-specific nonaccrual EIR, incomplete retained claims, new collection-cost ownership, pricing-measure conversion, empirical calibration and capital/FTP adoption. Freddie Mac's [mortgage security documentation](https://capitalmarkets.freddiemac.com/mbs/products), already cited in the local foundation, concerns security guarantees; those are distinct from whole-loan borrower collections. No agency terms or accounting approval are imported into this whole-loan contract.

# Explicit mortgage mixed expected accounting

Explicit schema: `mortgage-mixed-accounting-1`. It describes expected accounting of explicit supplied Physical whole-loan paths and a reviewed dated backbook in one native journal. It does not claim fitted behavior, accounting approval, full product adoption, or capital/FTP eligibility. Existing saved/monthly, library, candidate, cohort and Consumer/Card contracts remain unchanged.

The local implementation adds the unchanged frozen Core pending module/export, Ledger exclusive owner/hooks and a typed model-ledger branch. It preserves the original proof49/native143 independent evidence and all hashes. The prior proof admitted oversized opposing dated backbooks; its 10k limitation covered mortgage/opening inputs. The new schema adds explicit `money_domain: combined_gross_state_10k-1` and rejects this public-admission blocker without altering source math or tolerances.

Every dated position principal/basis/opening accrued/allowance/commitment, event component and recognition component is finite with absolute value at most10k. A separate conservative aggregate supplied-gross bound also applies. Runtime checks enforce actual gross GL, account/book state and unweighted native book/borrower/economic-claim lanes. No netting oversized assets against liabilities, clipping or closing plug is permitted. All scans are charged; failed runtime checks return no complete result/manifest. Scalar preflight does not certify every future numerical combination.

An explicit immutable source registry preserves complete raw values, original purchase/yield/contracts, reviewed dispositions, generator digest and141669 code bytes. Each run/path reference is supplied; identical selected source compiles once, each run receives separate Book/journal. No short-hash deduplication or implicit scenario reuse. Distinct sources, including zero participation, are precharged under8M/32MiB/64days before generation. The old2M product allowance remains unchanged.

Native Groups remain sole acquisition and monetary postings. Group Lines retain exact order/actions/reviews. Borrower/economic memo authority is the exact native post-group daily checkpoint; it cannot overwrite P/A/B, cash, original EIR or reviewed P&L. Claims remain origin-specific. Complete unweighted tails and all ordinary runs are mandatory, including future and zero allocations. Unsupported cost/nonaccrual/allowance/PCD policies remain rejected.

`prepare(Request)->Prepared` retains compiled immutable source and dated book. A typed borrowed preparation header avoids receipt cloning, then `run(Prepared, Write)` streams the existing Sim journal/report output under a32MiB writer and shared cancellation/deadline. The bounded dispatcher first performs a Value peek to select the schema. Only the selected new branch then re-deserializes its typed envelope from the original input bytes, preserving duplicate-field rejection; historical Value-based branches stay unchanged. No Risk/lifecycle term branch is necessary; contractual's separate market-indexed proposal does not overlap this model-ledger seam.

Transport-only engine changes add strict schemas and JSON serialization for mortgage lineage/daily/closing nested fields, without finance or float alteration. New independent functions `verify_preparation(raw, prepared_dated, receipt, check)` and `verify_stream(raw, checked_control, frames, check)` must reconstruct raw source and ordered GL, memo dispositions, interim state, full claims/tail and every table. Private checked control is never caller authority. Partitions are replayed incrementally; no all-table hydration or native financial callback.

Queued raw JSON and the native declared DTO have separate exact identities. Browser JSON can spell a whole monetary Number as an integer; Rust serializes declared f64 fields as binary64 while retaining its raw `dated.specification` Value unchanged. `verify_retained_request_identity` uses the existing independent complete admission to reconstruct this declared typed copy, then checks every field/type/value and signed zero exactly. The importer retains and separately checks the original queued input bytes and specification. It does not apply approximate numeric equality, infer unknown fields, change dates/metadata, or rewrite original input to match producer output. Fresh default-native and durable browser-number regressions exercise this boundary alongside exact tamper rejection.

Only successful independent persisted replay can mark `native_mortgage_source_recomputed`, `single_daily_gl_verified`, `pending_memo_phase_verified`, `complete_unweighted_tail_verified` true. Production-model/full-product/accounting/capital/FTP flags remain false. API uses the existing durable modeled job, immutable raw/source objects, exact schema/category allowlist and original trusted scalar deadline. Verification after Codec.dump re-reads queued input and every partition, checks lease/cancel/deadline and fresh source/artifact hashes through final publication. Existing bounded Windows retry/post-rename fence and unpublished cleanup remain mandatory.

UI adds an explicit research expected-accounting choice/example in the partitioned panel with supplied-path, registry reuse,64day/10k/8M/32MiB and false capital/FTP disclosures. No automatic saved-book adoption or backend selector.

Focused gates cover canonical one-source/two-run GL, pending default/prepay, EIR versus realization, memo boundaries, signed liability basis, future/zero allocation, unweighted tail rejection, distinct-source budget rejection, oversized components/gross offsets/runtime growth, strict aliases/duplicates, cancellation/atomic failure and complete old Consumer/Card1/Card2 NDJSON bytes. Independent source/GL and persisted tamper/fence tests remain separate from historical byte compatibility. Source changes are applied locally. Architecture/schema/native/engine/API/browser gates are required before recording installed acceptance; matching official artifacts must be rebuilt. Local validation does not deploy or restart production workers.

# New vertical admission contract (under validation)

The policy `combined_gross_state_10k-1` has scalar and separate aggregate domains. Each scanned amount is finite with `abs(amount)<=10000`; each defined gross lane sums absolute amounts and rejects `>10000` without tolerance/clamp. These are additional narrow public-schema restrictions, not changes to the frozen source or old entrypoints.

Supplied aggregate: account cash/equity/cash_floor/capital_deductions; position balance/book_adjustment/opening_accrued/allowance/commitment/pledged_face; every retained dated event's principal/cash_interest/accrued_interest/book_amortization/fees; every raw recognition segment's accrued_interest/book_amortization; every distinct registry source's three opening investor principals plus actual acquisition cost. Supplied values are scanned once; duplicate run references do not charge source raw twice. This deliberately conservative gross bound counts cash and recognition separately; it is not a future-state certificate.

Unweighted native runtime lanes (each independently <=10k): (1) all7 slots and all claim book P/A/B plus cumulative cash/original-EIR/reviewed-income; (2) all7 borrower principal plus contractual-interest memos; (3) every claim economic principal plus contractual-interest memo. Scan every native Group.committed, daily Book, and closing Book before successful preparation, including zero-weight sources. Scan staged runtime Book after each complete atomic group and each post-group daily memo. Group memo channels are not authoritative post-boundary economic changes; exact native daily memos remain a separate non-posting checkpoint.

Combined runtime lanes: staged full GL absolute balances before each complete transaction; actual account cash/equity/cash_floor/capital_deductions at each end-day; actual backbook P/B/allowance/accrued/commitment plus weighted mortgage slots/claim P/A/B at each end-day. The latter excludes duplicated aggregate active placeholder P/B/A. No opposing asset/liability netting can evade the gross domain. Guards run before the transaction's money mutation; a later day-domain failure aborts the stream and cannot publish a manifest. Existing journal/reconciliation gates are still mandatory; no numerical guarantee for every admitted scalar tuple is asserted.

All arithmetic for work/bytes is checked. Let D be full ledger days, R ordinary runs, N positions, A accounts, O dated owners, E stored events, Z raw recognition segments, B explicit mortgage bindings; each unique source i has Gi=max_groups, Di=days, Wi=unchanged native source+checkpoint work, Mi=unchanged native reserved bytes.

Each NEW copied pending admission exposes its already-native-admitted current interval_count ni; Ci=3*ni is the maximum origin-claim count. Native source math/work is unchanged. Assert every generated Book actually respects Ci before publication.
K=16*A+12*O+max_over_runs(sum_bindings_in_run(24+3*Ci)). A run has its own GL; do not sum key cardinalities across different GL instances.
T=A*R + sum_over_bindings(Gi) + 2*(D+1)*E*R.
replay=sum_over_bindings((D+1)*(1024+128*Ci)+Gi*(2048+128*Ci)).
input_components=6*N+5*E+2*Z+4*A+4*unique_sources.
money_guard=sum_unique((Gi+Di+2)*(1024+64*Ci)) + T*(9*K+128+max(48,16*N+16*A)) + (D+1)*R*(64*N+48*A+256) +16*input_components+128.
work=sum_unique(Wi)+replay+dated.work_units+money_guard <=8M.

The exact guard uses18 u64 limbs in units2^-1074 and compares the exact absolute sum to10000. It rounds only the reported supplied-gross metadata to nearest-even binary64. In particular 10000+the minimum positive subnormal REJECTS even if a rounded float sum is10000. No tolerance/clamp is involved. Any order of the same binary64 inputs gives the same admission decision. Permutation, subnormal, exact threshold and cooperative cancellation tests bind this rule; the independent oracle uses Fraction.from_float.

Two direct limb additions per value can each initiate one carry chain. Across the initially-zero accumulator, a propagation clears a full limb; direct updates can create at most2 full limbs per value and each stopped chain can create at most1 more. Thus at most4 full-limb clears plus2 stopped-chain updates plus2 direct additions per value: <=8 limb updates amortized, with overflow checked. The final18-limb compare, <=53 bit extraction, <=18-limb sticky scan and rounding are charged128 units per gross call. Source Book has <=38+5*Ci monetary components across three distinct gross calls. 1024+64*Ci covers these exact sums. Replay charges indexed claim maps, ordered source comparisons/copy, unweighted exact book lanes and weighted combined book scan. Per-transaction9*K includes one current-GL clone/key visit plus eight amortized exact-accumulator updates;128+max(48,16*N+16*A) covers final reduction and ordered entries, including the potentially larger opening transaction. Additional256/day charges two combined guard calls. Input16 charges scalar validation plus exact-add iterations. No source projection or journal amount is altered.

reserved = frozen formula with canonical raw bytes/new admission policy, but perbinding daily claim serialization bound uses Ci (the native source's exact interval cardinality, not48 globally); add128*K+3072*B+288 for staged GL/index maps and the two fixed18-limb working accumulators. Source retained/result arenas and DatedStore remain charged; escaped output checks include changed metadata. Bound32MiB is both reservation and complete emitted header+NDJSON cap. No all-table hydration occurs in the public stream; registry source is immutable and borrowed.

These counts are conservative admission units, not CPU/RSS guarantees. New public/runtime restrictions, full tails and all exact monetary gates are required together. All adoption/accounting/capital/FTP flags remain false; independent source/journal/persisted verification can establish only the separate publication markers.

# Native supplied mortgage product graph

`mortgage-product-graph-1` explicitly selects the bounded native
[`mortgage-state-1`](mortgage-state.md) model for pricing and physical source
analysis. It retains original payments, borrower/investor state, competing exits,
ARM fixings, investor entitlements, actual remittances, default/recovery claims
and supplied guarantee advances. Historical monthly mortgage economics are not
silently replaced. This stage does not add cohort publication, fitted histories,
an effective-yield income policy or mortgage journal adoption.

## Input and ownership

The request reuses `GraphIdentity`, `Scenario`, `OasTarget`, `Role` and
`BaseAnchor` from the advanced consumer graph. It requires `as_of_ordinal`,
currency, strictly increasing `reporting_ordinals` beginning at valuation,
`base_scenario_id`, `bump_bp`,
`terminal_policy="complete_generated_investor_cash_tail"`, supplied collateral
curves and positions. The [synthetic example](../../examples/models/mortgage-product-graph-1.json)
is a controlled short whole loan with supplied zero credit/turnover hazards.

Each position contains its original known `MortgageRequest`, target/locked OAS
and complete scenario-ordered history sets. The known template requires
contractual measure, empty `path` and empty ARM resets; it is not projected
directly. Every history explicitly supplies `path_id`, weight, assumption ID,
`MortgagePathPoint` records and `arm_resets`. Native generation declares physical
measure for P and pricing measure for central/down/up Q, then invokes the shared
mortgage state model. Fixed-rate histories must have no ARM resets. Index values,
publication timestamps and observed/projected source declarations remain inputs;
the graph does not derive future ARM fixings from the collateral discount curve.

Path weights must sum to one without normalization fallback. Every Q scenario
and bump side has identical ordered path IDs and exact weights. P is explicitly
separate. The required randomness domain is `supplied_paired_histories-1`; these
are supplied deterministic state recipes and expected population transitions,
not native sampled borrower paths. Matching IDs do not establish stochastic CRN
generation. Native shared-draw/model-policy integration remains an open gate.

Refinance, seasoning and burnout coefficients, state collection/recognition
fractions, LGD, complete recovery weights, guarantee policy and ARM contractual
terms remain supplied known-contract assumptions. P/Q paths supply their own
refinancing rates, turnover and credit intensities and selected ARM reset values.
This boundary does not infer HPI/geographic recoveries, pricing risk premia or
empirical coefficients. Changing contract recovery/agency assumptions requires
an explicit new base anchor rather than silently stressing a scenario parameter.
Unsupported securitization tranches, waterfalls, servicing-profit valuation,
guarantor default and implicit agency legal eligibility have no schema fallback.

## Full tails and unsupported interest rights

The projection horizon must include the complete remaining contractual payment
calendar. For agency ownership it must additionally extend through the final
contractual payment plus supplied default-buyout lag: the core generates complete
buyout cash but clips earned recognition at its projection end. This conservative
admission prevents omission of post-default investor coupon recognition.

Every generated path must finish with zero contractual reference principal,
live investor principal and live investor accrued interest. Full investor cash
principal plus explicit whole-loan principal loss must conserve opening investor
principal. No survivor scaling, terminal market value, fabricated recovery,
tail truncation or balancing cash is introduced. The state model's supplied
final contractual maturity payment remains explicit; it is distinct from a
reporting-horizon balloon.

Whole-loan default contractual/recognized accrued interest has no collection or
disposal policy in the shared state model. Such claims, or remaining borrower
interest rights, reject the entire graph rather than being assigned zero value
or silently omitted. The admitted whole-loan credit fixture therefore has zero
coupon and explicit principal recoveries/losses. Agency borrower arrears and
default interest remain issuer-side source evidence; supported guaranteed
investor coupon/buyout rights are separately generated and conserved. These
borrower rights are not added to investor valuation or discarded from results.

All actual remittance dates and complete borrower recovery cash remain in
sources even after reporting and projection. Valuation and physical-tail reports
include those dates. The supplied collateral curve's declared reject/flat-zero/
flat-forward tail applies; no undisclosed discount extension occurs. Supplied
calendar arithmetic is retained with `calendar_mapping_verified=false` from
the core; this is not a certified agency/index holiday mapping.

## Pricing, original anchors and risk

For each supplied Q path, investor cash after valuation is discounted as

```
PV = sum[(principal + interest + fees) × collateral_DF(t) × exp(-base_OAS × t)]
t = (actual remittance ordinal - valuation ordinal) / 365
```

The OAS target and source identity are explicit. Positive-future-cash targets
use bounded 100-step bisection in the original `[-5,5]` decimal OAS bracket with
log-sum-exp endpoint pricing. Signed future cash would require explicitly locked
OAS; it cannot enter that monotone positive-cash calibration. The shared state
model's present admitted investor cash is nonnegative. Zero-asset rights can
use locked OAS; a positive quote without positive future Q cash rejects.

`MortgageGraph::{new,request,snapshot,base_anchor,reprice,repriced}` holds immutable
`Arc` snapshots; `analyze` is the raw convenience route. Complete canonical base
content includes original known contract/state/policy, base Q path/fixing/reset
recipes, curve source/content, model/paired-history identity and OAS target.
Content equality is collision-safe and is not replaced by label equality or
hash equality. Repricing validates that anchor and holds the original OAS.
Changed base economic content requires an explicit new calibration. Current
non-base P/Q history edits and input revision changes can produce a new immutable
snapshot while preserving the original anchor.

`audit_admitted_work(&Request) -> Result<usize, String>` returns the exact
conservative structural work charge from the same graph admission, without
generating any path or solving OAS. After admitting aggregate bounds, it builds
each explicit measure/history request and calls shared
`mortgage_state::validate_request` for the existing core contract/fixing domains.
That helper forwards the projection's existing validator; it changes no model
economics. Output-dependent terminal/interest-rights rejection still requires
projection, and the audit does not prove that a requested quote is attainable.

`supplied_history_dv01` is the central difference of explicitly supplied Q down/up
histories with native negative/positive parallel curve bumps, divided by twice
the bump in basis points. It includes supplied ARM/index/behavior changes only
when those raw histories provide them. It is not evidence of a fitted joint
rate/HPI/credit law or a full native stochastic effective-DV01 model. Investor
remittance delays are discounted on the same supplied curve and fixed OAS as
other cash; no OAS-only delay shift is used in this versioned path.

## Physical reports and retained sources

`NativeSource` retains position/scenario/run/path/assumption identity, weight,
role and the entire `MortgageResult`. The graph request itself remains accessible;
publication must persist that complete raw request alongside its result. Each
result preserves original-loan/cohort identity, original payment, actual cash,
entitlements, ARM selected index/fixing revisions, state points, credit/default
claims, complete recoveries, agency buyouts and total advances.

Physical periods use actual `(left,right]` boundaries and report borrower versus
investor principal/interest cash, investor entitlements, principal defaults/loss,
separate recovery/buyout cash and `gross_recognized_investor_interest`. Explicit
positive-length recognition intervals are allocated uniformly when a reporting
cutoff splits them; instant cash-basis recognition remains on its original date.
This uniform report allocation does not reproduce intrainterval CTMC occupation
timing and is disclosed separately from the core's integrated reward amount.
Behavioral exits/default recovery clocks retain the core's interval-end expected
cash approximation. Supplied path refinement can change event timing.

`physical_tail` reports all generated dates after the final reporting boundary.
`physical_totals` separately retains scheduled/turnover/refinance principal and
aggregate guarantee principal/interest advances. The core returns aggregate
advances without individual origin dates; the graph does not invent period
allocations. Gross recognized investor interest is not frozen-yield NII,
servicing profitability, provisions or regulatory accounting income. No ledger
capture is exposed by this component.

## Bounds and evidence

Admission allows 256 positions, 13 scenarios, 128 paths per measure role, 120
reporting periods, 4,096 aggregate native projections, 250,000 conservatively
admitted/generated rows and eight million structural work units. It charges
combined payment/path/reset boundaries, worst-case default claims, complete
recovery/default-coupon tails, bounded shared operator evaluations, source
selection scans, OAS iterations and every physical reporting pass before
projection. The shared state/operator bounds remain additional. Canonical raw
input is limited to 32 MiB; retained request/result/base content uses a conservative
four-times serialized charge within 128 MiB. These component bounds do not claim
aggregate RSS or full graph/solver/daily scale acceptance. Checkpoints run across
native paths, scenario metrics and OAS iterations.

Independent fixtures calculate three ten-day scheduled payments: interest 0.1,
0.0661 and 0.0321661; remittance occurs two days after each entitlement. They
check actual-date PV/DV01 and full tail, distinct P refinance versus unchanged
Q, fixed original OAS through +/-200 bp, explicit Q bump histories, zero-coupon
whole-loan default/recovery conservation, agency advances/default buyouts without
duplicate borrower recoveries, ARM caps/original payment and annuity recast,
weighted zero-change identity and invalid domain/measure/tail/work admission.
The graph suite passed all 16 fixtures and targeted Clippy with warnings denied;
all 12 existing mortgage-state fixtures also passed after the validation-helper
addition. Tests include equal core/preflight invalid-contract/fixing errors and
issuer default-loss tails even when investor cash is entirely zero.
Source-component fixtures do not establish public/API publication or empirical
fit. Issue #13 retains dated empirical calibration/holdout/source hashes,
HPI/geographic recoveries, stochastic shared drivers, stressed loan/cohort audits,
effective-yield income, source-aware daily default/advance journals and complete
native runtime acceptance.

The CFPB's [index and margin explanation](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/for-an-adjustable-rate-mortgage-arm-what-are-the-index-and-margin-and-how-do-they-work-en-1949/)
supports retaining contractual index/margin inputs separately from market
discounting. Fannie Mae's [remittance description](https://singlefamily.fanniemae.com/servicing/principal-and-interest-remittance)
distinguishes payment activity reported by servicers from funds passed to
investors. These references motivate separate roles; they do not establish this
generic supplied guarantee model's legal or empirical accuracy.
