# Saved derivative adoption: implementation requirements

This is the remaining implementation plan for issue #20, not an implemented
schema or an acceptance receipt. The current native saved runner explicitly
rejects nonempty hedge books in `portfolio-decision-native/src/workflows/owned/ledger.rs`.
The rejection remains correct until the complete source and journal mapping exists.

## Current source boundaries

The historical `hedge_lifecycle::Swap` records notional, payer/receiver side,
fixed rate, maturity and floating spread. Its generated six-month fixed and
three-month floating legs use historical calendar/day-count conventions.
It contains no trade identifier, legal entity, counterparty, CSA, settlement
evidence or independent observed index-fixing source. A netting-set label cannot
recover these missing terms.

The separate `derivative_contract` owners already value complete dated raw swaps,
European cash/physical settlement and explicitly reviewed CSA/MPOR paths.
`derivative_accounting` already prepares balanced Physical journal intents from
complete daily raw marks, actual contractual fixing/election policies and opening
carrying/collateral anchors. These owners must supply the upgraded saved route;
the adapter must not recreate coupon, option, margin or loss calculations.

## Required native integration

1. Add an explicitly selected, immutable saved-trade source contract. Bind each
   saved-book row by its frozen book revision, complete raw content and row slot;
   identical economic rows still require distinct complete trade identities.
   Require exact one-to-one coverage and reject duplicate, missing or surplus
   mappings before pricing. A selected contractual upgrade retains its own
   reviewed revision; it does not silently reinterpret historical saved economics.
2. Require complete entity/currency/counterparty/netting/legal/CSA identities,
   contractual leg/reset/settlement terms, original opening anchors, and separate
   Physical/Pricing sources. Preserve observed-fixing information cutoffs and
   explicit future projection identity. Pricing projections cannot become
   physical settlement evidence. Legal netting and financial statement offsetting
   remain separately reviewed policies.
3. Integrate the existing raw derivative owners into the native pricing graph.
   Cache keys include the complete contract, curves, supplied histories, legal
   policy, measure, CRN and original valuation identity. Paired risk bumps share
   draws; any original spread/OAS anchor remains immutable. Holdout observations
   must not change training calibration. European settlement/exercise retains
   complete cash or delivered-leg tails exactly once.
4. Adopt derivative accounting intents as one exclusive owner in the actual
   shared daily Sim. Generic credit, coupon and maturity overlays must bypass
   that owner. Post opening cash/equity once for the combined book. Retain gross
   received/posted VM, segregated IM, unpaid contractual obligations and delivered
   ownership through default and complete closeout; margin principal transfers
   are not trading losses. Preserve each original ordered source transaction and
   reconcile the mixed GL to independently rebuilt raw derivative sources.
5. Prepare native strategy coefficients and Treasury exposure/flows from these
   verified owners. Constraint-only interactive evaluation stays coefficient-only.
   Capital and FTP use explicitly reviewed source/policy inputs; regulatory/XVA
   outputs cannot be inferred from a legal label, an economic loss memo or a
   physical journal. Journal and source permissions remain separate.
6. Queue the complete immutable input/code/native identity with one original
   deadline. Retain bounded source/output partitions, actual producer completion,
   independent raw and persisted reconstruction, and transaction-bound
   revision/attempt/token/lease/cancellation/source/body-hash checks. Reopening a
   completed source is provenance; a new job owns a new finite accepted deadline.

## Evidence required before closing the issue

All original issue #20 criteria remain required: independent par and signed-rate
swap schedules, payer/receiver parity, annuity/tenor and European exercise
convergence, cash versus physical settlement, legal netting versus gross buckets,
collateral lag/outage/segregation and default closeout conservation. Add missing
and duplicate saved mappings, zero/signed positions, same-day mixed acquisitions,
unpaid maturity tails, physical delivery and no second margin-loss posting.

Compare original default-free legacy output bytes independently. Run new native
graph/risk/strategy and actual combined journal checks, rebuilt default process
tests with Python financial callbacks forbidden, durable worker/restart/persisted
tamper/publication tests, and the actual saved-book UI flow. The combined
60,000-position graph/credit/solver/journal acceptance remains a separate required
scope; small source tests and component budgets cannot establish it.

## Primary research and remaining model limits

[BCBS counterparty-risk guidance, paragraphs 40.43 and 40.66](https://www.bis.org/committees/bcbs/basel-consolidated-guidelines/module/cri/40)
addresses reviewed enforceability, collateral-access delays, contractual netting,
material risk-factor correlations and MPOR collateral dynamics. Paragraph 40.70
addresses exposure backtesting against historical markets. These support the
explicit source and validation requirements above; they do not certify this
repository, supply jurisdiction-specific legal opinions or prescribe its
accounting policies. The existing supplied-path owners still need joint scenario
generation and observed exposure validation before predictive claims.

The ISDA 2021 Definitions InfoHub identifies confirmation templates and versioned
contractual conventions. Its search metadata was checked on 2026-10-03; direct
InfoHub and public PDF retrieval returned an error/403 in that check, so no new
formula or settlement convention is inferred from unread definitions. The full
admitted European/Bermudan boundary and unsupported own-default/DVA, dynamic IM,
cross-currency and formal hedge-accounting policies must remain explicit until
implemented and independently validated.

# Saved derivative mixed-source publication proposal

This additive route transports `saved-derivative-mixed-1` to the Rust
`portfolio-model-ledger` dispatcher. Rust rebuilds the explicit saved derivative
source, owns its dated postings in the daily ledger, and streams the single
journal and reports. Python supplies independent verification and durable
storage, never a financial execution alternative.

## Public boundary

`GET /derivatives/mixed/example` supplies the explicit research example.
`POST /derivatives/mixed/runs` accepts `expected_revision`, `specification` and
`timeout`; the worker operation is `saved_derivative.run`. This is a dedicated
raw-source route. It does not change saved-book pricing, Strategy evaluation,
hedge/netting inference, capital permissions or FTP eligibility.

The selected native branch reparses original bytes with duplicate-preserving
strict JSON and checks documented enum strings before source generation. A
tagged object remains an object where the contract requires one. Unit-object
aliases, booleans, nulls and unknown enum strings are rejected. Historical shared
Serde parsers are unchanged.

The immutable original raw JSON value and independently declared normalized
native DTO identities are checked separately. Financial comparisons retain their
existing tolerances; identifiers, reviews, lineage, flags, integer dates, types
and signed zero use exact identity. Neither native result flags nor a saved
trial balance supplies source authority.

## Source and journal verification

The seven `saved_derivative_*` engine modules divide independent financial
equations, mapping, dated accounting, identity, pooled stream replay, transport
and process execution. The private checked control is rebuilt from raw source
and the retained native preparation. It is sealed against post-return mutation.
`verify_stream` replays bounded partition iterators in original transaction order
and independently checks monetary postings, gross source rights, source phase
lineage and reports. Complete source objects and actual protocol-3 completion are
retained; completion is never synthesized from an empty iterator.

Gross rights verification reconciles every retained right. It does not assert
that arbitrary dated backbook future rights were extinguished or grant a closing
capital bridge permission. The durable receipt keeps empirical validation,
accounting-standard approval, capital/FTP eligibility and saved-pricing-graph
adoption false.

## Durable ownership

The server captures the accepted job's finite original deadline before worker
dispatch. Retry does not reset it. Immediate cancellation/deadline checks surround
numerical callbacks; SQL ownership polling is bounded without weakening forced
checks around reads, replay, hashes, uploads and publication.

Queued identity includes the executed binary, current engine identity, all seven
independent helper modules and applicable API/worker/storage code. Mutable
returned job, queue and result views cannot rebase the private authority. Raw,
source, actual completion and Parquet descriptors are immutable and checksummed.
Persisted output and every retained partition body are reread after replay and
within the final publication fence.

The final SQL transaction checks the same queued request/revision, token,
attempt, workspace lease and status before and after I/O. Pure clock/STOP probes
inside that transaction avoid nested repository connections. The worker supplies
`STOP.is_set` explicitly, so the jobs module has no worker import or new cycle.

## Bounds and validation scope

Native financial work remains limited to 8 million units, source owner capacity
to 128 MiB and complete serialized native stream to 32 MiB. Raw input is bounded
to 32 MiB. Strict parsing/enum traversal is separate from the financial-work
counter. These are component limits, not aggregate process RSS guarantees.
Transport separately limits compressed retained partitions to 128 MiB and 65,536
partitions; partition rows are configurable from 1 to 65,536.

Contained evidence uses an actual isolated full Rust dispatcher, the actual
copied worker, SQLite, Codec objects and Parquet reopen. The current-baseline
package passed 221 source, refusal, journal and publication checks. The selected
raw-domain successor passed 13 native tests and strict all-target Clippy and
retains byte-exact canonical source/Sim output. Generated HTTP contracts come
from the actual composed API; the dependency review adds no cycles.

Official-default engine/API and browser acceptance are authored but pending
application, native composition/rebuild and worker restart. SQLite evidence does
not certify PostgreSQL/S3 operation. This stage does not complete issue 20,
empirical calibration, observed validation, or combined 60,000-position scale.
Combining source2 deposits and derivatives in one ledger is a distinct reviewed
raw contract and independent pooled replay gate; standalone results must never
be concatenated to infer that acceptance.

# Saved derivatives in the shared dated journal

The explicit `saved-derivative-mixed-1` successor generates reviewed physical
derivative sources in Rust and executes their financial intents in the existing
dated daily `Sim`. It is currently isolated under `artifacts/derivative-mixed/`.
It is not installed public/default adoption or completion of issues #12/#20/#25.

## Inputs and ownership

The request contains `schema`, a complete `dated-ledger-1` backbook request, and
`owners`. Each owner names an actual ledger account and supplies one `runs` entry
for every configured ledger scenario, including baseline. Each entry names the
ledger scenario and supplies a raw `saved-derivative-source-1` request. Callers
cannot supply precomputed derivative intents, cash overrides or financial reports.

The saved-source contract validates original trade order, unique position and
legal ownership, calendar/source identities, complete opening anchors and explicit
reviewed legacy-row upgrades. All runs retain exactly the same saved book and
reviewed opening. Physical histories can differ between scenarios. Cash, entity,
currency, units and opening date must match the ledger account. A legal netting
bucket cannot be split between derivative owners of the same ledger account.
Legacy netting overlays and reverse-severity runs require their own complete joint
ownership contract and are rejected in this successor.

Risk owns all swap, European option, supplied-fixing, exposure, CSA, MPOR, default
closeout and physical derivative accounting calculations. The coordinator calls
that existing owner and transports its typed result. Ledger owns chronological
execution, GL reduction, daily account state and journal-derived closing reports.
Ledger does not import Risk or implement a second derivative valuation model.

## Opening and chronological replay

For each account, supplied actual opening cash and equity are posted once in the
shared opening transaction. Generated gross derivative assets, liabilities,
posted VM/IM and received VM extend that transaction. Independent native opening
stock admission incorporates those explicit gross anchors into the existing
balance-sheet equation; it does not alter the supplied cash/equity or insert a
balancing amount. Generated source stocks must reconcile to those admitted facts
in every scenario before replay.

The derivative source retains a shadow of its original cash/equity only to verify
its own source accounting. That shadow is never posted as another account opening.
Multiple derivative books may therefore share actual account cash without
duplicating it. Financial source intents post through the same `Sim::raw_post`
used by dated owners, preserving source line order and actual transaction dates.
Source P&L changes shared equity once. Each financial line retains its book,
source event, intent index, posting index, date and collision-safe instrument ID.

Received IM custody remains a balanced memo journal. Its opening and movements
retain source lineage but never enter cash, financial GL, assets, liabilities or
equity. Unpaid receivables/payables, derivative assets/liabilities and collateral
stocks retain separate gross ownership, including after physical option delivery.

Daily source reconciliation compares replayed categories with the complete native
source daily trial balances. Duplicate closing categories reject. At the source's
full tail, every individual gross derivative/rights/collateral and custody owner
must be closed and every intent consumed. If the shared dated backbook continues
longer, the closed derivative state is held; no additional mark, cash, settlement
or synthetic terminal payoff is generated.

## Admission and control

Original JSON is limited to 32 MiB and parsed with the shared duplicate-key
rejecting Core parser before Value conversion. Typed raw source mappings and
complete scenario coverage precede financial projection. The coordinator reserves
each selected source's existing 250,000 native financial work ceiling against
the eight-million raw joined source/backbook admission.

After generation, the owner separately admits actual source lines and complete
mixed-tail daily scans within eight million work units. It charges vector
capacities, retained source string capacities and conservative per-line shadow/GL
key allowances against 128 MiB. Retained native source wire data have a separate
64 MiB ceiling. Native NDJSON and final output each have a 32 MiB encoded limit.
These are distinct component/transport budgets, not an aggregate process RSS cap.
At most 64 selected source-run pairs and 512 dated backbook positions are admitted.

A required native Control spans input, projection, compilation, replay and output.
Checks also run during bounded stream writes. Independent tests use a 70-second
process watchdog for the 60-second native scope, since cooperative checks cannot
interrupt blocking I/O. Public durable adoption must preserve the original queued
deadline and final source/artifact/token/lease/publication fences through storage.

## Independent evidence and remaining integration

The independent checker reconstructs every raw derivative financial source with
the existing independent reference. It verifies exact saved identities, once-only
shared cash/equity opening, gross opening stocks, source financial/memo lineage,
ordered source transactions, actual pooled postings, closing GL and every daily
gross balance. The existing independent dated-source verifier separately checks
calendar recognition, scheduled settlement, rights, source provenance and closing
statements. No native financial callback is used to construct expected values.

Its current independently verified backbook is fully dated with unseasoned par
opening anchors and no discretionary policies, fees, tax, dividends or legacy
financial owners. Other backbook owners need their own independent combined
verification before they can obtain publication eligibility. This checker is a
test/analysis tool, never a production financial fallback.

Contained process checks cover swaps, receiver positions, signed coupons and
collateral interest, MPOR/default/closeout, cash and physical European exercise,
delayed settlement, collateral lag, supplied overnight conventions, distinct
physical scenarios and multiple derivative books sharing one opening cash pool.
Adversarial checks alter balanced postings, source policy, opening ownership,
ordered lineage, transaction identity, daily gross liabilities, dated recognition,
rights and completion. Native checks cover cancellation and admitted opening /
generated source binding. Current hand cases give combined closing cash 200.80
for the base swap plus dated loan and 200.42 for the reviewed MPOR case.

The frozen component source predecessor remains separately recorded in
`artifacts/saved-derivative-source/validation.json`; early failed mixed fixture
executions and missing historical test-fixture failures remain preserved.
Neither predecessor nor current contained evidence proves installed adoption,
empirical predictive accuracy, accounting-standard approval or complete scale.

Still required: public saved-book/native graph and paired risk integration,
cohort/library/candidate/strategy adoption, combined credit and behavioral owners,
capital/FTP policies, durable persisted publication, observed holdouts and the
complete 60,000-position graph/credit/solver/journal gate. The unchanged original
issue acceptance criteria remain authoritative in `implementation-plan.md`.

# Selected saved derivative stream adoption

This is an isolated source-adoption stage for issue #20. It moves the verified
`saved-derivative-mixed-1` coordinator into a proposed reusable Decision module and
adds a selected branch to the actual modeled-ledger dispatcher. Matching public
worker/API/saved-book acceptance remains required. The installed851 FTP bundle is
not changed by this proposal.

## Financial ownership

The existing native Risk saved-derivative source reconstructs raw trade terms,
contractual schedules, reviewed legal mapping, separate Pricing/Physical inputs,
collateral and closeout. The existing Ledger exclusive derivative owner receives
generated typed intents and opening stocks; it runs them through the actual shared
dated daily Sim and GL. The Decision coordinator binds source/run/account identities,
admits work, prepares each native source once and invokes that shared runner.

The public stream wrapper performs original-byte admission, bounded serialization
and checked output. It introduces no second coupon, option, exposure, collateral,
credit-loss or journal calculation. Generic owners cannot post a second copy of
derivative economics. Actual combined cash/equity are posted once; source custody
memo remains separate from financial GL, with gross derivative/collateral/unpaid
stocks retained through complete tails. See `saved-derivative-mixed.md` for the
financial contract and `saved-derivative-integration-plan.md` for full issue scope.

## Explicit public envelope and output

The proposed selected process accepts exactly:

```json
{"request":{"schema":"saved-derivative-mixed-1","dated":{},"owners":[]},"execution_timeout_ms":60000}
```

The empty nested objects above illustrate the envelope only; they are not valid
financial inputs. Complete dated sources, account opening anchors and every saved
owner/scenario source are mandatory. Timeout must be a valid positive native integer;
boolean, fractional, zero and unknown envelope fields reject. The original-byte
shared parser rejects duplicate object keys at every depth and trailing documents.
The selected original request retains JSON number categories and signed zero.

The first NDJSON record is a `workflow` header with
`schema="model-ledger-preparation-1"` and
`model_schema="saved-derivative-mixed-1"`. It retains both the original selected
request and the native source receipt with immutable original request, complete
native sources, joined work, owner capacity and explicit permission flags.
Subsequent records are the actual ordered shared journal/report stream, including
derivative source, opening and custody lineage. Exactly one actual native
`{"complete":true,"protocol":3}` record terminates the stream.

Financial source generation, full shared simulation and complete header/stream
byte admission finish before any header is emitted. Write, chunk and flush failures
propagate. Native control checks cover the scoped financial execution and output;
the transport watchdog and original accepted queue-time deadline must additionally
cover input, persistence and final publication in the remaining durable integration.
A native completion record alone is not a successful publication receipt.

## Independent evidence and bounds

The independent source gate rebuilds raw financial schedules, reviewed physical
accounting, complete source lineage, every ordered shared posting, once-only combined
opening and daily gross statements. Its seasoned successor also verifies asset and
funding premiums/discounts, gross accrued opening rights, immediate source fees,
day-zero/early cash and subsequent earned recognition. It preserves actual tiny
floating-point rights residues and existing final-output tolerances. Arbitrary
extra GL owners and altered raw source/posting evidence reject.

The selected body and complete public output are each at most32MiB. Existing
component limits retain up to64 run/source pairs,512 dated positions, eight million
joined work units and128MiB charged owner capacity. Native source transport and JSON
staging have separate budgets. None is an aggregate process-RSS guarantee or a
complete60000-position graph/credit/solver/journal acceptance receipt.

The frozen `artifacts/derivative-public-native/validation.json` records ten native
coordinator/wrapper checks,58 fresh historical compatibility checks, two strict
Clippy gates and29 actual public-process/independent source/journal checks. It pins
the exact851-source baseline, reviewed transplants and preserved FTP exports. The
contained harness compiles the exact proposed coordinator and shared owners; it
does not link the entire Decision/HiGHS library. The separate
`artifacts/derivative-public-dispatch/validation.json` now records a successful
complete copied Decision/HiGHS dispatcher build, 29 independent checks through its
actual `portfolio-model-ledger` executable, ten new coordinator/wrapper unit checks
inside the full Decision crate, and strict Clippy across that crate's targets.
The unit run filters to the new owner; it is not the full Decision test suite.
The executable SHA-256 is
`79b7249627af19fd4ef9b2927d4ad928652d2be207f333747005ae4feaa3e69a`;
the frozen validation receipt SHA-256 is
`1e7ed7dd3159e2616e1b5420cff74dd2b37a8c5e6d2fdccb6f3c3e08bbdb2766`.
The unchanged sources build under a shorter Windows target path. The original
`build.json` C++ path failure and the initial byte-limit error-wording assertion
failure are preserved. The assertion repair accepts the actual outer dispatcher's
32 MiB refusal without changing native source, admission or monetary tolerances.
Earlier fixture/module-path setup failures also remain preserved separately.

## Required follow-through

The next durable route must retain immutable raw request/source/executable identities,
an original finite deadline, exact attempt/token/lease/revision checks, bounded
Parquet partitions, producer completion and private raw/persisted reconstruction
through final scoped SQL publication. Paging/reopening cannot weaken these gates.

risk, coefficient-only strategy/library preparation, reviewed source-backed capital
and FTP, broader mixed credit/legacy ownership, empirical histories/holdouts and

issue is closed, no installed artifacts are replaced and no workers are restarted

# Explicit saved derivative source

The isolated `saved-derivative-source-1` contract binds a frozen saved book to the
existing Rust derivative accounting owner. Its schema and model version must be
selected explicitly. It is not installed-default or full issue #20 acceptance.

The book retains identity/revision, original as-of, entity/currency/unit, complete
dated trades and original legacy hedge rows. Every enhanced trade matches its
opening Physical node and legal mapping exactly, including order, curve/source
revisions and binary64 signed zero. Distinct rows with equal economics retain
distinct position owners. Each legacy row has one explicit position binding and
an explicit reviewed contractual upgrade. Notional, payer/receiver side, fixed
rate, final fixed/floating accrual ends and every indexed floating margin retain
the original saved anchors. Missing, surplus, duplicated or reordered ownership
rejects before financial projection. Complete enhanced books can have no legacy
rows or upgrade review.

This is an explicitly reviewed contractual upgrade. The old compact swap record
does not contain reset, calendar, fixing, settlement or legal terms; those terms
must be supplied in full. The binding does not infer them or assert that new
contractual schedules reproduce the historical generated schedules.

After mapping, the unchanged native `derivative_accounting` owner prepares marks,
coupon rights, European exercise/delivery, VM/IM, closeout and ordered journal
intents. Physical settlement evidence remains separate from Pricing projections;
XVA/funding diagnostics do not become journal loss or cash. Reviewed undesignated
policies, full daily calendars, original opening and complete rights/collateral
tails remain mandatory. Formal hedge accounting retains its existing rejection.

The independent verifier reconstructs saved coverage/economic anchors and exact
raw source identity, then uses the independent derivative raw-contract/journal
reference. Financial outputs retain the existing 1e-12 relative/1e-9 absolute
comparison. Source, metadata, dates, order, policies and binary64 source signs
use exact checks rather than those financial tolerances. Integer JSON spelling
is retained in the original request, while only explicitly declared financial
f64 cells receive typed normalization in the executed DTO.

## Shared transport utility and admission

The additive Core `strict_json` utility rejects duplicate object keys at every
depth before a `Value` decoder can erase them. It retains integer/float categories
and floating signed zero; it does not retain textual whitespace or number spelling.
Historical Value-first parsers are unchanged. This utility cannot recover keys
that an upstream HTTP parser has already discarded.

`serialized_size` counts escaped typed JSON without constructing an extra Value.
`encode` stages a bounded serialization without first cloning financial results
into a second JSON tree. Both refuse the first write exceeding the selected cap.
The selected source route bounds original and typed requests and staged output to
32 MiB, saved/legacy trades to 256 and Physical paths to one. Existing underlying
native admission includes 250,000 combined work, complete daily marks and its
separate product limits. These are component/wire limits, not an aggregate RSS
guarantee. Native cooperative checkpoints surround decoding/admission/projection
and encoding/writes; a process watchdog is still required for blocking IO.

## Recorded component evidence

`artifacts/saved-derivative-source/validation.json` records eight native tests,
strict all-target Clippy and 59 actual native process/independent checks. Receipt
SHA-256: `f708700aae668a1b55cd9e4b30340d3098f350fe350046e7394b4cc2c0213dd5`.
All 822 installed frozen files and the 162 copied baseline files were checked;
only two copied library export files changed, with additive source/helper files.
Underlying native derivative financial code is unchanged in that component.

Cases cover hand-computed coupon cash, signed rates, overnight conventions,
receiver and equal-economic rows, enforceable/gross legal buckets, European cash
and physical settlement, lag/outage/segregated collateral, default/MPOR and XVA
diagnostics. Refusal checks cover duplicate keys, row/owner aliases, partial or
permuted coverage, signed-zero source changes, wrong policies/measures/calendars
and altered raw/financial/journal receipts. No component receipt establishes
observed predictive accuracy, accounting/regulatory approval, saved UI/default
adoption, graph/risk/strategy/capital/FTP or full 60,000-position acceptance.

The successor `artifacts/derivative-mixed/` is connecting these native sources to
the existing Ledger Sim through a borrowed native interface. That successor is
in progress and has its own source, financial and independent mixed-journal gates;
the component receipt above must not be reused as proof that those gates pass.
The complete remaining requirements are in
[saved-derivative-integration-plan.md](saved-derivative-integration-plan.md).

# Explicit contractual term paths, conditional exercise and CD elections

`portfolio-risk-native::term_enhancements` adds three separate Rust capabilities:

| Native function | Raw protocol | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| `indexed::build_path(ContractPathRequest)` | `indexed-contract-1` | Supplied complete dated contractual/index scenario path |
| `exercise::value_exercise(ExerciseRequest)` | `conditional-exercise-1` | Native conditional continuation-value exercise on a supplied pricing tree |
| `cd::step_cd(CdElectionRequest)` | `cd-election-1` | Actual-date supplied physical withdrawal/maturity elections |

Every inner request requires schema `term-enhancements-1`, model version
`term-contracts-1`, uppercase three-letter currency, and monetary unit
`currency_units`. The native product JSON protocol wraps it with its route schema,
`threads` and `request`. Calculations execute in Rust; Python transports raw input.
These APIs are independent of the historical saved `annuity`, front-quarter
floating proxy, monthly option dates and threshold kernels. They do not change
those saved economics. Adoption requires explicit new input/model identity and a
rebuilt graph/unit library.

## Contractual path and floating index selection

The path specifies contract, assumption and path identities; actual accrual and
settlement dates; opening principal; a complete principal plan; and one coupon
specification per period. Payment may precede its unadjusted accrual end, including
modified-following or preceding settlement. Exact ordinals are retained. A
principal balance is constant within each supplied period; changing balances
require separate periods. Contractual cash recognition is separate from daily
earned-interest accounting.

Fixed coupons use `principal * annual_rate * actual_year_fraction`. Supported
actual day counts are ACT/360, ACT/365F and ACT/ACT ISDA. ACT/ACT splits leap-year
accrual at January 1. A caller requiring historical 30/360 uses the existing
explicit dated-term producer rather than silently changing its convention.

Indexed coupons require an index ID, kind and tenor/window; reference-calendar
identity; declared complete calendar mapping; exact reset and observation dates;
selected observed or conditional projected rates; separate index and all-in
bounds; margin treatment; and explicit lookback/observation-shift settings.

* `term_simple` requires a term or published-average index and one in-advance
  observation with an exact UTC reset cutoff at/before the accrual-start date.
* `daily_simple` and `daily_compounded` require an overnight index. Interest
  intervals exactly partition the coupon period. Under observation shift,
  observation intervals are also contiguous.
* Index bounds apply first. All-in bounds apply to selected index plus margin.
  They do not cap the final compounded effective period rate.
* With simple margin, index compounding uses the bounded all-in rate minus margin;
  margin accrues on the actual interest dates. A shifted observation changes the
  index weights, not the simple-margin weights.
* Compounded margin includes margin in each compound factor. Balance compounding,
  rate fallback, inferred publication, and missing observations are rejected.

For observation `i`, let `w_i` be its actual interest or shifted observation
year fraction and `u_i` its actual interest year fraction. Let `a_i` be the bounded
all-in rate and `m` the margin. On constant principal `B`:

```
daily simple, simple margin: B * sum((a_i - m) * w_i + m * u_i)
daily compounded, simple margin:
    B * (expm1(sum(log1p((a_i - m) * w_i))) + m * sum(u_i))
daily compounded, compounded margin:
    B * expm1(sum(log1p(a_i * w_i)))
```

Each compound factor must be positive. `log1p`/`expm1` preserve near-zero rates.
Signed negative interest is permitted within the positive claim-factor domain.

An observed source carries immutable fixing ID/revision and UTC publication time.
It must be available at the observation-selection cutoff and the declared observed
snapshot cutoff. The snapshot cutoff cannot follow the valuation date. A term
observation must also be available by its exact reset cutoff: an 08:00 publication
is rejected for a 07:00 reset and accepted for a 09:00 reset.

A projected source carries conditional model ID/revision, path ID/revision,
measure and UTC information time. Path and measure must equal the outer request;
projected coupons reject `Contractual` measure. Information must be available at
the exact observation-selection cutoff and, for term coupons, at reset. Projected
overnight selection must be on/before its observation date. The path is an explicit
conditional-model input, never inferred from a realized future discount ratio or
relabeled as a published benchmark.

**The arithmetic verifies dates, coverage and information availability; it does
not independently verify business-day calendar contents or the supplied business-
day lookback mapping.** Indexed audit records explicitly return
`calendar_mapping_verified=false`. The reviewed calendar/mapping producer must
establish that mapping before calling this API. Different index tenors are
different input identities even when a synthetic fixture happens to supply the
same rates.

`PrincipalPlan::Supplied` supports supplied sinking/equal-principal schedules and
balloons whose complete cash principal sums to opening principal.
`RetainedPayment` uses the supplied original payment, without recomputing it over
remaining tenor. Each regular principal amount is `original_payment - interest`.
Unsupported negative amortization rejects the request. The terminal rule is an
explicit residual payoff or a supplied extra balloon that must reconcile to the
recurrence. The last regular payment can shorten to the remaining principal.
Signed contractual fees are separate from principal/interest and do not imply
premium, discount or fee amortization.

The result retains all selected source identities, opening/closing principal,
coupons and terminal balloon audits. Its `DatedSchedule` contains the full tail;
`principal_after_reporting` is a separate report-horizon balance.

## Conditional call/put exercise

The exercise engine performs backward Bellman valuation over a supplied
chronological, topologically ordered conditional state DAG. Node zero is the sole
initial state at `asof`. Every node must be reachable; edges lead to later actual
dates. Branch probabilities are finite, positive and sum to one. Recombining
branches are supported. Child principal must equal parent principal after its
scheduled payment. Every unexercised leaf fully settles principal: no terminal
grid clipping or valuation residual is permitted.

Requests carry immutable contract, exercise policy, tree, market discount source,
base OAS anchor and common-random-number identities. Measure must be `Pricing` and
discount basis must be `market_without_oas`. Each edge supplies a conditional
probability and market discount factor. Rust applies

```
edge_discount = market_discount * exp(-fixed_base_oas * edge_year_fraction)
continuation = scheduled_cash + sum(probability * edge_discount * child_value)
```

Fixed base OAS is supplied and applied once. The component never recalibrates OAS,
draws random numbers or generates a rate tree. It preserves the supplied CRN
identity. Tree calibration, state sufficiency, branch probabilities and discount
source compatibility belong to the native market producer and its independent
validation.

Permitted call and put dates must occur exactly in the state DAG. Redemption is
face principal plus separately supplied accrued rights, clean redemption premium
and exercise fee. Clean price factors affect premium/discount cash fees rather
than changing extinguished face principal. A rule declares whether exercise
occurs before scheduled cash (scheduled payments are replaced) or after scheduled
cash (those payments survive and redemption applies to remaining principal).
Accrued rights have their own immutable source identity. An after-coupon right
must exclude the coupon just settled; that contractual rights allocation remains
the source producer's responsibility.

Issuer call selects `min(continuation, redemption)` and holder put selects
`max(continuation, redemption)` from the holder's perspective. Conflicting
same-date rights require explicit issuer or holder priority: the priority holder
acts last in the min/max composition. Strict comparisons retain the prior
decision on exact ties; absent a prior exercise, ties continue. Receipt/payment
direction changes the final reported sign, not the economic holder policy.

This is continuation-value exercise on the supplied pricing model. It does not
assert actual issuer behavior or optimality outside that model. It supports
immediate permitted-date settlement. Notice periods, delayed settlement,
make-whole reference pricing and other omitted contract mechanisms require a new
explicit policy representation, rather than a rate threshold or implicit date
move.

Durable `conditional-exercise-1` publication now independently replays the raw
tree's values, stopping policy and complete expected cash rights before and after
Parquet persistence. Native cooperative controls reach the tree through Rayon.
See [exercise publication and validation](term-exercise-publication.md) for the
receipt, unchanged financial tolerances and remaining adoption boundaries.

Forward alive-probability propagation follows the selected stopping policy and
removes future coupon/principal rights after exercise. The result reports node
continuation/value/decision and alive probability, a complete undiscounted expected
dated schedule, and expected principal after reporting. The expected schedule is
**Pricing measure**, not observed or Physical ledger cash. All call/put principal
cash reconciles to the initial face balance in expectation; premium is separate.
`canceled_future_principal` refers to the unexercised child principal tail.

## CD withdrawal, penalty and maturity state

`step_cd` takes a supplied `Physical` election and immutable contract/election/
policy identities. Opening state includes principal, signed accrued right,
last-accrual date, actual maturity, fixed annual rate and actual day count. Rust
earns interest to the election or maturity date, then applies the explicit grace
rate if election is within the contract's grace interval. It does not infer a
renewal during that delay. The earned delta is returned separately for state-aware
daily accounting; cash settlement is not itself another accrued recognition.

Early withdrawals must precede actual maturity, respect the earliest withdrawal
date, explicit channel restrictions, partial-withdrawal permission and minimum
remaining balance. Brokered withdrawals require an explicit contract override;
channel labels do not imply that liquidity exists.

Supported penalty rules are no penalty, a supplied number of interest days with
explicit penalty rate and 360/365 denominator, a principal fraction, or a fixed
amount. Inclusive dated waiver windows and a monetary cap are explicit. A policy
limits the penalty to positive allocated accrued interest or to principal plus
the signed allocated accrued claim. Penalty cannot create a negative total
withdrawal payment. Partial withdrawals allocate accrued rights pro rata to
withdrawn face principal; a contract requiring other allocations needs a distinct
policy, not a silent approximation.

Results separate gross principal removed, actual principal cash returned,
interest cash paid, penalty from accrued interest and penalty from principal.
Settlement components show gross extinguished principal, allocated interest and
the negative penalty fee; their sum equals external cash. Daily accounting must
use that explicit gross/net split. The remaining principal and accrued right
retain their complete dated maturity tail.

Maturity elections explicitly allocate principal and signed interest among
cash-out, renewal and switching. Both allocation sums must reconcile to the
matured state. Renewal and switching require permission and separately identified
new fixed-bullet contracts, with distinct position IDs, maturity, coupon and day
count. New principal includes the selected signed interest capitalization. It
must remain nonnegative. No future renewal is assumed.

`settlement_schedule` reports the same-date gross old claim settlement and each
new contract's reinvestment separately. `net_external_cash` therefore equals the
cash-out principal plus cash-out interest, with the declared direction.
`remaining_schedule` contains the old residual or new fixed bullet maturity
tails, separate from today's settlements. Consumers must not add those tails to
today's funding; they are future cashflows. All new maturities must fit the
explicit complete tail domain even when the report horizon ends earlier.

These policies implement reviewed supplied terms. They do not fit product,
channel or account withdrawal/renewal hazards, infer customer switching, or
certify a disclosure regime. Observed behavior holdout evidence is separate from
the synthetic financial fixtures.

## Bounds, identity and integration

The contractual path admits 1..4096 periods and at most 250,000 total index
observations. Exercise admits at most 100,000 nodes, 400,000 edges and 4096 permitted
dates. CD admits at most 256 ordered, nonoverlapping waiver windows and at most
366 grace days. Lookbacks are at most 366 business days. All actual-date domains
are at most 36,600 days and lie within Gregorian years 1..9999. Monetary values are
finite and bounded by shared `MAX_MONETARY_AMOUNT` (1e15). Metadata IDs/revisions
are 1..128 control-free bytes, with 32 MiB combined metadata admission. The native
JSON transport adds its separate request/output limits. These component bounds
are not an aggregate process RSS guarantee.

Inputs reject unknown fields. Every curve/tree/path/fixing/contract/calendar/
policy/measure/unit/model identity belongs in graph/cache identity, including
selection timestamps, exact dates, clean-price priority and complete tails.
Saved legacy models remain readable under their own identities. Model adoption
requires explicit source preparation, native graph/unit build and worker rebuild;
interactive strategy evaluation consumes prepared coefficients.

`build_path` deliberately generates contractual/indexed flows without borrower
default. Commercial borrower and issuer credit must use the appropriate shared
credit state, EAD/default-draw, nonaccrual and complete recovery tail coordinator;
they cannot be replaced by a second proportional survival haircut. The exercise
module requires the same credit interpretation in tree cashflows and discounts.
The CD module's modeled Physical elections must be joined to state-aware dated
accrual and accounting intents, then independently persisted-journal verified.
No successful publication or deployment is implied by these component tests.

## Independent examples and verification

The checked-in examples are complete native protocol envelopes, not calibrated
market or customer observations:

* `examples/models/term-indexed.json`: February 1 to March 1, 2024 has 29 days.
  One-month selected rate 0.02 plus margin 0.01 on face 100 gives
  `100 * 0.03 * 29 / 360 = 0.2416666666666667`; principal 100 is paid March 1.
  Reporting ends February 1, so principal after reporting remains 100.
* `examples/models/term-exercise.json`: after the January 2 coupon of 5,
  continuation is `5 + 105 = 110`; call costs `5 + 100 = 105`. The issuer calls.
  Value January 1 is `0.98 * 105 = 102.9`; maturity alive probability is zero.
* `examples/models/term-cd-election.json`: five days of interest at 0.365 on 100
  gives 0.5. Withdrawal face 40 allocates 0.2 interest. Penalty is
  `40 * 0.05 * 90 / 365 = 0.4931506849315068`. External cash is
  `40.2 - penalty = 39.70684931506849`; remaining face is 60 and complete
  January 11 maturity interest is 0.6.

`tests/term_indexed.rs`, `term_exercise.rs`, `cd_elections.rs` and
`term_examples.rs` provide 21 independent tests. They cover retained original
payments/balloons, leap stubs, fees, signed/zero coupons, complete tails,
publication/reset availability, distinct tenors, weekend/shift/bounds/near-zero
compounding, conditional exercise versus wrong perfect foresight, call/put bounds,
cash ordering, simultaneous priority, fixed OAS once, CRN identity, partial/full
withdrawals, penalty limits, brokered restrictions, grace, renewal/switch funding
and failure admission.

A stochastic refinement fixture uses normalized binomial states converging to
`100 exp(0.3 Z - 0.3^2/2)`. Its independent analytical call cap is
`E[min(100, terminal)] = 200 Phi(-0.15) = 88.0764615259515`.
16/64/256-step approximations approach this value. This validates the conditional
exercise arithmetic and discretization of this synthetic fixture; it is not
convergence evidence for a calibrated production rate tree. A separate
deterministic discount subdivision preserves option-free economics exactly within
existing numerical tolerance.

## Primary sources and remaining issue scope

The [ARRC syndicated-loan technical appendices](https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/Microsites/arrc/files/2020/ARRC-Syndicated-Loan-Conventions-Technical-Appendices.pdf)
distinguish daily simple/compound methods and lookback/observation-shift weighting.
This implementation makes those choices explicit rather than substituting the
front-quarter simulated rate. The caller still supplies the reviewed date mapping
and conditional index model.

[Lim, Li and Linetsky's callable/putable bond research](https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.5046)
formulates exercise as a stopping game with backward valuation. The
[QuantLib callable-bond source](https://github.com/lballabio/QuantLib/blob/master/ql/experimental/callablebonds/discretizedcallablefixedratebond.cpp)
separates call/put application and coupon ordering. These support the explicit
Bellman and same-date-order design; this implementation does not import QuantLib
or claim its market-model calibration.

[CFPB Regulation DD account-disclosure guidance](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1030/4/)
addresses early-withdrawal penalty calculation and renewal/grace terms. Its
[interest guidance](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1030/7/)
also distinguishes withdrawn principal, accrued interest and grace-period
interest. These motivate explicit supplied contract policies. They do not imply
that one penalty or renewal rule applies to every CD.

Issues #15/#16 remain broader than these components: native conditional market
projection/tree generation and graph risk adoption, complete commercial/issuer
credit integration, unit/ledger/NII/FTP follow-through, supported delayed or
make-whole exercise, and empirical withdrawal/renewal calibration still require
their own acceptance evidence. A component implementation alone does not close
those issue acceptance criteria.

## Chronological CD sequence stage

The contained Rust `cd-election-sequence-1` owner in
`artifacts/cd-election-sequence-stage/` uses the same native CD contractual step
for repeated withdrawals, renewal and later elected actions. Native-derived
balances and original/new contract identities condition each subsequent action.
Only actual election settlements and the final unsuperseded bullet tails enter
its complete cash schedule. Earlier step-level maturity forecasts remain source
receipts and must not be added to that cash a second time. Same-date action
precedence is explicit; renewal acquisition cash offsets old gross settlement
only through signed external cash, without erasing either transaction.

For face100 at36.5% actual/365 from Jan1 to Jan11, withdrawing40 on Jan6 and20
on Jan9 allocates interest0.20 and0.16; remaining face40 pays interest0.40 at
maturity. Total0.76 is the outstanding-face time integral. A Jan8 reporting
date neither truncates the tail nor implies an invented repayment. Penalty,
signed coupon rights and renewal math remain owned by the existing shared native
contract. The sequence CLI retains original JSON separately from its typed DTO.

Eight native cases and four independent actual-process tests pass, including
twelve independently calculated signed rate/penalty fixtures; all-target strict
Clippy passes. The retained validation receipt SHA-256 is
`ba7df7d1e97de6d9d70a1960fc0db1242551d1782052434d8f9e87bf2157fa28`.
No installed source/default native artifact changed. This stage requires at least
one election; a shared no-election terminal projection is required before
complete graph-history adoption. Expanded switch/grace policies, compounding/
periodic payout and explicit remaining-rate changes require additional source
policies and independent raw replay. The original issues still require public
graph/base-OAS/cache, accounting/FTP/library/saved-book adoption, joint exercise
generation and observed holdouts. Detailed schemas, control bounds and primary
modeling references are in the stage README; none of these checks establish
empirical behavior or regulatory/accounting eligibility.

# Corporate exercise source verification and publication

## Local acceptance: 0.29.9, 2026-10-10 UTC

The final matching-source checks pass **409 native product all-target tests**,
strict all-target/all-feature product Clippy, **88 affected engine tests in
17.18 seconds**, and **285 affected API/worker/persistence tests in 113.80
seconds**. The API slice includes complete model-worker restart coverage, scalar
transport, exercise corruption/type/identity gates and source/persisted/final
publication failures. The engine slice includes native corporate/CD ownership,
enhanced contracts and the thirteen independent exercise-oracle cases.

All three official release artifact builds succeed; the unchanged ledger build
is current. Product rebuild takes 6m20s and dependent decision rebuild 8m26s;
these are compilation times, not model performance measurements. Official
decision release Clippy also passes. Architecture, seven boundary-script tests,
native ABI and HTTP contracts, version/lock consistency and packaged operator
mirrors pass. The version is synchronized at 0.29.9 and financial schemas/ABI
are unchanged.

The initial combined Python collection used an incorrect working root and
failed to import the API package. The suites were rerun separately. An initial
release attempt failed because concurrent tests held the Windows DLL; tests
then exited and the rebuild succeeded. An intermediate API rerun was stopped
before dependent builds finished; the final 285-case run is complete. None of
those failed/interrupted predecessors is counted as passing evidence.
The broader 2,378-engine/920-API checkpoint in the implementation ledger is
previous-turn evidence, not a fresh full-suite run for this stage. Changes remain
local and uncommitted. #15 is open and its complete original acceptance is retained.

This #15 follow-through applies to the existing `conditional-exercise-1` route.
It changes neither `term-contracts-1` economics nor historical saved contracts.
Rust performs conditional exercise valuation. The durable worker now requires
an independent complete raw-tree replay before formatting and again after
reopening its immutable Parquet result, using the original publication deadline.

## Financial verification

`analytics.term_exercise_reference` independently constructs values from the
immutable raw request. It calls no native callback or production pricer. The
only shared arithmetic helper is the independent actual-day-count reference.
For each node it computes scheduled cash plus conditional discounted child
values, applies the fixed original OAS exactly once per edge, and compares
continuation against permitted immediate redemption. Issuer call minimizes
holder value; holder put maximizes it. Simultaneous priority, exact tie behavior,
before/after scheduled cash, signed accrued rights, clean premiums and fees
remain explicit supplied policies.

Forward stopped-probability propagation independently reconstructs every
expected cashflow. Recombining nodes sum incoming live probability; exercised
branches retain no future rights. Reporting principal is separate from the full
maturity tail. Complete node audits, including unreachable-under-policy nodes,
cash components, accrual periods, actual dates, measure, provenance, policy,
original OAS and shared-draw identity must match. Unknown/missing fields, wrong
counts, nonfinite amounts, boolean amounts and floating-point dates reject.
The financial comparison uses the existing independent-reference tolerances
of 1e-12 relative and 1e-9 currency units absolute; it does not alter production
financial tolerances. Disclosure text is required but is not a financial source.
The original supplied OAS must match exactly. Probability comparisons use
1e-12 relative and 1e-14 absolute tolerance, separately from currency amounts.

The receipt records independently recomputed node/edge/event counts and explicitly
retains `measure="pricing"`, `physical_journal_eligible=false` and
`empirical_validation=false`. Persisted publication requires the same recomputed
receipt and scalar summary, plus the existing raw-input, source, executable,
deadline, cancellation and lease/token fences. A receipt alone is insufficient.

## Cooperative execution

`value_exercise_with_check` checkpoints during admission, every node and branch
in backward valuation and forward propagation, principal conservation and final
audit construction. The existing public wrapper uses native compute control.
The dispatcher explicitly transfers the caller's control across Rayon and
preserves `COMPUTE_CANCELLED` and `COMPUTE_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`. Failed execution
returns no partial policy. Bounded schedule validation and JSON conversion have
fences around them; their inner library operations are not separately interruptible.
The standalone process watchdog remains in force. Component work/transport
bounds are unchanged and are not an aggregate RSS guarantee.

## Validation and limitations

Tests compare raw replay against Rust for simultaneous rights, both cash timings,
receipt/payment signs, signed accrued rights, original OAS and recombining states.
Option-free, called and puttable supplied-state refinements at 16/64/256 steps
are compared with independent normal-integral lognormal expectations. The
option-free value remains 100; the call-capped limit is
`100 * erfc(0.15 / sqrt(2))` and the put floor is its complementary `200 - cap`.
This synthetic terminal-right fixture verifies supplied-tree numerical
convergence, not a calibrated corporate rate model. Existing native checks for
actual dates, call/put ordering, no perfect foresight and complete tails remain.

Fault tests alter policy, values, all stopped cash components, identities,
dead-node audits, shape and numerical domains. Every native checkpoint is tested
for both failure reasons; real delayed Rayon dispatch checks inner failure
independently of the outer scope. Durable fault tests cover corruption and
cancellation before and after persistence, missing receipts and final fences.

The min/max exercise and explicit coupon ordering agree with the financial
operations in [QuantLib's callable-bond implementation](https://github.com/lballabio/QuantLib/blob/master/ql/experimental/callablebonds/discretizedcallablefixedratebond.cpp).
That implementation's nearby-date snapping is not part of this exact-date
contract. No QuantLib code was copied into the independent oracle.

This closes an exercise-result publication gap. It does not generate a calibrated
tree, joint credit/market states, notice-delayed settlement, commercial draws,
nonaccrual, recoveries, ledger postings, library coefficients or saved-book/cohort
adoption. Those #15 gates and observed validation remain required. Rebuild native
product and dependent ledger/decision artifacts before use; deployed workers and
saved sessions need their existing explicit restart/rebuild procedure. Local
validation is not deployment or empirical acceptance.

# Supplied CD election sequence graph (proposal)

`term-product-graph-2` selects chronological CD sequence pricing in the existing native term graph. `term-product-reprice-2` supplies `{base,current}`. The nested graph schema is `term-product-graph-2`; the history schema is `cd-election-sequence-2`. These are an unapplied proposal, requiring rebuilt native libraries before use. The Python methods only transport the raw request.

## Sources and immutable original economics

Every position has known opening terms, a complete authorized renewal/switch term universe, reviewed policy identities and a locked original OAS. `original_base` contains the complete original scenario and ordered original physical/pricing/down/up histories for every position. `original_quotes` contains one ordered reviewed signed future-cash quote per position. Creation checks that quote against the original pricing cash and original collateral curve with the supplied original OAS. It never solves an OAS. As-of settlement is retained as opening cash and excluded from that future-cash quote.

Current scenarios and histories are separate editable inputs. Their ordered pricing/down/up path IDs and weights must match each other and the original pricing pairs. Physical histories are supplied independently; there is no Physical-to-Pricing transformation or inferred election behavior. Zero weights remain retained and validated. Contract, action and policy identities may not be reused with different content. Authorized terms and policy ownership must match exactly, including negative-zero financial identity. A renewal uses its actual supplied maturity, coupon and contract identity; no automatic renewal is inferred.

`TermGraph::new` prepares all original and current native sources and binds the original receipt. `TermGraph::reprice` validates the current request on every call, retains the original source/anchor, and prepares only the current sources. Its immutable base key includes schema, model/pairing parent identity, opening calendar, known terms, locked OAS, complete original parents and quotes. Original quote, curve, path or term edits require a rebuild; editable current collateral/history changes cannot rewrite them.

## Cash and pricing ownership

The sequence owner uses the existing `cd::step_cd`/`step_cd_pricing` contractual arithmetic and shared pure `cd::project_cd_tail`. No-election sequences use that tail projector directly. Each action accrues its live owner to the election date, settles the actual instruction and retains live closing/new owners. Stable supplied same-date action order is explicit precedence. Final pricing cash contains every actual election settlement plus only the final unsuperseded live tails. Intermediate step preview tails are evidence, never additional priced cash.

For each future event, the existing native pricing function computes

`cash * DF_collateral(actual_days/365) * exp(-original_OAS * actual_days/365)`.

Cash is the signed sum of principal, interest and fees. The existing within-path compensated sum and supplied path-order weighted reduction remain unchanged. Supplied-history DV01 prices the paired down/up histories with the declared collateral/OAS bumps. This can include supplied election differences; it is not an optimal-exercise Greek or a calibrated behavioral model.

Physical reports distinguish principal, interest, fees and action diagnostics. Penalty/gross-extinguished/new-principal diagnostics are not additional cash. Reporting intervals are `(left,right]`; as-of cash has a separate opening amount. Pricing and retained physical tails continue past the last report. These are contractual cash metrics, not reviewed original-EIR daily NII or journal recognition.

## Signed and post-principal-zero rights

Negative contractual coupons and signed accrued rights are retained. Principal reaching zero does not retire a nonzero earned-interest right. An exact regression retains `8.881784197001252e-16` after full withdrawal and pays its signed amount at the actual maturity date; it is neither clamped nor used as a balancing plug. The preceding frozen tail-stage proof was insufficient for this residual-right edge. Residual states are explicitly before their separately retained terminal settlement, not certified accounting closing balances.

## Admission and runtime limits

The graph retains the existing limits: 256 positions, 13 scenarios, 120 reporting intervals, 128 paths per role, 4,096 joined original/current runs, 250,000 conservative/generated rows and 8,000,000 work units. Sequence histories allow at most 256 actions and 256 live policy owners, and at most 1 MiB typed raw bytes each. The complete graph raw input is bounded at 32 MiB. Full-tail/calendar checks reject inadequate source tails rather than invent terminal cash.

Before projection, checked conservative admission reserves original and current source rows, retained raw/source metadata, original/current curve nodes, metric/risk calls and transient index/risk work. The component bound is `12*typed_raw_bytes + 32768*reserved_rows + 8*reserved_work <= 128 MiB`. It intentionally retains the historical conservative pricing-call reserve even though the new branch does not calibrate OAS. After generation, actual retained serialization and key bytes are checked again against 128 MiB. This is a component capacity contract, not an aggregate process-RSS or 60,000-position claim.

The new strict selected boundary rejects duplicate nested fields and non-string aliases of declared unit enums before financial preparation. Historical graph1 admission uses its mechanically copied DTO-only parser; explicit new null/empty fields and sequence variants remain historical unknown-field/variant errors. Its shared native financial owner is unchanged. Raw requests that have already been collapsed to JSON Value cannot prove duplicate-key absence retroactively.

The contained proof carries an active native Control through parsing, admission, source generation, pricing and checked output writes/flushes. The proposed dispatcher propagates active control through Rayon only for this new selected branch. Existing public `term_call` has no per-call controlled capability for these schema names; default-library process watchdog or future durable-job fences must not be described as cooperative caller cancellation. Default native, persisted, API and browser execution remain pending installation/rebuild.

## Validation and remaining gates

Contained evidence: 35 native tests and strict all-target Clippy; 9 independent tests reconstruct CD sequence cash, native source receipts, signed PV, paired DV01, original quote/anchor and physical cash. There are 26 accepted and 5 rejected serialized process cases, plus a real duplicate-key byte rejection. Test-only native counters prove zero solver calls at creation and warm repricing. Twelve historical native fixtures and a complete nonempty legacy output/errored mutation comparison preserve graph1 behavior.

Authored installed-default gates forbid Python financial callbacks and use the ordinary default library in fresh processes. They are proposals, not executed acceptance. The independent reference currently admits CD-only graph2 books; indexed-term coexistence is supported natively but needs a composed independent source gate before publication. Intermediate preview settlement tails are not independently certified accounting inputs. The separate [CD public publication proposal](cd-sequence-publication.md) adds complete raw/persisted preview/cash/risk checks through the real native owner and copied durable worker; installed default acceptance remains a distinct gate. Real incremental registry, saved-book/library/cohort mapping, joint stochastic exercise, empirical calibration, mixed daily journals, capital and FTP adoption remain open. The result explicitly marks joint optimal exercise, accounting, empirical validation, saved/library/cohort adoption and capital/FTP eligibility false.

Contractual/math foundations: [term enhancements](term-enhancements.md), [existing term graph](term-product-graph.md), and [floating-rate conventions](floating-rate.md). No accounting-standard or depositor-behavior approval is inferred from supplied research policies.

# Supplied indexed-term and CD product graph

`term-product-graph-1` adds Rust graph analysis for explicit term contractual
paths and supplied CD elections. It is the graph/API stage of #15/#16, with
joint credit/market optimal exercise, empirical behavior, complete library,
saved-book/verified ledger and treasury acceptance still separate gates.
The public API is `term_product_graph::analyze(&Request)` and immutable
`TermGraph::{new,request,snapshot,base_anchor,reprice,repriced}`.

Each position supplies typed known terms: `indexed_term` has a contractual
`indexed::ContractPathRequest`; `cd_election` has `CdKnown` with explicit source
model version, currency, direction, policy, opening state and complete tail.
The graph consumes per-scenario supplied P/Q/Q-down/Q-up requests with explicit
path IDs/probabilities and native run IDs. P can have independent paths/weights;
ordered Q identities/weights match across all scenarios and bumps for each
position. Weights sum to one within `1e-12` without normalization, and zero-weight
paths still execute. The supplied paired-history domain generates no random
draws and does not fit a Physical-to-Pricing probability conversion.

## Original contract and rate-source preservation

Indexed histories preserve known contract/source version, original principal
plan/payment, dates, direction, fees, fixed coupon rates, index descriptor,
daycount, margin/bounds, reset/selection convention and observation geometry.
Only explicitly conditional index rate/source/path slots may vary. Observed
fixings are immutable by ID/revision/index/fixing date/rate/publication across
the graph. Projected information must be available at its selected reset;
future publication is never synthesized as an observed fixing. Complete native
coupon audits preserve selected sources and supplied calendar mappings remain
reported as unverified. No front-quarter proxy or curve-implied fallback exists.

Original supplied amortization or retained payment remains original. A scenario
does not recompute payment using remaining tenor. Saved legacy `annuity` remains
the existing equal-principal convention under its old identity; this new graph
does not reinterpret saved contracts. See [term-enhancements.md](term-enhancements.md)
and [contractual-amortization.md](contractual-amortization.md) for the existing
explicit contract equations and supported model boundaries.

The new CD helper `cd::step_cd_pricing` requires explicitly declared Pricing
requests and uses the same private arithmetic with native cash events tagged Q.
Original `cd::step_cd` remains Physical-only with identical financial output,
admission, source and disclosure. This additive helper does not take a Physical
request and relabel its behavior as Q: each graph pricing history must independently
declare its supplied election, reviewed policy/source and pricing probability.

## Supported CD path and owned full tails

The graph supports **one supplied CD election per path**, followed by the
native component's complete fixed remaining maturity/renewal/switch tails.
It preserves known contractual policy and asof opening state; it does not infer
later withdrawals, automatic renewal, issuer optimization or borrower liquidity.
Known `last_accrual_ordinal` must equal graph asof. Source reporting handoff is
`max(graph final report,election date)` because the existing election component
reports at/after its modeled election. Graph cash reports still use their own
actual `(left,right]` boundaries, including reports ending before the election.

Opening and generated CD accrued rights cannot be negative/prepaid; a terminal
zero-principal state cannot retain unowned accrued rights. Remaining maturity
interest cannot represent negative prepaid rights in this graph tier. The
standalone Physical CD API's signed-interest scope is unchanged. Indexed term
cash supports signed coupons and either receipt/payment direction.

Every new renewal/switch position has an explicit contract/source/date/rate and
belongs to its originating graph position. New IDs cannot collide with existing
positions, another child in the same election or children assigned to another
parent. Unused/contradictory contracts and out-of-tail maturities fail under the
native election validator. Additional future actions are not accepted/pruned.

Partial withdrawal retains the remaining original principal/accrual in its full
native maturity tail. Penalty separates accrued-interest forfeiture from
principal-funded cost and gross face extinction from principal returned. Native
cash records **gross constructive allocated interest and principal plus the
full negative penalty fee** (sign reversed for a liability). Graph principal/
interest/fee fields preserve those exact components. Separate signed
`cd_interest_cash_paid`, `cd_principal_cash_returned` and `cd_net_external_cash`
diagnostics retain the actual after-penalty settlement and are never added again
to cash or PV. `cd_interest_accrued_through_election` is a native diagnostic on
the election date, not a daily earned-income allocation or effective-yield NII.

Renewal/switch preserves one gross old settlement and separate reinvestment,
followed by the new fixed tail. The graph iterates settlement and remaining
schedules once each; it does not also add `net_external_cash` or retain the old
unmodified maturity after its extinguishment. Complete principal/cash rights and
all fixed tails survive the reporting horizon. No terminal cash is invented.

## Pricing and immutable base

PV uses future native declared-Q principal/interest/fees, the scenario's supplied
collateral DF and original per-position `exp(-base_oas*actual_days/365)` spread.
`after_opening_actions` excludes same-asof settlements from future PV and
`(left,right]` reporting but retains them in `opening_actions`. Receipt direction
gives asset-positive cash; Payment gives liability-negative cash. Curve sources,
log-DF interpolation and reject/flat-zero/flat-forward tails remain explicit.

Locked OAS lies in [-5,5]. `calibrate_positive_cash` targets positive magnitude
in the position's explicit direction, preserving signed liability PV/DV01. Any
opposing future event, including constructive renewal funding, requires locked
OAS; the positive solver does not silently net events or change target semantics.
Original base calibration retains complete known terms/base Q histories, target
source, base curve/scenario, model/source/paired identity and timing convention.
Changed dependencies report `BASE_ANCHOR_CHANGED`. Nonbase scenarios, P/down/up
histories, input revision and compatible report boundaries may change while
retaining that exact original anchor. Scenario pricing never re-solves OAS.
Signed `supplied_history_dv01` combines native +/- curve bumps and supplied paired
Q down/up cash with the original OAS.

The separate [conditional exercise DAG](term-enhancements.md) remains its own
native reviewed route. This graph does not claim market-curve consistent joint
call/put/credit optimal exercise adoption or treat a threshold as optimization.
Those generation/integration limits remain open explicitly.

## Bounds, fixtures and example

Before projection, admission bounds 256 positions, 13 scenarios, 120 report
periods, 128 paths per role, 4,096 runs and 4,096 periods/observations per supported
indexed field; CD paths have one election and bounded waiver windows. Worst-case
native audit/source/cash rows are limited to 250,000 and report/calibration/source
work to 8 million units. Streamed input byte counting precedes canonical
dependency comparisons at 32 MiB; full raw/native result/base identities use a
128 MiB retained capacity estimate. These are component limits, not aggregate
RSS or a combined 60,000-position lifecycle claim. Native financial domains,
full principal/tails and chronological election feasibility fail closed.

The [synthetic raw example](../../examples/models/term-product-graph-1.json) has
a 100-principal loan at 0.36 ACT/360 for 29 days: future receipt is 102.9.
The CD liability starts at 100 with 0.365 ACT/365F and withdraws 40 on day 5;
earned accrued interest is 0.5, withdrawal allocation 0.2, penalty
`40*0.05*90/365 = 0.4931506849315068`, and principal-funded penalty
`0.2931506849315068`. Remaining principal 60 and interest 0.6 settle on day 10.
With collateral rate 0.05 and locked OAS -0.05 cancelling, CD signed PV is
`-100.30684931506849`. Its gross cash components are principal -100, interest
-0.8 and fee +0.4931506849315068; the after-penalty withdrawal cash is
-39.70684931506849. This is a synthetic hand fixture, not observed behavior.

Tests independently cover actual cash/signs, original retained payment,
Physical-only compatibility and declared-Q event tags, partial penalties,
constructive renewal once-only cash, closed-form OAS and frozen repricing,
explicit indexed measures, paired identity, negative/unowned rights and budget
failure. Reference tolerances stay `1e-12` relative and `1e-9` absolute.

The [New York Fed reference-rate methodology](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/additional-information-about-reference-rates)
motivates exact observation/publication and revision identities. The underlying
contract/exercise/CD primary sources and limitations are in
[term-enhancements.md](term-enhancements.md). Inputs still require reviewed
applicable contract/election policies; this graph makes no universal issuer,
accounting-standard or empirical market-probability claim.
